dervis-irab:86-86.t:
* I'rab:
(أُولئِكَ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject). (الَّذِينَ): a relative noun, khabar (predicate). (اشْتَرَوُا): the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (الْحَياةَ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الدُّنْيا): naʿt (adjective) qualifying «الحياة». (بِالْآخِرَةِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اشتروا». (فَلا): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), and «لا» is negating. (يُخَفَّفُ): a passive imperfect verb, and the clause is a second khabar of the demonstrative. (عَنْهُمُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يخفف». (الْعَذابُ): nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (وَلا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction joining to what preceded, «لا» is negating, «هم» is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause «ينصرون» is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
The dependent implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya al-tabaʿiyya) in buying the life of this world with the Hereafter; its like has already been discussed.

dervis-irab:87-87.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قَفَّيْنا): "We made [them] follow"; the whole root denotes following. «القفا» is anything that follows, and it is the back of the neck; from it comes «قافية» of poetry (the rhyme), because it follows the verse. (عِيسَى): a non-Arabic proper name; in Syriac it is «ايشوع» (Yeshuʿ), and it is not derived from «العيس», which is a whiteness mixed with a reddish tinge.
(مَرْيَمَ): a non-Arabic proper name, and for this reason it is a diptote. In the Arabic language, «المريم» among women is like «الزير» among men; «الزّير» is the one who mixes with women and jests with them, without wrongdoing or with it.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ): the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is [in] the answer to an omitted oath, and «قد» is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). (آتَيْنا): a verb and its fāʿil (agent). (مُوسَى): first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الْكِتابَ): second mafʿūl bihi. (وَقَفَّيْنا): conjoined to «آتينا». (مِنْ بَعْدِهِ): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (بِالرُّسُلِ): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «قفينا». (وَآتَيْنا): conjoined to what preceded. (عِيسَى): first mafʿūl bihi. (ابْنَ): badal (substitute) or naʿt (adjective). (مَرْيَمَ): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الْبَيِّناتِ): second mafʿūl bihi; the sign of its accusative is the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. (وَأَيَّدْناهُ): conjoined to what preceded. (بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «أيدناه». (أَفَكُلَّما): the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «كلما» is an adverb of time containing the sense of a condition. (جاءَكُمْ): a past verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi. (رَسُولٌ): fāʿil of «جاء», and the clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (بِما): the bāʾ is a preposition, and «ما» is a relative noun, genitive by the bāʾ in position; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «جاءكم». (لا): negating. (تَهْوى): an imperfect verb. (أَنْفُسُكُمُ): fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila (relative clause). (اسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ): a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. (فَفَرِيقاً): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «فريقا» is a fronted mafʿūl bihi. (كَذَّبْتُمْ): a verb [with its agent]. (وَفَرِيقاً): the wāw is a conjunction, and «فريقا» is a fronted object of «تقتلون». (تَقْتُلُونَ): an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil.

dervis-irab:88-88.t:
* Vocabulary:
(غُلْفٌ): plural of «أغلف», which originally is the uncircumcised one, i.e. [the heart] that does not take in or understand; the meaning is: they are covered with wrappings, and no one knows what lies behind them.

* I'rab:
(وَقالُوا): the wāw is resumptive, and «قالوا» is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). (قُلُوبُنا): mubtadaʾ (subject), and «نا» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (غُلْفٌ): khabar (predicate) of «قلوبنا», and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (بَلْ): a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb). (لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ): a past verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil. (بِكُفْرِهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «لعنهم», i.e. because of their disbelief. (فَقَلِيلًا): the fāʾ is resumptive, and «قليلا» is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "they believe with a little belief". (ما): a vague indefinite noun, an adjective of «قليلا». (يُؤْمِنُونَ): an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).

dervis-irab:89-90.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ): they seek victory; «فتح الله على نبيه» means He gave him victory. Here is a curious aspect of the description of the Jews: they used to seek victory against the disbelievers when they fought them, saying: "O Allah, give us victory through the Prophet who is mentioned among us in the Torah."

* I'rab:
(وَلَمَّا): the wāw is resumptive, and «لما» is adverbial meaning "when" (ḥīna), or it is a particle merely for linking; it contains the sense of a condition. (جاءَهُمْ): a verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (كِتابٌ): fāʿil (agent). (مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب»; the clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it if we parse «لما» as adverbial, or has no grammatical position if it is a linking particle; the answer of «لما» is omitted, its implied form being "they disbelieved" or the like. (مُصَدِّقٌ): also a naʿt of «كتاب». (لَمَّا): the lām is a preposition, and «ما» is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «مصدق». (مَعَهُمْ): mafʿūl bihi, an adverb of place attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause). [Translator's note: the source reads «مفعول به ظرف مكان»; «مع» is an adverb (mafʿūl fīhi), so «مفعول به» appears to be a slip, likely for «مفعول فيه».] (وَكانُوا): the wāw is a conjunction, and what is conjoined is the omitted answer; «كان» and its noun. (مِنْ قَبْلُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ): an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is verbal, in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of «كانوا». (عَلَى الَّذِينَ): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to «يستفتحون». (كَفَرُوا): a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (فَلَمَّا): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «لما» is temporal (ḥīniyya) or linking. (جاءَهُمْ): its i'rab has preceded. (ما): a relative noun, fāʿil. (عَرَفُوا): a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. (كَفَرُوا بِهِ): a verbal clause with no grammatical position because it is the answer of «لما». (فَلَعْنَةُ): the fāʾ is causal, and «لعنة» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause has no grammatical position because it is in the status of a resumptive clause. (اللَّهِ): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of «لعنة»; the meaning is that the curse of Allah is caused by what preceded. (بِئْسَمَا): «بئس» is a past verb for expressing blame, and «ما» is a complete (tāmma) indefinite noun meaning "a thing", in the position of the accusative as tamyīz (specification); it explains the fāʿil of «بئس», meaning "evil is it as a thing". (اشْتَرَوْا): a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is an adjective of «ما». (بِهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «اشتروا». (أَنْفُسَهُمْ): mafʿūl bihi. (أَنْ يَكْفُرُوا): «أن» and what falls within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), a mubtadaʾ, because it is the specifically blamed (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm), and the clause of «بئس» is the fronted khabar. (بِما): the bāʾ is a preposition, and «ما» is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يكفروا». (أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ): a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. (بَغْياً): mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); it is the reason for «اشتروا» or the reason for «يكفروا». (أَنْ يُنَزِّلَ اللَّهُ): «أن» and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "they transgressed because of Allah's sending down". (مِنْ فَضْلِهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are also attached to «ينزل». (عَلى مَنْ يَشاءُ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «ينزل»; «يشاء» is a verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). (مِنْ عِبادِهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl explaining «لمن يشاء». (فَباؤُ بِغَضَبٍ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, «باءوا» is a verb and its fāʿil, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «باءوا». (عَلى غَضَبٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of «غضب», or [the phrase is] synonymous. (وَلِلْكافِرِينَ): the wāw is resumptive, and «للكافرين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (عَذابٌ): a deferred mubtadaʾ. (مُهِينٌ): an adjective of «عذاب».

* Benefits:
1- (ما) attached to «نعم» and «بئس», the verbs of praise and blame: the grammarians differed about it. Most hold that it is a complete (tāmma) indefinite noun meaning "a thing", so it is in the position of the accusative as tamyīz (specification). It has also been said that it is a relative noun, in which case it is the fāʿil.
2- The specifically praised or blamed (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ wa-l-dhamm) is parsed as a mubtadaʾ, and the verbal clause before it is its khabar; you may also parse it as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ whose omission is obligatory.

dervis-irab:145-145.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَئِنْ): the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), the lām is the lām that paves the way for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam), and إن is conditional. (أَتَيْتَ): a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent). (الَّذِينَ): a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ): a passive past verb; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and الكتاب is the second object of أوتوا. (بِكُلِّ آيَةٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) أتيت. (ما): negative. (تَبِعُوا): a past verb and its fāʿil. (قِبْلَتَكَ): mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath, and it has made the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) unnecessary because the oath comes first; when a condition and an oath come together, the answer belongs to whichever of them comes first. (وَما): the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is the Ḥijāzī negative mā. (أَنْتَ): the noun (ism) of ما. (بِتابِعٍ): the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and تابع is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar (predicate) of ما. (قِبْلَتَهُمْ): mafʿūl bihi of the active participle تابع; this clause is conjoined to what precedes. (وَما بَعْضُهُمْ بِتابِعٍ قِبْلَةَ بَعْضٍ): the clause is conjoined to the one before it. (وَلَئِنْ): the wāw is resumptive, and the i'rab of لئن has already been given. (اتَّبَعْتَ): a verb and its fāʿil. (أَهْواءَهُمْ): mafʿūl bihi. (مِنْ بَعْدِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اتبعت. (ما): a relative noun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (جاءَكَ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. (مِنَ الْعِلْمِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (إِنَّكَ): إن and its noun. (إِذاً): a particle of answer and requital; it is inoperative (muhmala), brought to emphasise the oath. (لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ): the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of إن; the clause of إن and what falls within its scope has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath, and for that reason it is not linked with the fāʾ.

dervis-irab:146-147.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الامتراء): doubt. A question may occur to the inattentive, namely: did the Prophet ﷺ doubt that the truth was from his Lord, so that he was forbidden to doubt?
The answer: this is a kind of speech which the Arabs cast in the form of a command or prohibition to the addressee while someone other than him is meant.

* I'rab:
(الَّذِينَ): a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). (آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ): a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الكتاب is the second object of آتيناهم, and the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. (يَعْرِفُونَهُ): an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause يعرفونه is the khabar (predicate) of الذين. (كَما): the kāf is a preposition, and ما is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, which is the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (يَعْرِفُونَ): the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the particle relative, namely the maṣdariyya ما. (أَبْناءَهُمْ): mafʿūl bihi. (وَإِنَّ فَرِيقاً): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and إن and its noun; the clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). You may also make the wāw resumptive, so that the clause is a fresh sentence (mustaʾnafa) establishing their state. (مِنْهُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted naʿt of فريقا. (لَيَكْتُمُونَ): the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and يكتمون is a verb and its fāʿil. (الْحَقَّ): mafʿūl bihi; the clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إن. (وَهُمْ): the wāw is circumstantial, and هم is a mubtadaʾ. (يَعْلَمُونَ): the verbal clause is the khabar of هم, and the clause after the wāw is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (الْحَقُّ): mubtadaʾ. (مِنْ رَبِّكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar; the clause is resumptive. (فَلا): the fāʾ is resumptive, and لا is prohibitive. (تَكُونَنَّ): the clause تكونن: an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, in the position of jussive by the prohibitive لا; the noun of تكونن is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "you" (أنت). (مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِينَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar.

dervis-irab:148-148.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وِجْهَةٌ) [Translator's note: the source text of this entry is damaged — the opening parentheses and the first letters of the cited Qur'anic words are lost (e.g. «ِجْهَةٌ)», «َ لِكُلٍّ)»); the words have been restored from the verse in brackets for readability, and the commentary is translated as written.]: with ḍamma or kasra on the wāw; it is the direction (al-jiha) toward which one turns. One says: ضلّ وجهة أمره, i.e. he lost the direction of his affair. الجهة may take any of the three vowels on the jīm, and the kasra is the best known.

* I'rab:
(وَلِكُلٍّ): the wāw is resumptive, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate). (وِجْهَةٌ): the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). (هُوَ): mubtadaʾ. (مُوَلِّيها): khabar; the nominal clause is a naʿt (adjective) of وجهة. (فَاسْتَبِقُوا): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), i.e. "if you wish to know what is most correct, then race"; استبقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (الْخَيْراتِ): accusative by removal of the preposition, because استبق is intransitive, i.e. "to the good deeds"; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition. (أَيْنَ ما): a jussive conditional noun, accusative as an adverb of place, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar of تكونوا. (تَكُونُوا): an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the wāw is its noun, and the clause تكونوا is resumptive. (يَأْتِ): the apodosis, and the sign of its jussive is the deletion of the weak letter. (بِكُمُ): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يأت. (اللَّهُ): fāʿil. (جَمِيعاً): ḥāl (circumstantial). (إِنَّ اللَّهَ): إن and its noun. (عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to قدير. (قَدِيرٌ): the khabar of إن; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya) and has no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:149-149.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمِنْ حَيْثُ): the wāw is resumptive, and the preposition and its genitive noun are apparently attached to (mutaʿalliq) وَلِّ; but that would involve what comes after the fāʾ governing what precedes it, which is not allowed. Yet the meaning depends on this apparent reading, so it is better to attach them to an omitted verb explained by فولّ, i.e. "turn your face from wherever you go out". (خَرَجْتَ): a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (فَوَلِّ): the fāʾ links the clause because of the scent of condition in «حيث», and ولّ is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the weak letter; the clause has no grammatical position because it is explicative (mufassira). (وَجْهَكَ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ): an adverb of place attached to ولّ, and المسجد is muḍāf ilayhi. (الْحَرامِ): naʿt (adjective). (وَإِنَّهُ): the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial, and إن and its noun. (لَلْحَقُّ): the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and الحق is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ. (مِنْ رَبِّكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ): its i'rab has been given before.

dervis-irab:150-151.t:
* I'rab:
(وَمِنْ حَيْثُ خَرَجْتَ فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ): its i'rab has been given before; it is a second emphasis, and the statement is repeated to stress the matter of the qibla and to remove doubt after abrogation befell the qibla, which was Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis). (وَحَيْثُ ما كُنْتُمْ فَوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُ): a third emphasis, so that no argument remains for the obstinate, in their view, through which they could get through, nor a breach through which they could slip into spreading alarming rumours. (لِئَلَّا): the lām is the lām of causation (lām al-taʿlīl), and أن, assimilated into the negative لا, is a maṣdar-forming particle that puts the verb in the subjunctive. (يَكُونَ): a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, subjunctive by أن; the preposition and its genitive noun «the lām and the interpreted maṣdar» are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ولّوا. (لِلنَّاسِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of يكون. (عَلَيْكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of حجة; when the adjective came before the noun it qualifies, it was parsed as a ḥāl, as the rule is. (حُجَّةٌ): the postponed nominative noun of يكون. (إِلَّا): a particle of exception. (الَّذِينَ): a connected excepted (mustathnā muttaṣil) from الناس. (ظَلَمُوا): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause). (مِنْهُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (فَلا): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), i.e. "if you know that and its reality has become firm in your souls", and لا is prohibitive. (تَخْشَوْهُمْ): an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَاخْشَوْنِي): the wāw is a conjunction, and اخشوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, because its imperfect is one of the five verbs (al-afʿāl al-khamsa); the nūn is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), the wāw is the fāʿil, and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. (وَلِأُتِمَّ): conjoined to لئلا يكون, so it is a second cause. (نِعْمَتِي): mafʿūl bihi, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. (عَلَيْكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أتمّ. (وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction, لعل and its noun, and the clause تهتدون is its khabar. (كَما أَرْسَلْنا): the kāf is a preposition, ما is maṣdariyya, and أرسلنا is a verb and its fāʿil; the kāf and its genitive — the interpreted maṣdar — are in the position of accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), while Sībawayh parsed it as a ḥāl. (فِيكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أرسلنا. (رَسُولًا): mafʿūl bihi. (مِنْكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted naʿt. (يَتْلُوا): the verbal clause is a second naʿt of رسولا. (عَلَيْكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يتلو. (آياتِنا): mafʿūl bihi, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. (وَيُزَكِّيكُمْ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ): the two imperfect verbs are conjoined to يتلو. (الْكِتابَ): mafʿūl bihi. (وَالْحِكْمَةَ): conjoined to الكتاب. (وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ): conjoined to what precedes; the kāf is the first object. (ما): a relative noun, the second object. (لَمْ): a particle of negation, of turning the tense to the past (qalb), and of jussive. (تَكُونُوا): a defective imperfect verb, jussive by لم; the wāw is its noun, and the verbal clause is the ṣila of ما. (تَعْلَمُونَ): the verbal clause is the khabar of تكونوا.

dervis-irab:152-154.t:
* I'rab:
(فَاذْكُرُونِي): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), i.e. "if you wish to be guided to the highway of what is right, then remember Me". اذكروني: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), the nūn is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أَذْكُرْكُمْ): an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab); the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "I" (أنا), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi. (وَاشْكُرُوا): conjoined to اذكروني; شكر is sometimes transitive by itself and sometimes by a preposition, equally. (لِي): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) اشكروا. (وَلا): the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is prohibitive. (تَكْفُرُونِ): an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is the nūn of protection, and the yāʾ — deleted to match the verse-endings (fawāṣil) — is mafʿūl bihi, the kasra indicating it. (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has been given many times. (اسْتَعِينُوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (بِالصَّبْرِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to استعينوا. (وَالصَّلاةِ): conjoined to الصبر. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ): إن and its noun. (مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ): مع is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar (predicate), and الصابرين is muḍāf ilayhi. The clause of إن and what falls within its scope is nominal and has no grammatical position because it is causal (taʿlīliyya). (وَلا تَقُولُوا): the wāw conjoins to what precedes, لا is prohibitive, and تقولوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا. (لِمَنْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تقولوا; and the clause (يُقْتَلُ) is the ṣila (relative clause) and has no grammatical position. (فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يقتل. (أَمْواتٌ): the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are dead"; the nominal clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (بَلْ): a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction. (أَحْياءٌ): the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to the clause هم أموات. (وَلكِنْ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and لكن is lightened from the heavy form, so it is merely for rectification (istidrāk). (لا): negative. (تَشْعُرُونَ): an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs (al-afʿāl al-khamsa); the clause is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

* Rhetoric:
1- Concision (ījāz) in the last verse, namely concision by omission (ījāz al-ḥadhf): the mubtadaʾ is omitted because of the importance of mentioning the khabar, since they did not imagine that they were alive; so He, Glorified be He, refuted this hasty first impression with a graceful depiction.
2- The antithesis (ṭibāq) between أموات and أحياء in the verse is a graceful antithesis with no artificiality in it.

dervis-irab:91-91.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمْ آمِنُوا): the i'rab of its parallels has preceded; the clause «آمنوا» is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ): the bāʾ is a preposition, and «ما» is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ; the clause «أنزل الله» has no grammatical position. (قالُوا): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. (نُؤْمِنُ): the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech. (بِما أَنْزَلَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نؤمن». (عَلَيْنا): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أنزل». (وَيَكْفُرُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (بِما): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يكفرون». (وَراءَهُ): an adverb attached to an omitted [verb], which has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ): the wāw is circumstantial, «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «الحق» its khabar (predicate); the clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (مُصَدِّقاً): an emphasizing ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida), because the Qur'an's confirming is inseparable and does not change. (لِما): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «مصدقا». (مَعَهُمْ): an adverb of place attached to the omitted ṣila of «ما». (قُلْ): an imperative verb. (فَلِمَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, because it discloses an implied condition, i.e. "if your claim is true, then why do you kill"; the lām is a preposition and «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of the genitive by the lām, i.e. "for what thing"; the alif of «ما» was dropped to distinguish it from the declarative (khabariyya) «ما»; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «تقتلون». (تَقْتُلُونَ): an imperfect verb. (أَنْبِياءَ اللَّهِ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (مِنْ قَبْلُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): «إن» is conditional; in «كنتم», «كان» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is its noun, and the clause «تقتلون» is its khabar; the apodosis is omitted because what precedes indicates it, i.e. "then why do you kill". [Translator's note: the source says the clause «تقتلون» is the khabar of «كنتم»; in the verse the khabar of «كنتم» is «مؤمنين».]

* Benefits:
1- (وراء) is one of the adverbs of intermediate declinability (mutawassiṭat al-taṣarruf); it is an adverb of place. The well-known view is that it means "behind", but it may mean "in front", so it is one of the words with opposite meanings (al-aḍdād).
2- When the interrogative «ما» is preceded by a preposition, its alif is dropped and the two words are treated as one word, so you say: «إلام»، «علام»، «حتام»، «لم»، «بم»، «حتّام»، «عمّ»، «فيم»، «ممّ».

dervis-irab:92-93.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ): the wāw is resumptive, the lām is [in] the answer to an omitted oath, and «قد» is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). (جاءَكُمْ مُوسى): a verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the fāʿil (agent); the speech is resumptive, brought to object against them for killing the prophets while claiming that they believe in the Torah, and the Torah in no way permits that. (بِالْبَيِّناتِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جاءكم». (ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ): «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence with delay, «اتخذتم» is a verb and its fāʿil, and «العجل» is mafʿūl bihi. (مِنْ بَعْدِهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَأَنْتُمْ ظالِمُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial, «أنتم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «ظالمون» its khabar (predicate); the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (وَإِذْ): its i'rab has preceded. (أَخَذْنا مِيثاقَكُمْ): a past verb, its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (وَرَفَعْنا): conjoined to «أخذنا», and you may parse it as circumstantial. (فَوْقَكُمُ): an adverb of place attached to «رفعنا». (الطُّورَ): mafʿūl bihi. (خُذُوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the object of an omitted speech, and the clause of speech is accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "saying to you". (ما): a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. (آتَيْناكُمْ): a verb, its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is a ṣila (relative clause). (بِقُوَّةٍ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَاسْمَعُوا): conjoined to what preceded. (قالُوا): a verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, brought to mention their hearing and disobeying at one and the same time, and that is a nature ingrained in the Jews. (سَمِعْنا وَعَصَيْنا): the two clauses are the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (وَأُشْرِبُوا): the wāw is circumstantial or a conjunction; «أشربوا» is a passive past verb and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أشربوا». (الْعِجْلَ): second mafʿūl bihi, on the assumption of an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the love of the calf". (بِكُفْرِهِمْ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أشربوا»; the bāʾ is causal, i.e. because of their disbelief. (قُلْ): an imperative verb whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, and the clause is resumptive. (بِئْسَما): its i'rab preceded shortly before. (يَأْمُرُكُمْ): an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause has no grammatical position. [Translator's note: the source says "a latent fāʿil", but the overt fāʿil is «إيمانكم», as the source itself states next.] (بِهِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يأمركم». (إِيمانُكُمْ): fāʿil. (إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): a condition and its verb, and the apodosis is omitted: "then why did you do that"; «كان» and its noun, and «مؤمنين» its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
(The eloquent simile, al-tashbīh al-balīgh): i.e. their hearts, because the love of the calf took firm hold of them, were made as though they drank it. Like it is the saying of Zuhayr:
فصحوت عنها بعد حبّ داخل ... والحبّ يشربه فؤادك دائما
(I recovered from her after a love that had entered deep; and love is something your heart drinks continually.)
He expressed the love of the calf as drinking rather than eating only because drinking water penetrates the limbs until it reaches their inner parts, whereas food does not penetrate them.

dervis-irab:94-95.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ): an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you"; the clause is resumptive, brought to enter another kind of the false rumours they weave. (إِنْ): conditional, putting two verbs in the jussive. (كانَتْ): a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (لَكُمُ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of «كانت». (الدَّارُ): its deferred noun. (الْآخِرَةُ): naʿt (adjective) of «الدار». (عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): an adverb of place attached to «خالصة». (خالِصَةً): ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الدار», i.e. "safe [for you]". (مِنْ دُونِ النَّاسِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl that emphasizes the [first] ḥāl, because «دون» is used for exclusivity; one says: "This is mine دونك" or "من دونك", i.e. you have no right to it. (فَتَمَنَّوُا): the fāʾ occurs in the apodosis because the speech is a request (ṭalabī); «تمنوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (الْمَوْتَ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): its i'rab has been repeated, and the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "then wish for death". (وَلَنْ): the wāw is resumptive, and «لن» is a particle of negation, the accusative and the future. (يَتَمَنَّوْهُ): an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by «لن», the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi. (أَبَداً): an adverb of time attached to «يتمنوه». (بِما): the preposition and its genitive noun are also attached to «يتمنوه». (قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ): a verbal clause with no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما»; the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "which their hands sent forth". (وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive. (بِالظَّالِمِينَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «عليم».

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «فتمنوا الموت» the imperative departs from its original meaning to the meaning of challenging to incapacity (taʿjīz), because that is not among their traits nor among their familiar outward ways. Wishing for death is the way of the righteous who are brought near, because whoever is certain of martyrdom longs for it and weeps in yearning for it. It is narrated of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib that he would go about between the two battle lines in a thin undergarment, and his son al-Ḥasan said: "This is not the dress of warriors." He said:
"My son, your father does not care whether he falls upon death or death falls upon him." When Khālid ibn al-Walīd was dying he wept, and it was said to him: "What makes you weep?" He said: "By Allah, I do not care out of fear of death; but [I weep] because I was present at such-and-such a number of battles, and then I die like this, as a she-goat dies. May the eyes of cowards never sleep." It is narrated of Ḥudhayfa that he used to wish for death, and when he was dying he said: "A beloved has come at a time of need; may whoever regrets not prosper" — meaning [regrets] the wishing. [Translator's note: the source reads «قال حبيب», apparently a corruption of «قال: حبيب», which is how it is translated here.] And from the Prophet ﷺ: «Had they wished for death, every person would have choked on his saliva and died on the spot, and not a Jew would have remained on the face of the earth».

dervis-irab:96-96.t:
* Vocabulary:
(زحزح): it is used both transitively and intransitively, and the repetition of the letters is like the repetition of the action.

* I'rab:
(وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, the lām is [in] the answer to an omitted oath, and «تجدنهم» is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; its fāʿil (agent) is a pronoun obligatorily latent (mustatir) in it, its implied form being "you", and the hāʾ is its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أَحْرَصَ النَّاسِ): its second mafʿūl bihi. (عَلى حَياةٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أحرص». (وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا): the wāw is a conjunction, and the conjunction here is construed according to the meaning; the implied form is "more eager than those who associate partners", but «أحرص» was omitted for specification after generalization. (يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمْ): an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), or resumptive with no grammatical position. (لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ): «لو» is a non-governing maṣdar particle (maṣdariyya), i.e. "he wishes to be given long life"; it is particular to the verb of wishing, and it together with the verb after it is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the object of «يود», i.e. "he wishes for long life"; «يعمر» is a passive imperfect verb, and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is optionally latent in it, its implied form being "he". (أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ): an adverb of time attached to «يعمر». (وَما هُوَ): the wāw is circumstantial, «ما» is the Ḥijāzī negating «ما», and «هو» is its noun. (بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ): the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and «مزحزحه» is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar (predicate) of «ما». (مِنَ الْعَذابِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «مزحزحه». (أَنْ يُعَمَّرَ): «أن» and what falls within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of the nominative as fāʿil of «مزحزحه», because it is an active participle. The pronoun in His saying «وما هو» refers to «أحدهم». It has also been said that it refers to the maṣdar indicated by «يعمر», i.e. "and the long life is not going to remove him", in which case His saying «أن يعمر» is a badal (substitute) from it; both are good. (وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِما يَعْمَلُونَ): the wāw is resumptive, and «ما» may be a relative noun or a maṣdar particle.

* Rhetoric:
1- Concision (al-ījāz) in the verse: in making «حياة» indefinite there is a wonderful benefit, whose gist is that the eager one must be alive, and his eagerness cannot be for the past and present life, since both are already attained, but for the future life. And since the eagerness is not attached to life absolutely but to life in some circumstances, the indefinite was necessary. In the omission there is a great rebuke to the Jews, because those who do not believe in the Return and know nothing but the life of this world — their eagerness for it is not unlikely; so when the People of the Book exceed them in eagerness, while they affirm the Resurrection and the Recompense, they are more deserving of blame and rebuke.
2- Metonymy (al-kināya) in His saying (أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ): it is a metonymy for great number, so a thousand in particular is not meant.

dervis-irab:97-98.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ): an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is "you". (مَنْ): a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «قل» is resumptive, brought to show another of the patterns of their obstinacy and stubbornness. (كانَ): a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its noun refers back to «من». (عَدُوًّا): its khabar (predicate). (لِجِبْرِيلَ): the lām is a preposition, and «جبريل» is a noun genitive by the lām; the sign of its genitive is the fatḥa in place of the kasra because it is a non-Arabic proper name; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of «عدوا». (فَإِنَّهُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction joining to the omitted apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), serving as a cause for it; the implied form is "then let him die of rage" or "then there is no reason for his enmity". His saying «فإنه» cannot be the apodosis, because the apodosis must contain a pronoun referring back to it [the conditional noun] — you cannot say "Whoever honours me, then Zayd is standing" — and «إن» and its noun; and because the act of sending down is realized in meaning, whereas the recompense can only be future. (نَزَّلَهُ): a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the pronoun refers to the Qur'an, and making it a pronoun when it has not been mentioned before magnifies the standing of what it refers to, as though it indicated itself; the clause «نزله» is the khabar of «كأن». [Translator's note: the source reads «كأن»; the particle in the verse is «إنّ».] (عَلى قَلْبِكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «نزله». (بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (مُصَدِّقاً): a second ḥāl. (لِما): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «مصدقا». (بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ): the adverb is attached to an omitted [verb] that has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (وَهُدىً وَبُشْرى): both conjoined to «مصدقا». (لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «بشرى» or to an omitted adjective. The khabar of «من» is the protasis together with the omitted apodosis. (مَنْ): a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ. (كانَ): a defective past verb whose noun is latent, referring back to «من». (عَدُوًّا): khabar of «كان». (لِلَّهِ): both are attached to an omitted adjective of «عدو». (وَمَلائِكَتِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكالَ): conjoined. (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَدُوٌّ لِلْكافِرِينَ): the clause is conjoined to the apodosis, and the establishment of that has preceded.

* Benefits:
When the Arabs pronounce a non-Arabic word they modify it. «جبر» means "servant", and «ايل» is "Allah", so it is equivalent to ʿAbd Allāh; the meaning of «ميكال» or «ميكائيل» is "little servant of Allah" (ʿUbayd Allāh), so it is as if he is of lower rank than Jibrīl.

dervis-irab:261-262.t:
* Vocabulary:
(السنبلة) is well known; its pattern is fanʿala, so the nūn is redundant (zāʾida). One says: أسبل الزرع — the crop sent out what is in it. Some lexicographers report سنبل الزرع, in which case the nūn is radical and the pattern is faʿlal. Al-Asās and al-Lisān report:
«أسبل الزرع وسنبل: its ears (سبله and سنبله) came out».
(المن): to count one's kindness against the one to whom one has been kind.

* I'rab:
(مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوالَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) is a resumptive statement brought to strike a parable for spending wealth in the way of Allah. A muḍāf must be taken as omitted, i.e. "the likeness of their spending". (مثل) is the mubtadaʾ (subject); (الذين) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause (ينفقون) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (أموالهم) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (في سبيل الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ينفقون). (كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أَنْبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنابِلَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate); here too a muḍāf must be taken as omitted, i.e. "like the likeness of the sower of a grain". (أنبتت) is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) is "it" (هي); (سبع) is the direct object; (سنابل) is muḍāf ilayhi, its sign of the genitive being the fatḥa because it is a diptote, being on the pattern of the ultimate plural (ṣīghat muntahā al-jumūʿ); and the clause (أنبتت) is an adjective of (حبة). (فِي كُلِّ سُنْبُلَةٍ مِائَةُ حَبَّةٍ): (في كل) — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (سنبلة) is muḍāf ilayhi; (مائة حبة) is the postponed mubtadaʾ; and the nominal clause is an adjective of (سنابل), so it is in the position of the genitive, or an adjective of (سبع), so it is in the position of the accusative. (وَاللَّهُ يُضاعِفُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ; (يضاعف) is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he", referring to Allah the Exalted; the clause (يضاعف) is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ «الله»; (لمن) — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (يضاعف); and the clause (يشاء) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of (من). (وَاللَّهُ واسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ; (واسع) is the first khabar and (عليم) the second khabar. (الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوالَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): you may make it follow the preceding clauses as a badal (substitute) from them, or you may make it resumptive, brought to mention spending that is not tainted by reproach. (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ, or a badal from the first (الذين); the clause (ينفقون أموالهم) has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila; and (في سبيل الله) is attached to (ينفقون). (ثُمَّ لا يُتْبِعُونَ ما أَنْفَقُوا مَنًّا وَلا أَذىً): (ثم) is a conjunction expressing sequence and delay, in time and in rank; (لا) is negating; (يتبعون) is an imperfect verb conjoined to (ينفقون); (ما) is a relative noun, the first direct object; the clause (أنفقوا) is the ṣila of (ما); (منا) is the second direct object; and (ولا أذى) is conjoined to «منا». (لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are a fronted khabar; (أجرهم) is the postponed mubtadaʾ; the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (ربهم) is muḍāf ilayhi; and the nominal clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar of (الذين) if it is taken as a mubtadaʾ; but if it is a badal, the clause is resumptive. (وَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ): the i'rab of this verse, letter for letter, has preceded.

* Rhetoric:
1- Representational simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī): the spending of those who spend in the way of Allah is likened to a grain in the multiplication of the reward; when the planter plants it, it puts forth a stalk from which seven branches spread, each with an ear. It contains a splendid embodiment by setting up a correspondence between the thing likened and the thing it is likened to. The purpose of the simile here is, first, to clarify the meaning and bring it near to minds; second, to support it with tangible proof that no obstinate person can dispute and no stubborn person can quibble with; and third, to adorn and beautify the thing likened and to kindle desire for it, so that no one hesitates to spend after having seen with his own eyes, in advance, the reward prepared for it.
2- «ثم» in its original coinage indicates that there is a delay (tarākhī) between what is conjoined by it and what it is conjoined to. People have differed over this delay; some say:
It is a delay in time and the distance between the two. Al-Zamakhsharī, may Allah have mercy on him, takes it as a disparity in rank. So to which of the two is it to be referred in this verse?
The scholars of rhetoric have spoken at length on this matter. Some said: what is meant is delay in time, given what is usual, namely that reproach and injury necessarily occur after the spending; indeed they follow from it and cannot be conceived of before it occurs. This is good and fine. Al-Zamakhsharī held that the delay here is to be understood as a disparity in ranks and the distance between them, since it cannot be taken as temporal because of a context in the verse that refuses that. The upshot is that it has been borrowed from distance between times for distance in rank. This is among the most wonderful things that sound thought and deep intelligence can reach, for drawing out this metaphor in this form is not grasped by the short-sighted and the beginners. On this basis it is said: its original meaning is the delay of the time of the act's occurrence and coming about, and the meaning to which it is borrowed is the continuance of the act's existence and the prolongation of the time of its remaining.

dervis-irab:155-157.t:
* Vocabulary:
(البلاء): testing and trial.

* I'rab:
(وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُمْ): the wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), the lām paves the way for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam), and نبلونّ is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the fāʿil (agent) is obligatorily latent (mustatir), implied as "We" (نحن), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (بِشَيْءٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) نبلونكم. (مِنَ الْخَوْفِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of شيء. The clause نبلونكم has no grammatical position because it is the answer to an omitted oath for which the lām paved the way; it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis because it is an affirmative, future imperfect joined to its lām. (وَالْجُوعِ): conjoined to الخوف. (وَنَقْصٍ): also conjoined. (مِنَ الْأَمْوالِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نقص, because it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of نقص, or to an omitted naʿt of نقص, because it is indefinite. (وَالْأَنْفُسِ وَالثَّمَراتِ): both conjoined to الأموال. The clause of the oath and its answer is resumptive, brought to test their states and the extent of their patience under trial and their submission to the decree, with something of fear and hunger. (وَبَشِّرِ): the wāw is a conjunction, and بشر is an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, implied as "you" (أنت). (الصَّابِرِينَ): mafʿūl bihi. The clause بشر is conjoined to ولنبلونكم; do not say that it is a request-verb (fiʿl ṭalabī) [and so cannot be conjoined to a statement], for the content of both is a request; it is thus a case of conjoining content to content, i.e. the testing occurs at the time of trial and at the time of glad tidings. (الَّذِينَ): naʿt of الصابرين. (إِذا): an adverb of future time, attached to its answer, which is قالوا. (أَصابَتْهُمْ): the clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (مُصِيبَةٌ): fāʿil; the clause of the condition and its answer has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause). (قالُوا): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition. (إِنَّا): إن and its noun. (لِلَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to راجعون. (وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ): conjoined to the clause إنا لله. (راجِعُونَ): the khabar (predicate) of إن. (أُولئِكَ): the demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject). (عَلَيْهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted, fronted khabar. (صَلَواتٌ): the postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of the demonstrative. (مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted naʿt of صلوات. (وَرَحْمَةٌ): conjoined to صلوات; the demonstrative clause and what follows it is resumptive, brought to explain what they were given glad tidings of. (وَأُولئِكَ): the wāw is a conjunction, and أولئك is a mubtadaʾ. (هُمُ): a second mubtadaʾ, or a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position. (الْمُهْتَدُونَ): the khabar of «هم» or the khabar of أولئك; [in the first case] the clause is the khabar of أولئك.

dervis-irab:263-265.t:
* Vocabulary:
(رِئاءَ) is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of راءى, مراءاة and رئاء. Its origin is ريايا: the first hamza replaces a yāʾ that is the middle radical of the word, and the second replaces a yāʾ that is the final radical, because it fell at the end after a redundant alif. The mufāʿala form has its usual meaning of mutual participation, because the show-off shows people his deeds so that they show him praise and respect.
(صَفْوانٍ): a large, smooth rock.
(الوابل): heavy rain. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: the lightest and weakest rain is الطلّ, then الرذاذ, which is stronger than it, then البغش and الدّث, and like it الرّكّ and الرهمة. Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: the first of rain is رش and طش, then طل and رذاذ, then نضح and نضخ, then هطل and تهتان, then وابل and جود.
(صلد): hard and smooth, or bare, clean of the soil that had been on it.

* I'rab:
(قَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ صَدَقَةٍ يَتْبَعُها أَذىً): (قول) is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and beginning with an indefinite noun is permissible because it is qualified; (معروف) is an adjective of (قول); (مغفرة) is conjoined to (قول); (خير) is the khabar (predicate); (من صدقة) is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خير); (يتبعها) is an imperfect verb, the hāʾ being the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is an adjective of (صدقة); (أذى) is the fāʿil (agent). (وَاللَّهُ غَنِيٌّ حَلِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ; and (غني) and (حليم) are its two khabars. (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has preceded many times. (لا تُبْطِلُوا صَدَقاتِكُمْ بِالْمَنِّ وَالْأَذى) is a resumptive statement brought to set out the ruling on this matter, namely the nullifying of charity by reproach and injury. (لا) is prohibitive; (تبطلوا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لا); the wāw is the agent; (صدقاتكم) is the direct object, accusative with the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (بالمن) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تبطلوا); and (الأذى) is conjoined to (المن). (كَالَّذِي): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted maṣdar, so it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "do not nullify them with a nullifying like the nullifying of the one who…"; or it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of the implied maṣdar, as Sībawayh stated explicitly; or from the agent of (تبطلوا), i.e. "do not nullify your charity resembling the one who spends his wealth to be seen by people". Both views are good. (يُنْفِقُ مالَهُ رِئاءَ النَّاسِ): the clause (ينفق ماله) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun and has no grammatical position; (رئاء الناس) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and it has fulfilled the conditions for the accusative, so one does not turn from that to another view, as some grammarians claimed. (وَلا يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is negating; (يؤمن) is an imperfect verb whose agent is "he"; (بالله) is attached to (يؤمن); and (اليوم الآخر) is conjoined to (الله). (فَمَثَلُهُ كَمَثَلِ صَفْوانٍ): the fāʾ is resumptive, brought merely to link the clauses; (مثله) is the mubtadaʾ; (كمثل) — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar; or the kāf is a noun meaning "like", the khabar, and it is muḍāf, (مثل) being muḍāf ilayhi; and (صفوان) is in construct with (مثل). (عَلَيْهِ تُرابٌ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (تراب) is the postponed mubtadaʾ; and the nominal clause is in the position of the genitive as an adjective of (صفوان). (فَأَصابَهُ وابِلٌ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, conjoining (أصابه) to what (عليه) is attached to, i.e. "it settled on it, then it was struck"; the hāʾ is the direct object and (وابل) the agent. (فَتَرَكَهُ صَلْداً): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (ترك) is a past verb taking two objects, the first being the hāʾ and the second (صلدا). (لا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلى شَيْءٍ): the clause is resumptive, brought in reply to a question, as if it were said: "So what was their outcome?"
And it was said: "They have no power". (لا) is negating; (يقدرون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative, its sign being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the agent; (على شيء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يقدرون). The pronoun is brought back in the plural though it is outwardly singular, because by «الذي» is meant the party that spends and the kind (genus) that spends. (مِمَّا كَسَبُوا): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of (شيء); and the clause (كسبوا) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما). (وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الْكافِرِينَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to hint that reproach and injury are among the traits of the unbelievers; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ; the clause (لا يهدي) is the khabar; (القوم) is the direct object; and (الكافرين) is an adjective of (القوم). (وَمَثَلُ الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوالَهُمُ): the wāw conjoins to «فمثله»; (مثل) is the mubtadaʾ, and a muḍāf must be implied, namely "the spendings of"; (الذين) is muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause (ينفقون أموالهم) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (ابْتِغاءَ مَرْضاتِ اللَّهِ) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, the conditions for the accusative being present in it; and (مرضاة الله) is muḍāf ilayhi. (وَتَثْبِيتاً مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ) is conjoined to (ابتغاء), and (من أنفسهم) is attached to «تثبيتا», i.e. proceeding from the root of their own selves. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said:
«It is not sound for ابتغاء to be an object of purpose, because «تثبيتا» is conjoined to it, and «تثبيتا» cannot be an object of purpose because spending is not from the root of confirming». For this reason Abū Ḥayyān preferred that «ابتغاء» be a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "seeking" (متغين) [Translator's note: thus in the source; presumably مبتغين], and likewise «وتثبيتا». Their words contain no small amount of depth and fine estimation. But it can be said that confirming (التثبيت) is one of the acts of the heart, because it issues from it, and it drives the owner of the heart to confirming; for this reason we prefer the i'rab we have given. (كَمَثَلِ جَنَّةٍ بِرَبْوَةٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ «مثل الذين»; and (بربوة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of (جنة). (أَصابَها وابِلٌ): a verb, direct object and agent, and the clause is also an adjective of (جنة). (فَآتَتْ أُكُلَها ضِعْفَيْنِ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (آتت) is a past verb whose agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it" (هي), referring to (جنة); (أكلها) is the direct object, the hāʾ being muḍāf ilayhi; and (ضعفين) is a ḥāl. (فَإِنْ لَمْ يُصِبْها وابِلٌ فَطَلٌّ): the fāʾ is resumptive; (إن) is conditional; (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; (يصبها) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by «لم», in the position of the jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ links the apodosis; (طل) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then what strikes it is a drizzle"; and the clause is in the position of the jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (بصير); the clause (تعملون) is the ṣila of the relative noun; and (بصير) is the khabar of (الله).

* Rhetoric:
1- The first representational simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī): spending wealth to be seen by people, and then following it with reproach and with lording one's kindness over others, is likened to the soil placed on a smooth rock; a downpour of rain comes upon it, scatters it and carries it away, leaving no trace of it.
2- The second representational simile: spending wealth free of show, in the way of Allah and seeking His good pleasure, is likened to a garden of spreading shade on a high hill, for which a little rain suffices for it to swell, stir, flourish and become fertile.

dervis-irab:158-158.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الصَّفا): a hill in Mecca. The original meaning of الصفا is that it is the plural of صفاة, i.e. a smooth rock; its alif is converted from a wāw. (الْمَرْوَةَ): also a hill in Mecca.
The original meaning of المروة is soft stones; it is also said: those with hardness in them.
Abū Dhuʾayb said:
حتى كأنّي للحوادث مروة ... بصفا المشقّر كلّ يوم تقرع
(Until it is as if I were, to misfortunes, a marwa-stone on the rocks of al-Mushaqqar, struck every day.)
(الشعائر): plural of شعيرة, which is a mark/sign.
(حَجَّ): he aimed at, set out for.
(اعْتَمَرَ): he visited the venerated House in the prescribed manner.
Then al-ḥajj and al-ʿumra became proper names for setting out for the House and visiting it.
(لا جناح) الجناح: inclining toward sin; then it came to be used for sin itself. One says: جنح إلى الشيء, i.e. he inclined toward it; from it comes جنح الليل, i.e. the inclining of the night with its darkness, and جنح الطائر and جناحه (the bird's wing).

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الصَّفا): إن and its noun. (وَالْمَرْوَةَ): conjoined to الصفا. (مِنْ شَعائِرِ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of إن; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. (فَمَنْ): the fāʾ is resumptive, and من is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). (حَجَّ الْبَيْتَ): حج is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), referring to من, and البيت is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أَوِ اعْتَمَرَ): أو is a conjunction, and اعتمر is a past verb conjoined to حج. (فَلا جُناحَ): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) because it is a nominal clause; لا is the lā of generic negation, and جناح is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa. (عَلَيْهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of لا. (أَنْ يَطَّوَّفَ): the maṣdariyya أن and what falls within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in that he goes round". (بِهِما): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يطوف. The clause فلا جناح عليه is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the clause of the protasis and its apodosis is in the position of nominative as the khabar of من. (وَمَنْ تَطَوَّعَ): the wāw is a conjunction; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; تطوع is a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis, and its fāʿil is latent, implied as "he" (هو). (خَيْراً): a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, so it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "he volunteers a good volunteering". You may also parse it as accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "with good". Sībawayh chose to parse it as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied, definite maṣdar; had Sībawayh not been the one who said it, I would have declared it wrong. (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ): the fāʾ links the apodosis, and إن and its noun. (شاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ): two khabars of إن; the clause فإن الله is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من.

dervis-irab:159-160.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ): إن and its noun. (يَكْتُمُونَ): an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause). The clause of إن and what falls within its scope is resumptive, brought to state in general terms the ruling on whoever conceals anything of the rulings of the religion. It was revealed concerning the Jews who equivocate out of love of disputation and haughty obstinacy; the specificity of the occasion does not prevent the generality of the ruling. (ما): the object of يكتمون. (أَنْزَلْنا): a verb and its fāʿil; the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. أنزلناه; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila. (مِنَ الْبَيِّناتِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "in the state of being clear, bearing witness to the realities". The verse alludes to the Jews' attempt to hide certain verses indicating the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, or those depicting their faults and the sins they commit. (وَالْهُدى): conjoined to البينات. (مِنْ بَعْدِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يكتمون. (ما بَيَّنَّاهُ): ما is maṣdariyya, and بيناه is a verb, its fāʿil and its object. The interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, i.e. "after its being made clear". (لِلنَّاسِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to بيناه. (فِي الْكِتابِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are also attached to بيناه. Attaching two prepositional phrases to a single verb is permissible when they differ in meaning and wording.
You may also attach «في الكتاب» to an omitted ḥāl of the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "being in the Book". (أُولئِكَ): the demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject). (يَلْعَنُهُمُ): an imperfect verb, and the hāʾ is its object. (اللَّهُ): its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the demonstrative. (وَيَلْعَنُهُمُ اللَّاعِنُونَ): conjoined to the preceding clause; the nominal demonstrative clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إن. (إِلَّا): a particle of exception. (الَّذِينَ): excepted from the mafʿūl bihi, i.e. the hāʾ in يلعنهم. (تابُوا): a verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila. (وَأَصْلَحُوا وَبَيَّنُوا): conjoined to تابوا. (فَأُولئِكَ): the fāʾ is linking, because the relative noun has a scent of condition, and the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ. (أَتُوبُ): an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), implied as "I" (أنا); the clause أتوب is the khabar of the demonstrative, and the demonstrative clause is resumptive. (عَلَيْهِمْ): attached to أتوب. (وَأَنَا): the wāw is a conjunction, and أنا is a mubtadaʾ. (التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ): two khabars of أنا; the clause is conjoined.

* Rhetoric:
1- Repetition (takrīr) in mentioning the curse; its purpose is to intensify the censure.
2- Iltifāt (shift of person) in His saying «يلعنهم الله»: the context required Him to say "We curse them", but He shifted to the third person to show the manifestation of His wrath upon them, and so that the speech would go further in bringing the curse down upon them and attaching banishment to them.

dervis-irab:161-163.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ): إن and its noun. (كَفَرُوا): a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) and has no grammatical position. (وَماتُوا): the wāw is a conjunction, and the clause ماتوا is conjoined to the clause كفروا. (وَهُمْ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject). (كُفَّارٌ): the khabar (predicate) of «هم»; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (أُولئِكَ): a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (عَلَيْهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar. (لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ): the postponed mubtadaʾ. (وَالْمَلائِكَةِ وَالنَّاسِ): conjoined to الله; the nominal clause is the khabar of أولئك, the clause of أولئك and what falls within its scope is the khabar of إن, and the clause of إن and what falls within its scope is resumptive, brought to state the fate of the second group of those who conceal; the fate of those who repent has been stated in the exception. (أَجْمَعِينَ): tawkīd (emphasis). (خالِدِينَ): a ḥāl of the pronoun in عليهم. (فِيها): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to خالدين; the pronoun refers to the Fire, which is left unexpressed to frighten and to magnify the horror. It may also refer to the curse figuratively, the relation being one of place (al-ʿalāqa al-maḥalliyya). (لا يُخَفَّفُ): لا is negative, and يخفف is a passive imperfect verb. (عَنْهُمُ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يخفف. (الْعَذابُ): nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the verbal clause is in the position of accusative as a second ḥāl of الذين كفروا, from the pronoun concealed in خالدين, so it is an overlapping ḥāl (ḥāl mutadākhila). (وَلا): the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is negative. (هُمْ): mubtadaʾ. (يُنْظَرُونَ): a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil, i.e. they are not granted respite or deferred; the verbal clause is the khabar of «هم», and the nominal clause is conjoined to the clause لا يخفف. (وَإِلهُكُمْ): the wāw is resumptive, and what follows it is a resumptive clause with no grammatical position, brought to answer the disbelievers of Quraysh who said: "O Muhammad, describe your Lord to us"; إلهكم is a mubtadaʾ. (إِلهٌ): khabar. (واحِدٌ): naʿt (adjective) of إله. (لا): the lā of generic negation. (إِلهٌ): its noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative. (إِلَّا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (هُوَ): a badal (substitute) from the position of لا and its noun, because their position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ; or a badal from the pronoun concealed in the omitted khabar. More of the sayings of the grammarians and exegetes on the i'rab of the word of testimony (kalimat al-shahāda) will follow, as an exercise for the mind. (الرَّحْمنُ الرَّحِيمُ): two khabars of an omitted mubtadaʾ, implied as "He" (هو).

* Benefits:
The grammarians and exegetes have gone into the i'rab of «لا إله إلا الله», the word of testimony, at great length, and they agreed that the khabar of لا is omitted, i.e. "for us" (لنا), or "in existence" (في الوجود), or the like. We shall present to you a useful summary of what they said, because of its importance:

Al-Zamakhsharī:
He composed a fine short treatise on the i'rab of the word of testimony. After citing what they agreed upon, namely the omission of the khabar of لا, he said: «So they said; but the correct view is that it is a complete statement with no omission, and that the original form is: الله إله, a mubtadaʾ and khabar, just as you say: زيد منطلق. Then the particle of restriction was brought, the khabar was placed before the noun and compounded with لا, just as the mubtadaʾ is compounded with it in, for example, لا رجل في الدار; so «الله» is a postponed mubtadaʾ and «إله» a fronted khabar. On this basis its parallels are explained, such as:
لا سيف إلا ذو الفقار ولا فتى إلا عليّ
(There is no sword but Dhū l-Faqār, and no young hero but ʿAlī.)»

Al-Zamakhsharī also:
Al-Zamakhsharī said in al-Mufaṣṣal, in his discussion of the khabar of the lā of generic negation: «The people of the Ḥijāz often omit it, saying: لا أهل, لا مال, لا بأس, لا فتى إلا عليّ, لا سيف إلا ذو الفقار; and from this is the word of testimony, whose meaning is: there is no god in existence except Allah. The Banū Tamīm never express it in their speech at all.»

Ibn Yaʿīsh:
The commentator on al-Mufaṣṣal, Muwaffaq al-Dīn Ibn Yaʿīsh, said: «Know that they omit the khabar of لا from: لا رجل, لا غلام, لا حول, لا قوة, and in the word of testimony, as in لا إله إلا الله. The meaning is: no man, no boy, no might and no power belongs to us; likewise: no god in existence except Allah; no family for you, no wealth for you, no harm upon you; no young hero in existence except ʿAlī, and no sword in existence except Dhū l-Faqār. So the khabar is the preposition with its genitive noun, and it is omitted. It is not correct for the khabar to be «الله» in your saying لا إله إلا الله, for two reasons:
a- that it is definite, and «لا» does not govern a definite noun;
b- that the noun of «لا» here is general, while your saying إلا الله is particular, and the particular cannot be the khabar of the general.
Its parallel is: الحيوان إنسان (the animal is a human), which is impossible, because among animals there are those that are not human; whereas your saying: الإنسان حيوان (the human is an animal) is permissible, because the human is truly an animal and there is nothing in the human that is not animal. The khabar may be expressed, as in:
لا رجل أفضل منك and لا أحد خير منك. This is the school of the people of the Ḥijāz. As for the Banū Tamīm, they do not permit the khabar of «لا» to be expressed at all, saying it is one of the rejected original forms, and they reinterpret whatever is attested of it; they say of the expression:
لا رجل أفضل منك, that «أفضل» is a naʿt of رجل according to its position, and likewise «خير منك» is a naʿt of أحد according to its position.» [Translator's note: the source says «لا يجيزون تقديم خبر لا» ("do not permit fronting the khabar of lā"); from the context the intended sense is that they do not permit the khabar to be expressed; the opening quotation mark of this passage is not closed in the source.]

Al-Badr al-Damāmīnī:
Al-Badr al-Damāmīnī criticised al-Zamakhsharī in his gloss on al-Mughnī, saying: «The weakness of this view — meaning al-Zamakhsharī's view — is not hidden; it entails that the khabar is compounded with لا, whereas only the mubtadaʾ is compounded with it. Moreover, if it were so, it would not be permissible to put the Mighty Name in the accusative, yet they have permitted it.»

Al-Ṣalāḥ al-Ṣafadī:
Al-Ṣalāḥ al-Ṣafadī presented in al-Ghayth al-Musjam an interesting discussion in which he said: «Among the cases of omission of the khabar is your saying: لا إله إلا الله; «إله» is its noun and the khabar is omitted, which the grammarians have implied as "in existence" or "for us"; so they parsed it.»

Al-Rāzī:
Imam Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī raised a difficulty against al-Ṣafadī's i'rab, saying: this negation is general and comprehensive [Translator's note: the source has «متفرّق» ("dispersed"), probably for «مستغرق» ("all-encompassing")], and restricting it with "existence" is a specification of it, while "for us" is even more specific. If that is so, the negation no longer remains general, and in that case this statement would not be an affirmation of oneness in the absolute sense.

Al-Ṣalāḥ al-Ṣafadī also:
Al-Ṣalāḥ al-Ṣafadī answered, saying: «We do not concede that restricting it with "existence", if it is a specification, prevents it from remaining with the generality intended by the negation; for what is meant is the negation of gods in external reality except Allah the Exalted, in the sense that negating their existence entails negating their very essence, as if He said: no god exists except Allah. On this basis the negation remains general in the sense intended by it.»

Al-Samīn:
Al-Shihāb al-Ḥalabī, known as al-Samīn, said: «His saying: إلا هو is nominative as a badal from the noun of لا according to its position, since its position is nominative as a mubtadaʾ; or it is a badal from لا and what it governs, because it and what follows it are in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ.»

Abū Ḥayyān:
Al-Samīn went on to say: Abū Ḥayyān found it problematic that it should be a badal from إله, because it is not possible to repeat the governing word; you do not say: لا رجل إلا زيد [with لا repeated before the badal]. What appears to me is that it is a badal neither from إله nor from رجل in your saying لا رجل إلا زيد; rather it is a badal from the pronoun concealed in the omitted khabar. So if we say:
لا رجل إلا زيد, the implied form is: no man being or existing except Zayd. So زيد is a badal from the pronoun concealed in the khabar, not from رجل, and it is not a badal from the position of the noun of لا; rather it is a nominative badal from a nominative pronoun, which pronoun, in its implied form, refers back to the noun of لا. [Translator's note: the bracketed clarification is the translator's.]

Ibn Hishām:
Ibn Hishām said: «The statement of some of them about «لا إله إلا الله», that the name of Allah, Glorified be He, is the khabar of the lā of exoneration (lā al-tabriʾa), i.e. of generic negation, is refuted by the fact that it governs only a negated indefinite noun, whereas the name of Allah the Exalted is definite and affirmed. Yes, it is correct to say that it is the khabar of «لا» together with its noun, for the two are in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ according to Sībawayh.»
Then Ibn Hishām went on at length in refuting al-Zamakhsharī, in a way that the scope of this book cannot accommodate.

Shaykh Muṣṭafā al-Ghalāyīnī:
Shaykh Muṣṭafā al-Ghalāyīnī, one of the modern men of letters of Beirut, said:
«His saying, Exalted be He: لا إله إلا الله, i.e. no god exists; and الله is either a badal from the pronoun latent (mustatir) in the omitted khabar, or a badal from the position of لا and its noun.
Outside the verse it may be put in the accusative as an excepted noun.»

dervis-irab:266-266.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَخِيلٍ) النخيل: it is said that it is a collective-plural noun (ism jamʿ) whose singular is نخلة. It is also said:
it is the plural of نخل, and نخل is a generic noun (ism jins).
(الأعناب): the plural of عنب, or it is a generic noun whose singular is عنبة. (إِعْصارٌ): a violent wind that rises high; it is also said to be the scorching wind (al-samūm).
It was so named because it twists as a wrung-out (maʿṣūr) garment twists; it is also said, because it wrings (taʿṣir) the clouds. إعصار is pluralised as أعاصير.

* I'rab:
(أَيَوَدُّ أَحَدُكُمْ) is a resumptive clause brought to strike another parable for the spending of those who show off and those who reproach. The hamza is interrogative; (يود) is an imperfect verb; (أحدكم) is its fāʿil (agent); and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (أَنْ تَكُونَ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ): (أن) and what follows it are a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the accusative as the object of (يود); (له) — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); and (جنة) is its postponed noun (ism). (مِنْ نَخِيلٍ وَأَعْنابٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (جنة); and (أعناب) is conjoined to (نخيل). (تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ): (تجري) is an imperfect verb; (من تحتها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تجري); the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; (الأنهار) is the agent; and the clause is a second adjective of (جنة). (لَهُ فِيها مِنْ كُلِّ الثَّمَراتِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (فيها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (من كل الثمرات) — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of the postponed, omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "he has provision consisting of all the fruits, while it is in it"; and the clause is a third adjective of (جنة). (وَأَصابَهُ الْكِبَرُ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause (أصابه الكبر) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; «قد» must be implied. (وَلَهُ ذُرِّيَّةٌ ضُعَفاءُ): the wāw is circumstantial; (له) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (ذرية) is the postponed mubtadaʾ; (ضعفاء) is an adjective of (ذرية); and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the hāʾ in «أصابه». (فَأَصابَها إِعْصارٌ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (أصاب) is a past verb; the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (إعصار) is the agent; and the clause is conjoined to the adjective of the garden. (فِيهِ نارٌ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (نار) is the postponed mubtadaʾ; and the nominal clause is an adjective of (إعصار). (فَاحْتَرَقَتْ) is conjoined to (أصابها). (كَذلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمُ الْآياتِ): the preposition and its genitive noun «كذلك» are attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), or are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; (يبين) is an imperfect verb in the nominative; (الله) is the agent of (يبين); (لكم) is attached to (يبين); (الآيات) is the direct object, accusative with the kasra; and the clause (يبين) is resumptive. (لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ): (لعل) and its noun, and the clause (تتفكرون) is its khabar; and the clause of hope is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse Qur'anic eloquence soars to the highest summit the human mind can conceive, though all the verses of the Qur'an are of lofty, sublime eloquence. But this verse — and many verses that have come and will come in their places — have attained the utmost from the rhetorical side and gone beyond the limit. It serves as the parable of the spending of the show-off who spends to boast and to proclaim his self-love, and to make people imagine that he has reached the furthest goals, while his deeds go to waste. We shall discuss it at a length matching its far-reaching aims; what follows is what we have grasped of it:
1- The interrogative in His words «أيود؟» is for disapproval and negation. As for where the negation falls, it is on His words «فأصابها إعصار», because that is its point of attachment and its resting place.
