Beautiful is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbās about it: «It is a parable of a man who did acts of obedience, then Satan made things fair-seeming to him, so he did acts of disobedience until he burned up his deeds and they were lost».
2- This verse also contains the device of completion (al-tatmīm), which has been referred to before.
We shall expand on it further here, and say: it is that the poet or writer brings into his speech words which, if they were dropped, would diminish its meaning or its images, though the speech would remain sound.
Here are the images it comprises:
a- When He, Glorified is He, mentioned the garden (الجنة), He was not content to mention it free of any qualification, because in the language الجنة is a word applying to any dense, intertwined trees that cover whoever takes shelter in their spreading shade. Among such trees are some of limited benefit, like the tamarisk (الأثل) and the arak (الخمط) and other trees fit only for firewood; and among them are some whose benefit is multiplied: their fruit is eaten, other useful materials are extracted from them, and then their wood is fit for fuel. So He completed that deficiency by saying «من نخيل وأعناب», and it was understood self-evidently that this garden was distinguished by its trees being of the second kind, of multiplied benefit. That is, the burning of that garden — even if it contained tamarisk, arak and the like, of limited benefit — would grieve its owner; so how much more if it was of date-palms and grapevines? Would not the sorrow over it be more intense?
And the grief at its burning greater?
b- Then He completed that by mentioning the flowing rivers, to indicate the permanence of fertility. For what use is it if the waters in it dry up? Would its end not be dryness and withering?
c- And to remove the false impression that might occur to the listeners that this garden might be restricted to these two kinds of fruit, namely date-palms and grapes, He completed it by saying «له فيها من كل الثمرات», i.e. that it gathers every variety of fruit; so the regret at its burning is then more intense, and the sorrow over its perishing more comprehensive.
d- When He had finished describing the garden, He began describing the destructive event that led to the garden's perishing, by saying: «فأصابها إعصار», which sweeps away the green and the dry and destroys tillage and offspring.
e- However, a whirlwind, however great its effect, might be of delayed destruction; so He removed this false impression by saying «فيه نار», so it burned it after having destroyed its trees. And He was not content with mentioning the fire, because it may consume part of what it burns while something else of it remains afterwards; so He removed this false impression once more by mentioning the burning (فاحترقت).
Al-Buḥturī and completion:
An example of completion in poetry is the saying of al-Buḥturī describing camels worn thin by travel by day and by night:
كالقسيّ المعطّفات بل الأسهم مبريّة بل الأوتار
(Like bent bows — nay, like arrows pared thin — nay, like bowstrings.) He likened the camels to bent bows, a beautiful simile because of its allusion to leanness and to the humped, curved build of camels. Then he made them pared (like arrows) by way of a correction (iḍrāb) that hints at a mistake, and then rose further and made them like bowstrings. All of this is among al-Buḥturī's rare gems, which the ancient critics called «chains of gold». However, I afterwards came across a hadith of the Arab Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and learned that al-Buḥturī did not originate these deep meanings cast in the most beautiful expression, but that he gazed at the sky of the Prophetic hadith and took from it in a way that outran his pared arrows. It is his saying ﷺ: «If you prayed to Allah until you became like bows, and fasted until you became like bowstrings». This is among what was taken in its very wording and substance.
3- This verse also contains the device of «obedience and disobedience» (al-ṭāʿa wa-l-ʿiṣyān). This name was coined by the poet of the philosophers and philosopher of the poets, Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī, when he examined the poetry of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī and discussed it in his book «Muʿjiz Aḥmad», meaning Aḥmad al-Mutanabbī. He came to his saying:
يردّ يدا عن ثوبها وهو قادر ... ويعصي الهوى في طيفها وهو راقد
(He holds back a hand from her garment though he is able, and disobeys desire in her phantom though he is asleep.)
He said: «Al-Mutanabbī wanted antithesis (al-ṭibāq), but it disobeyed him, and paronomasia (al-jinās) obeyed him. For he wanted to say: "He holds back a hand from her garment while awake (مستيقظ)", but that disobeyed him because it could not enter the metre; so he said "though he is able" (قادر), because one who is able is awake and more, so that there would be a correspondence between it and the rhyme. Thus the reversed paronomasia between قادر and راقد obeyed him, and the antithesis between راقد and مستيقظ disobeyed him».
I say: this is what Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī mentioned, but there is nothing of that in al-Mutanabbī's verse. Had he wanted to say «يردّ يدا عن ثوبها وهو ساهر» or «متنبها», dropping the word «وهو», he would have achieved his aim of antithesis and the metre would not have disobeyed him. Rather, his intent is to show the chastity of one who is able, not of anyone else, i.e. that despite his power over her he does not permit himself to stretch his hand to her wrap, just as, when he sees her image in sleep, he refrains from it as he refrains from it when awake. He is describing himself as having a lofty aspiration far from flirting with women. So the device of obedience and disobedience, which al-Maʿarrī invented but was not successful in illustrating, was affirmed by the scholars of rhetoric, who illustrated it with the saying of Ibn al-Nabīh:
بيضاء حجّبها الواشون حين سرت ... عني فلو لمحت صبغ الدجى لمحت
(A fair one whom the slanderers veiled when she travelled by night away from me; had she glanced at the dye of the darkness, she would have been seen.)
He wanted to say: "had she glanced at the blackness (سواد) of the darkness", to bring in the colour-device (al-tadbīj) through "white" (بيضاء) and "blackness" (سواد); but the metre disobeyed him, so he said «صبغ الدجى», which is equivalent to blackness. So it holds true of him that the tadbīj disobeyed him and the device of indirect expression (al-irdāf) obeyed him.
Like it is the saying of al-Arrajānī:
كم رعت هذا الحي إما زائرا ... فردا وإما سائرا في جحفل
(How often I have alarmed this tribe, either visiting alone or marching in a great army.)
He wanted to say "or warring" (محاربا), so that the contrast would be between visitor and warrior — and no doubt the visitor is peaceable — [as there is] between his saying «فردا» and his saying «في جحفل»; but the metre disobeyed him and gave him [Translator's note: the source reads «وأعطاه لجناس», presumably «وأطاعه الجناس», "and paronomasia obeyed him"] the consecutive paronomasia (al-jinās al-lāḥiq) between زائر and سائر. As for the noble verse we are dealing with, completion occurs in it, and we have spoken of it a little earlier. Since the speaker originally aims at equivalence (al-musāwāh) in all he says, if equivalence disobeys him for the purposes mentioned above, completion obeys him. So take note of this, for it is among the subtleties of the devices.

dervis-irab:267-267.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تُغْمِضُوا) الإغماض: lowering the gaze. One says أغمضت العين إغماضا and غمّضتها تغميضا: I closed the eyelids. What is meant here is overlooking, tolerance and leniency.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has preceded; the vocative clause and what follows it are resumptive, brought to set out what one should spend from, i.e. spend from the lawful and the good of what you have earned. (أَنْفِقُوا مِنْ طَيِّباتِ ما كَسَبْتُمْ): (أنفقوا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (من طيبات) — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أنفقوا); (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa); and the clause (كسبتم) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (وَمِمَّا أَخْرَجْنا لَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ): (ومما) is conjoined to (من طيبات); the clause (أخرجنا) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; (لكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أخرجنا); and (من الأرض) is attached to (أخرجنا). You may instead attach it to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "issuing from the earth". May Allah have mercy on the jurists, how penetrating their minds were: Abū Ḥanīfa kept it general with respect to zakat, and al-Shāfiʿī restricted it to what human beings cultivate, and both are correct. (وَلا تَيَمَّمُوا الْخَبِيثَ مِنْهُ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (تيمموا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لا); the origin of (تيمموا) is تتيمموا with two tāʾs, one of which was dropped for lightness; the wāw is the agent; (الخبيث) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (منه) is attached to an omitted ḥāl from (الخبيث). (تُنْفِقُونَ): the clause is circumstantial, and the object of (تنفقون) is omitted, i.e. "spending it". (وَلَسْتُمْ بِآخِذِيهِ): the wāw is circumstantial; (ليس) and its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (آخذيه) is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar (predicate) of (ليس); the nūn was dropped because of the construct; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause is a ḥāl from the agent of (تنفقون), i.e. the wāw. (إِلَّا أَنْ تُغْمِضُوا فِيهِ): an instrument of restriction; (أن) and what is in its scope are a maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "except by your closing your eyes", and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, so it is an exception from the most general of states; you may instead attach them to (آخذيه), which is easier. (وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (اعلموا) is an imperative verb; the wāw is the agent; and (أن), its noun and its two khabars stand in place of the two objects of (اعلموا).

* Rhetoric:
This verse contains an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), in His words «إلا أن تغمضوا فيه»: overlooking something that deserves to be taken to task is likened to closing the eye to a disliked thing that a person avoids seeing [Translator's note: the source has the misprint «رؤبته» for «رؤيته»].

dervis-irab:164-164.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْفُلْكِ): ships. It can be singular, as in His saying, Exalted be He: «في الفلك المشحون», and it is then masculine. It can be plural, as in this verse, as shown by His saying:
«التي تجري في البحر»; and all of that is in a single form. The author of al-Munjid blundered remarkably over it, making it both masculine and feminine. His wording is: «الفلك: the ship; it is feminine and masculine.» The origin of the blunder is that he did not reflect — while copying the wording of al-Qāmūs haphazardly — that the masculine belongs specifically to the singular, while the feminine comes upon it through its being made a broken plural. The text of al-Qāmūs is: «الفلك, with ḍamma, is the ship; it is treated as masculine, and it is for the singular and the plural; or the فلك that is a broken plural of the فلك that is singular, and it is not like جنب, which is singular and plural, and its like, because فُعْل and فُعُل share in one thing, like العُرْب and العَرَب.» [Translator's note: the vowelling of the patterns in the quotation is not marked in the source.] If it is said that a broken plural must involve some change, the answer is that its change is implied: the ḍamma when it is plural is like the ḍamma in حُمْر and بُدْن, and when it is singular like the ḍamma in قُفْل. Moreover, Ibn Barrī added a correction, saying: «If you make الفلك singular, it is masculine only, and if you make it plural, it is feminine only.» So reflect on this paragraph, for it excels all paragraphs.
(الرِّياحِ): plural of ريح. The yāʾ of الريح and الرياح is from a wāw; the original forms are روح and رواح, and it was converted into yāʾ only because it is vowelless and preceded by a kasra. This is a regular substitution, and therefore, when the cause of its conversion disappeared, it returned to its origin, and one says: أرواح.
Maysūn bint Baḥdal said:
لبيت تخفق الأرواح فيه ... أحبّ إليّ من قصر منيف
(A tent in which the winds flutter is dearer to me than a lofty palace.)
In the plural it is mostly used for good, and in the singular for evil.
ʿUmāra ibn ʿAqīl ibn Bilāl ibn Jarīr committed a solecism with this word, using الأرياح in his poetry. Abū Ḥātim said to him: الأرياح is not permissible. ʿUmāra said: do you not hear them say رياح? Abū Ḥātim said to him: that is different from this. He said to him: you are right, and retracted. We say: but the plural أرياح does occur in al-Qāmūs of al-Fīrūzābādī; the text of his wording is: «الريح is feminine, and its plural is أرياح, أرواح, رياح and رِيَح like عنب, and the plural of the plural is أرواح and أراييح.» The author of al-Munjid copied his wording almost verbatim.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ): a particle resembling the verb. (فِي خَلْقِ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of إن. (وَاخْتِلافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ): conjoined to خلق السموات. (وَالْفُلْكِ): also conjoined. (الَّتِي): naʿt (adjective) of الفلك. (تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ): the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause). (بِما): the bāʾ is a preposition and ما is a relative noun in the position of genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). You may also make ما maṣdariyya, so that it, with the interpreted maṣdar it governs in the genitive, is attached to تجري, [in the sense of] "by means of what benefits people". (يَنْفَعُ النَّاسَ): the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of ما in either case. (وَما): conjoined to the first ما. (أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ): the clause is the ṣila of ما. (مِنَ السَّماءِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أنزل. (مِنْ ماءٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are a badal (substitute) from His saying من السماء, a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl). The objection of attaching two identical particles to a single governing word does not apply, for what is forbidden is that they be identical together without conjunction or substitution. (فَأَحْيا): conjoined to فأنزل. (بِهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أحيا. (الْأَرْضِ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (بَعْدَ مَوْتِها): the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَبَثَّ): conjoined to أنزل or أحيا. (فِيها): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (مِنْ كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to بث. (وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّياحِ): conjoined to «خلق». (وَالسَّحابِ): also conjoined. (الْمُسَخَّرِ): naʿt of السحاب. (بَيْنَ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ): the adverb is attached to مسخر, because it is a passive participle. (لَآياتٍ): the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and آيات is the postponed noun of إن. (لِقَوْمٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted naʿt of آيات. (يَعْقِلُونَ): an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is a naʿt of قوم. This verse is an explicit exhortation to the obligation of reflection and contemplation; it is reported from the Prophet ﷺ: «Woe to whoever recites this verse and spits it out», i.e. does not take a lesson from it.
So the verse is a resumptive clause, brought to urge reflection and taking lessons from dazzling wisdom.

dervis-irab:99-101.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نبذ): this verb has remarkable properties. Originally it means "throwing away"; one says «نبذ الشيء من يده», i.e. he threw the thing away and cast it off; and «صبي منبوذ» (a foundling child); and al-munābadha in selling was forbidden, which is that you say: "Throw the goods to me" or "I throw them to you". Among the figurative uses of this verb is their saying «نبذ أمري وراء ظهره» when someone does not act on it, and from it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: «نبذ فريق من الذين أوتوا الكتاب كتاب الله وراء ظهورهم». They said: «نبذ» must be one of the verbs of transformation or becoming (afʿāl al-taḥwīl aw al-taṣyīr), because it indicates moving from one state to another. On this basis «كتاب الله» is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and «وراء ظهورهم» is the second mafʿūl bihi. It is far-fetched, indeed impossible, to make it an adverb of «نبذ», because the adverb must contain the fāʿil (agent) of the verb governing it, and those who cast [it] away are not located behind their own backs. However, some grammarians do not require the presence of the fāʿil and the mafʿūl in the adverb. Ibn Ḥajar said in Sharḥ al-Minhāj: "You may say that the rule has a sound rationale, because the adverb of place belongs to sensible things; so when it is made the adverb of a sensible transitive verb, the fāʿil and the mafʿūl must be in it, because the said verb is only realized by the existence of both; unlike the abstract verb, which is foreign to the sensible adverb, so what is necessary for it on every assumption — the fāʿil only — suffices." The jurists have rulings in legislation based on this long disagreement. So reflect on this section, for though it has grown somewhat long, it is, like beauty, not wearisome.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ): the wāw is resumptive, the lām is [in] the answer to an omitted oath, and «قد» is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). (أَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ): a verb and its fāʿil, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أنزلنا». (آياتٍ): mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. (بَيِّناتٍ): an adjective. (وَما): the wāw is a conjunction and «ما» is negating. (يَكْفُرُ بِها): an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to it. (إِلَّا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (الْفاسِقُونَ): fāʿil of «يكفر». (أَوَكُلَّما): the hamza is for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the wāw is a conjunction joining to something omitted, its implied form being "Did they disbelieve in the clear signs?"; or else the original order is the conjunction before the interrogative particle, and the hamza was put first only because it has the head of the sentence. «كلما» is an adverb of time containing the sense of a condition, and its i'rab has preceded. (عاهَدُوا): a verb and its fāʿil. (عَهْداً): mafʿūl bihi; «عاهدوا» means "they gave", and the first object is omitted, i.e. "they gave Allah a covenant"; we may also parse «عهدا» as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (نَبَذَهُ): a verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi. (فَرِيقٌ): fāʿil. (مِنْهُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of «فريق». (بَلْ): a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction. (أَكْثَرُهُمْ): mubtadaʾ (subject). (لا يُؤْمِنُونَ): «لا» is negating, and the clause «لا يؤمنون» is the khabar (predicate) of «أكثرهم»; the nominal clause is conjoined to the previous clause. (وَلَمَّا): the wāw is a conjunction, and «لما» is adverbial-temporal (ḥīniyya) or linking. (جاءَهُمْ): a verb and its mafʿūl bihi. (رَسُولٌ): fāʿil; the clause «جاءهم» is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it, or has no position. (مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of «رسول». (مُصَدِّقٌ): a second adjective. (لَمَّا): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «مصدق». (مَعَهُمْ): an adverb of place attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (نَبَذَ فَرِيقٌ): a verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. (مِنَ الَّذِينَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of «فريق». (أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ): a past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and a second mafʿūl bihi. (كِتابَ اللَّهِ): the object of «نبذ». (وَراءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ): the second object of «نبذ», because it includes the meaning of «جعل» (to make); or an adverb of place attached to an omitted [word] which is the second object; the discussion of this has preceded. (كَأَنَّهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): «كأن» and its noun, and the clause «لا يعلمون» is its khabar; the clause «كأنهم» is circumstantial (ḥāliyya).

dervis-irab:102-102.t:
* Vocabulary:
(هارُوتَ وَمارُوتَ): two non-Arabic proper names, as shown by their being diptotes; had they been from «الهرت» and «المرت», i.e. breaking, as some claimed, they would have been declined [as triptotes]. Curious legends have been woven around them, for which one may refer to the lengthy works.
(خَلاقٍ): with fatḥa on the khāʾ, i.e. a share.
(بابل): an ancient city; it is a diptote because of being a proper name and non-Arabic. Its ruins lie on the Euphrates near al-Ḥilla, east of Baghdad.

* I'rab:
(وَاتَّبَعُوا): the wāw is a conjunction, and «اتبعوا» is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). (ما): a relative noun, the object of «اتبعوا». (تَتْلُوا الشَّياطِينُ): an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (عَلى مُلْكِ سُلَيْمانَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تتلو»; «سليمان» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the sign of its genitive being the fatḥa because it is a diptote for being a proper name and non-Arabic — and [the explanation by] the added alif and nūn depends on knowing the derivation. (وَما كَفَرَ): the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive, and «ما» is negating. (سُلَيْمانَ): fāʿil of «كفر». (وَلكِنَّ): the wāw is a conjunction, and «لكن» is a particle of rectification (istidrāk) resembling the verb. (الشَّياطِينُ): the noun of «لكن». (كَفَرُوا): the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of «لكن». (يُعَلِّمُونَ): an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or a second khabar. (النَّاسَ): first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (السِّحْرَ): second mafʿūl bihi. (وَما أُنْزِلَ عَلَى الْمَلَكَيْنِ): the wāw is a conjunction, «ما» is a relative noun conjoined to «السحر», the clause «أنزل» is the ṣila of «ما», and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «أنزل». (بِبابِلَ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (هارُوتَ وَمارُوتَ): badal (substitute) from «الملكين». (وَما): the wāw is resumptive and «ما» is negating. (يُعَلِّمانِ): an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the alif is the fāʿil. (مِنْ أَحَدٍ): «من» is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and «أحد» is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is the object of «يعلمان». (حَتَّى): a particle of limit and of the genitive. It is strange that Abū al-Baqāʾ claimed it comes in the meaning of «إلا»; it has not occurred in the language with this meaning. (يَقُولا): an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by «أن» implied after «حتى». (إِنَّما): a restraining particle and the restrained [particle] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). (نَحْنُ): mubtadaʾ (subject). (فِتْنَةٌ): khabar, and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (فَلا تَكْفُرْ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, «لا» is prohibitive, and «تكفر» is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لا», i.e. "if you wish to follow the right path, then do not disbelieve by learning it". (فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ): the fāʾ is resumptive; Sībawayh said it is a conjunction. (مِنْهُما): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يتعلمون». (ما): a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. (يُفَرِّقُونَ): the clause is the ṣila of «ما». (بِهِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يفرقون». (بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِ): the adverb is also attached to «يفرقون». (وَما): the wāw is circumstantial, and «ما» is Ḥijāzī. (هُمْ): its noun. (بِضارِّينَ): the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and «ضارين» is genitive in form, the khabar of «ما» in position. (بِهِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «ضارين». (مِنْ أَحَدٍ): «من» is a redundant preposition; «أحد» is genitive in form and accusative in position because it is the object of «ضارين», which is an active participle. (إِلَّا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl from the latent (mustatir) pronoun that is the fāʿil of «ضارين», or from the mafʿūl bihi, which is «أحد». (وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ): conjoined to what preceded. (ما): a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. (يَضُرُّهُمْ): the clause is the ṣila of «ما». (وَلا يَنْفَعُهُمْ): conjoined to the ṣila. (وَلَقَدْ): the wāw is resumptive, brought to begin explaining their state after learning magic; the lām is [in] the answer to an omitted oath, and «قد» is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). (عَلِمُوا): a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath. (لَمَنِ): the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), giving emphasis, and «من» is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ; and the clause (اشْتَراهُ) has no grammatical position. (ما): negating or Ḥijāzī. (لَهُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar, or the khabar of «ما». (فِي الْآخِرَةِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (مِنْ): a redundant preposition. (خَلاقٍ): a noun genitive in form by «من», a deferred mubtadaʾ or the noun of «ما»; the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «من», and the whole sentence is within the domain of the accusative, filling the place of the two objects of «علموا», which is suspended (muʿallaq) from governing. (وَلَبِئْسَ): the wāw is a conjunction, the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam), and «بئس» is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame. (ما): an indefinite noun meaning "a thing", in the position of the accusative as tamyīz (specification), explaining the fāʿil of «بئس», i.e. "as a thing". (شَرَوْا): a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is an adjective. (بِهِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «شروا». (أَنْفُسَهُمْ): mafʿūl bihi. (لَوْ): conditional. (كانُوا): «كان» and its noun, and the clause (يُعَلِّمُونَ) is its khabar [Translator's note: the source vocalizes the word as «يُعَلِّمُونَ»; the word in the verse is «يَعْلَمُونَ»]; the answer of «لو» is omitted, i.e. "they would not have embarked on the contrary deeds they committed".

* Rhetoric:
In this verse is a lofty art among the arts of rhetoric: treating the one who knows as one who does not know (tanzīl al-ʿālim manzilat al-jāhil). The beginning of the verse indicates that knowledge is established [for them] that there is no benefit for them in buying the books of magic and sorcery and choosing them over the books of Allah, while the end of the verse negates knowledge of them, since «لو» indicates the impossibility of the second because of the impossibility of the first. However, negating knowledge of them is for a rhetorical purpose, in view of the fact that they do not act according to what knowledge requires. Yet there is hyperbole in that, in pointing out that their knowledge of the absence of reward would suffice to hold them back — so how much more their knowledge of [its] blameworthiness and baseness.

dervis-irab:103-104.t:
* Vocabulary:
(راعِنا): "watch over us and be patient with us until we understand it". It is narrated that the Muslims used to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he delivered some knowledge to them, «راعنا». The Jews had a Hebrew word with which they insulted one another, which was «راعنا»; it was said:
its meaning is "Hear, may you not hear". When they heard the believers' saying «راعنا» they seized the opportunity of that and addressed the Messenger [with it]. When Saʿd ibn Muʿādh heard it from them — and he knew Hebrew — he said: "O enemies of Allah, the curse of Allah be upon you! By the One in whose hand is my soul, if I hear it from any man of you saying it to the Messenger of Allah, I will strike his neck." They said: "Do you not say it yourselves?" So the verse was revealed.
(انْظُرْنا): give us respite and grant us delay.

* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ): the wāw is resumptive or a conjunction, and «لو» is conditional. Sībawayh has a curious name for it: "a particle for what would have happened because of the happening of something else". (أَنَّهُمْ): «أن» and its noun. (آمَنُوا): a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of «أن», and «أن» with its noun and khabar is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "if their faith were established". It has also been said that it is in the position of the nominative as fāʿil of an omitted verb, i.e. "if their faith had been established". (وَاتَّقَوْا): conjoined to «آمنوا». (لَمَثُوبَةٌ): the lām is of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ); it has also been said that it occurs in the answer of «لو». The nominal clause was preferred over the verbal one in the answer of «لو» to indicate the permanence and continuance of the reward. «مثوبة» is a mubtadaʾ, and beginning with an indefinite was permissible because it has been qualified. (مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of «مثوبة». (خَيْرٌ): khabar of «مثوبة». (لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ): its i'rab has preceded; the answer of «لو» is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "they would have been rewarded". (يا أَيُّهَا): «يا» is a vocative particle, and «أي» is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of the accusative; the hāʾ is for drawing attention. (الَّذِينَ): badal (substitute) from «أيها». (آمَنُوا): a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (لا): prohibitive. (تَقُولُوا): an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by «لا». (راعِنا): an imperative verb, whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you", and «نا» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) — that is in origin; but what is meant here is quotation (ḥikāya), so it is parsed as a word whose wording, not its meaning, is intended, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (وَقُولُوا): conjoined to «لا تقولوا». (انْظُرْنا): in origin an imperative verb with «نا» its object; what is meant here is quotation. (وَاسْمَعُوا): the wāw is a conjunction, and «اسمعوا» is conjoined to «لو» [Translator's note: so in the source; it is presumably conjoined to «قولوا»], and the object is omitted, i.e. "hear what the Messenger speaks to you and the questions he delivers to you that lead to…" [Translator's note: the source text here, «المؤدية إلى فلا حكم», is corrupt and its ending cannot be translated with confidence.] (وَلِلْكافِرِينَ): the wāw is resumptive, brought for summarizing after detailing, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar. (عَذابٌ): a deferred mubtadaʾ. (أَلِيمٌ): naʿt (adjective) of «عذاب».

* Rhetoric:
The verse alludes to one of the most sublime arts of rhetoric, and the one that most draws in lofty aims and high ideals: the art of refinement (fann al-tahdhīb), i.e. repeatedly reviewing what the writer writes and the poet composes. It has been freed from ambiguity (al-īhām) and has pointed to the etiquette of address, so that speech may be free of grounds for reproach and far from ambiguous double meanings (al-malāḥin).

dervis-irab:105-105.t:
* Vocabulary:
(اختص): a transitive verb. One says «خصّه بكذا», «اختصّه», «خصّصه» and «أخصّه», and then «اختصّ به». Every word whose first radical is khāʾ and whose second radical is ṣād indicates gathering, abundance and joining together: as «خصب المكان» and «أخصب», i.e. fertility came upon it, which is the gathering and abundance of vegetation; and «خاصر المرأة», he held her by the waist. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥassān ibn Thābit said:
ثم خاصرتها إلى القبة الخضر ... اء تمشي في مرمر مسنون
(Then I walked with her, waist in hand, to the green dome, as she stepped on polished marble.)
And «خصف الأوراق»: he joined the leaves one to another; and «هم خصوم» and «خصاء» — and that only happens in a gathering.

* I'rab:
(ما): negating. (يَوَدُّ): an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). (الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): fāʿil (agent) of «يود», and the clause «كفروا» is a ṣila (relative clause). (مِنْ): a preposition. (أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ): genitive by «من», and the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَلَا الْمُشْرِكِينَ): conjoined to «أهل الكتاب»; «لا» was introduced for emphasis, and were it not in the Qur'an its omission would be permissible. (أَنْ يُنَزَّلَ): «أن» and what falls within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the object of «يود»; «ينزل» is passive. (عَلَيْكُمْ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ينزل». (مِنْ): a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. (خَيْرٍ): genitive in form, nominative in position as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): an adjective of «خير». (وَاللَّهُ): the wāw is resumptive, and «الله» is a mubtadaʾ (subject). (يَخْتَصُّ): an imperfect verb, nominative, whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he"; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «الله». (بِرَحْمَتِهِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يختص». (مِنْ): a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (يَشاءُ): the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَاللَّهُ): the wāw is a conjunction, and «الله» is a mubtadaʾ. (ذُو الْفَضْلِ): khabar, the sign of its nominative being the wāw because it is one of the five nouns. (الْعَظِيمِ): naʿt (adjective) of «الفضل».

dervis-irab:106-107.t:
* Vocabulary:
(النسخ): removal and transfer. One says «نسخت الريح الأثر», i.e. the wind removed the trace, and «نسخت الكتاب», i.e. I copied the book. It carries the meaning of the arrival of a better state. Every word whose first radical is nūn and whose second is sīn indicates renewal and change and the arrival of what is better, or going away and moving. Of that is «نسأ الشيء والأمر», he postponed it; «أنسأ الله أجلك», may Allah postpone your term and lengthen it; and «نسب», he composed love poetry and described a woman with descriptions suited to her charms. This is among the wonders of our Arabic language, so reflect on it, for it is something we have devised for the first time. The meaning of the verse is also wonderful: i.e. every verse that We take away, according to what wisdom requires — removing its wording, or its ruling, or both together — We bring one better than it.

* I'rab:
(ما): a jussive conditional noun, in the position of a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «ننسخ». (نَنْسَخْ): the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm). (مِنْ آيَةٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of the conditional noun. The conditional noun is not definite, so the preposition and its genitive noun cannot be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it. The meaning is "whatever thing of the verses We abrogate", so it is a singular occurring in the place of a plural; this is regular after the condition because of the sense of generality in it, and on this basis everything that comes in this construction is explained, as in His saying: «ما يفتح الله للناس من رحمة» and «وما بكم من نعمة فمن الله». Some permitted «من آية» to be in the position of the accusative as tamyīz (specification), the thing specified being «ما», and that too is not far-fetched. Ibn Hishām parsed it as being in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and that too is not far-fetched. (أَوْ): a conjunction. (نُنْسِها): conjoined to «ننسخ»; the hamza has been softened, so the sukūn does not appear; the original is «ننسئها», i.e. We defer it; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. (نَأْتِ): the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter. (بِخَيْرٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «نأت». (مِنْها): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «خير», because it is an elative (ism tafḍīl). (أَوْ مِثْلِها): conjoined to «بآية». [Translator's note: so in the source; it is conjoined to «بخير».] (أَلَمْ): the hamza is for interrogation of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī), and «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and the jussive. (تَعْلَمْ): an imperfect verb in the jussive by «لم». (أَنَّ اللَّهَ): «أن» and its noun. (عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «قدير». (قَدِيرٌ): khabar (predicate) of «أن»; «أن» and what falls within its scope fill the place of the two objects of «تعلم». (أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ): a second [interrogation of] affirmation. (أَنَّ اللَّهَ): «أن» and its noun. (لَهُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ): a deferred mubtadaʾ (subject). (وَالْأَرْضِ): conjoined to «السموات». (وَما لَكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, «ما» is negating, and «لكم» is a fronted khabar. (مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (مِنْ وَلِيٍّ): «من» is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and «ولي» is genitive in form and nominative in position as a deferred mubtadaʾ. (وَلا نَصِيرٍ): conjoined to «ولي».

dervis-irab:268-270.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الفحشاء): what is meant by it here is stinginess, and الفاحش is the miser. Ṭarafa ibn al-ʿAbd said:
أرى الموت يعتام الكرام ويصطفي ... عقيلة مال الفاحش المتشدّد
(I see death choosing the noble, and selecting the choicest wealth of the tight-fisted miser.)
Al-Kalbī said: «Every فحشاء in the Qur'an means fornication, except this place».

* I'rab:
(الشَّيْطانُ يَعِدُكُمُ الْفَقْرَ) is a resumptive statement brought to warn against listening to Satan and his whisperings. (الشيطان) is the mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (يعدكم) is the khabar (predicate); and (الفقر) is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or accusative by removal of the preposition. (وَيَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالْفَحْشاءِ) is conjoined to «يعدكم الفقر», and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يأمركم). (وَاللَّهُ يَعِدُكُمْ مَغْفِرَةً مِنْهُ وَفَضْلًا) is conjoined to the resumptive clause; (مغفرة) is the second direct object; (منه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (مغفرة); and (فضلا) is conjoined to (مغفرة). (وَاللَّهُ واسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ; and (واسع) and (عليم) are two khabars of (الله). (يُؤْتِي الْحِكْمَةَ مَنْ يَشاءُ): the clause is a third khabar of (الله), or a resumptive clause. (يؤتي) is an imperfect verb in the nominative whose fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he"; (الحكمة) is the first direct object; (من) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the second direct object; and the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (وَمَنْ يُؤْتَ الْحِكْمَةَ): the wāw is resumptive; (من) is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (يؤت) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), passive, its sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; and (الحكمة) is the second direct object. (فَقَدْ أُوتِيَ خَيْراً كَثِيراً): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (قد) is a particle of realisation; (أوتي) is a passive past verb whose deputy agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; (خيرا) is the second direct object; (كثيرا) is an adjective; the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as apodosis; and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of (من). (وَما يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّا أُولُوا الْأَلْبابِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (يذكر) is an imperfect verb in the nominative; (إلا) is an instrument of restriction; (أولو) is the agent, nominative, its sign being the wāw because it is attached to the sound masculine plural; and (الألباب) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (وَما أَنْفَقْتُمْ مِنْ نَفَقَةٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the accusative as a fronted direct object of (أنفقتم); (من نفقة) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). Many made it redundant (zāʾida), which is easier, but it is not according to the rule (ghayr maqīs). (أَوْ نَذَرْتُمْ مِنْ نَذْرٍ) is conjoined to what precedes. (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُهُ): the fāʾ links the apodosis; (إن) and its noun, and the clause (يعلمه) is its khabar; and the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as apodosis. (وَما لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ أَنْصارٍ): the wāw is resumptive; (ما) is negating; (للظالمين) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (من) is a redundant preposition; and (أنصار) is the postponed mubtadaʾ.

dervis-irab:271-272.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنْ تُبْدُوا الصَّدَقاتِ فَنِعِمَّا هِيَ) is a resumptive statement brought to detail what was stated summarily in the preceding conditional clause, and for that reason the conjunction was left out. (إن) is a jussive conditional particle; (تبدوا) is an imperfect verb, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and (الصدقات) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (فنعما): the fāʾ links, because the apodosis is an inflexible (jāmid) verb. One of them said about the places where the apodosis is linked by the fāʾ:
اسمية طلبية وبجامد ... وبما ولن وبقد وبالتنفيس
(A nominal clause, a clause of request, and with an inflexible verb, with mā, lan, qad, and with the particle of futurity [sa-/sawfa].)
(نعم) is an inflexible past verb for expressing praise; (ما) is a complete indefinite noun meaning "a thing", in the position of the accusative as tamyīz (specification); the agent of (نعم) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun explained by «ما»; (هي) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being the clause (نعما), because it is the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ); and the clause (نعما هي) is a nominal clause in the position of the jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (وَإِنْ تُخْفُوها وَتُؤْتُوهَا الْفُقَراءَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (تخفوها) is an imperfect verb, the protasis, its sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the agent and the hāʾ the direct object; (تؤتوها) is conjoined to it, the hāʾ being the first direct object and (الفقراء) the second direct object. (فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ): the fāʾ links the apodosis; (هو) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (خير) is the khabar; (لكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خير); and the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as apodosis. (وَيُكَفِّرُ عَنْكُمْ مِنْ سَيِّئاتِكُمْ): the wāw is resumptive; (يكفّر) is an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the clause is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and Allah removes from you"; (عنكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يكفر). It was also read in the jussive, conjoined to the position of the fāʾ in His words «فهو خير لكم», because that is the apodosis. (من سيئاتكم) is attached to an omitted adjective of an omitted direct object, i.e. "something of your misdeeds"; Sībawayh stated this explicitly, and it is better than making it redundant (zāʾida) in affirmative speech, as grammarians such as Abū al-Baqāʾ and others did. (وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ and (خبير) its khabar; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (خبير); and the clause (تعملون) has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila (relative clause). (لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ هُداهُمْ) is a resumptive statement brought to be strict in creed and to forbid laxity with the enemies of Allah and the enemies of His religion. It is known that there were kinships and ties by marriage here among the Jews, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade giving them charity in order to induce them to join the upright religion. (ليس) is a deficient past verb; (عليك) is its fronted khabar; and (هداهم) is its postponed noun, a maṣdar (verbal noun) in construct with its object. (وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ): the wāw is parenthetical with no grammatical position, and the clause has no grammatical position; (لكن) and its noun, and the clause (يهدي) is its khabar; (من) is a relative noun, the object of (يهدي); and the clause (يشاء) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَما تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلِأَنْفُسِكُمْ): the wāw conjoins to what precedes; (ما) is a jussive conditional, in the position of the accusative as a fronted direct object of (تنفقوا); (تنفقوا) is the protasis; (من خير) is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial); the fāʾ links the apodosis; (لأنفسكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being "then it is for yourselves"; and the clause is in the position of the jussive as apodosis. (وَما تُنْفِقُونَ إِلَّا ابْتِغاءَ وَجْهِ اللَّهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (تنفقون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative, its sign being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its agent; (إلا) is an instrument of restriction; (ابتغاء) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), so the exception is from the most general of causes; and (وجه الله) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (وَما تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ): its i'rab has preceded. (يُوَفَّ إِلَيْكُمْ): the apodosis, jussive, its sign being the dropping of the weak letter; its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, its implied form being "it"; and (إليكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يوفّ). (وَأَنْتُمْ لا تُظْلَمُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; (أنتم) is the mubtadaʾ; the clause (لا تظلمون) is the khabar of (أنتم); and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. You may make the wāw resumptive, in which case the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:165-165.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَنْداداً) النّدّ: an equal, a like; what is meant here is the idols, or anything their souls enticed them to worship.

* I'rab:
(وَمِنَ النَّاسِ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to state that some people did not believe in oneness after it had been established by conclusive proof; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate). (مِنَ) [Translator's note: so in the source; the word meant is مَنْ]: a relative noun in the position of nominative as the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), or a qualified indefinite noun (nakira mawṣūfa) in the position of nominative as the postponed mubtadaʾ. (يَتَّخِذُ): the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause), or it is a naʿt (adjective) of «من»; the fāʿil (agent) of يتخذ is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he" (هو), referring to the wording of من. (مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يتخذ. (أَنْداداً): mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (يُحِبُّونَهُمْ): an imperfect verb, nominative, with its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is a naʿt of أندادا, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun concealed in يتخذ. (كَحُبِّ اللَّهِ): the kāf and its genitive are in the position of accusative as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), so it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); it may also be parsed as a ḥāl, which Sībawayh preferred. The maṣdar is annexed to its object. (وَالَّذِينَ): the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial, and the relative noun is a mubtadaʾ. (آمَنُوا): a verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. (أَشَدُّ): the khabar of the relative noun. (حُبًّا): tamyīz (specification). (لِلَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to حبا. (وَلَوْ): the wāw is resumptive, and لو is a non-jussive conditional particle. (يَرَى): an imperfect verb. (الَّذِينَ): fāʿil. (ظَلَمُوا): the verbal clause is the ṣila and has no grammatical position. (إِذْ): an adverb of past time attached to يرى. (يَرَوْنَ): the verbal clause is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الْعَذابَ): the first object; the second object is omitted, implied as "descending upon them at the time of their seeing". (أَنَّ الْقُوَّةَ): أن and its noun. (لِلَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar; أن and what follows it take the place of the two objects of يرى. (جَمِيعاً): ḥāl. (وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعَذابِ): conjoined to what precedes. The apodosis (jawāb) of لو is omitted, i.e. "you would have seen a wonder, and there would have been from them regret and anguish beyond description".

* Rhetoric:
Concision (ījāz) in the verse, through the omission of the apodosis of لو as stated above; this is very common in their speech and occurs often in the Qur'an. Abū Tammām al-Ṭāʾī clung to the fringes of this eloquence when he said in his ode «The Conquest of Amorium»:
لو يعلم الكفر كم من أعصر كمنت ... له المنيّة بين السّمر والقضب
(If unbelief knew for how many ages death had lain in ambush for it among the brown spears and the swords…)
Its implied completion is: if unbelief knew that, it would have made its preparations and taken precautions for itself — but how far off that is!

* Benefits:
(دُونِ): an adverb of place, the opposite of فوق ("above"), as in هو دونه, i.e. he is lower than him in rank or standing. It comes in the sense of "in front of", as in: الشيء دونك, i.e. in front of you; and in the sense of "behind", as in: قعد دون الصف, i.e. behind it. It may come in the sense of "poor, base", and then it is not an adverb, as in: هذا شيء دون (this is an inferior thing), and in that case it takes the various i'rab positions freely. It also comes in the sense of "other than", as in the verse, and in that case it is most often used in the genitive with من.

dervis-irab:166-167.t:
* I'rab:
(إِذْ): an adverb of past time; together with what it governs it is a badal (substitute) from the إذ that came earlier in the previous verse. (تَبَرَّأَ الَّذِينَ): a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). (اتُّبِعُوا): a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the clause تبرأ is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it. They are the leaders. (مِنَ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) تبرأ; اتبعوا is an active past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil — they are the followers — and the clause is a ṣila. (وَرَأَوُا): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or a conjunction, and رأوا is a verb and its fāʿil. (الْعَذابَ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is circumstantial with قد implied, i.e. they disowned them while seeing the punishment; or it is conjoined to the clause تبرأ. (وَتَقَطَّعَتْ بِهِمُ الْأَسْبابُ): conjoined to what precedes. (وَقالَ): the wāw is a conjunction, and قال is a past verb. (الَّذِينَ): fāʿil. (اتَّبَعُوا): the clause is the ṣila; اتبعوا is a passive past verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil. [Translator's note: so in the source; here اتَّبَعُوا is active ("those who followed"), the wāw being the fāʿil, as the author himself parsed it above.] (لَوْ): a non-jussive conditional particle that includes the meaning of wishing (tamannī). (أَنَّ لَنا كَرَّةً): أن, its fronted khabar (predicate) and its postponed noun; أن and what falls within its scope is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (فَنَتَبَرَّأَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (al-sababiyya), and نتبرأ is an imperfect verb, subjunctive by an implied أن after the fāʾ of causation preceded by the wish contained in لو; its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "we" (نحن). (مِنْهُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نتبرأ. (كَما): the kāf with its genitive is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and ما is maṣdariyya. (تَبَرَّؤُا): a past verb and its fāʿil. (مِنَّا): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تبرءوا. (كَذلِكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. a showing like that showing. Sībawayh chose the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it is correct. (يُرِيهِمُ): an imperfect verb. The seeing here may be visual, in which case it takes two objects, the first being the pronoun and the second أعمالهم; or it may be mental, which is perhaps preferable, in which case it takes three. (اللَّهُ): fāʿil. (أَعْمالَهُمْ): second object. (حَسَراتٍ): third object, or ḥāl. (عَلَيْهِمْ): attached to an omitted naʿt of حسرات. (وَما): the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is Ḥijāzī. (هُمْ): the noun of the Ḥijāzī ما. (بِخارِجِينَ): the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and خارجين is genitive in form, accusative in position as the khabar of ما. (مِنَ النَّارِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to خارجين.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the verse there is the device of jumbled involution and evolution (al-laff wa-l-nashr al-mushawwash): mentioning several things in detail or in summary, then mentioning what belongs to each one and referring it back to what it belongs to. Their disowning one another goes back to His saying: إذ تبرأ, and His showing them the severity of the punishment goes back to His saying: ورأوا العذاب. What is meant is that He showed them these two things as a punishment for their taking equals besides Allah; just as He punished them for their beliefs, He punished them for their deeds. This device has many branches, discussed at length in the books of rhetoric. Among its instances in poetry is the saying of Abū Firās al-Ḥamdānī:
وشادن قال لي لمّا رأى سقمي ... وضعف جسمي والدّمع الذي انسجما
أخذت دمعك من خدّي وجسمك من ... خصري وسقمك من طرفي الذي سقما
(A young gazelle said to me when he saw my sickness, my wasted body and my flowing tears: "You took your tears from my cheek, your body from my waist, and your sickness from my languid eye.")
2- In His saying: إذ تبرأ الذين اتبعوا… to the end of the verse, there is a device called tarṣīʿ (inlaying), which is for the speech to be in rhymed prose; it occurs in the verse in two places, and it is frequent in the Qur'an. As for poetry, among its instances is the saying of Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
في تاجه قمر في ثوبه بشر ... في درعه أسد تدمى أظافره
(In his crown a moon, in his robe a man, in his coat of mail a lion whose claws drip blood.)
And Abū Tammām said:
تدبير معتصم بالله منتقم ... لله مرتغب في الله مرتقب
(The governance of one who holds fast to Allah, takes vengeance for Allah, longs for Allah, and watches [for His reward].)
3- In His saying: «وتقطعت بهم الأسباب» there is a majāz mursal (non-metaphorical trope) whose relation is causality: السبب originally is the rope by which one climbs to what is high, then it came to be used for everything by which one reaches something, whether material or abstract. You may also make it a case of explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): He likened the deeds they used to practise in this world to the ropes a person clings to for safety, then omitted the thing likened and kept the thing it is likened to. Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā said:
ومن هاب أسباب المنايا ينلنه ... وإن يرق أسباب السماء بسلم
(Whoever fears the ropes of death, they will reach him, even if he climbs the ropes of heaven with a ladder.)
4- The device of omission (ḥadhf): the apodosis of the conditional لو is omitted, and it is implied in the verse, its implied form being: there would have been from them what is beyond description.

* Benefits:
Every noun whose singular is on the pattern «فَعْلة», with fatḥa on the first letter and the second letter vowelless, has its plural on فَعَلات, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and the ʿayn, like شهوة and تمرة, whose plurals are شهوات and تمرات, with the second letters vowelled. But if it is an adjective, you leave its second letter vowelless, like ضخمة and عبلة, which you pluralise as ضخمات and عبلات, with the second letters vowelless.

dervis-irab:168-169.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الخطوات), with two ḍammas: plural of خطوة, which is the space between the feet of the one walking.
Among the curious things about the khāʾ and the ṭāʾ is that when they occur as the first and second radicals (fāʾ and ʿayn) of a word, this indicates a trace (athar). The trace of a step is well known; hence they said: اتبع خطواته (he followed his steps), as if it left a trace on him and he followed it. Error (الخطأ) in opinion and in a question has an evident trace; among their proverbs is: «Among the misses there is an arrow that hits.» الخطب is a calamity, and its trace is clear. Say the like of this about الخطل, i.e. foolishness — it is the drooping of the ears, or foolishness — and the Umayyad poet was named al-Akhṭal. All of this we discovered after investigation and careful scrutiny, so reflect on it.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ): يا is a vocative particle for one at a middle distance; أي is the one addressed, an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative; the hāʾ is for drawing attention, and الناس is a badal (substitute) of أي. (كُلُوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (مِمَّا): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) كلوا. (فِي الْأَرْضِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted [verb that is the] ṣila (relative clause). (حَلالًا): mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of كلوا, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما». (طَيِّباً): naʿt (adjective); an interesting discussion of it will follow. (وَلا): the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is prohibitive. (تَتَّبِعُوا): an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (خُطُواتِ): mafʿūl bihi; the sign of its accusative is the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. (الشَّيْطانِ): muḍāf ilayhi. (إِنَّهُ): إن and its noun. (لَكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally a naʿt of عدو and has come before it. (عَدُوٌّ): the nominative khabar (predicate) of إن. (مُبِينٌ): naʿt of عدو. The vocative clause and what follows it is resumptive, brought to state the domains of the lawful and the unlawful, and that this rests with Allah the Exalted. The clause إنه and what follows it has no grammatical position because it gives the reason for the prohibition of following the steps of Satan in that. (إِنَّما): a restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa), rendered inoperative. (يَأْمُرُكُمْ): a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil referring to Satan, and a mafʿūl bihi. (بِالسُّوءِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يأمركم; the clause is resumptive, brought to show Satan's enmity and expose its aims. (وَالْفَحْشاءِ): conjoined to His saying بالسوء. (وَأَنْ تَقُولُوا): the maṣdar cast from أن and what falls within its scope is also conjoined to السوء. (عَلَى اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تقولوا. (ما): a relative noun, the object of تقولوا. (لا): negative. (تَعْلَمُونَ): an imperfect verb, nominative, and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of ما.

* Rhetoric:
The dependent metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tabaʿiyya) in Satan's commanding, in answer to a question that may occur to the mind, namely: how can Satan be a commander when Allah the Exalted says: «إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان»? His making evil seem attractive to them, inciting them to it, and kindling the fire of desires in souls is likened to the command of one who commands; so it is an explicit, dependent metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tabaʿiyya). In reality, Satan's command is an expression for the stirrings that assail us and drive us to commit evil deeds.

* Benefits:
The grammarians and the jurists differed over the meaning of this adjective, i.e. طيبا. Some said it is a confirming adjective, because the meaning of طيبا and حلالا is the same; Mālik adopted this. Others said it is a specifying adjective, because its meaning differs from that of حلال, namely what is found pleasant; al-Shāfiʿī adopted this. For that reason the eating of filthy animals and everything vile is forbidden.

dervis-irab:108-108.t:
* I'rab:
(أَمْ): a disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) conjunction meaning «بل». (تُرِيدُونَ): an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (أَنْ تَسْئَلُوا): «أن» and what falls within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the object of «تريدون». (رَسُولَكُمْ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «تسألوا». (كَما سُئِلَ مُوسى): the kāf is a preposition, and «ما» is a maṣdar particle (maṣdariyya) which together with what follows is interpreted as a maṣdar, [the phrase being] a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or a ḥāl (circumstantial); «موسى» is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of «سئل». (مِنْ قَبْلُ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سئل». (وَمَنْ): the wāw is resumptive, and «من» is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). (يَتَبَدَّلِ): the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (الْكُفْرَ): mafʿūl bihi. (بِالْإِيمانِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يتبدل»; it is the thing given up. (فَقَدْ): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and «قد» is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). (ضَلَّ): a past verb whose fāʿil is "he". (سَواءَ السَّبِيلِ): its object, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis.

dervis-irab:109-109.t:
* I'rab:
(وَدَّ كَثِيرٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتابِ): a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of «كثير». (لَوْ يَرُدُّونَكُمْ): «لو» is a maṣdar particle (maṣdariyya), interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the object of «ود»; «يردونكم» is a verb, its fāʿil and its first object. (مِنْ بَعْدِ إِيمانِكُمْ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يردون», and «إيمانكم» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (كُفَّاراً): second object of «يردونكم». (حَسَداً): mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). (مِنْ عِنْدِ أَنْفُسِهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «ود», in the sense that they wished that you would apostatize from your religion, and their wishing that was from their own selves, not from any inclination toward the truth, because they wished that after it had become clear to them that you are upon the truth; this is confirmed by His saying afterwards: «تلك أمانيهم». (مِنْ بَعْدِ ما تَبَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الْحَقُّ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «ود»; «ما» is a maṣdar particle interpreted together with the verb after it as a maṣdar annexed to «بعد», and «الحق» is fāʿil of «تبين». (فَاعْفُوا): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and «اعفوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (وَاصْفَحُوا): conjoined to «فاعفوا». (حَتَّى يَأْتِيَ اللَّهُ بِأَمْرِهِ): «حتى» is a particle of limit and of the genitive; «يأتي» is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by «أن» implied after «حتى»; «الله» is the fāʿil; and in «بأمره» the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يأتي». (إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): «إن» and its noun, and «قدير» its khabar (predicate); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «قدير»; the clause «إن الله» is resumptive or serves as a causal explanation (taʿlīl).

dervis-irab:110-110.t:
* I'rab:
(وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ): the wāw is resumptive; «أقيموا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and «الصلاة» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَآتُوا الزَّكاةَ): conjoined to what preceded. (وَما تُقَدِّمُوا): the wāw is resumptive, and «ما» is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi; «تقدموا» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is the fāʿil. (لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تقدموا». (مِنْ خَيْرٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of the conditional noun, or tamyīz (specification), as has preceded. (تَجِدُوهُ): the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. (عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): the adverb is attached to «تجدوه» or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (إِنَّ اللَّهَ): «إن» and its noun. (بِما تَعْمَلُونَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «بصير». (بَصِيرٌ): khabar (predicate) of «إن»; the clause of «إن» and what follows it is resumptive or causal (taʿlīliyya).

dervis-irab:111-112.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقالُوا): conjoined to «ودّ»; the pronoun refers to the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians. (لَنْ): a particle of negation, the accusative and the future. (يَدْخُلَ): an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by «لن». (الْجَنَّةَ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa). (إِلَّا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (مَنْ): a relative noun, fāʿil (agent). (كانَ): a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he". (هُوداً): its khabar (predicate). (أَوْ نَصارى): conjoined to «هودا». (تِلْكَ): a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject). (أَمانِيُّهُمْ): khabar; the nominal clause has no grammatical position because it is a parenthesis between His saying «وقالوا» and His saying «قل هاتوا برهانكم». (قُلْ): an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "you", and the clause is resumptive. (هاتُوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (بُرْهانَكُمْ): mafʿūl bihi. (إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ): a condition and its verb; the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then bring your proof". (بَلى): a particle of reply affirming what they negated, namely others' entering Paradise. (مَنْ): a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ. (أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُ): the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (لِلَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أسلم». (وَهُوَ): the wāw is circumstantial, and «هو» is a mubtadaʾ. (مُحْسِنٌ): its khabar, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (فَلَهُ أَجْرُهُ): the fāʾ is linking; the preposition and its genitive noun are a fronted khabar, and «أجره» is a deferred mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ): the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَلا خَوْفٌ): the wāw is a conjunction, «لا» is negating, and «خوف» is a mubtadaʾ; beginning with it was permissible because the negation precedes it. (عَلَيْهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar of «خوف». (وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ): conjoined to what preceded.

* Benefits:
The lexicographers differed over the nūn of «البرهان». Some said it is augmentative, because it is derived from «البره», which is cutting, since it is a proof that yields decisive (qaṭʿī) knowledge; and from it is «البرهة» for a long stretch of time; so its pattern is «فعلان». Others said it is a root letter, because it is from «برهن يبرهن برهنة», and «البرهنة» is making clear; so its pattern is «فعلال». On this basis, «برهان», if it is the proper name of a man, may be declined or made a diptote, according to the two views just mentioned.

* Rhetoric:
(The plural «الأماني»), although what they wished for does not exceed a single wish, namely entering Paradise, is for a wonderful secret in the craft of eloquence: because of the intensity of their wishing for this wish and its being rooted in their souls, it was put in the plural, as though it were many wishes distributed in every heart, leaving no room for anything else.

dervis-irab:273-274.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أُحْصِرُوا): jihad confined them and kept them in readiness for fighting in the way of Allah, and turned their souls away from occupying themselves with anything else. أرصد الشيء means to prepare a thing for some matter; in the hadith: «except that I set it aside (أرصده) for a debt I owe». Today they use it wrongly, writing «رصد المبلغ لكذا» (the sum was earmarked for such-and-such), whereas the correct form is:
«أرصد». So take note.
(سيماهم) السيما, with the short ending, is a mark; it may also be lengthened: السيماء.
Some of Banū Asad and Thaqīf say: بسيميائهم. Of this is the saying of Ibn ʿAnqāʾ al-Fazārī: غلام رماه الله بالحسن يافعا ... له سيمياء لا تشق على البصر
(A youth whom Allah endowed with beauty in his adolescence; he has a mark that does not weary the eye.)
(الإلحاف): great importunity in asking. In the hadith: «Whoever asks while he has forty dirhams has been importunate (ألحف)».

* I'rab:
(لِلْفُقَراءِ الَّذِينَ أُحْصِرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "your charities are for the poor"; (الذين) is an adjective of (الفقراء); the clause (أحصروا في سبيل الله) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (أحصروا). (لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ ضَرْباً فِي الْأَرْضِ): the clause is in the place of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The clause (للفقراء) is resumptive, brought as an answer to a question arising from what preceded, as if, when they were commanded to give charity, they asked: "For whom is it?" and it was said: "It is for these". (لا) is negating; (يستطيعون) is an imperfect verb, its sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (ضربا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (في الأرض) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ضربا). (يَحْسَبُهُمُ الْجاهِلُ أَغْنِياءَ مِنَ التَّعَفُّفِ): the clause is a second ḥāl of (الفقراء). (يحسبهم) is an imperfect verb; the hāʾ is the first object of (يحسب); (الجاهل) is the agent; (أغنياء) is the second direct object; and (من التعفف) is a preposition and its genitive noun in the place of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). It was put in the genitive with «من» because it lacks one of its most important conditions, namely identity of the agent: the agent of the reckoning is the ignorant person, and the agent of the abstaining is the poor. (تَعْرِفُهُمْ بِسِيماهُمْ): the clause is a third ḥāl of (الفقراء); and (بسيماهم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تعرفهم). (لا يَسْئَلُونَ النَّاسَ إِلْحافاً): the clause is a fourth ḥāl. (لا) is negating; (يسألون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative; the wāw is the agent; (الناس) is the direct object; and (إلحافا) may be parsed as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, i.e.
"being importunate with importunity"; or as a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl [Translator's note: the source says «مصدرا مؤولا» (an interpreted maṣdar), though إلحافا is an explicit maṣdar], i.e. "they do not ask while being importunate"; or as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, having fulfilled its conditions. (وَما تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ): its i'rab has preceded shortly before. (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ): the fāʾ links; (إن) and its noun, and the clause [Translator's note: thus in the source; the khabar here is the single word عليم] is its khabar; and the clause is nominal, in the position of the jussive as apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) [Translator's note: the source has the misprint «جوان» for «جواب»]; (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar «عليم». (الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوالَهُمْ بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهارِ سِرًّا وَعَلانِيَةً) is a resumptive clause brought to begin setting out the manner and time of charity. The verse's having been revealed concerning Abū Bakr or ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib does not strip it of the comprehensiveness and generality of the ruling. (الذين) is the mubtadaʾ; (ينفقون) is an imperfect verb and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; the wāw is the agent; (أموالهم) is the direct object; (بالليل) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (تنفقون) [Translator's note: thus in the source, for ينفقون]; (النهار) is conjoined to (الليل); and (سرا) and (علانية) are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) in the accusative as ḥāls, or by removal of the preposition. (فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ): the fāʾ links, to indicate that what precedes it is the cause of what follows it, and because the relative noun has a scent of the conditional; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (أجرهم) is the postponed mubtadaʾ; the adverb (عند) is attached to an omitted ḥāl; (ربهم) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause is the khabar of the relative noun «الذين». (وَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ): its i'rab, letter for letter, has preceded many times.

* Rhetoric:
In His words, the Exalted, «لا يسألون الناس إلحافا» there is one of the most wonderful rhetorical devices, which they call «negating a thing by affirming it» (nafy al-shayʾ bi-ījābih). Its definition is that the poet or writer affirms something in the outward sense of his words and then negates what pertains to its cause. It is frequent in the Noble Qur'an. In this verse, what is negated in the outward sense of the words is importunity in asking, not asking itself — figuratively; and what is negated in the inner sense of the words, in reality, is asking itself, whether importunate or not. This is what praise requires. As you see, it is among the delightful points of the science of eloquence. Among the brilliant examples is the saying of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib describing the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his gatherings:
«لا تثنى فلتاته», i.e. his slips are not spread abroad. The outward sense of this wording is that there were slips, except that they were not spread. But that is not what is meant; what is meant is that the Prophet had no slips to be spread. This is among the strangest things in which our Arabic language has extended itself. Ibn al-Athīr claimed in his book «al-Mathal al-Sāʾir» that it is rare in poetry, and that only one verse of it was heard, by Imruʾ al-Qays, namely his saying:
على لاحب لا يهتدي بمناره ... إذا ساقه العود الدّيافيّ جرجرا
(Along a clear-worn track whose waymarks give no guidance; when an old Dayāfī camel is driven along it, it groans.)
His saying «لا يهتدي بمنارة» [Translator's note: thus in the source, for بمناره] gives the impression that it has waymarks, except that no guidance is had by them. But that is not what is meant; rather, what is meant is that it has no waymark by which guidance might be had. Ibn al-Athīr forgot the saying of Muslim ibn al-Walīd, nicknamed Ṣarīʿ al-Ghawānī:
تراه في الأمن في درع مضاعفة ... لا يأمن الدهر أن يدعى على عجل
لا يعبق الطيب خديه ومفرقه ... ولا يمسح عينيه من الكحل
(You see him, even in safety, in double-woven mail, never secure from being summoned in haste; perfume does not cling to his cheeks and the parting of his hair, nor does he wipe his eyes of kohl.)
The outward sense of the words negates the clinging of perfume and the wiping of kohl, whereas what is meant is negating perfume and kohl altogether, because of his absorption in leading armies, guarding the frontiers and keeping watch on the battle lines.
2- The verse also contains the device of correspondence (al-muqābala), for antithesis (ṭibāq) is repeated between night and day and between secret and open.

dervis-irab:113-113.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقالَتِ الْيَهُودُ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to show one of the states of ignorance rooted in their souls. It is narrated that when the delegation of Najrān came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the rabbis of the Jews came to them, and they debated until their voices were raised and each party declared the other astray. (لَيْسَتِ النَّصارى عَلى شَيْءٍ): «ليس» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; its pattern is «فعل» with kasra on the second radical, which is a rare form among triliteral verbs whose second radical is yāʾ; «النصارى» is its noun and «على شيء» its khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (وَقالَتِ النَّصارى لَيْسَتِ الْيَهُودُ عَلى شَيْءٍ): conjoined to the first clause. (وَهُمْ): the wāw is circumstantial, and «هم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject). (يَتْلُونَ): an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is their khabar, and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (الْكِتابَ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (كَذلِكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "they said a saying like that"; you may also parse the preposition and its genitive noun as being in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (قالَ الَّذِينَ): a verb and its fāʿil. (لا يَعْلَمُونَ): «لا» is negating, «يعلمون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila (relative clause). (مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ): an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); the meaning is "like the saying of the Jews and the Christians". (فَاللَّهُ): the fāʾ is resumptive, and «الله» is a mubtadaʾ. (يَحْكُمُ): an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is "he", and the clause is the khabar of «الله». (بَيْنَهُمْ): an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يحكم». (يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ): the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (فِيما): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يحكم». (كانُوا): «كان» and its noun, and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. (فِيهِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يختلفون». (يَخْتَلِفُونَ): the verbal clause is the khabar of «كانوا».

dervis-irab:275-276.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الرِّبا) الإرباء is increase upon a thing. From it one says: أربى فلان على فلان, when he exceeded him. A hillock is called رابية only because of its increase in size and its overlooking the level ground around it.
(الْمَسِّ): madness.

* I'rab:
(الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ الرِّبا) is a resumptive statement brought to mention the ruling on usury (ribā), which is increase in dealings with money. (الذين) is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (يأكلون الربا) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (لا يَقُومُونَ إِلَّا كَما يَقُومُ الَّذِي يَتَخَبَّطُهُ الشَّيْطانُ مِنَ الْمَسِّ): (لا) is negating; (يقومون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative, its sign being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and the verbal clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of (الذين). (إلا) is an instrument of restriction. (كما يقوم): the kāf is a preposition and (ما) is maṣdariyya; together with what it governs it is to be interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause (يقوم) has no grammatical position because it occurs after a particle-relative (mawṣūl ḥarfī); (الذي) is the agent; the clause (يتخبطه الشيطان) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; and (من المس) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يقومون), i.e. "they do not rise, on account of the touch, except as the epileptic rises". You may instead attach it to (يقوم), i.e. "as the epileptic rises from his madness".
