Abū Ḥayyān chose to attach it to (يتخبطه), by way of emphasis and to remove the figurative sense that «يتخبطه» could bear; this is admissible, but what we chose is better. (ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ قالُوا): the demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the punishment that befalls them; the bāʾ is a preposition; (أن), its noun and its khabar are to be interpreted as a maṣdar in the genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of «ذلك», i.e. "because of their saying"; the demonstrative clause is resumptive; (قالوا) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the agent. (إِنَّمَا الْبَيْعُ مِثْلُ الرِّبا): (إنما) is the restraining (kāffa) and restrained particle, made inoperative; (البيع) is the mubtadaʾ; (مثل) is the khabar of (البيع); (الربا) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), its sign of the genitive being the implied (muqaddar) kasra; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). (وَأَحَلَّ اللَّهُ الْبَيْعَ وَحَرَّمَ الرِّبا): the wāw is circumstantial, with «قد» implied after it. This indicates that analogy (qiyās) is demolished by the text, because it may be unsound, and there is no analogy more unsound than theirs for making lawful what Allah has forbidden. (أحل) is a past verb; (الله) is its agent; (البيع) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (حرم الربا) is conjoined; and the clause after the wāw is circumstantial. (فَمَنْ جاءَهُ مَوْعِظَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ): the fāʾ is resumptive; (من) is a jussive conditional noun, the mubtadaʾ; (جاءه) is a verb and direct object, in the position of the jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (موعظة) is the agent; and (من ربه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of (موعظة). (فَانْتَهى): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (انتهى) is conjoined to (جاءه), its agent being "he". (فَلَهُ ما سَلَفَ): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (ما) is a relative noun, the postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause (سلف) is the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَأَمْرُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ): the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial; (أمره) is the mubtadaʾ; and (إلى الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar. The clause (فله ما سلف) is in the position of the jussive as apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of (من). (وَمَنْ عادَ فَأُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ):
the wāw is a conjunction; (من) is a jussive conditional noun, the mubtadaʾ; (عاد) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as protasis; the fāʾ links; the demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ and (أصحاب النار) the khabar; the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as apodosis; and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of (من). (هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ): (هم) is the mubtadaʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (خالدون); (خالدون) is the khabar of «هم»; and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (يَمْحَقُ اللَّهُ الرِّبا): the clause is resumptive, brought to set out the fate of usury; (يمحق) is an imperfect verb; (الله) is its agent; and (الربا) its object. (وَيُرْبِي الصَّدَقاتِ) is conjoined to (يمحق الله الربا). (وَاللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ أَثِيمٍ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ; the clause (لا يحب) is the khabar; (كل) is the direct object; (كفار) is muḍāf ilayhi; and (أثيم) is an adjective of (كفار).

* Rhetoric:
1- Representational simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī), in likening those who consume usury, when they come out of their graves, to one struck by madness, whose nature is disordered and whose condition is overturned, who staggers in his walk and stumbles in his step, and sways like a drunken drinker, then falls headlong on his face — from ill fortune, the ugliness of the return and the hideousness of the fate; and recompense, customarily and rationally, is of the same kind as the deed.
2- Reversed simile (al-tashbīh al-maqlūb): in their saying «إنما البيع مثل الربا», whereas they mean to say that usury is like sale, so as to reach their aim, which is to make lawful what Allah has forbidden. So they reversed the statement for hyperbole. In eloquence this is a high rank, in which the thing likened-to comes to depend on the thing likened [Translator's note: the source has the misprint «بالمشيّه» for «بالمشبّه»] and to follow it. Of it in poetry is the saying of al-Buḥturī describing a pool built by al-Mutawakkil ʿalā Allāh:
كأنّها حين لجّت في تدفّقها ... يد الخليفة لمّا سال واديها
(As if, when it surged in its outpouring, it were the hand of the Caliph when its valley flowed.) The original is to liken the Caliph's hand to the pool, but he reversed the statement for hyperbole.
And the saying of another:
وبدا الصباح كأن غرته ... وجه الخليفة حين يمتدح
(And the morning appeared as if its blaze were the face of the Caliph when he is praised.)

dervis-irab:114-115.t:
* Vocabulary:
(المساجد): plural of «مسجد», a noun of place for prostration. By right it should have come on the pattern «مفعل» with fatḥa on the second radical, because the second radical of its imperfect has ḍamma; but it was heard with kasra irregularly, just as [other] words came irregularly with kasra although they are formed from verbs whose imperfect has ḍamma on the second radical: «المطلع», «المغرب», «المشرق», «المسجد», «المنسك», «المجزر», «المنبت», «المسقط», «المفرق» and «المسكن». Fatḥa is permissible in them, but what is heard [from the Arabs] is more eloquent.

* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ): the wāw is resumptive, and «من» is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); its meaning is negation. (أَظْلَمُ): khabar (predicate) of «من». (مِمَّنْ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أظلم». (مَنَعَ مَساجِدَ اللَّهِ): a past verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) referring to «من»; «مساجد الله» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (أَنْ يُذْكَرَ): «أن» and what falls within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), the second object of «منع»; you may also parse the maṣdar as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. out of dislike that His name be mentioned in them. (فِيهَا): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يذكر». (اسْمُهُ): nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). You may also parse the maṣdar as a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from «مساجد الله», because they contain the remembrance. (وَسَعى): conjoined to «منع». (فِي خَرابِها): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «سعى». (أُولئِكَ): a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ, and the clause is resumptive. (ما): negating. (كانَ): a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. (لَهُمْ): the fronted khabar of «كان». (أَنْ يَدْخُلُوها): the interpreted maṣdar formed from «أن» and what falls within its scope is the deferred noun of «كان». (إِلَّا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (خائِفِينَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of «يدخلوها». (لَهُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are a fronted khabar. (فِي الدُّنْيا): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (خِزْيٌ): a deferred mubtadaʾ, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive. (وَلَهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; «لهم» is a fronted khabar. (فِي الْآخِرَةِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (عَذابٌ): a deferred mubtadaʾ. (عَظِيمٌ): naʿt (adjective) of «عذاب». (وَلِلَّهِ): the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun are a fronted khabar. (الْمَشْرِقُ): a deferred mubtadaʾ. (وَالْمَغْرِبُ): conjoined to «المشرق». (فَأَيْنَما): the fāʾ is resumptive, and «أينما» is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, attached to what follows it. (تُوَلُّوا): the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (فَثَمَّ): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and «ثم» is an adverb of place attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (وَجْهُ اللَّهِ): a deferred mubtadaʾ, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ واسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ): «إن», its noun and its two khabars.

* Benefits:
(ثم): with fatḥa on the tāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the letter is thāʾ], and for the feminine one says «ثمة»; it points to a distant place, and the two are only put in the genitive by «من» and «إلى».

dervis-irab:116-117.t:
* Vocabulary:
(اتَّخَذَ): one of the verbs of transformation (afʿāl al-taḥwīl) which put two objects in the accusative; its sisters are «تخذ», «صير», «ردّ», «ترك», «جعل» and «هب». A curious battle has been stirred up around «اتخذ». Ibn Hishām corrected al-Jawharī, author of al-Ṣiḥāḥ, saying: "Al-Jawharī's statement about «اتّخذ», that it is iftaʿala from «الأخذ», is a mistake; rather the tāʾ is a root letter, and it is from «تخذ», like «اتبع» from «تبع»." Ibn Hishām relies, in faulting al-Jawharī, on the fact that if it were from «أخذ», one would have to say «ايتخذ», because the rule in that is that you say, for iftaʿala from «الإزار», «ايتزر», changing the hamza into a yāʾ, and it is not permissible to change this yāʾ into a tāʾ and assimilate it into the [following] tāʾ, because this yāʾ is a substitute for a hamza and is not original. Others corrected Ibn Hishām, saying: venturing to declare al-Jawharī mistaken is no light matter; it may be that this was a view (madhhab) of his. And it is not to be said that al-Jawharī is not one of those who hold their own views, especially as the apparent [form] supports him. So what al-Jawharī said is one view, and the second view is what Ibn Hishām mentioned.

* I'rab:
(وَقالُوا): the wāw is a conjunction, and «قالوا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent). (اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَداً): a verb, its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (سُبْحانَهُ): mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, and the clause is parenthetical, for declaring [Allah] transcendent. (بَلْ): a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb). (لَهُ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). (ما): a relative noun, a deferred mubtadaʾ (subject). (فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (كُلٌّ): a mubtadaʾ; beginning with it was permissible because of the sense of generality in it, and the tanwīn on «كل» is a substitute for a word, i.e. "every individual among the created things". (لَهُ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «قانتون», i.e. submissive and compliant. In [the statement of] ownership, the non-rational was given precedence, so He said «ما في السموات», because what is meant is their subjection to Him by the natural subjection, in which choice is not a condition — not the legal subjection, expressed as obligation (taklīf), which the acquirer does by his choice; in the natural subjection the rational and the non-rational are equal, though it is more evident in the non-rational. When He mentioned their devout submission (qunūt) to Him the Exalted, He put it in the sound masculine plural, giving precedence in it to rational beings, because qunūt is properly from the rational being who perceives its cause and does it by his choice — even though the non-rational has a qunūt befitting it. (قانِتُونَ): khabar of «كل». (بَدِيعُ السَّماواتِ): khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; it is a case of annexing the resembling adjective (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha) to its fāʿil, the original being "whose heavens are originated" (بديع سمواته). (وَالْأَرْضِ): conjoined to «السموات». (وَإِذا): an adverb for future time, putting its protasis in the genitive [by annexation] and made accusative by its apodosis. (قَضى أَمْراً): the clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (فَإِنَّما): the fāʾ is linking, and «إنما» is a restraining particle (kāffa). (يَقُولُ لَهُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يقول», and the clause has no grammatical position. (كُنْ): an imperative verb from the complete (tāmma) «كان», meaning "to come about". (فَيَكُونُ): the fāʾ is resumptive, and «يكون» is a complete imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), i.e. "so it comes about"; the clause «كن» is the object of speech.

* Rhetoric:
(The rational trope, al-majāz al-ʿaqlī): attributing the verb, or what has its meaning, to something other than what it belongs to, because of a relationship, with an indicator (qarīna) preventing [the literal] attribution; it is perceived by the intellect. Among its splendid examples in poetry is the saying of al-Mutanabbī:
كلّما أثبت الزمان قناة ... ركب المرء في القناة سنانا
(Whenever time sets up a spear-shaft, man fixes a spearhead on the shaft.)
It may be confused with metaphor (al-istiʿāra); the difference between them is the intention of simile or its absence, as is established in the books of rhetoric.

dervis-irab:277-279.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) is a resumptive statement brought to set out the state of the believers who act [righteously]: (إن) and its noun; and the clause (آمنوا) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ وَأَقامُوا الصَّلاةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكاةَ):
the three clauses are conjoined to the ṣila and fall within its scope. (لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (أجرهم) is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and the nominal clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar of (إن). (وَلا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ): its i'rab, letter for letter, has preceded. (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has also preceded. (اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ): an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; and the clause is resumptive. (وَذَرُوا ما بَقِيَ مِنَ الرِّبا): the wāw is a conjunction; (ذروا) is an imperative verb; the wāw is the agent; (ما) is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (بقي) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (بقي), or to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of (بقي). (إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is a deficient past verb in the position of the jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is its noun and (مؤمنين) its khabar; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "then leave it"; and the clause is resumptive. (فَإِنْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا): the fāʾ is resumptive; (إن) is conditional; (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; and (تفعلوا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لم), and it is the protasis. (فَأْذَنُوا بِحَرْبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ): the fāʾ links the apodosis; (أذنوا) is an imperative verb and its agent; the preposition and its genitive noun (بحرب) are attached to (أذنوا); (من الله) is attached to an omitted adjective of (حرب); (رسوله) is conjoined to (الله); and the clause is in the position of the jussive as apodosis. (وَإِنْ تُبْتُمْ فَلَكُمْ رُؤُسُ أَمْوالِكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (تبتم) is a past verb and its agent, in the position of the jussive as protasis; the fāʾ links the apodosis; (لكم) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (رؤوس أموالكم) is the postponed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is in the position of the jussive as apodosis.
(لا تَظْلِمُونَ وَلا تُظْلَمُونَ): the clause (لا تظلمون) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and it is in the active voice; and the clause (ولا تظلمون) is conjoined to it, and it is in the passive voice.

dervis-irab:280-281.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نظرة), with kasra on the ẓāʾ: a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning postponement.
(مَيْسَرَةٍ): a mīmī maṣdar meaning ease and plenty, or a noun of time, i.e. the time of ease.

* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ كانَ ذُو عُسْرَةٍ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, to establish the obligation of granting respite and delay to the insolvent debtor. In that lies the welfare of the servants and the bringing together of hearts. (إن) is conditional; (كان) is a complete past verb meaning "occurred" and "existed", and it suffices with its fāʿil (agent) like all other verbs, i.e. "and if someone in hardship occurs"; (ذو) is its agent, its sign of the nominative being the wāw because it is one of the five nouns; and (عسرة) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (فَنَظِرَةٌ إِلى مَيْسَرَةٍ): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (نظرة) is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then the ruling is postponement"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) (نظرة), or to an omitted adjective of it; and the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as apodosis. (وَأَنْ تَصَدَّقُوا خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ): the wāw is resumptive; (أن) and what is in its scope are an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (خير) is the khabar; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (خير), because it is an elative noun (ism tafḍīl) formed irregularly. (إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ): (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is a deficient past verb; the tāʾ is its noun; the clause (تعلمون) is in the position of the nominative as its khabar; the apodosis is omitted; and the conditional clause is resumptive. (وَاتَّقُوا يَوْماً تُرْجَعُونَ فِيهِ إِلَى اللَّهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (اتقوا) is an imperative verb; the wāw is the agent; (يوما) is the object; (ترجعون) is a passive imperfect verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of (يوما); (فيه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and (إلى الله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (ترجعون). (ثُمَّ تُوَفَّى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ما كَسَبَتْ): (ثم) is a conjunction expressing sequence with delay; (توفى) is a passive imperfect verb; (كل نفس) is the deputy agent; (ما) is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause (كسبت) has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila (relative clause). (وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial; (هم) is the mubtadaʾ; the clause (لا يظلمون) is in the position of the nominative as khabar; and the clause (وهم لا يظلمون) is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.

* Benefits:
(كان) has particular features which its sisters share with it, and features it has alone.
These are taken from the books of grammar. Here it is particular in being complete (tāmma), and its sisters share this with it, except for three verbs that are always deficient: (ما فتئ), (ما زال) and (ليس). Among its important questions regarding completeness is the well-known example «كائنا ما كان» ("whatever it may be"). We use it often in our writing, so we see fit to give its i'rab to make things easy for students. The grammarians differed over its i'rab. Al-Fārisī said: both are complete in both places, and (ما) is maṣdariyya; it and what follows it are an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the nominative as the agent of (كائنا), i.e. "its being". It was also said: both are deficient in both places; in «كائنا» there is a pronoun that is its noun, and the khabar is the relative (ما); the clause (كان) is the ṣila of (ما); the noun of (كان) is a pronoun latent (mustatir) in it; and its khabar is omitted, its implied form being إياه. The latent noun of «كائنا» and the khabar of (كان) both refer back to the person struck in your saying:
لأضربنه كائنا الذي كان إياه ("I shall surely strike him, being whatever he was"), and (كائنا) is a ḥāl from the object of (لأضربنه).

dervis-irab:170-170.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا): the wāw is resumptive, and إذا is an adverb of future time attached to (mutaʿalliq) قالوا. (قِيلَ): a passive past verb; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), implied as "it" (هو); the clause is resumptive, brought to show how firmly rooted they are in error and how far they go in misguidance. (لَهُمُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to قيل. (اتَّبِعُوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (ما): a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. (قالُوا): a verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition. (بَلْ): a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction. Every iḍrāb in the Qur'an is intended as a transition from one story to another, except in this verse and in another verse that will come. (نَتَّبِعُ): an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is "we" (نحن); the clause is conjoined to an implied clause, i.e. "we do not follow what Allah has sent down; rather we follow". (ما): a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. (أَلْفَيْنا): a verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila. (عَلَيْهِ): a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of accusative as the second object of ألفينا. (آباءَنا): the first object of ألفينا. The meaning of ألفينا is "we found". (أَوَلَوْ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (istifhām inkārī), and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); the clause is circumstantial, brought to censure their following their fathers in every state, even in the state in which there is no room for a rational person to follow them and incline toward them, namely their not being clothed with the absence of reason and the lack of guidance [Translator's note: so in the source, «عدم تلبسهم بعدم العقول»; the sense intended is evidently "their being clothed with the absence of reason"]. لو is conditional and does not need an apodosis in a construction like this, because its purpose is to generalise the states; for that reason it is not permissible to omit the wāw that enters upon it, to draw attention to the fact that what follows it is not in keeping with what precedes it. (كانَ آباؤُهُمْ): كان and its noun. (لا): negative. (يَعْقِلُونَ): an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the negated clause is the khabar (predicate) of كان. (شَيْئاً): mafʿūl bihi or mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (وَلا يَهْتَدُونَ): the clause is conjoined to the clause لا يعقلون.

* Rhetoric:
Iltifāt (shift of person) in His saying: لهم…, from second person to third person, to record publicly the proclamation of their misguidance; for there is none more astray than the blind imitator, who follows another in places that ruin and destroy him, and is led along without thought or deliberation.

dervis-irab:171-171.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَنْعِقُ) النّعيق: crying out in general. Al-Akhṭal said:
فانعق بضأنك يا جرير فإنّما ... منّتك أمّك في الخلاء ضلالا
(So shout at your sheep, O Jarīr, for your mother only filled you with vain hopes in the wilderness.)
One says: نعق المؤذن (the muezzin called out), and: I heard the call (نعقة) of the muezzin. As for the sound of the crow, it is النغيق, with the dotted ghayn.

* I'rab:
(وَمَثَلُ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to strike a parable for the disbelievers in their worship of idols. This verse has occupied the grammarians and the exegetes, who differed over it greatly; the views they presented amount to four [Translator's note: so in the source; three views are listed under Rhetoric below], of which we choose one, and we set out their details under Rhetoric, because they are almost equally weighty. مثل is a mubtadaʾ (subject). (الَّذِينَ): muḍāf ilayhi. (كَفَرُوا): a verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). A muḍāf must be implied before the relative noun, i.e. "the likeness of the one who calls them to faith", i.e. "the likeness of the caller of those who disbelieved", meaning that whoever tries to guide them is like one who addresses what does not hear, and even if it hears, it understands nothing of what it hears. (كَمَثَلِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate). (الَّذِي): a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi. (يَنْعِقُ): an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is "he" (هو); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila. (بِما): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ينعق. (لا يَسْمَعُ): لا is negative and يسمع an imperfect verb; the verbal clause is the ṣila of ما. (إِلَّا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (دُعاءً): mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَنِداءً): conjoined to دعاء. (صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ): three khabars of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they". (فَهُمْ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and هم is a mubtadaʾ. (لا يَعْقِلُونَ): the negated verbal clause is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there are many devices, among them:
1- The representative simile (al-tashbīh al-tamthīlī): He likened the one who calls the disbelievers to faith, despite their persistence and obstinacy, to one who shouts at beasts that hear nothing but the call and the scolding; it is a simile of an image with an image, or of a multiple with a multiple. The views presented by the scholars of rhetoric and grammar can be summed up as follows:
a- that the parable is struck to liken the caller and the disbeliever to the shouter and the one shouted at;
b- that the parable is struck to liken the disbeliever, when the Messenger ﷺ calls him, to the sheep that are shouted at;
c- that the parable is struck to liken the disbeliever, in his calling upon idols, to the one who shouts at sheep.
2- Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya) in likening the disbelievers to the deaf, the dumb and the blind, omitting the thing likened and keeping the thing it is likened to.
3- Concision (ījāz) in the omission of a muḍāf, implied as: the likeness of the caller of those who disbelieved. The caller — namely the Messenger — is not named explicitly, in keeping with the lofty etiquette of gentle address, and the refinement that should mark poets and writers.

dervis-irab:172-173.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الاهلال): it has been said before that it is raising the voice when undertaking some matter. In their Jāhiliyya it was their religion to raise their voices when undertaking such things as slaughter and the like, saying: "In the name of al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā."
(باغٍ): a wrongdoer.
(عادٍ): one who transgresses against others.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has been given before, so refresh your acquaintance with it. The vocative clause and what follows it is resumptive, as a preface to beginning the explanation of kinds of forbidden things, after He, Glorified be He, commanded the eating of good things. (كُلُوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (مِنْ طَيِّباتِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of the omitted object, so that the hearer may imply it in whatever way his soul yearns for. The meaning of the preposition من here is partitive (tabʿīḍ), i.e. eat some of them — and how many are the good things available to us! (ما): a relative noun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (رَزَقْناكُمْ): a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). (وَاشْكُرُوا لِلَّهِ): conjoined to كلوا; لله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اشكروا, and a discussion of it will follow under Benefits. (إِنْ): a conditional particle that puts two verbs in the jussive. (كُنْتُمْ): a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is its noun. (إِيَّاهُ): a detached pronoun, a fronted object of تعبدون. (تَعْبُدُونَ): the verbal clause is in the position of accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كنتم. The clause of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then give thanks". (إِنَّما): a restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa). (حَرَّمَ): a past verb; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), implied as "He" (هو), referring to Allah the Exalted. (عَلَيْكُمُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to حرم. (الْمَيْتَةَ): mafʿūl bihi. (وَالدَّمَ وَلَحْمَ الْخِنْزِيرِ): both conjoined to الميتة. (وَما): the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is a relative noun, accusative by conjunction with what precedes. (أُهِلَّ): a passive past verb. (بِهِ): a preposition and its genitive noun standing in place of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is the ṣila. (فَمَنِ): the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), i.e. "if there are states of necessity that compelled him to eat something of what is forbidden"; the clause after it has no grammatical position because it is the answer of an implied, non-jussive condition. من is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). (اضْطُرَّ): a passive past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; the nāʾib fāʿil is latent, implied as "he", referring to the one compelled. (غَيْرَ): a ḥāl of «من», as if it were said: "he was compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing, so it is lawful for him". (باغٍ): muḍāf ilayhi; the sign of its genitive is the kasra implied on the yāʾ, which is deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. (وَلا عادٍ): conjoined to غير باغ. (فَلا): the fāʾ links the apodosis because it is a nominal clause, and لا is the lā of generic negation. (إِثْمَ): its noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa. (عَلَيْهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to its omitted khabar; the clause joined to the fāʾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من, according to the soundest view. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ): إن and its noun. (غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): two khabars of إن; the clause of إن and what falls within its scope has no grammatical position because it is causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Rhetoric:
1- These two verses contain two beautiful concisions by omission (ījāz bi-l-ḥadhf): the omission of the object of كلوا, as stated above, and the omission of the apodosis of the conditional إن, i.e. "then thank Him"; omission of the apodosis is common in the speech of the Arabs.
2- Fronting (taqdīm), in placing إياه first, to convey exclusivity (ikhtiṣāṣ), because He, Glorified be He, is exclusively the one they should worship.
3- Iltifāt (shift of person) from the first person to the third person: the context of the speech required Him to say "and thank Us", but He shifted to the third person because of the great importance of attention to Him, Glorified be He. In it there is an allusion to the Prophetic ḥadīth: «Allah the Exalted says: I, the jinn and mankind are in a momentous affair: I create and another is worshipped; I provide and another is thanked.» The scholars of rhetoric have been accustomed to define iltifāt as something used in speech only for variety and moving from one style to another, to refresh the hearer's alertness. This is a fine definition, because the soul tires of speech that runs on a monotonous pattern. But an objection to this definition is that refreshing comes only after weariness has occurred, and there is no weariness in reciting the Qur'an; so there must be something beyond the transition from one style to another. However, that cannot be defined, because art is beauty, and the secret of beauty lies in its being undefinable, since it is hard to attain. We have shown you, in the discussion of al-Fātiḥa, secrets lying behind the lines. Here He turned from the first person to the third, as stated above, and in order to state the name of Allah explicitly — and in that there are incentives to gratitude that need no description.

A poetic example:
Since we are dealing with the secrets of iltifāt, it is fitting for us to present to the reader a poetic example by Abū Tammām al-Ṭāʾī, so that our students and those cultivating letters may measure by its pattern. He said it in praise of Abū Dulaf al-ʿIjlī, describing in it a band of riders travelling through remote wastes, so as to make his transition to extolling the generosity of the one praised; do not miss what it contains of personification and embodiment:
وركب يساقون الركاب زجاجة ... من السّير لم تقصد لها كفّ قاطب
ففد أكلوا منها الغوارب بالسّرى ... وصارت لهم أشباحهم كالغوارب
يصرّف مسراها جذيل مشارق ... إذا آبه هم عذيق مغارب
يرى بالكعاب الزّود طلعة ثائر ... وبالعرمس الوجناء غرةّ آئب
كأنّ بها ضغنا على كلّ جانب ... من الأرض أو شوقا إلى كلّ جانب
إذا العيس لاقت بي أبا دلف فقد ... تقطّع ما بيني وبين النوائب
(A band of riders who pour out for their mounts a cup of travel that no mixer's hand has diluted; by night-journeys they have worn away the camels' humps, and their own bodies have become like humps; their night-travel is steered by an expert of the east, who, when care returns to him, is an expert of the west; he sees in the full-breasted [she-camel] the face of an avenger, and in the hard, strong-cheeked she-camel the brow of one returning home; as if she bore a grudge against every quarter of the earth, or a longing for every quarter. When the camels bring me to Abū Dulaf, then all that is between me and misfortunes is cut off.) [Translator's note: «ففد» in the second line is so in the source, evidently for «فقد».]
In the first [line cited] he said: يصرف مسراها, addressing the absent, following the preceding style in describing the riders; then after that he said: إذا العيس لاقت بي, turning to address himself, because when he came to speaking face to face with the one praised and mentioning his name explicitly, he then addressed himself, giving himself the glad tidings of distance from hardships and nearness to what is desired. This is lawful magic, and indeed some eloquence is magic.

* Benefits:
(شكر) is a transitive verb, but it may be used like an intransitive verb, contenting itself with the fāʿil, when only the occurrence of the act is meant. It is used as directly transitive to a single mafʿūl bihi; Allah the Exalted said: «ربّ أوزعني أن أشكر نعمتك». It takes two objects, as in the saying of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr:
سأشكر عمرا ما تراخت منيتي ... أيادي لم تمنن وإن هي جلت
(I shall thank ʿAmr, as long as my death is delayed, for favours not held over me as a reproach, great though they were.)
The two objects are عمرا and أيادي, the plural of يد, which is a favour. It may also be made transitive with the lām to a single mafʿūl bihi, as in the verse here.

dervis-irab:118-119.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقالَ الَّذِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): the wāw is resumptive, «قال» is a past verb, «الذين» is its fāʿil (agent), and the clause «لا يعلمون» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (لَوْلا يُكَلِّمُنَا اللَّهُ): «لولا» is a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ) meaning «هلّا»; «يكلمنا الله» is a verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the fāʿil. (أَوْ): a conjunction. (تَأْتِينا): conjoined to «يكلمنا». (آيَةٌ): fāʿil. (كَذلِكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), or a ḥāl (circumstantial); its discussion has preceded. (قالَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): a verb and its fāʿil, and «من قبلهم» is the ṣila of the relative noun. (مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِمْ): badal (substitute) from «كذلك». (تَشابَهَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ): a verb and its fāʿil. (قَدْ): a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). (بَيَّنَّا الْآياتِ): a verb and its fāʿil, and «الآيات» is mafʿūl bihi, the sign of its accusative being the kasra. (لِقَوْمٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بينا». (يُوقِنُونَ): the clause is an adjective of «قوم». (إِنَّا): «إن» and its noun. (أَرْسَلْناكَ): a verb, its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi. (بِالْحَقِّ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, "clothed with it and accompanied by it"; the clause «أرسلناك» is its [«إن»'s] khabar (predicate). (بَشِيراً): also a ḥāl. (وَنَذِيراً): conjoined to «بشيرا». (وَلا تُسْئَلُ): the wāw is resumptive according to the most likely view, «لا» is negating, and «تسأل» is a passive imperfect verb whose nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a pronoun obligatorily latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you". (عَنْ أَصْحابِ الْجَحِيمِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «تسأل».

dervis-irab:120-121.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَنْ): the wāw is resumptive, and «لن» is a particle of negation, the accusative and the future. (تَرْضى): an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by «لن». (عَنْكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ترضى». (الْيَهُودُ): fāʿil (agent). (وَلَا النَّصارى): conjoined to «اليهود». (حَتَّى): a particle of limit and of the genitive. (تَتَّبِعَ): an imperfect verb, accusative by «أن» obligatorily implied after «حتى». (مِلَّتَهُمْ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "you". (قُلْ): an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the clause is resumptive. (إِنَّ): a particle resembling the verb. (هُدَى اللَّهِ): its noun, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (هُوَ): mubtadaʾ (subject). (الْهُدى): its khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is the khabar of «إن». (وَلَئِنِ): the wāw is resumptive, the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam), and «إن» is a jussive conditional particle. (اتَّبَعْتَ): a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is the fāʿil. (أَهْواءَهُمْ): mafʿūl bihi; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer to the oath. (بَعْدَ): an adverb. (الَّذِي): a relative noun in the position of the genitive by annexation; the adverb is attached to «اتبعت»; and the clause (جاءَكَ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and «من العلم» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (ما لَكَ): «ما» is negating, and «لك» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (مِنَ اللَّهِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «ولي». (مِنْ وَلِيٍّ): «من» is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and «ولي» is genitive in form and nominative in position because it is a deferred mubtadaʾ. (وَلا نَصِيرٍ): conjoined to «ولي». (الَّذِينَ): a relative noun, mubtadaʾ. (آتَيْناهُمُ الْكِتابَ): a verb, its fāʿil and the two objects of «آتينا»; the clause «آتيناهم» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (يَتْلُونَهُ): an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of «الذين». (حَقَّ تِلاوَتِهِ): mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (أُولئِكَ): a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. (يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ): the clause is the khabar of «أولئك», and the clause «أولئك يؤمنون به» is a khabar after a khabar. (وَمَنْ): the wāw is a conjunction, and «من» is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ. (يَكْفُرْ): the protasis. (بِهِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يكفر». (فَأُولئِكَ): the fāʾ is linking, and the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ. (هُمُ): a second mubtadaʾ. (الْخاسِرُونَ): khabar of «هم», and the nominal clause is the khabar of «أولئك». It is also possible that «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), or a "support" (ʿimād), with no grammatical position.

* Benefits:
When a condition and an oath come together, the answer of the one that comes first suffices for the answer of the later one, because of the greater attention paid to the one that comes first — unless a mubtadaʾ precedes them both, in which case the side of the condition prevails.

dervis-irab:122-123.t:
* I'rab:
(يا بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ): «يا» is a vocative particle for one at a middle distance; «بني» is the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf), and «إسرائيل» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the i'rab of its parallel has preceded. (اذْكُرُوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (نِعْمَتِيَ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive, brought to remind of the favours that Allah lavished on the Children of Israel and which they denied. (الَّتِي): a relative noun, adjective. (أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (وَأَنِّي): «أني» and what follows it are conjoined to «نعمتي», i.e. "and My preferring you over the peoples of your time". (فَضَّلْتُكُمْ): a verb, its fāʿil and its object, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of «أني». (عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «فضلتكم». (وَاتَّقُوا): the wāw is a conjunction, and «اتقوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (يَوْماً): mafʿūl bihi, with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "fear its punishment". (لا تَجْزِي): «لا» is negating, and «تجزي» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). (نَفْسٌ): fāʿil. (عَنْ نَفْسٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «تجزي». (شَيْئاً): mafʿūl bihi or mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and the verbal clause is an adjective of «يوما». (وَلا يُقْبَلُ مِنْها عَدْلٌ): conjoined to what preceded, and «عدل» is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (وَلا تَنْفَعُها شَفاعَةٌ): also conjoined. (وَلا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ): also conjoined; «هم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the clause «ينصرون» is its khabar, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil.

dervis-irab:124-124.t:
* Vocabulary:
(إِبْراهِيمَ): its meaning in Syriac is "merciful father".

* I'rab:
(وَإِذِ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought for taking example from what happened to those of the past, which points to the Oneness [of Allah] and restrains from associating partners. «إذا» [Translator's note: so in the source; the word is «إذ»] is an adverb for past time, in the position of the accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "remember". (ابْتَلى): a past verb. (إِبْراهِيمَ): a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (رَبُّهُ): a deferred fāʿil (agent); the clause «ابتلى» is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (بِكَلِماتٍ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ابتلى». (فَأَتَمَّهُنَّ): conjoined to «ابتلى». The meaning of completing them is performing them in the best manner, without neglect or slackness; what is meant by the words is the commands and prohibitions revealed to him. (قالَ): a past verb whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he"; the clause is explicative, with no grammatical position. (إِنِّي): «إن» and its noun. (جاعِلُكَ): its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (لِلنَّاسِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «جاعلك»; you may also attach it to an omitted [word] in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was originally an adjective of «إماما». (إِماماً): the second object of «جاعلك»; as for the second object, it is the kāf, because it is a case of annexing the active participle to its object. [Translator's note: so in the source; the kāf is evidently meant to be the first object.] (قالَ): a past verb whose fāʿil is "he". (وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِي): the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun are conjoined to the kāf, as though he said "and making some of my offspring", as when it is said to you "I will honour you" and you say "and my brother". This is how many have parsed it, but there is some reservation about it; the better view in our opinion is that the two are attached to an omitted [verb], the implied form being "and make of my offspring an imam". (قالَ: لا يَنالُ عَهْدِي الظَّالِمِينَ): «عهدي» is the fāʿil and «الظالمين» is mafʿūl bihi.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse is a curious art among their arts, called the art of exchange (fann al-murājaʿa): the speaker relates an exchange of words that took place between him and an interlocutor in conversation, or between two others, in the most concise expression, the most eloquent allusion and the most elegant dialogue, with sweetness and strength of wording and ease of composition. Look at this piece of speech, whose words number thirteen, how it has gathered the meanings of speech: statement and inquiry, command and prohibition, promise and threat. This is the detail:
1- Statement, in His saying «إني جاعلك», which is in reality a promise to make him a vicegerent over people.
b- Inquiry, included in the statement, because it is a branch of it, since a statement becomes an inquiry by placing at its head what indicates interrogation.
c- Command, in his saying «ومن ذريتي», for its meaning is asking for his offspring what was promised of vicegerency, as though he said: "My Lord, and do that for some of my offspring." Every request is a command, but when it is [addressed] to Allah, glorified is He, good manners require that it be called supplication (duʿāʾ) and that the word "command" not be applied to it, even though it is a command in its basic form. [Translator's note: the source reads «في أصل الوعد» ("in the basis of the promise"), probably for «في أصل الوضع» ("in its basic form"), which is how it is translated here.]
d- Prohibition, included in the command, because commanding a thing is prohibiting its opposite; so it is as if its meaning were "and do not deprive some of my offspring of that".
e- Promise, whose explanation has preceded under statement.
And threat, in His saying «لا ينال عهدي الظالمين», for its upshot is that the wrongdoers among your offspring will not attain My vicegerency, and being deprived of that is the utmost threat.
Among the poetic witnesses of this art is the saying of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa al-Makhzūmī:
بيننا ينعتني ابصرنني ... دون قيد الميل يعدو بي الأغر
(While [one of them] was describing me, they caught sight of me, less than a mile off, my white-blazed horse racing with me.)
قالت الكبرى: ترى من ذا الفتى؟ ... قالت الوسطى لها: هذا عمر
(The eldest said: "Who, do you think, is that young man?" The middle one said to her: "This is ʿUmar.")
قالت الصغرى وقد تيمتها ... قد عرفناه وهل يخفى القمر؟
(The youngest, whom I had enthralled, said: "We have recognised him — and can the moon be hidden?")
In these verses there are two eloquent subtleties that show the poet's strength of expression — he of "the shelled pistachio", as they call his poetry — and his knowledge of putting speech in its proper places. They are:
1- That the rhymes of the verses, if pronounced with their final vowels, would all be nominative.
2- That he made the one who recognised him among the girls, and identified him, and likened him with a likeness that shows her passionate love for him, the youngest of them, to indicate by implication (dalālat al-iltizām) that he was young in age, since a young woman generally inclines only to a young man; thereby he slips in his excuse of youthful passion, and that it only came from him in the days of youth.
3- And a third subtlety surpassing all that preceded lies in the closing statement (al-tadhyīl), which he cast in the form of a current proverb when he said, relating it from her: «وهل يخفى القمر». Let no one think that the youngest inclined to him because of her inexperience, the weakness of her mind and its shortfall in discernment, and her lack of experience. That is because he related of the eldest that she did not know him, yet he pleased her and she was smitten with love when she saw him, so that she could not restrain herself from asking about him; or that she did know him and only asked about him to cover up her state and conceal it, by way of feigned ignorance of the knower (tajāhul al-ʿārif), either to show excessive infatuation and bewilderment in love, or because she was waiting to be answered with his name so as to delight in hearing it. As for the middle one, she stated his name plainly, because her rank in soundness and sagacity of mind and in steadiness and purity of intellect is below that of the eldest; so when the eldest veiled herself by asking about him, as her intellect required, the middle one stated his name and his identity by lineage. And the youngest revealed what she felt for him by describing him with a description that shows the greatness of his place in her heart, because of her age relative to her two sisters. This is among the wonders heard on this subject. We do not wish to close the discussion of this art before adducing some witnesses. Among its witnesses is the saying of Dīk al-Jinn, whose name is ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Raghbān:
مرّت فقلت لها: تحية مغرم ... ماذا عليك من السلام؟ فسلمي
(She passed by, and I said to her: "A greeting from one in love — what harm is there in a greeting? So greet [me].")
قالت: بمن تعني؟ فطرفك شاهد ... بنحول جسم قلت: بالمتكلّم
(She said: "Whom do you mean? For your glance bears witness to a wasted body." I said: "The one speaking.")
فتضاحكت، فبكيت قالت: لا ترع ... فلربّ مثل هواك بالمتبسّم
(She laughed, and I wept. She said: "Do not be alarmed, for perhaps one who smiles has a love like yours.")
قلت: اتفقنا في الهوى فزيارة ... أو موعدا قبل الزيارة قدّمي
(I said: "We agree in love — so grant a visit, or a promise before the visit.")
فتبسمت خجلا وقالت: يا فتى ... لو لم أدعك تنام بي لم تحلم
(She smiled shyly and said: "Young man, had I not let you sleep [dreaming] of me, you would not have dreamed.")
And by al-Buḥturī, whose name is al-Walīd:
ونديم حلو الشمائل كالد ... ينار محض النّجار عذب المصفّى
(And a boon companion of sweet manners, like the dinar, of pure stock, sweet when refined,)
بتّ أسقيه صفوة الرّاح حتى ... وضع الكأس مائلا يتكفّا
(I spent the night pouring him the purest wine, until he set down the cup, swaying and tottering.)
قلت: عبد العزيز تفديك نفسي ... قال: لبيك قلت: لبيك ألفا هاكها قال: هاتها قلت: خذها ... قال: لا أستطيعها ثمّ أغفى
(I said: "ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, may my soul be your ransom!" He said: "At your service." I said: "At your service a thousand times — here it is." He said: "Give it." I said: "Take it." He said: "I cannot manage it" — and then he dozed off.)
And what has preceded suffices us.

dervis-irab:174-176.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ): إن and its noun; the clause is resumptive, brought to narrate the story of the leaders and rabbis of the Jews who used to receive gifts and food from their common people, and who used to hope that the awaited Prophet, described among them in the Torah, would be one of them. They feared the loss of the blessings that kept streaming in upon them, which would consequently lead to the end of their leadership, so they set about concealing his matter. (يَكْتُمُونَ): an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause). (ما): a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يكتمون. (أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ): a verb and its fāʿil; the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of ما. (مِنَ الْكِتابِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted pronoun referring back to the relative noun, its implied form being: what Allah sent down, in the state of its being from the Book. (وَيَشْتَرُونَ): the wāw is a conjunction, and يشترون is a clause conjoined to the clause أنزل الله. (بِهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يشترون. (ثَمَناً): mafʿūl bihi. (قَلِيلًا): naʿt (adjective). (أُولئِكَ): the demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject). (ما): negative. (يَأْكُلُونَ): an imperfect verb, nominative; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the demonstrative. (فِي بُطُونِهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يأكلون, because they [the bellies] are the receptacles of eating. (إِلَّا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (النَّارَ): mafʿūl bihi. The clause أولئك ما يأكلون is the khabar of إن. (وَلا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ): the wāw is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to the clause ما يأكلون. (يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ): the adverb is attached to يكلمهم. (وَلا يُزَكِّيهِمْ): the clause is conjoined to the clause لا يكلمهم الله. (وَلَهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted, fronted khabar. (عَذابٌ): the postponed mubtadaʾ. (أَلِيمٌ): naʿt. (أُولئِكَ): the demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. (الَّذِينَ): a relative noun, khabar. (اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلالَةَ بِالْهُدى): the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila; it has come before word for word. (وَالْعَذابَ بِالْمَغْفِرَةِ): conjoined to الضلالة بالهدى; what is given up is what the bāʾ enters upon. (فَما): the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the disclosing fāʾ), as if it disclosed their astonishing fate; ما is a complete indefinite (nakira tāmma) meaning "a thing", for wonder (taʿajjub), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ according to the soundest view. We said "according to the soundest view" only to ward off the views the grammarians have floundered about with, which yield nothing but artificiality. (أَصْبَرَهُمْ): a frozen (jāmid) past verb for expressing wonder; its fāʿil is a pronoun obligatorily latent (mustatir) here specifically, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar of ما. (عَلَى النَّارِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أصبرهم. (ذلِكَ): the demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. (بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ): the bāʾ is a preposition, and أن and what falls within its scope are in the position of genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition with its genitive is the khabar of the demonstrative. The meaning of the bāʾ is causation; and أن and its noun. (نَزَّلَ الْكِتابَ): a past verb with a latent fāʿil referring to Allah the Exalted, and الكتاب is mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar of أن, i.e. that punishment is because Allah sent down the Book. (بِالْحَقِّ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نزل, or to an omitted ḥāl. (وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial, and إن and its noun. (اخْتَلَفُوا): the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila. (فِي الْكِتابِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اختلفوا. (لَفِي شِقاقٍ): the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of إن. (بَعِيدٍ): naʿt.

* Rhetoric:
1- Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya) in buying misguidance for guidance; the verse has come before word for word.
2- Majāz mursal (non-metaphorical trope) in eating fire, the relation being causality: what is a cause of the Fire is made fire.
3- Allusion (taʿrīḍ): in Allah's not speaking to them, [alluding] to their being deprived of the state of the people of Paradise and of their being purified by His speech, Exalted be He. Taʿrīḍ is a kind of kināya (metonymy), because when a kināya is oblique, brought for the sake of someone described who is not mentioned, it is fitting to call it taʿrīḍ. Among the delightful instances of this device is the saying of Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī, as he gazed at the lofty heaven of the Qur'an:
أبا المسك هل في الكأس فضل أناله ... فإني أغني منذ حين وتشرب
(O Abū l-Misk, is there anything left in the cup for me to obtain? For I have been singing for a while, and you drink.)
He addresses Kāfūr al-Ikhshīdī, saying: my praise of you delights you as singing delights the drinker, so it is time for you to give me to drink from what is left in your cup.
4- Contrast (muqābala) in the antithesis between الضلالة and الهدى and between العذاب and المغفرة.
Muqābala is a device with a subtle path, which only one expert in the styles of speech can tread; otherwise it becomes a detestable artificiality. Abū l-Ṭayyib reached the utmost in it with his saying:
أزورهم وسواد الليل يشفع لي ... وأنثني وبياض الصبح يغري بي
(I visit them while the blackness of night intercedes for me, and I turn back while the whiteness of morning sets [people] upon me.)
He contrasted أزور with أنثني, سواد with بياض, الليل with الصبح, يشفع with يغري, and لي with بي. Among its instances is the saying of Ibn Zaydūn:
سرّان في خاطر الظلماء يكتمنا ... حتى يكاد لسان الصبح يفشينا
(Two secrets in the mind of darkness, which conceals us, until the tongue of morning almost reveals us.)

dervis-irab:177-177.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ابْنَ السَّبِيلِ): the traveller. He is called "son of the road" only because he keeps to the road, just as a water bird is called "son of the water" because it keeps to it, and a man upon whom ages have passed is called "son of the days and nights". [Translator's note: the source has «لطبر الماء», evidently for «لطير الماء» ("water bird").]

* I'rab:
(لَيْسَ): a frozen (jāmid), defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. It was made frozen only because its form is the form of the past while its meaning is negation of the present, so no other form was contrived for it, and it was used in one form; and because it differs from the rest of the verbs in that it was coined to negate meaning.
It is not in the nature of verbs to be coined for negating meaning; they are coined only for affirming it. So it was treated like a particle, frozen and not inflected. The proof that it is a verb is that nominative pronouns attach to it as they attach to the rest of the verbs.
Its original pattern is ليِس, on the pattern فَعِل with kasra on the ʿayn. Were it not that the yāʾ of ليس is kept vowelless, so that it came to be treated like the yāʾ of ليت, the rules of morphology would require it to be converted into alif because it is vowelled and preceded by a fatḥa, and its pronunciation would become «لاس», just as you say هاب in the past tense from the word الهيبة. (الْبِرَّ): the fronted khabar (predicate) of ليس. (أَنْ تُوَلُّوا): أن is a maṣdar-forming particle that puts the verb in the subjunctive, and تولوا is an imperfect verb, subjunctive by أن; the maṣdar cast from أن and what falls within its scope is the postponed noun of ليس. It has been read with البرّ in the nominative, as the noun of ليس, with أن تولوا as its khabar. (وُجُوهَكُمْ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (قِبَلَ): an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) تولوا. (الْمَشْرِقِ): muḍāf ilayhi. (وَالْمَغْرِبِ): conjoined to المشرق. (وَلكِنَّ): the wāw is a conjunction, and لكن is a particle resembling the verb. (الْبِرَّ): its noun. (مَنْ آمَنَ): من is a relative noun, the khabar of لكن; an omitted muḍāf must be understood, i.e. "the righteousness of one who believed". It is possible [Translator's note: the source has «ويسكن», evidently for «ويمكن»] to say: there is no omission; rather righteousness is made to be the very person who believed, for hyperbole. The clause آمن is a ṣila (relative clause) with no grammatical position. (بِاللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to آمن. (وَالْيَوْمِ): conjoined to الله. (الْآخِرِ): naʿt (adjective). (وَالْمَلائِكَةِ وَالْكِتابِ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ): also conjoined to الله. (وَآتَى): a past verb conjoined to آمن, within the scope of the ṣila; its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he" (هو). (الْمالَ): mafʿūl bihi. (عَلى حُبِّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its object, i.e. despite loving it. (ذَوِي الْقُرْبى): the object of آتى, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ, because it is the plural of ذو meaning "possessor"; القربى is muḍāf ilayhi. (وَالْيَتامى وَالْمَساكِينَ وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ وَالسَّائِلِينَ): all conjoined to ذوي. (وَفِي الرِّقابِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are also conjoined, i.e. and he gave wealth for freeing them from captivity or emancipating them. (وَأَقامَ الصَّلاةَ وَآتَى الزَّكاةَ): conjoined to آتى المال. (وَالْمُوفُونَ): conjoined to «من آمن»; you may also parse it as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), because of its distance, i.e. "they are those who fulfil". (بِعَهْدِهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to الموفون, because it is the plural of مُوفٍ, which is the active participle of أوفى. (إِذا): an adverb attached to الموفون. (عاهَدُوا): a verb and its fāʿil; the verbal clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, because it comes after the adverb. (وَالصَّابِرِينَ): the flow of the speech would have it conjoined [Translator's note: the source has «منسوفا», evidently for «منسوقا» ("conjoined")] to what precedes, but He cut it off from the conjunction and put it in the accusative in praise, by an omitted verb implied as "I praise", to indicate the merit of patience and to extol that merit. (فِي الْبَأْساءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to الصابرين. They are two maṣdars that come on the pattern فَعْلاء with no corresponding أَفْعَل; or they are nouns standing for the maṣdar (ism maṣdar), meaning البؤس (misery) and الضرّ (harm), applying to masculine and feminine. Like them is أشأم in the saying of Zuhayr ibn Abī Sulmā describing war:
فتنتج لكم غلمان أشأم كلهم ... كأحمر عاد ثم ترضع فتفطم
(Then it will bring forth for you boys of ill omen, every one of them like the Red One of ʿĀd; then it will suckle and wean them.)
He means: it will bring forth for you boys of ill omen. (وَحِينَ الْبَأْسِ): an adverb of time attached to الصابرين; البأس is muḍāf ilayhi, and it is the intensity of fighting in the way of Allah. (أُولئِكَ): a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. (الَّذِينَ): a relative noun, khabar. (صَدَقُوا): the clause of the verb and its fāʿil has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila. (وَأُولئِكَ): the wāw is resumptive or a conjunction, and أولئك is a mubtadaʾ. (هُمُ): a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), or support pronoun (ʿimād), with no grammatical position, or a second mubtadaʾ. (الْمُتَّقُونَ): the khabar of أولئك, or of هم, [in which case] the nominal clause is the khabar of أولئك.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there are various devices of rhetoric, among them:
1- The device of concision (ījāz) by omitting the muḍāf in His saying:
ولكن البر من آمن; or the device of hyperbole (mubālagha), if we make him righteousness itself.
2- Majāz mursal (non-metaphorical trope) in His saying:
«وفي الرقاب», the relation being part-for-whole (al-juzʾiyya): mentioning the part and meaning the whole.
3- Cutting off the dependent from the word it follows (qaṭʿ al-tābiʿ ʿan al-matbūʿ). Its rule is that when attributes of praise or blame are mentioned, the i'rab is varied, for variety in speech and to draw attention to the fact that what the described one is qualified by, or the attributes ascribed to him, deserve to command attention; for altering the familiar and usual indicates greater encouragement to listen to what is mentioned and greater concern for its importance. The verse is an example of cutting off the dependent from what it follows in praise. Its example in blame is His saying, Exalted be He, in Sūrat Tabbat (وَامْرَأَتُهُ حَمَّالَةَ الْحَطَبِ): حمالة is put in the accusative in blame, while in reality it is an attribute of امرأته; this will come.

dervis-irab:282-282.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَدايَنْتُمْ): you dealt in debt with one another. One says: داينت الرجل, i.e. I dealt with him (on credit). Ruʾya [Translator's note: thus in the source, «رؤية»; the rajaz poet is Ruʾba] said:
داينت أروى والدّيون تقضى ... فمطلت بعضا وأدّت بعضا
(I dealt in debt with Arwā — and debts are repaid — so she delayed some and paid some.)
And they say: أبعت بدين أم بعين؟ ("Did you sell on credit or for ʿayn?"), ʿayn being cash. دنت, أدّنت, تديّنت and استدنت mean: I borrowed. Kuthayyir said:
قضى كلّ ذي دين فوفّى غزيمه ... وعزّة ممطول معنّى غريمها
(Every debtor has settled and paid his creditor in full, while ʿAzza's creditor is put off and tormented.) [Translator's note: «غزيمه» in the first hemistich is presumably a misprint for «غريمه».]
(وَلْيُمْلِلِ): from الإملال and الإملاء, with one meaning. The yāʾ has been substituted for a fair number of letters by way of irregularity (shudhūdh), and no analogy is drawn from it. Of this is their saying أمليت الكتاب; the Exalted said: «فهي تملى عليه بكرة وأصيلا».
The origin is أمللت; and the Exalted said: «وليملل الذي عليه الحقّ». The [correct] view is that they are two dialectal forms, because their conjugation is the same: you say أملى الكتاب يمليه إملاء, and أملّه يملّه إملالا; so making one of them the original and the other derived is no more justified than the reverse. They also said قصّيت أظفاري ("I clipped my nails"), which Ibn al-Sikkīt reported for قصّصت: they substituted a yāʾ for the third ṣād because of the heaviness of the doubling. It may also be that what is meant is تقصّيت أظفاري, i.e. I reached their furthest ends (أقاصيها), because what is taken is their tips, and the tip of everything is its furthest point. This is a topic on which one could speak at length, so we make do with what has preceded; you will come across other good examples in this book.
(فَرِهانٌ), with kasra on the rāʾ: a maṣdar (verbal noun), or the plural of رهن. الرهن is what is put down as security for a debt; also detaining a thing in general; and the thing pledged. It was also read فرهن with two ḍammas, likewise a plural of رهن.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has preceded; the vocative clause and what follows it are resumptive, brought to begin setting out the rulings on debt and on dealing with people in a way that guarantees the general social welfare. (إِذا تَدايَنْتُمْ بِدَيْنٍ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى فَاكْتُبُوهُ): (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of the conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the clause (تداينتم) is in the position of the genitive by construct (iḍāfa); (بدين) is attached to (تداينتم); (إلى أجل) is attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (دين); (مسمى) is an adjective of (أجل); the fāʾ links the apodosis of (إذا); (اكتبوه) is an imperative verb, fāʿil (agent) and mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause joined with the fāʾ has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (وَلْيَكْتُبْ بَيْنَكُمْ كاتِبٌ بِالْعَدْلِ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the lām of command; (يكتب) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the lām; (بينكم) is an adverb of place attached to (يكتب); (كاتب) is the agent; and (بالعدل) is attached to (كاتب), serving as an adjective of it, i.e. by a scribe trusted with what he writes, with fairness and caution, not adding to what ought to be written and not omitting. There is no need for what Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentioned, that the bāʾ is attached to His words «وليكتب» and not to (كاتب), because [on that view] he would be bound not to write a document unless he were himself of upright character, whereas a boy or a careful slave may write it if they master its legal content [Translator's note: the reasoning is compressed in the source; it reports Ibn ʿAṭiyya's argument]. (وَلا يَأْبَ كاتِبٌ أَنْ يَكْتُبَ كَما عَلَّمَهُ اللَّهُ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (يأب) is an imperfect verb in the jussive, its sign being the dropping of the weak letter; (كاتب) is the agent; (أن) and what is in its scope are an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, because أبى means "refrained"; (كما علمه الله): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), or are in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); and the clause (علمه) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the particle-relative (mawṣūl ḥarfī). (فَلْيَكْتُبْ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "when you know this ruling, then let him write"; the lām is the lām of command; (يكتب) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by the lām, and the agent is "he". (وَلْيُمْلِلِ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ الْحَقُّ): the wāw is a conjunction; (الذي) is the agent of (يكتب) [Translator's note: thus in the source; it is the agent of يملل]; (عليه) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (الحق) is the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (وَلْيَتَّقِ اللَّهَ رَبَّهُ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the lām of command; (يتق) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by the lām, its sign being the dropping of the weak letter; the agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he"; the Name of Majesty is the direct object; and (ربه) is a badal (substitute). (وَلا يَبْخَسْ مِنْهُ شَيْئاً): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (يبخس) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by (لا), and the agent is "he"; (منه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يبخس), or to an omitted ḥāl, because it was an adjective of «شيئا» and was placed before it; and (شيئا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq or a direct object, i.e. "let him not diminish anything of it". (فَإِنْ كانَ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِ الْحَقُّ سَفِيهاً أَوْ ضَعِيفاً): the fāʾ is resumptive; (إن) is conditional; (كان) is a deficient past verb in the position of the jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (الذي) is the noun of (كان); (عليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (الحق) is the postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila; (سفيها) is the khabar of (كان); (أو) is a conjunction; and (ضعيفا) is conjoined to (سفيها). (أَوْ لا يَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ يُمِلَّ هُوَ): (أو) is a conjunction; (لا) is negating; (يستطيع) is an imperfect verb; (أن) and what is in its scope are to be interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of the accusative as the object of (يستطيع); and (هو) is the agent, or a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent agent. (فَلْيُمْلِلْ وَلِيُّهُ بِالْعَدْلِ): the fāʾ links the apodosis; the lām is the lām of command; (يملل) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by the lām; (وليه) is the agent; (بالعدل) is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "being just", or you may attach it to His words (فليملل); and the clause is in the position of the jussive as apodosis. (وَاسْتَشْهِدُوا شَهِيدَيْنِ مِنْ رِجالِكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (استشهدوا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the agent; (شهيدين) is the direct object; and (من رجالكم) is attached to an omitted adjective, or to His words (واستشهدوا). (فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُونا رَجُلَيْنِ): the fāʾ is resumptive; (إن) is conditional; (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; (يكونا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by (لم), and it is the protasis; the alif is its noun and (رجلين) its khabar. (فَرَجُلٌ وَامْرَأَتانِ): the fāʾ links the apodosis; (رجل) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; (امرأتان) is conjoined to (رجل); the implied form is "then the witnesses are a man and two women", or "then a man and two women shall bear witness"; and the clause is in the position of the jussive as apodosis. (مِمَّنْ تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ الشُّهَداءِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective; the clause (ترضون) has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila; and (من الشهداء) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (أَنْ تَضِلَّ إِحْداهُما): (أن) and what is in its scope are to be interpreted as a maṣdar in the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), because going astray is a cause for reminding; it is as though it were said: "out of wanting one of them to remind the other". More on this i'rab will come in the section of Benefits. (إحداهما) is the agent of (تضل). (فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْداهُمَا الْأُخْرى): the fāʾ
is a conjunction; (تذكر) is conjoined to (أن تضلّ); (إحداهما) is the agent; and (الأخرى) is the direct object. (وَلا يَأْبَ الشُّهَداءُ إِذا ما دُعُوا): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (يأب) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by (لا), its sign being the dropping of the weak letter; (الشهداء) is the agent; (إذا) is an adverb of the future containing the meaning of the conditional, attached to the apodosis; (ما) is redundant (zāʾida); (دعوا) is a passive imperfect verb [Translator's note: thus in the source; دُعُوا is a past verb]; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and the clause is in the position of the genitive by construct. (وَلا تَسْئَمُوا أَنْ تَكْتُبُوهُ صَغِيراً أَوْ كَبِيراً إِلى أَجَلِهِ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (تسأموا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by (لا); the wāw is the agent; (أن) and what is in its scope are the direct object of (تسأموا); (صغيرا) is a ḥāl; the wāw [Translator's note: thus in the source; the Qur'anic text has أو] is a conjunction, and «كبيرا» is conjoined to «صغيرا»; and (إلى أجله) is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "remaining as an obligation until it falls due". It may not be attached to (تكتبوه), because the writing does not continue until its term. (ذلِكُمْ أَقْسَطُ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَأَقْوَمُ لِلشَّهادَةِ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is explicative; (ذلكم) is the mubtadaʾ and (أقسط) its khabar. Note that the elative noun (ism tafḍīl) has come from a quadriliteral verb, whereas the rule is that it comes from a triliteral one, because the verb is أقسط, i.e. "acted justly", whereas the triliteral قسط means "acted unjustly"; the Exalted said: «وأما القاسطون فكانوا لجهنم حطبا». (عند) is an adverb of place attached to (أقسط); the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (أقوم) is conjoined to (أقسط); and (للشهادة) is attached to (أقوم), the meaning being "sounder and firmer". (وَأَدْنى أَلَّا تَرْتابُوا): the wāw is a conjunction; (أدنى) is conjoined to (أقوم); (أن) and what is in its scope are to be interpreted as a maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "nearer to the absence of doubt", and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (أدنى). (إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ تِجارَةً حاضِرَةً): (إلا) is an instrument of exception; (أن) and what is in its scope are a maṣdar in the accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because it is present trade that does not need witnessing or writing. However, it is sound to regard it as a joined exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), as though it were an exception from trade: the command to write remains in force, and He excepted writing with present trade. (تكون) is an imperfect verb whose noun is latent, its implied form being "it", i.e. the trade, and (تجارة) is the khabar. It is also sound to regard «تكون» as complete (tāmma) and (تجارة) as the agent; it has been read both ways.
(حاضرة) is a naʿt of (تجارة). (تُدِيرُونَها بَيْنَكُمْ): the clause is a second adjective of (تجارة); and (بينكم) is an adverb of place attached to (تديرونها). (فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُناحٌ أَلَّا تَكْتُبُوها): the fāʾ is a conjunction, conjoining this clause to the clause «إلا أن تكون تجارة», i.e. the removal of blame for not writing results from that. (ليس) is a deficient past verb; (عليكم) is attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (جناح) is its postponed noun; and (أن) and what is in its scope are an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in your not writing it", and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of (جناح). (وَأَشْهِدُوا إِذا تَبايَعْتُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (أشهدوا) is an imperative verb; the wāw is the agent; (إذا) is an adverb of the future containing the meaning of the conditional, attached to the apodosis; the clause (تبايعتم) is in the position of the genitive by construct; and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then take witnesses". You may strip (إذا) of its conditional sense and make it a mere adverb of time, i.e. "perform the witnessing at the time of mutual selling". (وَلا يُضَارَّ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (يضار) is an imperfect verb which may be active, its origin being يضارِر with kasra on the first rāʾ, or may be passive, its origin being يضارَر with fatḥa on it; it is jussive in either case, and it was voweled with the fatḥa for its lightness because it is a doubled verb. (كاتِبٌ وَلا شَهِيدٌ): (كاتب) is the agent or the deputy agent; the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is negating; and (شهيد) is conjoined to (كاتب). (وَإِنْ تَفْعَلُوا فَإِنَّهُ فُسُوقٌ بِكُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (تفعلوا) is an imperfect verb, the protasis, jussive, its sign being the dropping of the nūn; the fāʾ links the apodosis; (إن) and its noun, and (فسوق) is its khabar; (بكم) is attached to an omitted adjective of (فسوق), i.e. "attaching [to you]"; and the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as apodosis. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (اتقوا) is an imperative verb; the wāw is the agent; and the Name of Majesty is the direct object. (وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ اللَّهُ): the wāw is resumptive. There is no room to make it circumstantial, as al-Jalāl established and many commentators and grammarians followed him, because the circumstantial wāw does not directly precede an affirmative imperfect verb — even though some tried to imply an omitted mubtadaʾ so that the clause would be nominal, i.e. "while He teaches you", because of the forcedness in that. And making it a conjunction is contrary to what is preferable, because it involves conjoining an informative statement (khabar) to a performative one (inshāʾ), which is a point of disagreement that will come in its place in this book. (الله) is the agent of (يعلمكم), and the kāf is the object of (يعلمكم). (وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ; (بكل شيء) is attached to (عليم); and (عليم) is the khabar of (الله).

* Rhetoric:
Perhaps this verse is among the verses richest in mentioning the matters of livelihood by which the affairs of the servants are ordered, and which guarantee a good return [in the Hereafter] to whoever follows them. In it Allah, Glorified is He, laid stress on good dealing, which is the sum and pillar of religion, and was emphatic in enjoining the safeguarding of lawful wealth and surrounding it with what protects it from loss. For that reason it contains kinds of emphasis, which we summarise below, leaving the reader to consult the well-known sources.
1- He commanded writing by saying «فاكتبوه», as a precaution against exposure to error or forgetfulness.
2- He mentioned «بدين» although it is understood from His words «تداينتم», for emphasis, and so that the pronoun in His words «فليكتبوه» [Translator's note: thus in the source; the Qur'anic wording is «فاكتبوه»] would refer back to it — for had it not been mentioned, it would have had to be said "so write down the debt", which would impair the beauty of the composition — and to indicate generality, i.e. any debt, whether little or much.
3- He mentioned «إلى أجل مسمى» by way of emphasis, and so that it would be known that the term must properly be known by specifying it in years, months and days.
Had he said "until the harvest", for example, it would not be permitted, for lack of specification.
4- He entrusted the writing to a scribe marked by justice.
5- He forbade the one asked to write from refusing what he is charged with.
6- He repeated the command to write in another form, out of strictness about writing, saying:
«فليكتب».
7- He commanded the one who owes to dictate to the scribe with justice, so that no argument would remain for him.
8- He took precautions for the matter by commanding him to fear Allah, saying: «وليتق الله ربه».
