9- He followed the fear [of Allah] with what it necessitates, namely not diminishing (البخس), and used this word, which in its original lexical sense refers to the one-eyed eye: one says بخست عينه, i.e. it became blind. The embodied, vivid portrayal in this is not hidden.
10- He guarded against the weariness and boredom that may come upon human beings, and the negligence that results from them, whereupon chaos would spread and disorder arise, because they did not write down in full what they witnessed, whether great or small.
11- After enjoining what He enjoined, He drew attention to the fact that this is the most upright path and the most just way, and He mentioned His name, the Exalted, explicitly, saying: «عند الله», to make clear the known destination, and as a warning against the negligence of the negligent and the encroachment of the encroacher.
12- He closed the verse by mentioning Allah three times in succession, to strike awe into hearts, produce reverence in souls, entrench the ruling in minds, and convey that He, the Exalted, is aware of the secrets; the whispers of hearts and the stirrings of consciences do not escape Him.

* Benefits:
Al-Zamakhsharī illustrated His words, the Exalted, «أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى» with their saying: "I prepared the beam in case the wall should lean, so that I might prop it", and "I prepared the weapon in case an enemy should come, so that I might repel him". So it is as though it were said: "out of wanting one of them to remind the other". Al-Taftāzānī raised a question in his glosses on al-Kashshāf, saying: «Among what ought to be addressed is the reason for repeating «إحداهما». There is no hiding that it is not a case of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, since the one mentioned [first] is not the corresponding one — unless the second «إحداهما» is made to be in the position of the object; and placing the object before the agent is not permitted where there is ambiguity. Yes, it would be sound to say «فتذكر الأخرى», so there must be a subtle point (nukta) for the deviation». Al-Taftāzānī did not address the subtle point and left his reader perplexed. However, al-Damāmīnī mentioned in his commentary on al-Mughnī that what is intended is that the reminding is by one of them to the other, however it is construed, and this is only correct in this way. Do you not see that if it were said "that one of them should err and the other remind her (فتذكرها)", the object pronoun would have to refer to the one who erred, and so it would be fixed to her, and that would impair the intended meaning; because the one who errs now in the testimony may be the one who remembers it at another time, in which case the one reminded is the one who erred [Translator's note: thus in the source, «فالمذكرة حينئذ هي الضالة»]. So if it were said «فتذكرها الأخرى», it would not convey that, because the pronoun is fixed to refer to the one who erred. But if it is said «فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى», it is left indeterminate as to which of the two. So if one of them erred and the other reminded her and she remembered, it would be included; and then if the matter were reversed, with the very same testimony at another time, that too would fall under it, since His words «فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى» occur without specification. Thus the reason appears for which He turned from «فتذكرها» to «فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى».
There is something in the mind about this explanation that this book cannot bear.

dervis-irab:125-125.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَثابَةً): a place of resort and return for the pilgrims, who disperse from it and then return (yathūbūn) to it; so it is from «ثاب يثوب», i.e. to return. It has also been said that it is from «الثواب», which is recompense. It may be a mīm-maṣdar (al-maṣdar al-mīmī) or a noun of place. The hāʾ in it is either for intensity, as in «علّامة» and «نسّابة», because of the great number of those who return to it; or for the feminine of the maṣdar, as in «مقامة»; or for the feminine of "the spot" (al-buqʿa).

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ): the i'rab of its parallels has often preceded. (جَعَلْنَا): a verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (الْبَيْتَ): first object of «جعلنا». (مَثابَةً): second object of «جعلنا». (لِلنَّاسِ): attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of «مثابة». (وَأَمْناً): conjoined to «مثابة». (وَاتَّخِذُوا): the wāw is a conjunction, and «اتخذوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the object of an omitted speech conjoined to «جعلنا». (مِنْ مَقامِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «اتخذوا». (إِبْراهِيمَ): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive by the fatḥa because it is a diptote for being a proper name and non-Arabic. (مُصَلًّى): the object of «اتخذوا»; «من» is for the starting point, as though it were said: "Take a place of prayer, starting from this place." There is no need for the far-fetched aspects the parsers have laboured over, none of which is sound. (وَعَهِدْنا): a verb and its fāʿil. (إِلى إِبْراهِيمَ): attached to «عهدنا». (وَإِسْماعِيلَ): conjoined to «إبراهيم»; it too is a non-Arabic proper name, and it has two dialectal forms, with lām and with nūn. (أَنْ): the most evident view is that it is explicative (tafsīriyya), meaning «أي», because it occurs after a clause containing the meaning of speech without its letters. (طَهِّرا): an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is explicative; [«أن»] may also be a maṣdar particle, in which case the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition. (بَيْتِيَ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (لِلطَّائِفِينَ): attached to «طهرا». (وَالْعاكِفِينَ وَالرُّكَّعِ السُّجُودِ): conjoined to «الطائفين». Since «الركّع» and «السجود» are as one — because bowing and prostration together make up the prayer — He dropped the conjunction and treated the two as a single word; had He conjoined «السجود» with a wāw, it would have suggested that they are two separate acts of worship.

dervis-irab:126-126.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قالَ إِبْراهِيمُ): its i'rab has preceded. (رَبِّ): the one addressed (munādā), from which the vocative particle is omitted; it is annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person. (اجْعَلْ): an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is "you". (هذا): a demonstrative, first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (بَلَداً): second mafʿūl bihi. (آمِناً): an adjective. (وَارْزُقْ أَهْلَهُ): conjoined to «اجعل», and «أهله» is mafʿūl bihi. (مِنَ الثَّمَراتِ): attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ارزق». (مِنَ): a relative noun, badal (substitute) from «أهله». (آمَنَ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (مِنْهُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (بِاللَّهِ): both attached to «آمن». (وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ): conjoined to «الله». (قالَ): a past verb, and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position. (وَمَنْ): a relative noun conjoined to the first «من». (كَفَرَ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila. (فَأُمَتِّعُهُ): the fāʾ is linking, because the relative noun contains the sense of a condition; «أمتعه» is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi. (قَلِيلًا): mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (ثُمَّ): a conjunction. (أَضْطَرُّهُ): conjoined to «أمتعه». (إِلى عَذابِ النَّارِ): attached to «أضطره». (وَبِئْسَ): the wāw is resumptive, and «بئس» is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame. (الْمَصِيرُ): fāʿil of «بئس»; the specifically blamed (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "his destination".

dervis-irab:127-127.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ): the wāw is a conjunction joining to what preceded, and «إذ» is an adverb for past time; its discussion has preceded. (يَرْفَعُ إِبْراهِيمُ): an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (الْقَواعِدَ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (مِنَ الْبَيْتِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning of raising here is building. (إِسْماعِيلُ): conjoined to «إبراهيم». (رَبَّنا): the one addressed (munādā), annexed, with the vocative particle omitted; an omitted speech must be assumed, i.e. "the two saying: Our Lord"; the ḥāl is often omitted when it is a [verb of] saying, the thing said making it unnecessary. (تَقَبَّلْ): an imperative verb whose meaning is supplication. (مِنَّا): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تقبل». (إِنَّكَ): «إن» and its noun. (أَنْتَ): an attached pronoun with no grammatical position [Translator's note: so in the source; «أنت» is a detached pronoun, here in the role of a pronoun of separation], or a mubtadaʾ (subject). (السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ): two khabars (predicates) of «إن», or of «أنت», in which case the nominal clause is the khabar of «إن».

dervis-irab:128-129.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُزَكِّيهِمْ): He purifies them and cleanses their souls of sins and misdeeds.

* I'rab:
(رَبَّنا): the one addressed (munādā), annexed; its i'rab has preceded. (وَاجْعَلْنا): conjoined to what preceded. (مُسْلِمَيْنِ): second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (لَكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of «مسلمين». (وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّتِنا): the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted [verb] indicated by what is mentioned, i.e. "and make of our offspring". (أُمَّةً): first mafʿūl bihi of the omitted verb, and «من ذريتنا» is the second object. (مُسْلِمَةً): naʿt. (لَكَ): a second naʿt of «أمة». (وَأَرِنا): the wāw is a conjunction; «أر» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you"; and «نا» is an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative as first mafʿūl bihi. (مَناسِكَنا): second mafʿūl bihi. (وَتُبْ عَلَيْنا): also conjoined. (إِنَّكَ): «إن» and its noun. (أَنْتَ): a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (التَّوَّابُ): first khabar (predicate). (الرَّحِيمُ): second khabar, and the nominal clause is the khabar of «إن». You may also parse the pronoun as a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, and «التواب الرحيم» as two khabars of «إن». (رَبَّنا): the one addressed, annexed. (وَابْعَثْ): conjoined to what preceded. (فِيهِمْ): both attached to «ابعث». (رَسُولًا): mafʿūl bihi. (مِنْهُمْ): an adjective of «رسولا». (يَتْلُوا): the clause is either a second adjective or a ḥāl (circumstantial), because «رسولا» has been qualified by His saying «منهم». (عَلَيْهِمْ): both attached to «يتلو». (آياتِكَ): the object of «يتلو». (وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ): conjoined to «يتلو», and the hāʾ is first mafʿūl bihi. (الْكِتابَ): second mafʿūl bihi. (وَالْحِكْمَةَ): conjoined to «الكتاب». (وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ): conjoined to «يعلمهم». (إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): its i'rab preceded a little earlier.

dervis-irab:130-130.t:
* Vocabulary:
«رغب عن الشيء»: he turned away from the thing and disliked it. «رغب فيه»: he wanted it, inclined to it and loved it. «السفه»: lightness [of mind]; what is meant by it here is debasing oneself.

* I'rab:
(وَمَنْ يَرْغَبُ): the wāw is resumptive, and «من» is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation and disapproval, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «يرغب» is its khabar (predicate). (عَنْ مِلَّةِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يرغب». (إِبْراهِيمَ): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the sign of its genitive being the fatḥa because it is a diptote for being a proper name and non-Arabic. (إِلَّا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (مَنْ): a relative noun in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in «يرغب», because the statement is non-affirmative; or accusative as the excepted. (سَفِهَ نَفْسَهُ): «سفه» is a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he", and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. «نفسه» is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "he was foolish in himself". It has also been said that «سفه» is transitive by itself, as Thaʿlab and al-Mubarrad reported, so it is the object of «سفه»; one says «سفه نفسه», i.e. he debased it. It has also been said that it is accusative as tamyīz (specification); but that involves a definite tamyīz, which only occurs irregularly, so it is not permissible to construe the Qur'an by it. (وَلَقَدِ): the wāw is resumptive, the lām is [in] the answer to an omitted oath, and «قد» is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). (اصْطَفَيْناهُ): a past verb, its fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (فِي الدُّنْيا): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «اصطفيناه». (وَإِنَّهُ): the wāw is circumstantial, and «إن» and its noun. (فِي الْآخِرَةِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (لَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ): the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar of «إن».

dervis-irab:131-132.t:
* I'rab:
(إِذْ): if we join the verses to one another, the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «اصطفيناه»; but it is simpler to follow the pattern adopted in the Qur'an, to which we have become accustomed in it, namely attaching it to an implied [verb], i.e. "remember". (قالَ): the verbal clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (لَهُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «قال». (رَبُّهُ): fāʿil (agent) of «قال», and the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive by annexation. (أَسْلِمْ): an imperative verb whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you"; the verbal clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (قالَ): a past verb whose fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he". (أَسْلَمْتُ): the verbal clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech. (لِرَبِّ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أسلمت». (الْعالَمِينَ): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is attached (mulḥaq) to the sound masculine plural. (وَوَصَّى): the wāw is a conjunction, and «وصى» is a past verb. (بِها): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «وصى». (إِبْراهِيمُ): fāʿil of «وصى». (بَنِيهِ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ because it is attached to the sound masculine plural; the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive by annexation. (وَيَعْقُوبُ): conjoined to «إبراهيم», falling under its ruling. (يا بَنِيَّ): the one addressed (munādā), annexed, with an implied verb of saying, i.e. "saying", so the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (إِنَّ اللَّهَ): «إن» and its noun. (اصْطَفى): the verbal clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «إن», and the fāʿil of «اصطفى» is latent, its implied form being "he". (لَكُمُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «اصطفى». (الدِّينَ): mafʿūl bihi. (فَلا تَمُوتُنَّ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa — its meaning will come — i.e. "if you know this"; «لا» is prohibitive, and «تموتن» is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive «لا», the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the doubled nūn is for emphasis, and the wāw of the plural, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil; the original is «تموتوننّ». (إِلَّا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (وَأَنْتُمْ): the wāw is circumstantial, and «أنتم» is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (مُسْلِمُونَ): khabar, and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

* Benefits:
1- Attached (mulḥaq) to the sound masculine plural in its inflection is what has come from the Arabs as a sound masculine plural without meeting its conditions, such as «أولي», «أهلين», «عالمين», «وابلين», «أرضين», «بنين», «عشرين» to «تسعين», and «سنين» and its type — every triliteral whose third radical has been dropped and replaced by the feminine hāʾ, such as «عضين», «عزين», «ثبين», «مئين», «ظبين» and the like, whose singulars are «سنة», «عضة», «عزة», «ثبة», «مائة» and «ظبة». Also attached to it are nouns named with a sound masculine plural form, such as «عليّين», «سجّين» and others.
2- How to treat an emphasized verb in which nūns follow one another when it is in the jussive: one says about it: the original of «تموتنّ» is «تموتوننّ»; the first nūn is the sign of the nominative, and the second and third are the heavy nūn of emphasis. So three similar letters came together, and the nūn of the nominative was dropped for the jussive, because the heavy nūn of emphasis is more entitled to remain, as it indicates a future meaning. Then two quiescent letters met — the wāw and the first, assimilated nūn — so the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the ḍamma remained to indicate it. And so with everything of its kind.

* Rhetoric:
In prohibiting death, or commanding it, there is a splendid rhetorical subtlety. In itself it is neither prohibited nor commanded, because it is among the matters that do not fall under human will. But it was prohibited here to show that death on other than Islam is a death in which there is no good, and that it is not the death of the blessed. Likewise with commanding death: you say "Die as a martyr", not intending to command his death, but "die the death that will bequeath you an immortal name in this world, and Paradise and a comfortable life in the Hereafter". Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī seized on this subtlety and said:
عش عزيزا أو مت وأنت كريم ... بين طعن القنا وخفق البنود
(Live mighty, or die noble, amid the thrust of spears and the fluttering of banners.)

dervis-irab:283-283.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ عَلى سَفَرٍ): the wāw is resumptive; (إن) is conditional; (كنتم) is a deficient past verb in the position of the jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is its noun; and (على سفر) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of (كنتم). (وَلَمْ تَجِدُوا كاتِباً): the wāw is circumstantial; (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; (تجدوا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by (لم), its sign being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (كاتبا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause is circumstantial. You may make the wāw a conjunction, in which case the clause is conjoined to the protasis and is in the position of the jussive. (فَرِهانٌ مَقْبُوضَةٌ): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (رهان) is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and beginning with an indefinite noun is permissible because it is qualified; (مقبوضة) is an adjective; and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "by which you secure yourselves". You may parse it as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "then what is relied upon is pledges", because travel is a likely occasion for lacking scribes [Translator's note: the source has «الكتب», "writings"; presumably «الكتّاب», "scribes"].
The details of the question are set out at length in the books of jurisprudence. The nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as apodosis. (فَإِنْ أَمِنَ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضاً): the fāʾ is a conjunction; (إن) is conditional; (أمن) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as protasis; (بعضكم) is the agent and (بعضا) the direct object. (فَلْيُؤَدِّ الَّذِي اؤْتُمِنَ أَمانَتَهُ): the fāʾ links the apodosis; the lām is the lām of command; (يؤد) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by the lām, its sign being the dropping of the weak letter; and the clause is in the position of the jussive as protasis [Translator's note: thus in the source, «فعل الشرط»; it is the apodosis]; (الذي) is a relative noun, the agent; (اؤتمن) is a passive past verb whose nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he", and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); and (أمانته) is the direct object of (يؤد). (وَلْيَتَّقِ اللَّهَ رَبَّهُ): its i'rab, letter for letter, has preceded. (وَلا تَكْتُمُوا الشَّهادَةَ): the wāw is a conjunction; (لا) is prohibitive; (تكتموا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by (لا), its sign being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the agent; and (الشهادة) is the direct object. (وَمَنْ يَكْتُمْها فَإِنَّهُ آثِمٌ قَلْبُهُ): the wāw is resumptive; (من) is a jussive conditional noun, the mubtadaʾ; (يكتمها) is the protasis and the hāʾ its object; the fāʾ links the apodosis; (إن) and its noun, and (آثم) is its khabar; and (قلبه) is the agent of (آثم) because it is an active participle. In a construction like this it is also sound for the pronoun in (فإنه) to be the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), with (آثم) a fronted khabar and (قلبه) a postponed mubtadaʾ, the nominal clause being the khabar of (إن). The clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of (من). (وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ عَلِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ; (بما) is attached to (عليم); the clause (تعملون) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; and (عليم) is the khabar of «الله».

* Rhetoric:
1- Explicit dependent metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya al-tabaʿiyya) in His words, the Exalted, «على سفر»: their mastery of travel, their being trained in it and their practice of it are likened to a rider's mastery of his mount.
2- Rational (cognitive) metaphor (al-majāz al-ʿaqlī) in His words «آثم قلبه»: sin is ascribed to the heart, while what is meant is the whole person, not his heart alone, for a wonderful secret, namely that the heart is like the head of the limbs, and it is the lump of flesh which, if it is sound, the whole body is sound. Poets have clung to the skirts of this eloquence; it suffices us to mention the heart's turning in the splendid saying of al-Sharīf al-Raḍī:
ولقد وفقت على ديارهم ... وطلولها بيد البلى نهب
وبكيت حتى ضجّ من لغب ... نضوي ولج بعذلي الركب
وتلفتت عيني فمذ خفيت ... عني الطلول تلفت القلب
(I stopped at their dwellings, whose ruins are plunder in the hand of decay; I wept until my lean camel groaned from fatigue and the riders persisted in blaming me; my eye kept turning back, and once the ruins were hidden from me, my heart turned back.) [Translator's note: «وفقت» in the first line is presumably a misprint for «وقفت».]
And Diʿbil al-Khuzāʿī spoke explicitly of the crime of the heart and the eye in his saying:
أين الشباب وأية سلكا ... لا أين يطلب ضلّ بل هلكا
لا تأخذا بظلامتي أحدا ... قلبي وطرفي في دمي اشتركا
لا تعجبي يا سلم من رجل ... ضحك المشيب برأسه فبكى
(Where has youth gone, and which way did it take? No — where can it be sought? It did not stray; it perished. Do not, you two, hold anyone to account for the wrong done to me: my heart and my eye shared in my blood. Do not wonder, Salmā, at a man in whose head grey hair laughed, so he wept.)

dervis-irab:178-179.t:
* Vocabulary:
(كُتِبَ): it was made obligatory; from this is the saying of ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa:
كتب القتل والقتال علينا ... وعلى الغانيات جرّ الذّيول
(Killing and fighting have been prescribed for us, and for the fair ladies the trailing of their skirts.)

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has been given before. (كُتِبَ): a passive past verb. (عَلَيْكُمُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) كتب. (الْقِصاصُ): nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (فِي الْقَتْلى): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); you may also attach them to القصاص. The vocative clause and what follows it is resumptive, brought to state the ruling on retaliation (qiṣāṣ) in the usage of the Sharīʿa. (الْحُرُّ): mubtadaʾ (subject). (بِالْحُرِّ): attached to an omitted khabar (predicate). (وَالْعَبْدُ بِالْعَبْدِ): conjoined to what precedes; the nominal clause has no grammatical position because it is explicative (mufassira). (وَالْأُنْثى بِالْأُنْثى): also conjoined. (فَمَنْ): the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the disclosing fāʾ), because it discloses some of the details that come to mind; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (عُفِيَ): a passive past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (لَهُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to عفي. (مِنْ أَخِيهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. in the state of its being from his brother's blood. (شَيْءٌ): the nāʾib fāʿil of عفي. (فَاتِّباعٌ): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) because it is a nominal clause; اتباع is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted and fronted before it, i.e. "then upon him is a following". The clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من. (بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اتباع. (وَأَداءٌ): conjoined to اتباع. (إِلَيْهِ): attached to أداء. (بِإِحْسانٍ): attached to an omitted ḥāl. (ذلِكَ): the demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. (تَخْفِيفٌ): khabar. (مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective); the clause is resumptive. (وَرَحْمَةٌ): conjoined to تخفيف. (فَمَنْ): the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and من is conditional, mubtadaʾ. (اعْتَدى): a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis. (بَعْدَ ذلِكَ): the adverb is attached to اعتدى. (فَلَهُ): the fāʾ links the apodosis because it is a nominal clause, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted, fronted khabar. (عَذابٌ): the postponed mubtadaʾ. (أَلِيمٌ): naʿt of عذاب; the clause joined to the fāʾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are in the position of nominative as the khabar of من. (وَلَكُمْ): the wāw is resumptive, and what follows it is a resumptive clause brought to explain the wisdom in the legislation of retaliation; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted, fronted khabar. (فِي الْقِصاصِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (حَياةٌ): the postponed mubtadaʾ. (يا): a vocative particle. (أُولِي الْأَلْبابِ): the one addressed (munādā), annexed, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ, because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural; الألباب is muḍāf ilayhi. (لَعَلَّكُمْ): لعل and its noun. (تَتَّقُونَ): an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of لعل, and the clause of hope is a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse of retaliation there is an unparalleled height of eloquence, because it contains many devices, which we list below:
1- Concision (ījāz): the Arabs used to pride themselves on their saying: «القتل أنفى للقتل» (killing best prevents killing). Then the verse of the Qur'an, «في القصاص حياة» (in retaliation there is life), came, more concise and more elegant in expression, because it is four words — «في، ال، قصاص، حياة» — while the saying of the Arabs is six — «ال، قتل، أنفى, and its pronoun, since it is a derived noun, اللام، قتل»; and because its pronounced letters, fixed in pause and in continuation, are eleven letters, while the letters of the Arabs' saying are fourteen.
2- Majāz mursal (non-metaphorical trope) in His saying: «في القصاص حياة»: He made what is a taking away and removal of life a container for it, since retaliation is a strong deterrent against people's venturing upon killing; through it killing is lifted from people, and the lifting of a cause of death is a perpetuation of the previous life.
3- Making القصاص definite and الحياة indefinite, i.e. there was for you in this kind of retaliation a great life whose essence you do not grasp, because the would-be killer is deterred from killing, and the lives of the innocent are thereby protected, and transgressors are restrained, as well as those in whose souls the nature of criminality is implanted.
4- Hastening the encouragement and arousing desire by mentioning life: through it the hearer breathes in the scent of life, its sweetness and its pleasantness, because it comes as the inevitable result of retaliation — the opposite of the Arabs' saying, which begins by mentioning death. Abū l-Ṭayyib glimpsed the heaven of this meaning in his immortal verse:
إلف هذا الهواء أوقع في الأنفس أنّ الحمام مرّ المذاق
(Familiarity with this air has made souls believe that death is bitter to taste.)
5- Antithesis (ṭibāq) between life and death, to show the contrast between the two opposites; and the beauty of an opposite is shown only by its opposite, as the author of al-Yatīma said in a love poem:
فالوجه مثل الصّبح مبيضّ ... والفرع مثل الليل مسودّ
ضدّان لما استجمعا حسنا ... والضّدّ يظهر حسنه الضدّ
(The face is white like the morning, and the locks black like the night; two opposites which, when joined, became beautiful — and an opposite's beauty is shown by its opposite.)
In the verse, retaliation, which is originally an expression of death, has been made the place of its opposite, namely life.
6- The indefiniteness of الحياة indicates that in this human race there is a kind of life distinguished from others, which description cannot reach, because they used to kill a group for one person, so that strife would flare up and spread among them; in the legislation of retaliation there is safety and deliverance from all this.
7- Generality that goes beyond specification: killing alone is not the cause of retaliation; rather all wounds and head-injuries are included in it, because when the one who wounds knows that if he wounds he will be wounded, that becomes a cause for the survival of both the wounder and the wounded; and a wound may lead to death, so retaliation is taken from the wounder.
8- In the saying of the Arabs there is no word in which two vowelled letters come together except in one place; rather all of them are light syllables (asbāb khafīfa), most of them in succession, and that detracts from the soundness of the expression and its flowing on the tongue — unlike the verse of the Qur'an.
9- The original purpose, which is life, is stated explicitly in the verse, while it is indicated only by implication (bi-l-iltizām) in the saying of the Arabs.
10- Universal validity (iṭṭirād) in the verse, unlike their saying, since there is killing that does not prevent killing but rather invites it, such as killing unjustly; it holds universally only when it is by way of retaliation. [The term] is derived from اطّرد الماء, which is the water's flowing without stopping.
11- The verse is free of the repugnant word القتل and of the flowing blood and torn limbs it embodies.
12- The verse is free of repetition, despite the closeness and the unity and coherence of meaning.
13- The verse is free of the repetition of the qalqala of the qāf.
14- The verse covers the ruling on wounds to the limbs.
15- Hyperbole (mubālagha): retaliation is a container for life; in this, the opposite of a thing is made a source of it, as if it encompasses it to prevent its being lost.

dervis-irab:180-182.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الجنف), with two fatḥas: the maṣdar (verbal noun) of جنِف, like فرِح, i.e. he deviated from the truth and turned away with it.

* I'rab:
(كُتِبَ): a passive past verb. (عَلَيْكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) كتب; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. (إِذا): an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, attached to the omitted apodosis, i.e. "let him make a bequest". (حَضَرَ): a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa. (أَحَدَكُمُ): a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الْمَوْتُ): a postponed fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (إِنْ): a jussive conditional particle that puts two verbs in the jussive. (تَرَكَ): a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he" (هو). (خَيْراً): mafʿūl bihi, i.e. wealth; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the omitted apodosis of إذا, i.e. "let him make a bequest". (الْوَصِيَّةُ): the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of كتب; the verb may be masculine because الوصية is figuratively feminine and because there is a separation between them. (لِلْوالِدَيْنِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to الوصية. (وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ): conjoined to His saying للوالدين. (بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): i.e. with justice; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. being just, not unjust, so that he does not make a bequest to the rich and leave out the poor. (حَقًّا): a maṣdar, a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) confirming the content of the clause before it, namely كتب عليكم الوصية. It has also been said: it is a maṣdar specifying the kind, as shown by His saying (عَلَى الْمُتَّقِينَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to حقا; a confirming maṣdar does not govern and adds no meaning to what precedes it. (فَمَنْ): the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to mention a ruling concerning executors and witnesses; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (بَدَّلَهُ): a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis. (بَعْدَ ما سَمِعَهُ): بعد is an adverb of time, and ما is maṣdariyya, cast together with the verb after it into a maṣdar that is muḍāf ilayhi, i.e. after his hearing it and verifying it; the pronoun refers to the ruling. (فَإِنَّما): the fāʾ links the apodosis, and إنما is a restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa). (إِثْمُهُ): mubtadaʾ. (عَلَى الَّذِينَ يُبَدِّلُونَهُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate); the clause يبدلونه has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause); the nominal clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are in the position of nominative as the khabar of من. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ): إن and its noun. (سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ): two khabars of إن; the clause is resumptive, brought to threaten the one who alters. (فَمَنْ): the fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to threaten the one who deviates from the truth; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (خافَ): a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; its fāʿil is "he", referring to من. The meaning of fear here is expectation, as when you say: "I fear the sky will send down its rain", meaning expectation and supposition that stands in place of knowledge. (مِنْ مُوصٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to His saying جنفا, because it is a maṣdar. (جَنَفاً): mafʿūl bihi. (أَوْ): a conjunction. (إِثْماً): conjoined to His saying جنفا. (فَأَصْلَحَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and أصلح is a past verb conjoined to خاف; its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "he". (بَيْنَهُمْ): an adverb of place attached to أصلح, i.e. between the testator and the beneficiaries. (فَلا): the fāʾ links the apodosis, and لا is the lā of generic negation. (إِثْمَ): the noun of لا, indeclinable on the fatḥa. (عَلَيْهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of لا; the clause linked with the fāʾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are in the position of nominative as the khabar of من. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): إن, its noun and its two khabars; the clause gives the reason for the lifting of sin and has no grammatical position.

* Rhetoric:
1- Putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, to increase attention to its importance; had it followed the pattern of the preceding speech, He would have said: فإنما إثمه عليه وعلى من يبدله (its sin is upon him and upon whoever alters it).
That is for publicising and proclaiming the scandals of those who alter.
2- Majāz mursal (non-metaphorical trope) in His saying: خاف, which has come in the sense of supposition and expectation; the relation in this trope is causality, because it expresses the cause by the effect.

dervis-irab:133-133.t:
* I'rab:
(أَمْ): it may be connective (muttaṣila), conjoined to something omitted and implied, as though it were said:
"Do you claim Judaism for the prophets, or were you witnesses and present?" It may be disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa), meaning «بل», i.e. "you were not present when death came to Yaʿqūb"; «الشهداء» means those present, plural of «شاهد». It may also be merely for interrogation, meaning the hamza. (كُنْتُمْ): «كان» and its noun. (شُهَداءَ): its khabar (predicate). (إِذْ): an adverb for past [time], attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شهداء». (حَضَرَ): a past verb, and the clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (يَعْقُوبَ): a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الْمَوْتُ): a deferred fāʿil (agent). (إِذْ): an adverb, badal (substitute) from the first «إذ». (قالَ): a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the verbal clause is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (لِبَنِيهِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «قال». (ما تَعْبُدُونَ): «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi of «تعبدون»; «تعبدون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (مِنْ بَعْدِي): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (قالُوا): a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is resumptive. (نَعْبُدُ إِلهَكَ): the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech. (وَإِلهَ آبائِكَ): conjoined to «إلهك». (إِبْراهِيمَ): badal from «آبائك». (وَإِسْماعِيلَ وَإِسْحاقَ): conjoined to «إبراهيم». (إِلهاً): badal from «إلهك», or a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa), or accusative by specification (ʿalā al-ikhtiṣāṣ), to negate what might occur to the mind of a plurality of gods; so it was brought to ward off that misconception. (واحِداً): an adjective. (وَنَحْنُ): the wāw is either a conjunction — what follows it, being part of the answer, is conjoined to the first part, and the answer is composed of the two parts — or parenthetical, or circumstantial; «نحن» is a mubtadaʾ (subject). (لَهُ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «مسلمون». (مُسْلِمُونَ): khabar of «نحن».

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of Allah the Exalted (نَعْبُدُ إِلهَكَ وَإِلهَ آبائِكَ), to the end of the verse, there is an art of rhetoric called succession (al-iṭṭirād): the names of the addressee's forefathers flow successively for the speaker, arranged according to their order of birth. He passed over their nearest ancestor to their highest ancestor because he was the one who began the religion that is followed. There is also in it the art of equivalence (al-musāwāt), because the words for this meaning neither exceed it nor fall short of it. There is also in it beauty of exposition (ḥusn al-bayān), because it sets out the religion in the best exposition, so that no one hesitates in understanding it. There is also in it the art of guarding (al-iḥtirās): had he stopped at «آبائك», the soundness of the meaning would have been impaired, because "forefathers" in general covers everyone from the nearest father up to Ādam, and among the forefathers of Yaʿqūb, peace be upon him, are those whose religion need not be followed. So he guarded, by mentioning the badal, against what would be objected to the thing substituted for (al-mubdal minhu) had the speech been limited to it. So reflect and marvel.

dervis-irab:134-135.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حَنِيفاً): from «الحنف», with two fatḥas, which is inclining; its original use is for the feet, and it may be used for the hands. When ḥāʾ and nūn occur at the beginning of a verb, they indicate inclining and bending: from it is «الحنين إلى الوطن», yearning for the homeland, i.e. inclining to it and being drawn toward it; «حنا عليه», i.e. he was kind and inclined toward him; and «حنق عليه»: his belly clung to his back from pain.

* I'rab:
(تِلْكَ أُمَّةٌ): mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). (قَدْ خَلَتْ): the clause is an adjective of «أمة». (لَها): the preposition and its genitive noun are a fronted khabar. (ما): a deferred mubtadaʾ. (كَسَبَتْ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative «ما». (وَلَكُمْ ما كَسَبْتُمْ): conjoined to the previous clause. (وَلا تُسْئَلُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; «تسألون» is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is resumptive. (عَمَّا): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تسألون». (كانُوا): the clause is the ṣila of «ما». (يَعْمَلُونَ): the verbal clause is the khabar of «كانوا». (وَقالُوا): the wāw is resumptive, and «قالوا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent). (كُونُوا هُوداً): «كان», its noun and its khabar, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (أَوْ): a conjunction; the meaning of «أو» here is detailing (tafṣīl), and this is a case of al-laff wa-l-nashr (involution and evolution): the hearer refers to each party its own saying. (نَصارى): conjoined to «هودا». (تَهْتَدُوا): an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it occurs as the answer to the request. (قُلْ): an imperative verb, and the clause is resumptive. (بَلْ): a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction. (مِلَّةَ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, i.e. "we follow", or accusative by incitement (al-ighrāʾ), with the implied "hold fast to". (إِبْراهِيمَ): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (حَنِيفاً): ḥāl (circumstantial) from «إبراهيم». (وَما): the wāw is a conjunction, and «ما» is negating. (كانَ): a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "he". (مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to its omitted khabar.

dervis-irab:136-136.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْأَسْباطِ): plural of «سبط», with kasra on the sīn, which is the daughter's child, as opposed to «الحفيد», which is the son's child.

* I'rab:
(قُولُوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn because its imperfect is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (آمَنَّا): a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (بِاللَّهِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «آمنا». (وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنا): conjoined to «الله», and the clause «أنزل إلينا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative «ما». (وَما أُنْزِلَ إِلى إِبْراهِيمَ وَإِسْماعِيلَ وَإِسْحاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْباطِ): also conjoined. (وَما): also conjoined. (أُوتِيَ): the clause is the ṣila of «ما». (مُوسى): nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (وَعِيسى): conjoined to «موسى». (وَما أُوتِيَ النَّبِيُّونَ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ): also conjoined. (لا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ): the verbal clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «منهم» is an adjective of «أحد». (وَنَحْنُ): the wāw is circumstantial, and «نحن» is a mubtadaʾ (subject). (لَهُ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «مسلمون». (مُسْلِمُونَ): khabar (predicate) of «نحن», and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

* Rhetoric:
An indefinite noun occurring in the context of negation conveys generality in its wording, so that its singular is treated as a plural in covering the individuals; that is why «بين» could properly be used with it, though «بين» is only used between two things [or more].

dervis-irab:137-137.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الشقاق), with kasra on the shīn: disagreement, because each of the two parties in dispute is on a side (shiqq) other than the side of the other. In the language it has three meanings that do not depart from the first notion; the second is enmity, which is the offspring of disagreement; and the third is going astray, which is the mark of those who contend and dispute, because they go along with their whims. Among the curious things about shīn and qāf is that when they occur as the first and second radicals of a word, they indicate this meaning or something close to it: «الشّقّ» is a split, and «الاشتقاق» is splitting a word off from a word. This is something no one preceded us in drawing out.

* I'rab:
(فَإِنْ آمَنُوا): the fāʾ is resumptive, «إن» is a jussive conditional particle, and «آمنوا» is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (بِمِثْلِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) «آمنوا». (ما): a relative noun in the position of the genitive by annexation. (آمَنْتُمْ): the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (فَقَدِ): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and «قد» is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). (اهْتَدَوْا): a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the verbal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا): conjoined to «فإن آمنوا». (فَإِنَّما): the fāʾ is linking, and «إنما» is a restraining particle and the restrained [particle] (kāffa wa-makfūfa). (هُمْ): mubtadaʾ (subject). (فِي شِقاقٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of «هم». (فَسَيَكْفِيكَهُمُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction of immediate sequence (taʿqīb); the benefit of the immediate sequence is to signal that the sufficiency comes immediately after their dissension. The sīn is a particle of the future, and it is nearer in deferment than «سوف», i.e. in the near future. «يكفي» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and the hāʾ is the second mafʿūl bihi. (اللَّهُ): fāʿil. (وَهُوَ): the wāw is resumptive, and «هو» is a mubtadaʾ. (السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ): two khabars; multiple khabars are permissible.

dervis-irab:138-139.t:
* Vocabulary:
(صِبْغَةَ): with kasra on the ṣād, a maṣdar of manner (maṣdar hayʾa) from «صبغ» (to dye). What is meant by it here is the religion; it is called a dye because its effect appears on the one who embraces it.

* I'rab:
(صِبْغَةَ اللَّهِ): an emphasizing maṣdar (verbal noun), so it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. In it is an allusion to the self-evident truths of the mind that Allah has placed in people. (وَمَنْ): the wāw is a conjunction, and «من» is an interrogative noun — the interrogation here has departed to the meaning of negation — in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (أَحْسَنُ): khabar (predicate). (مِنَ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أحسن». (صِبْغَةَ): tamyīz (specification). (وَنَحْنُ): the wāw is a conjunction, and «نحن» is a mubtadaʾ. (لَهُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «عابدون». (عابِدُونَ): khabar of «نحن». (قُلْ): an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is "you". (أَتُحَاجُّونَنا): the hamza is for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī); «تحاجون» is an imperfect verb, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the pronoun shared [by speaker and others] («نا») is in the position of the accusative as the object. (فِي اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «تحاجوننا». (وَهُوَ): the wāw is circumstantial, and «هو» is a mubtadaʾ. (رَبُّنا): khabar, and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَرَبُّكُمْ): conjoined to «ربنا». (وَلَنا): the wāw is a conjunction, and «لنا», the preposition and its genitive noun, is a fronted khabar. (أَعْمالُنا): a deferred mubtadaʾ, and the clause is circumstantial. (وَلَكُمْ أَعْمالُكُمْ): conjoined to the previous clause. (وَنَحْنُ): the wāw is circumstantial, and «نحن» is a mubtadaʾ. (لَهُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «مخلصون». (مُخْلِصُونَ): khabar of «نحن», and the clause is also circumstantial.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «صبغة الله» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): He likened the religion of Islam to dye, omitted the thing likened and kept the thing it is likened to. Aʿshā Hamdān seized on both the meaning and the wording when he said:
وكل أناس لهم صبغة ... وصبغة همدان خير الصّبغ
(Every people has its dye, and the dye of Hamdān is the best of dyes.)
صبغنا على ذاك أولادنا ... فأكرم بصبغتنا في الصّبغ
(We dyed our children with that — how noble is our dye among dyes!)

dervis-irab:140-140.t:
* I'rab:
(أَمْ): a connective (muttaṣila) conjunction balancing the hamza, or disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) meaning «بل». (تَقُولُونَ): an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (إِنَّ إِبْراهِيمَ): «إن» and its noun. (وَإِسْماعِيلَ وَإِسْحاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْباطَ): nouns conjoined in sequence to «إبراهيم»; the clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (كانُوا): «كان» and its noun. (هُوداً): khabar (predicate) of «كان». (أَوْ): a conjunction. (نَصارى): conjoined to «هودا»; the verbal clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of «إن». (قُلْ): an imperative verb whose fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "you". (أَأَنْتُمْ): the hamza is for disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and «أنتم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject). (أَعْلَمُ): khabar. (أَمِ اللَّهُ): conjoined to «أنتم». (وَمَنْ): the wāw is resumptive, and «من» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ. (أَظْلَمُ): khabar. (مِمَّنْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أظلم»; the clause is resumptive, brought to allude to their concealment of Allah's testimony, and this has always been the habit of the Jews. (كَتَمَ): a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "he", and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (شَهادَةً): mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (عِنْدَهُ): the adverb is attached to an omitted adjective of «شهادة». (مِنَ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted second adjective of «شهادة»; you say "This is a testimony from me for so-and-so" when you testify for him. You may also attach it to «كتم», but then you must assume an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "whoever conceals, from the servants of Allah, a testimony he has". (وَمَا): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive, and «ما» is the Ḥijāzī negating «ما», which governs like «ليس». (اللَّهُ): its noun. (بِغافِلٍ): the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and «غافل» is genitive by the bāʾ in form, in the position of the accusative as the khabar of «ما». (عَمَّا): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «غافل». (تَعْمَلُونَ): an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila of «ما».

dervis-irab:284-286.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الوسع): what is within a person's capacity and does not constrain him.
(الطاقة): effort and ability. It is a maṣdar (verbal noun) that has come with the additional letters dropped; the original is الإطاقة.
(الإصر): the burden [Translator's note: the source has «العب», presumably «العبء»]. أصره means he confined him, and its conjugation class is ضرب (yafʿilu). What is meant by it is the arduous obligations under which the body staggers and from which the soul is exhausted.

* I'rab:
(لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ) is a resumptive statement with no grammatical position, brought to prove His words «والله بما تعلمون عليم» [Translator's note: thus in the source; the wording of the preceding verse is «بما تعملون»]. Non-rational beings were given precedence over the rational ones by using «ما», because they are more numerous.
The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (ما) is a relative noun, the postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); (في السموات) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted [verb] that has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; and (ما في الأرض) is conjoined to «ما في السموات». (وَإِنْ تُبْدُوا ما فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ): the wāw is resumptive, and the statement is resumptive, brought to set out the obligation. Being taken to account concerns the passing thoughts from which a person has no escape [Translator's note: thus in the source]. Someone versified the levels of intention, saying:
مراتب القصد خمس: هاجس ذكروا ... وخاطر فحديث النفس فاستمعا
يليه همّ فعزم كلها رفعت ... سوى الأخير ففيه الأخذ قد وقعا
(The levels of intention are five, so listen: a fleeting notion (hājis), as they mentioned, then a passing thought (khāṭir), then self-talk (ḥadīth al-nafs); after it comes inclination (hamm), then resolve (ʿazm). All of them have been lifted except the last, for in it accountability occurs.)
The details of this are set out at length in the extensive works; whoever wishes may consult them.
(إن) is conditional; (تبدوا) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause has no grammatical position; (ما) is a relative noun, the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and (في أنفسكم) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted [verb] that has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (أَوْ تُخْفُوهُ) is conjoined to (تبدوا), and the hāʾ is the direct object. (يُحاسِبْكُمْ بِهِ اللَّهُ): the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive; the kāf is an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative as direct object; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (يحاسبكم); (الله) is the agent; and the clause has no grammatical position. (فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ): the fāʾ is resumptive and (يغفر) is an imperfect verb in the nominative, i.e. "then He forgives". The fāʾ may also be a conjunction and (يغفر) an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by being conjoined to (يغفر) [Translator's note: thus in the source; it is conjoined to يحاسبكم]. Both readings are among the Seven. It was also read in the accusative, with «أن» implied, so that from this a maṣdar in the nominative is formed, conjoined to an imagined [maṣdar], i.e. "there will be a reckoning, then forgiveness". On this basis the verse of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī is explained:
فإن يهلك أبو قابوس يهلك ... ربيع الناس والشهر الحرام
ونأخذ بعده بذناب عيش ... أجب الظهر ليس له سنام
(If Abū Qābūs perishes, the spring of the people and the sacred month perish; and after him we shall hold on to the tail end of a life with a cut-off back, having no hump.)
It is narrated with (نأخذ) in the jussive, the nominative and the accusative. However, Sībawayh considered the accusative weak, because the reader al-Zaʿfarānī is not one of the Seven, and because it is affirmative [Translator's note: the source mixes the reading of the verse with Sībawayh's judgement on the line of poetry; translated as written]. The exact wording of Sībawayh is: «The accusative may be permitted in the affirmative under poetic necessity, but it is weak in speech». (لمن) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (يغفر), and the clause (يشاء) is a ṣila. (وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشاءُ) is conjoined to what precedes. (وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (الله) is the mubtadaʾ; (على كل شيء) is attached to (قدير); and (قدير) is the khabar of «الله». (آمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ) is a resumptive clause brought to report that the Messenger ﷺ believed in everything Allah made obligatory on the servants — prayer, zakat, fasting, pilgrimage, divorce, the oath of abstention (īlāʾ), menstruation and jihad — and in the stories of the prophets mentioned in the surah. (آمن الرسول) is a verb and agent; (بما) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (آمن); the clause (أنزل) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun, and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it"; (إليه) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (أنزل); and (من ربه) is a preposition and its genitive noun also attached to (أنزل), or you may attach it to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "while it has come down from his Lord", because it guarantees happiness for human society. (وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ): the wāw may be a conjunction and (المؤمنون) conjoined to (الرسول), in which case the pause is here. This i'rab is supported by the reading of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: «وآمن المؤمنون», where he made the verb overt. The wāw may also be resumptive and (المؤمنون) a first mubtadaʾ. (كُلٌّ آمَنَ): (كل) is a second mubtadaʾ; the clause (آمن) is its khabar; and the nominal clause is the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ, namely (المؤمنون), the linking pronoun being omitted — on the second view. On the first view the clause «كل آمن» is resumptive. Beginning with (كل), though it is indefinite, is permissible because it is intended as being in construct, i.e. "each one of them", the tanwīn being a substitute for the omitted word. (بِاللَّهِ وَمَلائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (آمن), and what follows is conjoined to it. (لا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ): this clause is the speech reported (maqūl) of an omitted verb of saying, and the clause of saying is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "saying: we make no distinction". (لا) is negating; (نفرق) is an imperfect verb in the nominative; (بين) is an adverb of place attached to (نفرق); (أحد) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and (من رسله) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of (أحد). He did not say "between individuals" (آحاد), because (أحد) covers both the one and the plural, as in His words, the Exalted, «فما منكم من أحد عنه حاجزين», where it is described with a plural because it has that meaning; for that reason (بين) is prefixed to it. A delightful detailed treatment of (أحد) will come in this book. (وَقالُوا سَمِعْنا وَأَطَعْنا): the wāw is resumptive; (قالوا) is a past verb; the wāw is the agent; and the two clauses (سمعنا) and (أطعنا) are the speech reported. (غُفْرانَكَ رَبَّنا): a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) with its governing verb implied. Of this is their saying غفرانك لا كفرانك, i.e. "we seek Your forgiveness and do not disbelieve in You". (ربنا) is a vocative in construct from which the vocative particle has been omitted. (وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ): the wāw is a conjunction, and what it is conjoined to is omitted, falling within the scope of the saying, i.e.:
"saying: from You is the beginning and to You is the return". (إليك) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and (المصير) is the postponed mubtadaʾ. (لا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْساً إِلَّا وُسْعَها) is a resumptive clause brought to remove hardship from souls and to make clear that accountability is restricted to what is within capacity and ability; anything beyond that, of the passing thoughts and notions of the soul, is not subject to reckoning. By this the difficulty that troubled some commentators is removed, for they said: error and forgetfulness are forgiven and not held to account, so what is the meaning of praying for that, when it almost amounts to seeking what is already obtained? (لا) is negating; (يكلف) is an imperfect verb in the nominative; (الله) is its agent; (نفسا) is the first direct object; (إلا) is an instrument of restriction; and (وسعها) is the second direct object. (لَها ما كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْها مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ): the clause explains what He stated summarily in His words «وسعها»; this will be set out in the section on Rhetoric.
(لها) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (ما) is a relative noun, the postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause (كسبت) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; and (وعليها ما اكتسبت) is conjoined to what precedes, its i'rab having been mentioned. (رَبَّنا لا تُؤاخِذْنا): (ربنا) is a vocative in construct; (لا) is prohibitive, its meaning here being supplication; (تؤاخذنا) is an imperfect verb in the jussive by (لا); (نا) is the direct object and the agent is "you"; the clause falls within the scope of the preceding saying; and the vocative clause is resumptive. (إِنْ نَسِينا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنا): (إن) is conditional; (نسينا) is a past verb in the position of the jussive as protasis; (نا) is the agent; (أو أخطأنا) is conjoined to it; the apodosis is omitted, i.e. "then do not take us to account"; and the conditional clause with its apodosis is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (رَبَّنا وَلا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنا إِصْراً): its i'rab has preceded. Placing the vocative between the two conjoined items is to show the extent of the beseeching and the plea for mercy, the utmost humility, and the acknowledgement of Allah's lordship, Glorified is He. (كَما حَمَلْتَهُ): it has preceded in a construction like this that it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq or a ḥāl, (ما) being maṣdariyya in either case. (عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِنا): (على الذين) is attached to «بجملة» [Translator's note: thus in the source; presumably «بحملته», i.e. to (حملته)]; and (من قبلنا) is attached to an omitted [verb that is the] ṣila of (الذين), i.e. "who were of the past nations". (رَبَّنا وَلا تُحَمِّلْنا ما لا طاقَةَ لَنا بِهِ) is conjoined to what precedes. (ما) is the second direct object of (تحملنا); (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (طاقة) is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative; (لنا) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (طاقة); and (به) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of (لا). (وَاعْفُ عَنَّا): a supplication conjoined to what precedes, and (عنا) is attached to (اعف). (وَاغْفِرْ لَنا): another conjunction. (وَارْحَمْنا): another conjunction. (أَنْتَ مَوْلانا): (أنت) is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (مولانا) is the khabar. The clause is resumptive, serving as an acknowledgement to Allah the Exalted that He is the Master (al-Mawlā), because مولى is a mīmī maṣdar from ولي يلي. The meaning is: You are our Master; in You we take refuge, to You we resort, and on You we rely. It is the right of the master to help those under his charge, to protect them when they fear, to surround them with his care and to guard them with his watchfulness. (فَانْصُرْنا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكافِرِينَ): the fāʾ is causal, and the clause is brought to give the reason for what precedes, for His being our Master is a cause [Translator's note: the word «سبب» is repeated in the source] for seeking help from Him. (على القوم) is attached to (انصرنا). The word (القوم) is mentioned for generality, because victory over individuals does not entail victory over the whole; so this false impression was removed by mentioning the word (القوم). (الكافرين) is an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
In these verses [Translator's note: the source says «الأبيات», "lines of poetry", presumably for «الآيات»] there is a group of rhetorical devices, which we summarise as follows:
1- Good closing (ḥusn al-khitām): its discussion has preceded. It befits Surat al-Baqara — since it contains numerous rulings and encompasses legislation and clarification — that its closing should take up thanks to the Bestower of favours who favoured man with reason so that he may think. It is the right of the one favoured to acknowledge the one who granted him blessings by thanking Him; and it is the right of the One who set up before him the sanctuaries of thought and the displays of creation that he should think about them and reflect on them, and bear witness to the One who originated them with might and power and uniqueness in oneness, which manifests itself on the hearts of the believers. By thought alone does man live, and by thought he infers His existence. How beautiful is his saying ﷺ: «The surah in which the Cow is mentioned is the pavilion (fusṭāṭ) of the Qur'an, so learn it, for learning it is a blessing and leaving it is a regret, and the baṭala cannot cope with it». It was said: "And who are the baṭala?" He said: "The sorcerers." The meaning of its being the pavilion of the Qur'an is that it contains most of the matters of religion, fundamentals and branches, and guidance to what brings a good livelihood in this world and success in the Hereafter.
2- Correspondence (al-muqābala): in His words «لها ما كسبت وعليها ما اكتسبت», for He set in antithesis (ṭābaqa) لها and عليها, and كسبت and اكتسبت. The first verb is particular to good and the second verb is particular to evil, for in iktisāb there is exertion; and evil is something the soul craves and inclines to by nature, unlike good, which descends upon the soul as the outpouring of Allah's blessings descends, and as certainty dawns in the soul —
a dawning that made believers of the Illuminationist philosophers, and made al-Ghazālī and Descartes penitent devotees...

* Benefits:
1- (بَيْنَ) is an adverb of place or time that is put in construct only with something multiple. In the verse it has been put in construct with «أحد» because it is a noun for whoever is fit to be addressed, in which singular, dual and plural are alike, just as masculine and feminine are alike in it. So the meaning of "we make no distinction between any one of the messengers" is: we make no distinction among a group of the messengers. The linguists differed: is (بين) repeated after occurring between two conjoined items or not?
For example: "I sat between Zayd and ʿAmr". Can one say: "I sat between Zayd and between ʿAmr"?
Some permitted that, with (بين) being for emphasis.
Among the splendid subtle points is that after it one conjoins only with the wāw; one does not say:
"I sat between Zayd, then ʿAmr" (with fa-). An objection was raised to this from the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays at the opening of his Muʿallaqa:
فقا نبك من ذكرى حبيب ومنزل ... بسقط اللوى بين الدّخول فحومل
(Halt, you two, and let us weep at the memory of a beloved and an abode at the edge of the sand-dune, between al-Dakhūl, then Ḥawmal.) [Translator's note: «فقا» is presumably a misprint for «قفا».]
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: the correct thing is to say "between al-Dakhūl and Ḥawmal", because one does not conjoin with the fāʾ in a "between" construction, since it indicates sequence. Yaʿqūb ibn al-Sikkīt said in defence of Imruʾ al-Qays: it is with a muḍāf omitted, the implied form being "between the people of al-Dakhūl, then Ḥawmal". Al-Murādī said: it is by treating it as multiple in effect, because al-Dakhūl is a place that may comprise multiple places, as you say "I sat among (بين) al-Kūfa", meaning among its houses and places. [Translator's note: the source reads «لا يجوز أن يشتمل» ("may not comprise"), which contradicts the argument; presumably «يجوز».]
Further, the vowel of the nūn may be lengthened so that it becomes «بينا» and «بينما», and it is then put in construct with clauses. Abū Dhuʾayb said:
بينا تعنقه الكماة وروغه ... يوما أتيح له جريء سلفع
(While the armoured warriors were embracing him and he was dodging, one day a bold, fierce one was destined for him.)

dervis-irab:183-185.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الصِّيامُ): linguistically, abstaining from food, drink, speech, sexual relations and travelling. It has two maṣdars: صوم and صيام. صامت الريح: the wind became still; صامت الشمس: the sun reached the meridian, i.e. it was at the middle of the sky; صامت الدابة: the riding animal held back from running. Al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī said:
خيل صيام وخيل غير صائمة ... تحت العجاج وأخرى تعلك اللجما
(Horses standing still, and horses not standing still, beneath the dust of battle, and others champing on the bits.)
i.e. holding back from running. Then Islam specified it for its well-known meaning.
(رمضان): originally the maṣdar of رمِض, said when something is burned by the scorching heat (الرمضاء); [the word شهر] was annexed to it, it was made a proper name, and it is a diptote because of being a proper name and the added alif and nūn. The connection between its meaning and the worship of the one fasting is clear. The Arabs annex the word شهر to each of the names of the months beginning with rāʾ, like ربيع and رمضان, and only رجب is excepted from that: they do not annex the word شهر to it. Someone versified this, saying:
ولا تضف شهرا إلى اسم شهر ... إلّا لما أوّله الرّا فادر
واستثن منه رجبا فيمتنع ... لأنه فيما رووه قد سمع
(Do not annex "month" to the name of a month, except to one whose first letter is rāʾ — so know it; and except Rajab from that, for it is not allowed, since that, in what they have related, is what has been heard.)
The question is in any case disputed, so hold to what is most cautious.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has been given before. (كُتِبَ): a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and it is passive, i.e. it was made obligatory. (عَلَيْكُمُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) كتب. (الصِّيامُ): the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of كتب. (كَما كُتِبَ): its i'rab has been given before; the preposition and its genitive noun are a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), or a ḥāl (circumstantial), as Sībawayh chose. (عَلَى الَّذِينَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to كتب. (مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted [verb] that has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause). The vocative clause and what follows it is resumptive, brought to state the legislation of fasting. (لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ): the clause of hope is circumstantial, and the clause تتقون is the khabar (predicate) of لعل. (أَيَّاماً): apparently an adverb attached to الصيام, but that would separate the maṣdar from its complement, which the grammarians have forbidden; therefore we prefer that it be accusative by an omitted verb indicated by what precedes it, the implied form being: "fast days". (مَعْدُوداتٍ): naʿt of الأيام; the sign of its accusative is the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural; the tanwīn conveys fewness, as an easing for those charged with obligations. (فَمَنْ): the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the disclosing fāʾ), and من is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). (كانَ): a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he" (هو). (مِنْكُمْ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (مَرِيضاً): the khabar of كان. (أَوْ): a conjunction. (عَلى سَفَرٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted [word] conjoined to «مريضا»; the sense of being upon (al-istiʿlāʾ) is beautiful here, i.e. mounted upon travel, fully engaged in it; so it is also a ḥāl. (فَعِدَّةٌ): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and عدة is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "then upon him is a number", or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, implied as "then the ruling is a number"; the nominal clause joined to the fāʾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من. (مِنْ أَيَّامٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted naʿt of عدة. (أُخَرَ): naʿt of أيام; the sign of its genitive is the fatḥa because it is a diptote, and its ruling will come under Benefits. (وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted, fronted khabar. (يُطِيقُونَهُ): an imperfect verb; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila, i.e. they undertake it with effort and hardship. (فِدْيَةٌ): the postponed mubtadaʾ. (طَعامُ مِسْكِينٍ): a corresponding badal (substitute) of فدية, and مسكين is muḍāf ilayhi. (فَمَنْ): the fāʾ is resumptive, and من is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ. (تَطَوَّعَ): a past verb; it is the protasis, and its fāʿil is latent, implied as "he". (خَيْراً): accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. by adding to the amount mentioned for the ransom; you may also parse it as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, so that it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) whose naʿt stands in for it, i.e. a good volunteering. (فَهُوَ): the fāʾ links the apodosis because it is a nominal clause, and هو is a mubtadaʾ. (خَيْرٌ): khabar. (لَهُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to خير, because it is an elative (ism tafḍīl) that has come irregularly; the nominal clause joined to the fāʾ is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من. (وَأَنْ تَصُومُوا): the wāw is resumptive, brought to establish the superiority [of fasting]; أن and what falls within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar, mubtadaʾ. (خَيْرٌ): its khabar. (لَكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to خير. (أَنْ) [Translator's note: so in the source; the particle in the verse is إِنْ]: conditional. (كُنْتُمْ): a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis, and the tāʾ is its noun. (تَعْلَمُونَ): the verbal clause is in the position of accusative as the khabar of كنتم; the apodosis is omitted, and examples of this have been given before. The conditional clause explains the declarative one, as if He said: He has legislated all these rulings for you out of preference for your good, so if you want good, do them and do not fall short in them. (شَهْرُ رَمَضانَ): the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, and رمضان is muḍāf ilayhi. (الَّذِي): naʿt of شهر. (أُنْزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْآنُ): the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila; القرآن is the nāʾib fāʿil. (هُدىً): ḥāl, i.e. guiding. (لِلنَّاسِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to هدى, or are a naʿt of هدى. (وَبَيِّناتٍ): conjoined to هدى, so it is also a ḥāl. (مِنَ الْهُدى): naʿt of بينات. (وَالْفُرْقانِ): conjoined to الهدى, i.e. that which distinguishes between truth and falsehood. (فَمَنْ): the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, i.e. "if you wish to know the ruling legislated about it"; من is a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ. (شَهِدَ): a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; its fāʿil is latent, referring to من. (مِنْكُمُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (الشَّهْرَ): accusative as an adverb (ʿalā l-ẓarfiyya); it cannot be a mafʿūl bihi, because the resident and the traveller are both witnesses of the month. (فَلْيَصُمْهُ): the fāʾ links the apodosis because the clause is a request (ṭalabiyya); the lām is the lām of command, and يصم is an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām. The hāʾ is the pronoun of the adverb; it is not accusative as an adverb and cannot be a mafʿūl bihi, so it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "let him fast in it". The request clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من. (وَمَنْ): the wāw is a conjunction; من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (كانَ): a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis; its noun is a latent pronoun, implied as "he". (مَرِيضاً): the khabar of كان. (أَوْ عَلى سَفَرٍ): conjoined to «مريضا»; this has been discussed before, so refresh your acquaintance with it. (فَعِدَّةٌ): the fāʾ links the apodosis, and عدة is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "then upon him is a number"; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. (مِنْ أَيَّامٍ): attached to an omitted naʿt of عدة. (أُخَرَ): naʿt of أيام, genitive with the fatḥa because it is a diptote; its ruling will come. (يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ): an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is causal (taʿlīl), as will come under Rhetoric. (بِكُمُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يريد. (الْيُسْرَ): mafʿūl bihi. (وَلا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ): the clause is conjoined to the preceding one. (وَلِتُكْمِلُوا): the wāw is a conjunction, and the lām is the lām of causation (lām al-taʿlīl); تكملوا [Translator's note: the source has «تكلموا», a misprint for «تكملوا»] is an imperfect verb, subjunctive by an implied أن after it; the lām and its genitive are attached to an omitted verb, i.e. "He legislated". (الْعِدَّةَ): mafʿūl bihi. (وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا): conjoined to His saying لتكملوا. (اللَّهُ) [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; in the verse it is اللَّهَ]: the Name of Majesty is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "to Allah"; you may also parse it as a mafʿūl bihi, on the basis of تكبروا being made to include the meaning of تحمدوا ("praise"); the proof of this is His saying (عَلى ما هَداكُمْ), for transitivity with the preposition of "being upon" (عَلى) belongs only to praise. ما is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar in the genitive by على; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تكبروا, i.e. for His guiding you. (وَلَعَلَّكُمْ): conjoined to what precedes; لعل and its noun. (تَشْكُرُونَ): the clause is the khabar of لعل.

* Rhetoric:
Involution and evolution (al-laff wa-l-nashr) in His saying, Exalted be He: «يريد الله بكم اليسر» to the end.
Here it appears like a spell of magic, with which the eloquent person cannot choose to take or leave, and few notice it. His saying «لتكملوا العدة» is the reason for the command to observe the number [of days]; His saying «ولتكبروا الله» is the reason for the command to make up [missed days]; and His saying «ولعلكم تشكرون» is the reason for the concession and the easing. This has been discussed before, and we will expand on it further, saying:
It is of two kinds: the first is for the evolution (nashr) to follow the order of the involution (laff); the second is for it not to follow the order of the involution, relying in it on the hearer's intelligence and taste. Examples of it that captivate minds will come.

* Benefits:
(أُخَرَ) is of two kinds:
- The plural of أخرى, the feminine of آخَر; it is an elative that is a diptote for two reasons: being an adjective and ʿadl (deviation from its proper form). The meaning of ʿadl is that it deviated from the alif and lām; that is because it is an elative, and the elative has three states:
a- joined to al-;
b- joined to the preposition من;
c- annexed.
Since أخر is not joined to anything and is not annexed, its deviation from the alif and lām is presumed.
- The plural of أخرى in the sense of آخِرة ("last"), which is a triptote because the cause of ʿadl is absent.

A necessary discussion:
The exegetes differed sharply over the interpretation of His saying, Exalted be He: «وعلى الذين يطيقونه» to the end — a difference there is no room to elaborate on. So we shall cite what they said by way of brief reference, then offer what has occurred to us; and Allah is the One who inspires to what is right.

The view of abrogation:
Some of them said that the ruling in it is abrogated by the verse after it, «فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه», and the concession in it is for the sick person and the traveller. This is what Imam al-Ṭabarī chose in his great exegesis, and al-Zamakhsharī related it in his Kashshāf and Abū Ḥayyān in al-Baḥr, explicitly stating that this is the view of most exegetes.
