However, Imam al-Ṭabarī also related the view of those who said: that was not abrogated; it is a ruling established from the time this verse was revealed until the Hour.

Ibn Kathīr's opinion:
Ibn Kathīr was cautious, saying, after summarising the views of the exegetes before him: the upshot of the matter is that abrogation is established with regard to the healthy resident, by making fasting obligatory upon him; as for the decrepit old man who cannot fast, he may break the fast and has no making-up upon him, because he has no state to which he will come in which he could make it up.

Al-Zamakhsharī hesitates:
Al-Zamakhsharī hesitated between the view of abrogation and interpreting the verse on the supposition: «and those who undertake it with effort on their part and with difficulty — they are the old men and old women — and the ruling for these is breaking the fast and the ransom»; on this view it is not abrogated.

And the problem of adding لا:
Moreover, those who hold that it is not abrogated took various approaches in interpreting the verse. Some of them stated explicitly that it is on the supposition of the omission of the negative «لا», which is intended. They related from Ibn ʿAbbās his saying: «There is no concession except for one who cannot bear fasting», and from ʿAṭāʾ: «He is the old man who cannot [fast] with effort, nor with any degree of effort; as for one who can [fast] with effort, let him fast, and he has no excuse for leaving it.» Abū Ḥayyān said in al-Baḥr: «Some of them permitted «لا» to be omitted, so that the verb is negated, its implied form being: «وعلى الذين لا يطيقونه» — «لا» was omitted while being intended.»

Abū Ḥayyān declares those who hold the omission to be wrong:
Abū Ḥayyān went on, commenting: «Implying «لا» is wrong, because it is a place of despair [Translator's note: so in the source, «لانه مكان اليأس»]; and al-Jalāl followed that.»

The jurists do not differ over the permissibility of breaking the fast for the old man and the sick:
We know of no disagreement among the jurists over the permissibility of breaking the fast and paying the ransom for the decrepit old man and the sick person whose recovery is not hoped for. But they differed over the nursing and the pregnant woman by analogy with the decrepit old man: Imam al-Shāfiʿī held that the ransom is due, by analogy with the decrepit old man, and made making-up obligatory upon them together with the ransom; whereas Imam Abū Ḥanīfa made making-up, not the ransom, obligatory upon the pregnant and the nursing woman — if they fear for the child — and rejected the analogy with the decrepit old man, because making-up is not obligatory upon him.

We consider the omission of لا unlikely:
However, we consider it unlikely that لا is omitted here while being intended. The verse is one of the verses of legislation and rulings, and the verb in it is affirmative; interpreting it on the supposition of an omitted «لا» would overturn the affirmation with a negation. Had the ransom been upon those who cannot bear it, the negative particle would have taken its place in the text of the legal ruling, and would not have left us room to differ over its interpretation between the two contradictories of affirmation and negation. As for الطاقة, in Arabic it is the utmost effort and the limit of endurance, and the Qur'an's use of الطاقة as a noun and as a verb indicates that it is something that exhausts effort and the capacity of endurance, as its three verses testify, all of them from Sūrat al-Baqara:
1- «قالوا لا طاقة لنا اليوم بجالوت وجنوده».
2- «ربنا ولا تحملنا مالا طاقة لنا به».
3- «وعلى الذين يطيقونه فدية طعام مسكين».
So we realise that the matter, in bearing the fast, is that if it exceeds capacity and passes into what cannot be borne, the obligation falls away, because there is no legal obligation to do what cannot be borne, and Allah, Glorified be He, does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.
3- [Translator's note: this numbering is so in the source.] The Arabs may imbue a word with the meaning of another word, so that it is given its ruling; this is called taḍmīn (implication). Thus «لتكبدوا» [Translator's note: so in the source, for «لتكبروا»] was made to include the meaning of «تحمدوا». From it is the saying of al-Farazdaq:
كيف تراني قالبا مجني؟ ... قد قتل الله زيادا عنّي
(How do you see me now, turning my shield over? Allah has killed Ziyād away from me.)
He made «قتل» include the meaning of «صرف» («turning away»); and this is frequent in their speech.

dervis-irab:141-142.t:
* I'rab:
(تِلْكَ): a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). (أُمَّةٌ): khabar (predicate). (قَدْ): a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). (خَلَتْ): a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied on the alif, which was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "she"; the verbal clause is an adjective of «أمة». (لَها): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar. (ما): a relative noun, a deferred mubtadaʾ. (كَسَبَتْ): the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of «ما». (وَلَكُمْ ما كَسَبْتُمْ): conjoined to the clause before it. (وَلا): the wāw is a conjunction and «لا» is negating. (تُسْئَلُونَ): a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (عَمَّا): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «تسألون». (كانُوا): «كان» and its noun. (يَعْمَلُونَ): the verbal clause is the khabar of «كانوا», and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. (سَيَقُولُ): the sīn is a particle of the future, and «يقول» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). (السُّفَهاءُ): fāʿil. (مِنَ النَّاسِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السفهاء». Those who say it are the Jews, marked by lightness of mind; the clause is resumptive, brought to indicate the continuance of their error and foolishness. (ما): an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ. (وَلَّاهُمْ): a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar of «ما», and the whole clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (عَنْ قِبْلَتِهِمُ): both attached to «ولاهم». (الَّتِي): a relative noun in the position of the genitive, an adjective of «قبلتهم». (كانُوا): «كان» and its noun, and the clause is the ṣila of «التي». (عَلَيْها): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar of «كانوا», i.e. "devoted to it in prayer", and it is Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). (قُلْ): an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you". (لِلَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (الْمَشْرِقُ): a deferred mubtadaʾ. (وَالْمَغْرِبُ): conjoined to «المشرق». (يَهْدِي): an imperfect verb, nominative, whose fāʿil is a latent pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted. (مِنَ): a relative noun, the object of «يهدي»; and the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of speech. [Translator's note: so in the source; the clause meant is evidently «لله المشرق والمغرب».] (يَشاءُ): an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "he", and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (إِلى صِراطٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يهدي». (مُسْتَقِيمٍ): an adjective of «صراط».

dervis-irab:143-143.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَسَطاً): choice, just, attested as upright by knowledge and action; masculine and feminine are the same in it. The choice part is the middle only because defects seep into the extremities, while the middles remain protected. Abū Tammām glimpsed the heaven of this meaning and said:
كانت هي الوسط المحميّ فاكتنفت ... بها الحوادث حتى أصبحت طرفا
(It was the protected middle, but misfortunes closed in around it until it became an edge.)

* I'rab:
(وَكَذلِكَ): the wāw is resumptive, the kāf is a preposition, and the demonstrative is in the position of the genitive by the kāf; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "like that making, We made you". (جَعَلْناكُمْ): a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and the first object of «جعلنا». (أُمَّةً): the second object of «جعلنا». (وَسَطاً): an adjective of «أمة». (لِتَكُونُوا): the lām is the lām of causation (lām al-taʿlīl), and «تكونوا» is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by «أن» optionally implied after the lām of causation; the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the wāw is its noun. (شُهَداءَ): its khabar (predicate). (عَلَى النَّاسِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «شهداء». (وَيَكُونَ): conjoined to «تكونوا». (الرَّسُولُ): the noun of «يكون». (عَلَيْكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «شهيدا». (شَهِيداً): khabar of «يكون». (وَما): the wāw is a conjunction, and «ما» is negating. (جَعَلْنَا): a verb and its fāʿil. (الْقِبْلَةَ): the first object of «جعلنا». (الَّتِي): a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the second object of «جعلنا». (كُنْتَ): «كان» and its noun. (عَلَيْها): the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar of «كنت», and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of «التي». More on the i'rab of this verse will come in the section on Benefits. (إِلَّا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (لِنَعْلَمَ): the lām is the lām of causation, and «نعلم» is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied «أن»; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "we". The position of «لنعلم» is mafʿūl li-ajlihi, so it is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh) from the most general of causes. (مَنْ): a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the object of «نعلم». (يَتَّبِعُ الرَّسُولَ): the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun, and «الرسول» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (مِمَّنْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «نعلم», which includes the meaning of "We distinguish". (يَنْقَلِبُ): the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (عَلى عَقِبَيْهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "turning back on his heels". (وَإِنْ): the wāw is circumstantial, and «إن» is lightened from the heavy [«إنّ»]; its noun is omitted, i.e. "while the situation is that it…". (كانَتْ): a defective past verb whose noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "the turning toward it"; the verbal clause is the khabar of «إن», and the clause of «إن» and what falls within its scope is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl. (لَكَبِيرَةً): the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), and «كبيرة» is the khabar of «كانت». (إِلَّا): a particle of exception. (عَلَى الَّذِينَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as the excepted; that from which the exception is made is omitted, its implied form being: "though it was indeed hard upon people, except upon the people whom Allah guided". You may also make «إلا» a particle of restriction, because the statement is incomplete, or because it includes the meaning of negation; then the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «كبيرة». (هَدَى اللَّهُ): the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of «الذين». (وَما): the wāw is a conjunction, and «ما» is negating. (كانَ اللَّهُ): «كان» and its noun. (لِيُضِيعَ): the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), preceded by a negated «كان»; «يضيع» is an imperfect verb, accusative by «أن» obligatorily implied after the lām of denial; the khabar of «كان» is omitted, its implied form being "intending", and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar. (إِيمانَكُمْ): mafʿūl bihi. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ): «إن» and its noun. (بِالنَّاسِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «رؤوف» or «رحيم». (لَرَؤُفٌ): the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «رؤوف» is the first khabar of «إن». (رَحِيمٌ): the second khabar of «إنّ»; the clause of «إن» and what falls within its scope has no grammatical position because it is causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Rhetoric:
1- Double meaning (al-tawriya) in His saying «وسطا»: the near, apparent meaning of «الوسط» is being in the middle, supported by the middle position of the Muslims' qibla; and its far, intended meaning is "the choice", as has preceded in the Vocabulary section.
2- Metonymy (al-kināya), also in «الوسط», for the utmost justice, as though it were the balance that shows no favour and inclines with no one.
3- The loose trope (al-majāz al-mursal) in His saying «على عقبيه», the relationship being outcome and final result; for there is nothing more ugly or hideous than the sight of a person with his form reversed, contrary to what is familiar and usual.
4- Fronting and deferring: He put «شهداء» before its complement, «على الناس», and put «شهيدا» after its complement, «عليكم», because the favour upon them is on both sides: in the first, by establishing that they are witnesses; and in the second, by establishing that they are witnessed for, with attestation of uprightness. What is put first is always the more important.

* Benefits:
1- We cannot avoid citing some views worthy of attention. The scholars have cited five parsings of this verse, which there is no room to cite; we have cited the one we chose among them, which al-Zamakhsharī also chose. Al-Jalāl chose that «القبلة» is the fronted second object and «التي كنت عليها» is the first object, arguing that "making into" (al-taṣyīr) is moving from one state to another, so what is clothed with the second state is the second object — do you not see that you say "I made the clay into pottery"? Abū Ḥayyān also chose it. It has also been said that «القبلة» is the first object and «التي كنت عليها» is an adjective, while the second object is omitted, its implied form being "abrogated" or the like.

A historical glimpse:
All agree that the Prophet ﷺ prayed toward the Rock of Bayt al-Maqdis [Translator's note: the source has «بيد المقدس», a misprint for «بيت المقدس»] for a period after the Hijra, and was then commanded to pray toward the Kaʿba. They differed only about his qibla in Mecca: was it the Kaʿba or Bayt al-Maqdis? What is narrated from the imams of the Prophet's Household (Ahl al-Bayt) is that it was Bayt al-Maqdis. Further, it is clear that the "making" in the verse is compound, not simple [i.e. it takes two objects], and the saying of Allah the Exalted «التي كنت عليها» is the second of its two objects, as most of the exegetes have stated. As for those who hold that he ﷺ used to pray toward the Kaʿba in Mecca, for them the "making" may be an abrogated making, considering the prayer in Medina toward Bayt al-Maqdis for a period, or an abrogating making, considering the prayer in Mecca. Al-Rāzī said: the saying of Allah the Exalted «التي كنت عليها» is not an adjective of «القبلة»; rather it is the second of the two objects of «جعلنا». Further, the Kaʿba was called «كعبة» because of its squareness; more discussion of that will come.
2- When «إنّ» is lightened, it enters both verbal and nominal clauses. If it enters a nominal clause, it may govern or be left ungoverning, and leaving it ungoverning is more common. If it enters a verbal clause, it must be left ungoverning, and mostly the verb is a past abrogating verb (nāsikh); because when the Arabs took it out of its original function by having it enter a verb, they wanted that verb to be one of the verbs of mubtadaʾ and khabar, so that its original function should not disappear entirely, as you see in the verse. A lām must come after it, called the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), to distinguish it from the negating «إن».
3- The lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd), i.e. the lām of negation, is the one that occurs after a negated past «كان». The khabar of «كان» is disputed: it has been said that it is omitted and is supplied according to the context, and the lām of denial, with the maṣdar made genitive by it, is attached to it, because the maṣdar «أن» is obligatorily implied after it. It has also been said that the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the khabar. This is easier, but the first is better known and more precise for the soundness of the khabar.

dervis-irab:144-144.t:
* Vocabulary:
(شَطْرَ): «الشطر» has two senses in the speech of the Arabs. One of them is "half", and from that is their saying «شاطرتك مالي» (I shared my wealth with you half and half). The other sense is "direction", one says:
«خذ شطر زيد», i.e. head in Zayd's direction; this is what is meant here. From it is their saying «حلبت الدهر أشطره», i.e. its good and its bad have passed over me. And from it «الشاطر» was named, who is the one who has exhausted his family with his wickedness.

* I'rab:
(قَدْ): here it is for multiplicity (taktīr), as indicated by the mention of turning; the multiplicity is with respect to the Prophet ﷺ, for otherwise it is impossible in relation to Allah the Exalted. (نَرى): an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), whose fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "we". (تَقَلُّبَ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَجْهِكَ): muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (فِي السَّماءِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تقلب», because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). (فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction for causation; the lām prepares for the oath (muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); «نولينك» is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we"; and the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi. (قِبْلَةً): second mafʿūl bihi; it may also be accusative by removal of the preposition. (تَرْضاها): an imperfect verb, nominative, whose fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you", and «ها» is mafʿūl bihi. The clause is an adjective of «قبلة», and the clause «فلنولينك» has no grammatical position because it is causal (taʿlīliyya). (فَوَلِّ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, and «ول» is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, whose fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you". (وَجْهِكَ): mafʿūl bihi, and the kāf is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive by annexation. (شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ): mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), an adverb of place attached to «ولّ», and «المسجد» is muḍāf ilayhi. (الْحَرامِ): an adjective of «المسجد»; the clause «فولّ» has no grammatical position. (وَحَيْثُ ما): the wāw is resumptive, and «حيثما» is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb, attached to the omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of «كنتم» [Translator's note: the source has «خير», a misprint for «خبر»]. (كُنْتُمْ): «كان», a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and its noun; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). By analogy it should have been in the position of the genitive by annexation, were it not for the impediment, namely that it [«حيثما»] is among the governors of verbs. (فَوَلُّوا): the fāʾ links the apodosis because it is a request (ṭalabī); «ولوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn because its imperfect is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (وُجُوهَكُمْ): mafʿūl bihi. (شَطْرَهُ): an adverb of place attached to «ولوا». (وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ): the wāw is resumptive, and «إن» and its noun. (أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ): the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; «الكتاب» is the second object of «أوتوا», and the first is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), which is the wāw. (لَيَعْلَمُونَ): the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and the clause «يعلمون» is the khabar of «إن». (أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ): «أن», its noun and its khabar; it fills the place of the two objects of «يعلمون». (مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَمَا): the wāw is resumptive, and «ما» is the Ḥijāzī negating «ما», which governs like «ليس». (اللَّهُ): the noun of «ما». (بِغافِلٍ): the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and «غافل» is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of «ما». (عَمَّا): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «غافل». (يَعْمَلُونَ): the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of «ما».

* Benefits:
1- (حَيْثُ ما) is a jussive conditional noun whose position is the accusative as an adverb of place. Its origin is «حيث», to which «ما» was added, so it became a jussive noun. «حيث» is an adverb of place, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and it is annexed to clauses, so it requires the genitive for what follows it; and what requires the genitive does not require the jussive. So when it was joined with «ما», the sense of annexation left it, as has preceded.
2- A historical glimpse:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Medina and prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen months, then turned toward the Kaʿba. That was in Rajab, two months before the battle of Badr, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at the mosque of [Banū] Salima. He had prayed two rakʿas of the ẓuhr or ʿaṣr prayer with his companions, and he turned during the prayer and faced the [new] qibla; and the men moved to the place of the women and the women to the place of the men. So the mosque was named the Mosque of the Two Qiblas. The wisdom in that is clear; indeed, it is the most splendid that human dealing can reach, which aims above all at winning hearts and softening feelings. Yet that availed nothing in removing the hardness that had covered the hearts of the Jews, and the Qur'an explained this hardness with the following verse:

dervis-irab:186-187.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الرفث), with two fatḥas: speech that occurs between men and women at the time of intercourse, which is considered indecent to mention at another time; it came to be used for intercourse itself because it usually accompanies it. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «رفث in his speech, رفثا, of the pattern طلب; and يرفِث with kasra is a dialect form. الرفث: intercourse, because of His saying, Exalted be He: أحل لكم ليلة الصيام الرفث إلى نسائكم.» In al-Asās and al-Lisān: it is also said: الرفث with the private parts is intercourse, with the tongue it is making appointments for intercourse, and with the eye it is winking for intercourse. The basic way of making الرفث transitive is with the bāʾ; it is made transitive in the verse with إلى only because it is made to include the meaning of الإفضاء (going in unto).
(تَخْتانُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ): you betray yourselves and diminish their share of good. The derivation of الاختيان is from الخيانة, like الاكتساب from الكسب, and it carries additional intensity.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذا): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to show that He, Glorified be He, answers everyone who calls upon Him. (سَأَلَكَ): a past verb, and the kāf is its object. (عِبادِي): fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (عَنِّي): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) سألك. (فَإِنِّي): the fāʾ links the answer, and إن and its noun. (قَرِيبٌ): its khabar (predicate); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a non-jussive condition. (أُجِيبُ): an imperfect verb, nominative; its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "I" (أنا); the verbal clause is a second khabar. (دَعْوَةَ): mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الدَّاعِ): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the kasra implied on the deleted yāʾ. The readers have customarily dropped the yāʾ from الداع and دعان, because it has no written form for them in the muṣḥaf: some readers drop it, following the orthography, in pause and in continuation; some retain it in both states [Translator's note: the source has «في الحين», evidently for «في الحالين» ("in both states")]; and some retain it in continuation and delete it in pause. (إِذا): the adverb is attached to أجيب. (دَعانِ): the clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا): the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the disclosing fāʾ); the lām is the lām of command, and يستجيبوا is an imperfect verb, jussive by the lām of command, i.e. let them seek My answering, because the sīn and tāʾ in استفعل are for seeking; and the meaning is: let them respond to Me with obedience. One says from it: استجبت له and استجبته, meaning أجبته (I answered him). [The poet] said:
وداع دعا يا من يجيب إلى الندى ... فلم يستجبه عند ذاك مجيب
(And a caller called out: "O who will answer to generosity?" — but no answerer answered him then.)
(لِي): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يستجيبوا. (وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا بِي): conjoined to His saying فليستجيبوا لي. (لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ): لعلّ and its noun; the clause of hope is circumstantial. (أُحِلَّ): a passive past verb. (لَكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أحل. (لَيْلَةَ الصِّيامِ): on the face of the speech, the adverb is attached to أحل, and many have parsed it so; but the problem with this is that the permission was established before that time. So it is better to attach it to an omitted [verb] indicated by the word الرفث, i.e. أن ترفثوا ("that you go in unto"). We have not attached it to الرفث because that would involve placing what is governed by the ṣila — understood from the al- — before the relative. (الرَّفَثُ): the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of أحل. (إِلى نِسائِكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to الرفث. The clause أحل and what follows it is resumptive, brought to remove confusion. The explanation of that is that at the beginning of the matter, when a man broke his fast, food, drink and intercourse were lawful for him until he prayed the late ʿIshāʾ or slept before it [Translator's note: the source has «قلبها», evidently for «قبلها» ("before it")]. Once he had prayed it or slept, that became forbidden to him until the following night. Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb had relations with his wife after the late ʿIshāʾ prayer. When he had performed the ritual bath, he began to weep and blame himself, and he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said:
"O Messenger of Allah, I apologise to Allah and to you for this erring self of mine," and he told him what he had done. He, upon him be blessings and peace, said: "You were not worthy of that, O ʿUmar."
Then [the verse] was revealed. (هُنَّ): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (لِباسٌ): khabar. (لَكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of لباس; the clause is explicative (mufassira) with no grammatical position, stating the reason for the permission. (وَأَنْتُمْ لِباسٌ لَهُنَّ): conjoined to the one before it. (عَلِمَ اللَّهُ): the clause gives the reason for the occasion of the verse's revelation. (أَنَّكُمْ): أن and its noun. (كُنْتُمْ): a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun. (تَخْتانُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ): the verbal clause is the khabar of كنتم.
أن and what falls within its scope take the place of the two objects of علم. (وَعَفا عَنْكُمْ): conjoined to the clause علم الله. (فَالْآنَ): conjoined to something omitted and implied, i.e. "so you repented and He turned to you"; الآن is an adverb of time attached to باشروهن. (بَاشِرُوهُنَّ): an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi. (وَابْتَغُوا): conjoined to باشروهن. (ما): a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ): a verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. (وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا): the wāw is resumptive, brought to generalise the ruling. It was revealed concerning Ṣirma ibn Qabs [Translator's note: so in the source; the name is usually given as Ṣirma ibn Qays]. That was because he used to work on a piece of land of his while fasting; when evening came he returned to his family and said: "Do you have any food?" She said: "No," and began to prepare food for him. Sleep overtook him from fatigue, and he disliked eating out of fear of Allah. So he began the morning fasting, exhausted and worn out in his work, and hardly had the day reached its middle before he fainted. When he came to, he went to the Prophet ﷺ and told him what had happened, and the verse was revealed. (حَتَّى): a particle of limit (ghāya) and genitive. (يَتَبَيَّنَ): an imperfect verb, subjunctive by an implied أن after حتى; the maṣdar cast from أن and the verb is attached [with حتى] to كلوا. (لَكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يتبين. (الْخَيْطُ): fāʿil. (الْأَبْيَضُ): naʿt; it is the first of the dawn to appear, lying across the horizon like a stretched thread. (مِنَ الْخَيْطِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يتبين; it is permissible to attach the two particles to a single verb, even though their wording is the same, because their meanings differ. (الْأَسْوَدِ): naʿt. (مِنَ الْفَجْرِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. in the state of the white being the dawn. Al-Bukhārī and Muslim related from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim, who said: When it was revealed, I took a black hobbling-cord and a white hobbling-cord and put them under my pillow, and I kept looking at them during the night, but it did not become clear to me. So in the morning I went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he said: "That is only the blackness of the night and the whiteness of the day." More explanation of this will come under Rhetoric.
(ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا): ثم is a conjunction for sequence with an interval, and أتموا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الصِّيامِ) [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; in the verse it is الصِّيامَ]: mafʿūl bihi. (إِلَى اللَّيْلِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أتموا. (وَلا تُبَاشِرُوهُنَّ): the wāw is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, and تباشروهن is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا. (وَأَنْتُمْ): the wāw is circumstantial, and أنتم is a mubtadaʾ. (عاكِفُونَ): khabar. (فِي الْمَساجِدِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عاكفون; the nominal clause is circumstantial. (تِلْكَ): a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. (حُدُودُ اللَّهِ): khabar and muḍāf ilayhi; the clause تلك is resumptive. (فَلا تَقْرَبُوها): the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, لا is prohibitive, and تقربوها is an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, i.e. "if you desire safety for yourselves, then desist and do not approach them"; for some of them used to go out while in iʿtikāf, have relations with their wives, and return. The clause is resumptive. (كَذلِكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or ḥāl. (يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ): an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. (آياتِهِ): mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. (لِلنَّاسِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يبين. (لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ): لعل and its noun, and the clause يتقون is its khabar; the clause of hope is circumstantial.

* Rhetoric:
1- Kināya (metonymy) in His saying: «هن لباس لكم وأنتم لباس لهن», because a garment is what is on a person's body; and the man and the woman, since each of them enfolds the other and they embrace, resemble a garment enfolding them both. Al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī said:
إذا ما الضجيع ثنى عطفها ... تثنت عليه فكانت لباسا
(When her bedfellow bends her side toward him, she bends over him and becomes a garment.)
Examples of kināya:
Kināya has been mentioned before, and here we expand on the subject further, saying: the purpose of kināya is to keep the tongue clean of what is unseemly to mention, alluding to it with the most elegant expression. Every kināya has a purpose, and the purposes are countless; for this reason the depth of kināya cannot be plumbed. Among the most delightful is the saying of al-Sharīf al-Raḍī:
برد السّوار لها فأحميت القلائد بالعناق
(Her bracelet grew cold, so I warmed her necklaces with embracing.)
i.e. when her bracelet grew cold at the end of the night, he knew that the breeze of dawn had arisen, so he warmed her necklaces with embracing, so that the necklaces would belie what the bracelet had indicated — the rising of the dawn that announces parting. So he turned away from stating that explicitly to the coldness of the bracelet, to carry the mind to the blowing of the dawn breeze that announces parting and calls for it. Kināya is well known in the ḥadīths of the Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, out of his propriety and loftiness. Among what has come of this brocade is his saying:
«There was a woman among those who were before us, and she had a cousin who loved her. He tried to seduce her, but she refused him, until, when hardship struck her, she came to him asking him [for help], and he tried to seduce her, and she yielded herself to him. When he sat from her where a man sits from a woman, she said to him: "It is not lawful for you to break the seal except by its right." So he got up from her and left her.» This is a kināya that falls exactly in its place. Also among that is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «Gently, your driving of the glass vessels!», by which he meant women; he alluded to them as glass vessels. That was on one of his journeys, when a black servant named Anjasha was singing to drive the camels, and he said to him: "O Anjasha, gently, your driving of the glass vessels!"
Also among the kināya in this verse is His saying: «فالآن باشروهن». المباشرة, in the view of the majority, is intercourse; it is also said: intercourse and what is less than it. It is derived from the contact of the two skins (البشرتين), so embracing and touching are included in it.
2- The eloquent simile (al-tashbīh al-balīgh): He likened the first of the dawn to appear, lying across the horizon, to a stretched white thread, and the darkness of the night stretched out with it to a stretched black thread; it is a very familiar simile. Had من الفجر not been mentioned, it would have been an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya); but the mention of the thing likened returned it to an eloquent simile with the particle of comparison omitted.
3- Antithesis (ṭibāq), because He contrasted white and black. As for mentioning the other colours, that is called tadbīj (embroidery), as in the saying of Abū Tammām:
تردّى ثياب الموت حمرا فما دجا ... لها الليل إلا وهي من سندس خضر
(He put on the garments of death, red; and night had not darkened upon them before they had become green silk brocade.)

* Benefits:
«حتّى» in speech is of three kinds:
1- It is for the end of the limit (intihāʾ al-ghāya); it puts nouns in the genitive with a meaning [Translator's note: so in the source, «على معنى»; probably «على معنى إلى», "in the meaning of إلى"], as in His saying, Exalted be He:
«سلام هي حتى مطلع الفجر»; and it puts verbs in the subjunctive by an implied أن after it, as in the verse.
2- It is a conjunction.
3- It is a particle of beginning (ḥarf ibtidāʾ), with which speech begins, as in the saying of al-Mutanabbī:
هو الجد حتى تفضل العين أختها ... وحتى يكون اليوم لليوم سيد
(It is fortune — so much so that one eye surpasses its sister, and one day is master over another day.)
He put the two verbs after it in the nominative because it is a particle of beginning. More of the never-ending discussions of (حَتَّى) will come; al-Farrāʾ used to say on his deathbed: "I die with something of حتى still in my heart."

dervis-irab:30-30.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ) The wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya); إذ is an adverb (ẓarf) of past time, in the accusative position as a direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember). This i'rab is the prevalent one for the إذ mentioned at the opening of the stories in the Qur'an, and it was chosen by al-Zamakhsharī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya and other i'rab scholars. Abū Ḥayyān and al-Karkhī rejected it, and it may be of interest to cite a curious passage of Abū Ḥayyān on this point. He said: «It is nothing, because it takes إذ out of its proper use, which is that it is not used in any way other than as an adverb, or with an adverb of time being annexed to it.» Ibn Hishām replied to him, as you will see in detail in the section on Benefits. Abū Ḥayyān went on: «What Arabic requires is to make it accusative by the words: قالوا أتجعل, that is, at the time of Allah's saying to the angels: إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة they said: أتجعل — just as you say in speech: إذ جئتني أكرمتك (when you came to me I honoured you), meaning at the time of your coming I honoured you, and إذ قلت لي كذا قلت لك كذا (when you said such-and-such to me I said such-and-such to you). Look at this easy, clear way — how most people were not guided to it, and instead plunged into a darkness and blundered like a night-blind camel.»
(قالَ) a past verb; the verbal clause is in the genitive position by the annexation of the adverb to it. (رَبُّكَ) fāʿil (agent). (لِلْمَلائِكَةِ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قال. (إِنِّي) inna is a particle resembling the verb, and the yāʾ is its ism (noun). (جاعِلٌ) its khabar (predicate). (فِي الْأَرْضِ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جاعل if it means "creator", and in the accusative position as a second direct object if it is an active participle from الجعل in the sense of "making into"; the clause إني جاعل is in the accusative position as the reported speech (maqūl al-qawl). (خَلِيفَةً) direct object of جاعل, because it is an active participle.
(قالُوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because of its attachment to the wāw of the group; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive. (أَتَجْعَلُ) The hamza is for a pure interrogative of astonishment, as though they were seeking to fathom a wisdom that was hidden from them, a dazzling one; تجعل is an imperfect nominative verb, its fāʿil an obligatorily latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت". (فِيها) a preposition and its genitive noun; you may attach them to جعل if it means "creating", or make them the second object, put forward, if it means "making into". (يُفْسِدُ) an imperfect verb, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; the clause has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila (relative clause). (فِيها) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يفسد. (وَيَسْفِكُ) an imperfect verb conjoined to يفسد, within the scope of the ṣila. (الدِّماءَ) direct object. (وَنَحْنُ) The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and نحن is a detached pronoun in the nominative position as mubtadaʾ. (نُسَبِّحُ) an imperfect verb, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "نحن"; the verbal clause is in the nominative position as the khabar of نحن. (بِحَمْدِكَ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "accompanied by Your praise". (وَنُقَدِّسُ) an imperfect verb conjoined to نسبح. (لَكَ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to نقدس; some made the lām redundant (zāʾida) with the kāf as the object of نقدس.
(قالَ) a past verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "هو"; the clause is resumptive. (إِنِّي) inna and its ism. (أَعْلَمُ) an imperfect nominative verb, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنا"; the clause is the khabar of inna. (ما) a relative noun in the accusative position as direct object. (لا) negative. (تَعْلَمُونَ) an imperfect verb, nominative by the presence of the nūn; the clause has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila; and the nominal clause إني أعلم is in the accusative position as the reported speech.

* Rhetoric:
In the interrogative found in His saying أتجعل, the question departs from its original meaning, being for astonishment, as we chose in the i'rab. It was also said that it is for seeking guidance (istirshād), that is: "Will You place in it one who will cause corruption, like those who were in it before?" It was also said that they were asking about their own state, i.e.: "Will You place in it a corrupter while we remain in obedience to You, never slackening from it for the blink of an eye?" Others said it is for affirmation (ījāb). In truth, every interrogative expression occurring in the Book of Allah the Exalted falls under one of the following six aspects:
1- Rebuke (tawbīkh), 2- astonishment (taʿajjub), 3- equivalence (taswiya), 4- affirmation (ījāb), 5- command (amr), 6- confirmation (taqrīr). As for a genuine question, it does not occur from Allah the Exalted in the Qur'an, because the questioner learns what he does not have, whereas Allah knows things before they come to be. Rebuke is, for example: «أذهبتم طيباتكم»; confirmation: «أأنت قلت للناس»؟; equivalence, for example: «سواء عليهم أأنذرتهم»; affirmation, for example: «أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها»; and command, for example: «أأسلمتم». By this, what occurs in the Book of Allah is recognised; so learn its places and ponder.

* Benefits:
1- إذ is an adverb of past time, and only a sentence follows it. The sentence may be omitted and replaced by tanwīn, called tanwīn al-ʿiwaḍ (compensatory tanwīn), for example: «ويومئذ يفرح المؤمنون». The original is "يوم إذ غلبت الروم يفرح المؤمنون"; the clause غلبت الروم was omitted and tanwīn brought as a replacement for it, so two sukūn letters met, the dhāl and the tanwīn, and the dhāl was given a kasra following the basic rule for the meeting of two sukūns. Its i'rab is summarised in five aspects:
a- That it be an adverb, for example: «فقد نصره الله إذ أخرجه الذين كفروا».
b- That it be a direct object (mafʿūl bihi): this is the prevalent case of the إذ mentioned at the opening of the Revelation.
c- That it be a substitute (badal) for the object, for example: «واذكر في الكتاب مريم إذ انتبذت»; إذ is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from مريم.
d- That a noun of time which can be dispensed with be annexed to it, for example: «يومئذ تحدث أخبارها».
e- And إذ comes for suddenness (mufājaʾa) and occurs after بينا and بينما. The poet said:
استقدر الله خيرا وارضينّ به ... فبينما العسر إذ دارت مياسير
(Ask Allah to ordain good and be content with it; for while there is hardship, behold, ease comes round.)
And when إذ is for suddenness, what is its i'rab? Then the more likely view is to regard it as a particle of suddenness.
2- Opinions have differed greatly about how the angels knew that the offspring of Adam would cause corruption on earth. The closest to logic that we have seen is that they knew it from the word "khalīfa" (vicegerent). They said: the khalīfa is the one who judges between disputants, and a disputant is either a wrongdoer or one wronged; and whenever mutual wrongdoing occurs among them, corruption occurs on earth and spreads.

dervis-irab:219-220.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْخَمْرِ): wine was named with the verbal noun of khamarahu khamran, "he covered it", to stress how it covers, hides and conceals the intellect. It is also said that khamr was so called because it was left until it matured; one says ikhtamara al-ʿajīn, meaning the dough reached its maturity. And it is said that khamr was so called because it mixes with the intellect, from mukhāmara, which means mixing. These three meanings are close to one another and all are found in wine. Here is a brief list of some names of wine, which are in fact descriptions:
al-Shamūl: because it envelops (tashmal) the people with its scent.
al-Mashmūla: the wine that was exposed to the north wind (shamāl).
al-Raḥīq: the choicest wine, in which there is no adulteration.
al-Khandarīs: the aged kind.
al-Ḥumayyā: the strong kind.
al-ʿUqār: with ḍamma on the ʿayn, because it has "grappled" (ʿāqarat) with the dregs.
al-Rāḥ: because its drinker is gladdened (yartāḥu) by it, or because its scent is found pleasant; and it is said, rather, that it is the one in which one finds a spirit (rūḥ). Ibn al-Rūmī gathered the meanings of al-rāḥ in his saying:
والله ما أدري لأية علّة ... يدعونها في الراح باسم الراح
ألريحها أم روحها تحت الحشا ... أم لارتياح نديمها المرتاح
(By Allah, I do not know for what reason they call wine in the cup by the name al-Rāḥ: is it for its scent, or for its spirit within the bowels, or for the delight of its cheerful drinking companion?)
al-Mudāma: the wine that was kept in its place until its movement settled.
al-Muʿattaqa: the wine that was kept in its place until it aged.
al-Qahwa: the one that makes its drinker lose appetite (tuqhī), that is, it takes away his desire for food.
al-Sulāf: the one whose juice flows out without pressing.
al-Ṣahbāʾ: because it wavers between redness and fairness.
al-Kumayt: with ḍamma on the kāf, because of the blackness and redness in it.
al-Qarqaf: because of its coolness. And other names besides.
(الْمَيْسِرِ): a mīmī verbal noun (maṣdar mīmī) from yasara, like al-mawʿid and al-marjiʿ. One says yasartuhu when you have beaten him at gambling (qamartuhu), and qamarahu means he overcame him in gambling. The poet said:
قالت: أنا قمرته ... قلت: اسكتي فهو قمر
(She said: "I beat him at gambling." I said: "Be quiet, for he is a gambler.")
The derivation of al-maysir is either from al-yusr (ease), because in it money is taken easily, without toil or fatigue; or from al-yasār, that is, wealth, because it is a cause of it. To this day people have shown great ingenuity in games of chance, which are forbidden by reason and by the Law, because they are a corruption beyond which there is no corruption. Adīb Isḥāq, one of the poets of the modern age, said:
لكل نقيصة في الناس عار ... وشرّ معايب المرء القمار
(Every defect among people brings shame, and the worst of a man's faults is gambling.)
(الْعَفْوَ): what exceeds need.

* I'rab:
(يَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْخَمْرِ وَالْمَيْسِرِ): a verb, an agent and a direct object (mafʿūl bihi); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يسألونك; and الميسر is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الخمر. The clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), introduced to explain the prohibition of wine and gambling because of the harmful social corruption they contain. (قُلْ): an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; the clause is also resumptive. (فِيهِما): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted predicate (khabar muqaddam). (إِثْمٌ): a delayed subject (mubtadaʾ muʾakhkhar). (كَبِيرٌ): an adjective (naʿt) of إثم; the nominal clause is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (وَمَنافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ): conjoined to إثم; and للناس is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective. (وَإِثْمُهُما): the waw is a conjunction; إثم is a mubtadaʾ, the hāʾ is its muḍāf ilayhi, and the mīm and the alif are two letters indicating the dual. (أَكْبَرُ): the khabar. (مِنْ نَفْعِهِما): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أكبر. (وَيَسْئَلُونَكَ): conjoined to يسألونك. (ماذا يُنْفِقُونَ): its i'rab was repeated, so it renews the acquaintance with it. (قُلْ): an imperative verb whose latent agent is "you"; the clause is resumptive. (الْعَفْوَ): a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "spend"; the clause is the content of the saying. (كَذلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or ḥāl (circumstantial); يبين is an imperfect verb in the nominative. (اللَّهُ): the agent of يبين. (لَكُمُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يبين. (الْآياتِ): a direct object. (لَعَلَّكُمْ): laʿalla and its noun. (تَتَفَكَّرُونَ): an imperfect verb and an agent; the clause is the khabar of laʿalla; the clause of hope is a ḥāl; and the clause كذلك يبين etc. is resumptive. (فِي الدُّنْيا وَالْآخِرَةِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تتفكرون or to يبين. On the first view the meaning is: in what is for your good in the two abodes; on the second: He makes clear to you the signs in what benefits you in the two abodes. (وَيَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْيَتامى): its i'rab has been given before. (قُلْ): an imperative verb with a latent agent; the clause is resumptive. (إِصْلاحٌ): a mubtadaʾ; it is permissible to begin with it because it is qualified by a preposition and its genitive noun. (لَهُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of إصلاح. (خَيْرٌ): the khabar of إصلاح; the nominal clause is the content of the saying. (وَإِنْ): the waw is resumptive and إن is conditional. (تُخالِطُوهُمْ): the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its sign of jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the waw is the agent and the hāʾ the direct object; that is, you treat them well by mixing with them and by good companionship. (فَإِخْوانُكُمْ): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); إخوانكم is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "they are your brothers"; the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. It is necessary to posit an omission, that is, "so that is permitted to you", and then He gave the reason for that with His saying: "they are your brothers". (وَاللَّهُ): the waw is resumptive, and the waw is a mubtadaʾ «[Translator's note: the source literally says "the waw is a mubtadaʾ"; the intended word is evidently الله]». (يَعْلَمُ): the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the agent of يعلم is a latent pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted. (الْمُفْسِدَ): a direct object. (مِنَ الْمُصْلِحِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يعلم because it implies the meaning of "distinguishes". (وَلَوْ): the waw is resumptive and لو is conditional. (شاءَ اللَّهُ): a verb and an agent; the object of the willing is omitted, its implied form being "to put you in hardship". (لَأَعْنَتَكُمْ): the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; أعنتكم is a verb with a latent agent and a direct object; the clause لأعنتكم has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ): inna and its noun. (عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ): the khabar of inna; the clause has no grammatical position, because it stands as a giving of reason.

* Benefits:
A historical and literary glimpse: four verses were revealed concerning wine.
1- The first was revealed in Mecca, namely: «and from the fruits of the date palms and grapevines you take intoxicant» (Q 16:67). The Muslims used to drink it, and it was lawful for them.
2- The second was revealed in Medina. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, Muʿādh ibn Jabal and a group of the Anṣār came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, give us a ruling on wine, for it takes away the intellect and robs of wealth." Some people gave it up because of His saying: «Say: In them is a great sin».
3- The third: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf prepared a meal and invited some people to it; they drank and became drunk, and the sunset prayer came. They put one of them forward to lead them in prayer, and he recited: «Say: O disbelievers, I worship what you worship», omitting the negative «lā». So Allah the Exalted revealed: «O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying» (Q 4:43). After that few people drank it.
4- The fourth: ʿItbān ibn Mālik invited some people, among them Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, to food and drink. They ate and drank wine until it took hold of them, and when they became drunk they boasted and recited poetry to one another, until Saʿd recited a poem containing a satire of the Anṣār. One of the Anṣār struck him with a camel's jawbone and wounded his head. Saʿd went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and complained to him about the Anṣārī. Then ʿUmar said: "O Allah, give us a clear and satisfying explanation concerning wine." So Allah the Exalted revealed: «Wine and gambling are but...» up to His saying «So will you not desist?» (Q 5:90-91). ʿUmar said: "We have desisted, O Lord."

dervis-irab:196-196.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْعُمْرَةَ) in the context of the Hajj is well known; one says "iʿtamara" (he performed ʿumra). Its root meaning is "visiting".
Al-Zajjāj said: The meaning of the ʿumra in practice is only the circumambulation of the House and the running between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa. The difference between the Hajj and the ʿumra is that the ʿumra may be performed by a person throughout the whole year, whereas the Hajj has a single time in the year. Their rulings belong to the science of jurisprudence. The plural is ʿumar and ʿumarāt.
(أُحْصِرْتُمْ) means "you were prevented". One says "aḥṣara fulān" when something prevents him, whether fear, illness or incapacity. Ibn Mayyāda said:
وما هجر ليلى أن تكون تباعدت ... عليك ولا أن أحصرتك شغول
(Leila's abandonment of you is not because she has grown distant from you, nor because preoccupations have kept you back.)
(اسْتَيْسَرَ) means "became easy" (tayassara). One says "yasara al-amr" and "istayasara".
(الْهَدْيِ) is applied to the animal which the pilgrim or the performer of ʿumra drives as an offering for the people of the Sanctuary. In al-Mukhtār: «ḥattā yablugha l-hadyu maḥillahu» was read with the dāl lightened and with it doubled (shaddada). The singular is hadya and hadiyya. One says "mā aḥsana hadyatahu", meaning "how fine is his conduct", and they used to swear by it in their oaths. Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Ḥudhayfa al-Ghanawī said: يقولون من هذا الغريب بأرضنا ... أما والهدايا إنني لغريب (They say, "Who is this stranger in our land?" By the sacrificial offerings, I am indeed a stranger!)
(مَحِلَّهُ) is a noun of place from "ḥalla yaḥillu", that is, the place where its slaughter becomes lawful (ḥalāl). The ḥāʾ is vowelled with kasra because the middle radical of its imperfect is vowelled with kasra.

* I'rab:
(وَأَتِمُّوا) The wāw is a conjunction; "atimmū" is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) by the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (الْحَجَّ) mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَالْعُمْرَةَ) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to "al-ḥajj". (لِلَّهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "purely for His sake"; or you may attach them to "atimmū", in which case the lām is the lām of the mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). The poets borrowed this beautiful expression and turned it to the purposes of love poetry. Dhū l-Rumma said, and excelled:
تمام الحجّ أن تقف المطايا ... على خرقاء واضعة اللثام
(The completion of the Hajj is that the riding beasts halt at Kharqāʾ, who has put down her veil.)
He made halting at Kharqāʾ, his beloved from Banū ʿĀmir, like one of the rites of the Hajj which one has no way to avoid completing. (فَإِنْ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (eloquent fāʾ), and "in" is conditional. (أُحْصِرْتُمْ) a past passive verb in the position of a jussive (majzūm), being the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (فَمَا) The fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ, and "mā" is a relative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "so upon you is what is easy", and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (اسْتَيْسَرَ) a past verb whose fāʿil is a latent pronoun; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of "mā". (مِنَ الْهَدْيِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "being of the offering". (وَلا) The wāw is a conjunction, and "lā" is prohibitive. (تَحْلِقُوا) an imperfect verb jussive by "lā", and the wāw is the fāʿil. (رُؤُسَكُمْ) mafʿūl bihi. (حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ) "ḥattā" is a particle of limit and of genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to "taḥliqū"; "yablugha" is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied "an". (الْهَدْيِ) fāʿil. (مَحِلَّهُ) mafʿūl bihi. (فَمَنْ) The fāʾ is resumptive, and "man" is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (كانَ) a defective past verb in the position of a jussive, being the protasis; its subject (ism) is a latent pronoun referring to "man". (مِنْكُمْ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (مَرِيضاً) khabar of "kāna". (أَوْ) a conjunction. (بِهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (أَذىً) a postponed mubtadaʾ, its nominative sign being an implied ḍamma on the omitted alif because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. (مِنْ رَأْسِهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ṣifa (adjective) of "adhan". (فَفِدْيَةٌ) The fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis, and "fidya" is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "so upon him is a ransom", and the clause is the apodosis. (مِنْ صِيامٍ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ṣifa of "fidya". (أَوْ) a conjunction. (صَدَقَةٍ) conjoined to "ṣiyām". (أَوْ) a conjunction. (نُسُكٍ) conjoined to "ṣiyām". The protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of "man". (فَإِذا) The fāʾ is resumptive and "idhā" is an adverb for what is to come of time. (أَمِنْتُمْ) The verbal clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. (فَمَنْ تَمَتَّعَ بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ) The fāʾ is the apodosis of "idhā"; "man" is a jussive-governing conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ; "tamattaʿa" is a past verb in the position of a jussive, the protasis; "bi-l-ʿumra" is attached to "tamattaʿa"; and "ilā l-ḥajj" is attached to an omitted element, i.e. "and his enjoyment and benefit from what is forbidden continued up to the Hajj". (فَمَا) The fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis, and "mā" is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "so upon him is what" (اسْتَيْسَرَ) a verb in the position of a jussive, the apodosis. (مِنَ الْهَدْيِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (فَمَنْ) The fāʾ is resumptive and "man" is conditional, a mubtadaʾ. (لَمْ يَجِدْ) "lam" is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive, and "yajid" is an imperfect verb jussive by "lam"; the jussive verb is the protasis; its fāʿil is a latent pronoun referring to "man"; its object is omitted because the meaning is evident, the implied form being "whoever does not find what is easy of the offering". (فَصِيامُ) The fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis, and "ṣiyām" is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "so upon him is fasting", and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis. (ثَلاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ) muḍāf ilayhi. (فِي الْحَجِّ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَسَبْعَةٍ) conjoined to "thalātha". (إِذا رَجَعْتُمْ) "idhā" is an adverb for what is to come of time, and the clause "rajaʿtum" is in the position of genitive by annexation. (تِلْكَ) a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. (عَشَرَةٌ) khabar. (كامِلَةٌ) ṣifa. (ذلِكَ) a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. (لِمَنْ) The lām is a preposition, and "man" is a relative noun in the position of genitive by the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar. (لَمْ يَكُنْ) "lam" is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive, and "yakun" is a defective imperfect verb jussive by "lam". (أَهْلُهُ) its ism; the clause "lam yakun" has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (حاضِرِي) khabar of "yakun". (الْمَسْجِدِ) muḍāf ilayhi. (الْحَرامِ) ṣifa. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ) The wāw is resumptive; "ittaqū" is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi. (وَاعْلَمُوا) conjoined to "ittaqū". (أَنَّ اللَّهَ) "anna" and its ism. (شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ) khabar of "anna"; "anna" and what is within its scope stand in the place of the two objects of "iʿlamū".

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there is a lofty figure of speech, subtle in its derivation, which the scholars of rhetoric call "repetition" (takrīr); its definition is that the expression indicates the meaning by repeating it. In the verse it is in the saying of the Exalted: «تلك عشرة كاملة» after "three" and "seven": it stands in place of saying "three and seven" twice, and then He said "kāmila" (complete), which is a third emphasis. When a command issues from the commander to the one commanded in repeated wording and is not restricted to a specific time, this is a summons to hasten to obey the command and comply with the ruling at once, without delay or tardiness. Hence the fasting of the seven days is obligatory immediately upon return. So take note of it, for it is among the secrets. Examples of repetition in the Noble Qur'an will come which will clarify it completely. The poets glanced at the sky of the Qur'an, and Abū Tammām said in praise:
نهوض بثقل العبء مضطلع به ... وإن عظمت فيه الخطوب وجلّت
(One who rises under the weight of the burden and is equal to it, even if the calamities in it are great and grave.)
"al-thiql" is the same as "al-ʿibʾ"; it was repeated only for emphasis. And al-Buḥturī said in love poetry:
ويوم تثنّت للوداع وسلّمت ... بعينين موصول بلحظهما السحر
توهمتها ألوى بأجفانها الكرى ... كرى النوم أو مالت بأعطافها الخمر
(On the day she swayed at the farewell and greeted me, with two eyes whose glance is joined to sorcery; I imagined her eyelids overcome by drowsiness, the drowsiness of sleep, or her body swaying with wine.)
He meant to liken her glance, in its languor, to that of a sleeper, so he repeated the meaning by way of muḍāf and muḍāf ilayhi, in his saying «kara l-nawm», to emphasise it and increase its clarity, or to remove any misgiving that might trouble the listener.
Al-Mubarrad said, and said well: "He mentioned that to indicate the completion of the number, lest someone imagine that after mentioning the seven something else remained."

dervis-irab:16-17.t:
* I'rab:
(أُولئِكَ) a demonstrative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (الَّذِينَ) khabar (predicate) of أولئك. (اشْتَرَوُا) a past verb, indeclinable on an implied ḍamma on the omitted alif, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (الضَّلالَةَ) mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (بِالْهُدى) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اشتروا; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (فَما) the fāʾ is a conjunction expressing immediate sequence, and ما is negative. (رَبِحَتْ) a past verb, and the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine. (تِجارَتُهُمْ) the fāʿil of ربحت. (وَما) the wāw is a conjunction, and ما is negative. (كانُوا) كان is a defective past verb and the wāw is its ism (subject). (مُهْتَدِينَ) its khabar, and the sign of its accusative case is the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. (مَثَلُهُمْ) mubtadaʾ. (كَمَثَلِ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted word that is the khabar of مثلهم; or else the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), serving as khabar, and مثل is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive complement). (الَّذِي) a relative noun in the position of genitive as the second term of the genitive construct. (اسْتَوْقَدَ) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, meaning أوقد ("he kindled"); it is the form istafʿala used in the sense of afʿala, like أجاب and استجاب, and أخلف and استخلف. The fāʿil is a latent pronoun (permissibly latent), its implied form being "he". The clause استوقد has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. The singular الذي is used in the place of the plural الذين, which is why He said afterwards: «بنورهم». (ناراً)
mafʿūl bihi. The clause مثلهم is resumptive, put forward to coin a parable for the state of the hypocrites who bought error with guidance, to bring the picture vividly to mind and to lift the veils from the realities. (فَلَمَّا) the fāʾ is a conjunction, and لما is an adverb meaning "when" (ḥīna) that contains the sense of a condition; it is also said to be a particle of "occurrence due to occurrence" (ḥarf wujūb li-wujūb), and Ibn Hishām called it a "linking" particle (rābiṭa). (أَضاءَتْ) a past verb, the tāʾ being the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun (permissibly latent), its implied form being "it" (feminine). (ما) a relative noun meaning "the place", mafʿūl bihi. (حَوْلَهُ) an adverb of place attached to an omitted word that is the ṣila of ما. Some lexicographers claimed that أضاء is an intransitive verb, in which case ما must be redundant (zāʾida), that is, "it shone around him". (ذَهَبَ اللَّهُ) verb and agent; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb) of a non-jussive condition. (بِنُورِهِمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ذهب. (وَتَرَكَهُمْ) a past verb, with a latent agent (permissibly latent) and a first direct object. (فِي ظُلُماتٍ) the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the second object of تركهم. (لا) negative. (يُبْصِرُونَ) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is in the position of accusative as an emphatic ḥāl (circumstantial), because whoever is in darkness does not see.

* Rhetoric:
These two verses contain rhetorical devices that the pages can hardly hold; we shall try to summarize these devices.
1- The explicit metaphor with embellishment (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tarshīḥiyya). The meaning is "they chose" and "they exchanged", and the clue to the metaphor is الضلالة. Then this metaphor is embellished by His words: فما ربحت تجارتهم, in which profit is attributed to trade. So the source of the metaphor, which is buying, is embellished with the words "profit" and "trade" because of the congruity between buying and profit. Embellishment (tarshīḥ) is to present the figurative expression in the form of the literal, and then to judge it with some of the attributes of the literal, so that one figure is added to another. An example is the line of Ḥumayda bint al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr: ؟؟ بكى الخزّ من روح وأنكر جلده ... وعجّت عجيجا من جذام المطارف (The silk wept over Rawḥ and disowned his skin, and the silk mantles cried out loudly over Judhām.) [Translator's note: the source text shows two question marks (؟؟) here, an apparent scanning/printing defect; they are reproduced as they stand.] ؟؟ She made the silk stand in for a person when it came into contact with Rawḥ, weeping for the lack of fit, by her words: وأنكر جلده. Then she added further embellishment of the figure by her words:
وعجّت, that is, the silk mantles shouted against the tribe of Rawḥ, which is the tribe of Judhām. The meaning of the verse is that Rawḥ and his tribe Judhām are not fit to wear silk and its mantles, because they have no habit of it, so she alluded to them in the manner she did in the verse.
2- The difference between اشتروا and استبدلوا in two respects:
a- Exchange (istibdāl) is not a purchase unless it contains a benefit sought by the one making the exchange, whether real or imagined.
b- Purchase takes place between two parties to a sale, unlike exchange: if you take one of your garments in place of another, it is said that you "exchanged a garment for a garment". So the meaning that the verse conveys is that those people chose error over guidance for a benefit they believed they would obtain from people in return for it; thus it is a transaction between two parties aiming at profit, and this is the meaning of ishtirāʾ (buying), as with "selling" (bayʿ) and "trading" (ibtiyāʿ), whereas mere exchange does not convey it. Once you know this, you will grasp the secret of choosing اشتروا over استبدلوا, and you will see that the Qur'an, which is the highest degree of eloquence, does not choose one word over another that could stand in its place except for a wisdom in that and a particularity not found in the other.
3- Completion (tatmīm) in His words: «وما كانوا مهتدين». Its definition is that a word or a statement comes in the speech which, if removed, would make the meaning deficient in itself or in its attributes, or it comes for a fine addition. So His words «وما كانوا مهتدين» complete what precedes, indicating that they are misguided in all the actions they undertake.
4- The representational simile (tashbīh tamthīlī) in His words: «مثلهم كمثل الذي استوقد نارا فلما أضاءت ما حوله ذهب الله بنورهم». The reality of the representational simile is that the point of likeness is a picture drawn from several elements: that is, the state of the hypocrites in their hypocrisy, showing the opposite of the disbelief they conceal, is like the state of one who kindled a fire to gain light by it, then it went out and he could no longer see anything. Thus it appears to you that the representational simile works like magic in joining disparate things; it shows you for meanings represented only by fancies a likeness in figures standing before you; it makes the mute speak for you, gives you eloquence from the inarticulate, shows you life in inanimate things, and makes the near thing far. An example of it in poetry is the saying of Bashshār:
كأن مثار النقع فوق رؤوسنا ... وأسيافنا ليل تهاوى كواكبه
(As though the raised dust above our heads, with our swords, were a night whose stars come tumbling down.) For he likened the dust stirred up and massed above the heads, with the swords clashing within it during the battle, to the pitch-black night in which the stars tumble and the meteors fall. And the saying of Abū Tammām describing spring:
يا صاحبيّ تقصّيا نظريكما ... تريا وجوه الأرض كيف تصوّر
تريا نهارا مشمسا قد شابه ... زهر الربا فكأنما هو مقمر
(O my two companions, strain your sight to the farthest, and you will see the face of the earth, how it is being shaped. You will see a sunlit day mixed with the blossoms of the hills, so that it seems moonlit.) He likened the sunny day in the splendid garden crowned with flowers to the calm, moonlit night.
5- The variation between the two pronouns. The pronoun is singular in استوقد and حوله, looking to the side of the wording, because the hypocrites all share one saying and one deed. As for regard for the side of meaning in (بِنُورِهِمْ وَتَرَكَهُمْ), it is because the context is one of denouncing their states and declaring their blame and misguidance, so the judgement is established for every one of them.
6- Muraʿāt al-naẓīr (observing the counterpart), a device known among the scholars of rhetoric as "congruity" and "harmony" (tanāsub, i'tilāf). Its definition is that the speaker joins a thing with what suits it while leaving out mention of its opposite, so as to exclude antithesis (muṭābaqa). Here it lies in the mention of "illumination" (ḍawʾ) and "light" (nūr). The secret of mentioning "light" although the context would require saying بضوئهم to match أضاءت, is that ḍawʾ carries an indication of increase, so had He said بضوئهم it would have suggested the taking away of the surplus while what is called nūr remained, whereas the aim is the removal of the light from them entirely and its complete obliteration. This meaning is confirmed by His saying ذهب بنورهم and not أذهب نورهم. The difference between the two is that أذهبه means "he removed it and made it go", whereas ذهب به means "he took it along and went off with it". The aim is to convey that no hope is left of that light ever returning to them at all; for had it been said أذهب الله نورهم, it might have been imagined that He only took the light away from them while it remained with Him, and that He might perhaps compensate them for what they lost. When He said ذهب الله بنورهم, that cut off and severed the root of any hope of their obtaining any good for themselves or from Him. This is among the loftiest that eloquence reaches. Ibn al-Rūmī clung to the fringes of this eloquence when he said, describing the Rāziqī grape:
لم يبق منه وهج الحرور ... إلّا ضياء في ظروف نور
(The blaze of the scorching heat left nothing of it but a radiance within vessels of light.) He made the grape's juice a radiance because it is more intensely blazing and gleams more, while its skin is like a light that protects and preserves that radiance. How skilled Ibn al-Rūmī was in borrowing it!

* Benefits:
1- The kāf of likeness has three states:
a- It must be a noun, which is when it is a khabar, a fāʿil, a mafʿūl, or governed by a preposition or by annexation, as in the verse above and as in the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib:
وما قتل الأحرار كالعفو عنهم ... ومن لك بالحر الذي يحفظ اليدا
(Nothing kills free men like pardoning them; and who will provide you a free man who remembers a favour?)
b- It must be a particle, which is when it occurs as the ṣila of a relative noun.
c- Both are permissible in what remains besides these, and further discussion of the kāf will come in this book.
2- ترك: originally means "he cast away and left", so it takes one object; sometimes it contains the sense of "making into", so it takes two.

dervis-irab:243-244.t:
* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِنْ دِيارِهِمْ) The hamza is for confirmatory interrogation (istifhām taqrīrī); لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussion; تر is an imperfect verb, jussive because of لم, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «تر». The clause خرجوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The seeing here is seeing of the heart (i.e. knowing), but it has been given the sense of "arriving at", so it is made transitive with إلى; the meaning is: "Has it not reached your knowledge?". The sentence is resumptive, introduced to establish the condition of those people. And من ديارهم is attached to خرجوا. (وَهُمْ أُلُوفٌ) The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāl); هم is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and ألوف the khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of an accusative ḥāl. (حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ) A mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). They were a people of the Children of Israel who fled from the plague that had swept over their land. (فَقالَ لَهُمُ اللَّهُ مُوتُوا) The fā' is a conjunction; قال is a past verb; ولهم is attached to قال; اللَّه is the agent; and the clause موتوا is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said. (ثُمَّ أَحْياهُمْ) ثم is a conjunction denoting sequence with a delay; أحياهم is conjoined to an omitted element, i.e. "so they died, then He gave them life". The conjunction ثم is used to convey the length of the interval between the causing of death and the giving of life. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى النَّاسِ) The sentence is resumptive, introduced to contrast Allah the Exalted's bounty to people with their denial of that bounty by not giving thanks. إنّ and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); ذو فضل is the khabar of إنّ; and على الناس is attached to an omitted adjective of فضل. (وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَشْكُرُونَ) The wāw is circumstantial; ولكنّ is a particle of rectification (istidrāk) and of accusative government; أكثر الناس is its noun; and the clause لا يشكرون is its khabar. (وَقاتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) The wāw is a conjunction on an implied element understood from the context, i.e. "do not flee, O believers, as the Children of Israel fled, and fight your enemies"; and في سبيل الله is attached to قاتلوا. (وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ) This is also a conjunction; أنّ and what is within its scope stand in place of the two objects of اعلموا; and سميع عليم is the khabar of إنّ [Translator's note: the source ends «خبر ان لأن», which appears to be a garbled phrase; translated as «the khabar of inna»].

* Rhetoric:
1- The intended meaning of the interrogative is confirmation (taqrīr), mixed with wonder and with a stirring of eagerness to know the gist of the story and grasp its point.
2- Majāz mursal (a loose figurative usage) in his words: «حذر الموت»; what is meant is the sickness of the plague that swept over them, the relation being regard for what this sickness leads to.
3- Ṭibāq (antithesis) between the causing of death and the giving of life.
4- Concision by omission (ījāz bi-l-ḥadhf) in his words «موتوا» and «ثم أحياهم»: "so they died" was omitted since it need not be mentioned, to draw attention to the fact that nothing falls short of His will, Exalted is He.

dervis-irab:245-245.t:
* Vocabulary:
(القرض): an ism maṣdar (noun of the verbal noun), because the maṣdar proper is إقراض; القرض here means the thing lent, and the effect of that shows in the i'rab, as will come.
(الأضعاف): plural of ضعف; it is possible that الضعف is an ism maṣdar, and the effect of that also shows in the i'rab.

* I'rab:
(مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي) من is interrogative, a mubtadaʾ; ذا is a demonstrative, the khabar; and الذي is a substitute (badal) for the demonstrative or an adjective of it; the sentence is resumptive. (يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ) The clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (قَرْضاً حَسَناً) A mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and it is permissible that it be in the sense of the thing lent, in which case it is a second direct object; and حسنا is an adjective. (فَيُضاعِفَهُ لَهُ أَضْعافاً كَثِيرَةً) The fā' is of causation; يضاعفه is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أنْ after the fā' of causation that occurs as the answer to an interrogative; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يضاعفه; and أضعافا is a clarifying ḥāl from the hā'. Abū l-Baqāʾ permitted construing it as a second direct object; and if we consider it an ism maṣdar, it may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq. Among examples of asmāʾ al-maṣdar (nouns of the verbal noun) is العطاء in the sense of الإعطاء; al-Quṭāmī said:
أكفرا بعد ردّ الموت عني ... وبعد عطائك المائة الرتاعا
(Is it ingratitude, after you turned death away from me, and after your giving of the hundred grazing camels?)
And كثيرة is an adjective of أضعاف, and the presence of this adjective favours construing it as a ḥāl. (وَاللَّهُ يَقْبِضُ وَيَبْصُطُ) The wāw is resumptive; اللَّه is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يقبض is its khabar; and ويَبْصُطُ is conjoined to يَقْبِضُ. (وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; وإليه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ترجعون; and the clause is conjoined to the preceding one.

* Rhetoric:
1- Istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya (explicit metaphor) in يقرض: the thing likened, namely the good deed, is omitted and the thing likened to is kept, namely what is borrowed of wealth and the like; and the metaphor is embellished (rushshiḥa) by the multiplication, as happens with loans and the returns that accrue on them.
2- Ṭibāq (antithesis) between يقبض and يبسط.

* Benefits:
Ibn Jarīr preferred the reading with the nominative in «فيضاعفه», with the alif retained and يضاعفه in the nominative. He justified his preference by saying that when the fā' enters the answer of a conditional, its answer with the fā' can only be nominative.

dervis-irab:246-246.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْمَلَإِ): of a people, their leading men and nobles; it is a collective noun with no singular from its own wording. They were so called because they fill the hearts and the eyes with beauty and splendour. The plural is أملاء, like سبب and أسباب. He said:
وقال لها الأملاء من كل معشر ... وخير أقاويل الرّجال سديدها
(The notables of every company said to her, and the best of men's sayings is the soundest.)
It is also said: هو مليء ومليّ, that is, wealthy and capable.

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الْمَلَإِ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ) The hamza is for confirmatory interrogation, and the speech is resumptive, introduced to establish a story full of lessons, as will come. لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussion, and «تر» is an imperfect verb, jussive because of لم. The seeing here is of the heart, containing the sense of knowing and arriving, so that transitivity with إلى is sound; its like has already been given.
