The agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; إلى الملأ is attached to «تر»; and من بني إسرائيل is attached to an omitted ḥāl; and the verbal clause is resumptive. (مِنْ بَعْدِ مُوسى) Attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "after his death also". (إِذْ قالُوا) إذ is an adverb of past time attached to the implied story, i.e. "to the story of the Children of Israel's notables". Since persons are not things one wonders at, the meaning becomes: "Have you not seen what happened to the notables of the Children of Israel after the death of Moses?". The clause قالوا is in the position of a genitive by annexation. (لِنَبِيٍّ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to قالوا. (لَهُمُ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective.
He is Joshua, the man of the story of the standing still of the sun, which was a splendid source of inspiration for poets, and which we shall relate shortly. (ابْعَثْ لَنا مَلِكاً) The sentence consists of an imperative verb and its agent, and is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said; ولنا is attached to ابعث; and ملكا is a direct object, i.e. a commander. (نُقاتِلْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) An imperfect verb, jussive because it is the answer to a request; في سبيل الله is attached to نقاتل; and the clause نقاتل is conjoined to ابعث. (قالَ) A past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; the clause is resumptive. (هَلْ عَسَيْتُمْ) هل is a particle of interrogation for confirmation; عسيتم is a past verb, one of the verbs of hope, and the tā' is its noun. (إِنْ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِتالُ) إن is conditional; كتب is a past verb, passive, in the position of a jussive, being the protasis; عليكم is attached to كتب; and القتال is the deputy agent. The apodosis is omitted, its implied form being:
"you will not hasten to fight". The protasis and its apodosis form a parenthetical clause between the noun of عسى and its khabar, which is his words (أَلَّا تُقاتِلُوا): أنْ is a particle of maṣdar and accusative government, لا is a negative, and تقاتلوا is an imperfect verb in the accusative by أنْ. The clause هل عسيتم is the content of what was said. (قالُوا) The clause is resumptive; قالوا is a verb and agent. (وَما لَنا أَلَّا نُقاتِلَ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) The wāw is a conjunction merely to link the speech to what precedes; ما is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ; ولنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; and أن لا نقاتل في سبيل الله: the maṣdar formed from أنْ and what is within its scope is in the position of an accusative by removal of the preposition, the implied form being: "What is the matter with us in leaving off the fight?". (وَقَدْ أُخْرِجْنا مِنْ دِيارِنا)
The wāw is circumstantial; قد is a particle of affirmation; أخرجنا is a past verb, passive, and the pronoun is the deputy agent; and من ديارنا is attached to أخرجنا. (وَأَبْنائِنا) Conjoined to «ديارنا»; the verb of expulsion must be taken to contain the sense of distancing for the conjunction to be sound. The clause is in the position of an accusative ḥāl. (فَلَمَّا كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْقِتالُ) The fā' is resumptive and «لما» is temporal or connective; كتب is a past verb, passive; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كتب; and القتال is the deputy agent. (تَوَلَّوْا إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ) The clause تولوا has no grammatical position because it is the answer to «لما», which is conditional but not jussive-governing; تولوا is a verb and agent; إلا is a particle of exception; and قليلا is an excepted noun, continuous (muttaṣil) because they are of the same kind as the people; and منهم is attached to an omitted adjective of «قليلا». (وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ) The wāw is resumptive; اللَّه is a mubtadaʾ and عليم its khabar; and بالظالمين, the preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to عليم.

dervis-irab:62-62.t:
* Vocabulary:
(هادُوا): "they became Jews" (tahawwadū). One says hāda yahūdu, tahawwada and yatahawwadu when someone enters Judaism; he is a hāʾid, and the plural is hūd.
(النَّصارى): the plural of naṣrān and naṣrānī. One says rajul naṣrān and naṣrānī, and imraʾa naṣrāna and naṣrāniyya; the yāʾ in naṣrānī is for intensification. They were so named because they supported (naṣarū) the Master, the Messiah, or because they were with him in a village called Naṣrān or Nāṣira, and so were named after it. Sībawayh said: it is not used in speech except with the yāʾ of relation.
(الصَّابِئِينَ): the plural of ṣābiʾ, from ṣabaʾa fulān, when someone leaves the religion. The Sabians were a people who worshipped the stars; among them was Abū Isḥāq al-Ṣābiʾ, the well-known secretary and poet.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ): a particle resembling the verb. (الَّذِينَ): a relative noun, its noun (ism). (آمَنُوا): a verbal clause with no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (وَالَّذِينَ): conjoined to the first (الَّذِينَ); the clause (هادُوا) has no position; and the clause of inna and what follows it is resumptive. (وَالنَّصارى وَالصَّابِئِينَ): conjoined to the noun of inna. (مَنْ): a relative noun, a badal (substitute) for the noun of inna, and the clause (آمَنَ) is the ṣila of the relative noun; you may also make it conditional, in the nominative position as mubtadaʾ (subject). (بِاللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to آمَنَ. (وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ): conjoined to اللَّهِ. (وَعَمِلَ): conjoined to آمَنَ. (صالِحاً): a direct object of عَمِلَ, or an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq), i.e. "he did a righteous deed". (فَلَهُمْ): the fāʾ is brought in because the relative noun implies the meaning of a condition, or it is the linking fāʾ of the apodosis; and لَهُمْ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted predicate placed first. (أَجْرُهُمْ): a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna if we make مَنْ a relative, or in the position of a jussive as the apodosis if we make it conditional; and the whole clause is in the nominative position as the khabar of inna. (عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ): the adverbial is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "deserved" or "settled". (وَلا خَوْفٌ): the wāw is a conjunction, لا is a negative, and خَوْفٌ is a mubtadaʾ for which beginning with it was permissible because the negative precedes it. (عَلَيْهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of خَوْفٌ. (وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ): conjoined to what precedes; its i'rab has already been given in full.

dervis-irab:63-64.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الطُّورَ): one of the mountains of Palestine, and the word is applied to any mountain, as in al-Qāmūs.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ أَخَذْنا): the i'rab of its like has already been given; and the clause أَخَذْنا is in the genitive position through the annexation of the adverbial to it. (مِيثاقَكُمْ): a direct object. (وَرَفَعْنا): conjoined to أَخَذْنا. (فَوْقَكُمُ): the adverbial is attached to رَفَعْنا. (الطُّورَ): a direct object. (خُذُوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; the clause is the quoted speech of an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "We said: take"; and the clause of saying is a ḥāl, the implied form being "saying: take". (ما): a relative noun, the object of خُذُوا; and the clause (آتَيْناكُمْ) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of مَا. (بِقُوَّةٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are in the accusative position as a ḥāl; the meaning is "take what We have given you while being resolved on earnestness and action". (وَاذْكُرُوا): conjoined to خُذُوا. (ما): a relative noun, the object of اذْكُرُوا. (فِيهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element that has no position, because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (لَعَلَّكُمْ): laʿalla and its noun, and the clause (تَتَّقُونَ) is its khabar. (ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ): a conjunction indicating delay, signalling that there was compliance with the command and then turning away from it. (مِنْ بَعْدِ ذلِكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تَوَلَّيْتُمْ. (فَلَوْلا): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and لَوْلا is a particle of prevention because of existence, implying the meaning of a condition. (فَضْلُ اللَّهِ): a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, the implied form being "existent". (عَلَيْكُمْ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to فَضْلُ. (وَرَحْمَتُهُ): conjoined to فَضْلُ. (لَكُنْتُمْ): the lām occurs in the apodosis of لَوْلا; and kāna and its noun. (مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of كُنْتُمْ; and the clause has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.

* Benefits:
(لولا) is a particle of prevention because of existence. It is specific to the nominal sentence, and the noun that comes after it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar must be omitted, because the speech indicates it and the apodosis of لولا takes its place in giving the benefit. The rule for the lām in its apodosis is as follows. If the speech is affirmative, then the common usage is for the lām to enter, as in this verse and its like. If it is negative, then if the negative particle is مَا, the common usage is to omit the lām, and bringing it is rare; but if the negative particle is something other than مَا, omitting the lām is obligatory.
Al-Mutanabbī said:
لولا مفارقة الأحباب ما وجدت ... لها المنايا إلى أرواحنا سبلا
(Were it not for the parting of the beloved ones, death would have found no ways to our souls.) [Translator's note: the source prints «أرا وحنا», evidently a corruption of «أرواحنا»; translated as «our souls».]
ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
عوجي علينا ربة الهودج ... لو لاك في ذا العام لم أحجج
(Turn toward us, O lady of the howdah; had it not been for you, I would not have made the pilgrimage this year.)
This is so that two lāms do not follow one another. And لو ما is like لولا in all its rules.

dervis-irab:65-66.t:
* Vocabulary:
(السَّبْتِ): originally a verbal noun of sabata, meaning to cease work. It is derived either from al-subūt, which is rest and ease, or from al-sabt, which is cutting, because things were cut off (sabatat) in it and their creation was completed; the day of the week was then named after it. (خاسِئِينَ): driven away and expelled, from khusūʾ, which is abasement and expulsion.
(نَكالًا): nakāl is prevention; al-nakl is the name for an iron fetter. Punishment is called nakāl because it prevents the one who is not punished from doing what the other did, and prevents the one who is punished from returning to his first deed.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ): the wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; and قَدْ is a particle of certainty. (عَلِمْتُمُ): verb and agent. (الَّذِينَ): a relative noun, direct object. (اعْتَدَوْا): verb and agent; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (مِنْكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl from the pronoun in اعْتَدَوْا. (فِي السَّبْتِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اعْتَدَوْا, because it is the time of the transgression; their transgression was catching fish, which they had been forbidden. (فَقُلْنا): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and قُلْنا is verb and agent, the clause conjoined to the clause اعْتَدَوْا. (لَهُمْ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قُلْنا. (كُونُوا): an imperative defective verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is its noun. (قِرَدَةً): its khabar. (خاسِئِينَ): a second khabar; nothing prevents making it an adjective. It was also said that both are khabars and that they are treated as one word, and this is a good view. (فَجَعَلْناها): the clause is conjoined to what precedes. (نَكالًا): the second object of جَعَلْنا. The pronoun in جَعَلْناها appears because it refers to the transformation (maskha) understood from the folds of the discourse. (لِما): the lām is a preposition, and مَا is a relative noun in the genitive position through the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of نَكالًا. (بَيْنَ يَدَيْها): the adverbial is attached to an omitted element that has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَما): conjoined to the first مَا. (خَلْفَها): an adverbial attached to an omitted ṣila of the second مَا. (وَمَوْعِظَةً): conjoined to نَكالًا. (لِلْمُتَّقِينَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of مَوْعِظَةً.

* Benefits:
The commentators have a long discussion on the story of this transgression. In summary: Allah the Exalted forbade them work and the catching of fish on the Sabbath, so the fish would appear in great numbers on it and go away when it went; so they devised various stratagems to catch them, such as digging a pit or tying the fish up, and when the Sabbath had passed they took them. Then this became frequent until it became their habit, down to the end of that delightful story, which portrays the nature of the Jews and their artfulness in scheming.

dervis-irab:67-67.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قالَ مُوسى لِقَوْمِهِ): the i'rab of its like has been repeated. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ): inna and its noun, and the clause (يَأْمُرُكُمْ) is its khabar. (أَنْ): a particle of the maṣdar and of the accusative. (تَذْبَحُوا): an imperfect verb put in the accusative by أَنْ; and أَنْ with what is within its scope is in the interpretation of a maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "to slaughter (bi-an tadhbaḥū) a cow". (بَقَرَةً): a direct object. (قالُوا): verb and agent. (أَتَتَّخِذُنا): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval; and تَتَّخِذُنا is a verb with a latent agent and an attached first object. (هُزُواً): the second object; and the verbal clause is the quoted speech. (قالَ): a past verb whose agent is "he"; and the clause (أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ) is the quoted speech. (أَنْ أَكُونَ): أَنْ with what is within its scope is a maṣdar in the accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "from being (min an akūna)"; and the noun of أَكُونَ is latent, the implied form being "I". (مِنَ الْجاهِلِينَ): its khabar.

dervis-irab:68-68.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الفارض): the old cow, because she has "cut" (faraḍat) her age, that is, she has passed through it and reached its end.
(البكر): the young, immature one.
(العوان): the middle-aged one; the plural is ʿūn, with ʿayn damma and wāw sukūn. Al-Kisāʾī said: al-ʿawān is the one that has had a mate; from this is said "ḥarb ʿawān" (a war of the second round).

* I'rab:
(قالُوا): verb and agent. (ادْعُ): an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the weak letter, and its agent is a latent pronoun, the implied form being "you"; and the clause is the quoted speech. (لَنا): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ادْعُ. (رَبَّكَ): a direct object. (يُبَيِّنْ): an imperfect verb jussive because it is the answer to a request. (لَنا): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يُبَيِّنْ. (ما): an interrogative noun in the nominative position as mubtadaʾ. (هِيَ): a detached pronoun in the nominative position as khabar, and the nominal clause is in the accusative position as the object of يُبَيِّنْ. (قالَ): a past verb. (إِنَّهُ): inna and its noun; the hamza of inna is vowelled with kasra because it is preceded by saying; and the clause (يَقُولُ إِنَّها بَقَرَةٌ) is the khabar of inna, and the clause of inna with what is within its scope is the quoted speech. (لا): a negative. (فارِضٌ): an adjective of بَقَرَةٌ. (وَلا بِكْرٌ): conjoined to what precedes; when an indefinite noun is described by something that a negative has entered, the negative is repeated, and likewise with the khabar and the ḥāl. (عَوانٌ): also an adjective of بَقَرَةٌ. (بَيْنَ ذلِكَ): the adverbial is attached to an omitted adjective of عَوانٌ, and ذلِكَ is a muḍāf ilayhi (annexed noun); the demonstrative has stood in for two things, since it is used to point to the old cow and the young one together. Similar is the saying of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zibaʿrā on the day of Uḥud before his conversion to Islam: "إن للخير وللشرّ مدى ... وكلا ذلك وجه وقبل" (Good and evil each have a limit, and both of these have a direction and a front). (فَافْعَلُوا): the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquent omission (fāʾ faṣīḥa), and افْعَلُوا is verb and agent. (ما): a relative noun, direct object; the clause (تُؤْمَرُونَ) is the ṣila of the relative noun, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "bihi". Some permitted that مَا be a maṣdar, i.e. "so do your command", with the maṣdar in the sense of the passive object, i.e. "what you are commanded".

dervis-irab:31-33.t:
* Vocabulary:
(آدَمَ): a foreign proper noun (ism ʿalam aʿjamī) like آذر, عابر and عاذر, and it is a diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) because of being a proper name and foreign. He erred who claimed that it is derived from الأدمة, i.e. swarthiness, or from أديم الأرض, i.e. its surface, because derivation is among the characteristics of Arabic. Imam al-Ṭabarī had a claim, and we do not know how it issued from him, namely that it is a quadriliteral verb used as a name. Of this same error is their attempt to derive يعقوب from العقب and إبليس from الإبلاس. In that case we are entitled to ask: why were these proper names made diptotes, were it not for being proper names and foreign? So take note of this section.

* I'rab:
(وَعَلَّمَ) The wāw is a conjunction; علم is a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو", referring to Allah; the clause is conjoined to omitted clauses, whose implied form is: "so He placed a vicegerent on earth and named him Adam". (آدَمَ) first direct object. (الْأَسْماءَ) second direct object. (كُلَّها) tawkīd (emphasis) of الأسماء. (ثُمَّ) a conjunction of order with delay. (عَرَضَهُمْ) conjoined to the clause وعلّم, i.e. "and He presented the named things" or "cast them into their hearts"; the rational beings were given precedence over the non-rational, and that is one of the practices of the Arabs in their speech. (عَلَى الْمَلائِكَةِ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عرضهم. (فَقالَ) conjoined to the clause عرضهم. (أَنْبِئُونِي) an imperative verb; the intent of the command here is to challenge them (taʿjīz); it is indeclinable with the omission of the nūn because its imperfect belongs to the five verbs (al-afʿāl al-khamsa); the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is the protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is an attached pronoun in the accusative position as direct object. (بِأَسْماءِ) the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the second object. (هؤُلاءِ) a demonstrative, indeclinable on the kasra, in the genitive position by annexation. (إِنْ) a jussive conditional particle. (كُنْتُمْ) a defective past verb (kāna), and the tāʾ is its ism. (صادِقِينَ) its khabar; and كنتم is in the jussive position as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "فأنبئوني".
(قالُوا) verb and fāʿil. (سُبْحانَكَ) absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq); it is a maṣdar that is hardly used except in annexation, accusative by the implication of its verb, like معاذ الله. (لا) negative of the genus, one of the sisters of inna, which resemble the verb. (عِلْمَ) its ism, indeclinable on the fatḥa. (لَنا) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of لا. (إِلَّا) a particle of restriction. (ما) a maṣdar particle or a relative noun, and together with what follows it, or by itself, it is in the nominative position as a substitute (badal) for the position of لا and its ism, as in لا إله إلا الله; the details of this will come in their place. (عَلَّمْتَنا) verb, fāʿil and object; the clause has no position because it is a ṣila of the relative. (إِنَّكَ) inna and its ism. (أَنْتَ) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or support (ʿimād), with no position. (الْعَلِيمُ) the first khabar of inna. (الْحَكِيمُ) the second khabar of inna. It is also permissible to parse أنت as a mubtadaʾ whose two khabars are العليم الحكيم, with the nominal clause in the nominative position as the khabar of inna.
(قالَ) a past verb, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; the clause is an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya) with no position. (يا آدَمُ) yā is a particle of vocative for a mid-distance addressee, and آدم is a singular proper-name vocative, indeclinable on the ḍamma. (أَنْبِئْهُمْ) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت", and the hāʾ is the direct object; the verbal clause is in the accusative position as reported speech. (بِأَسْمائِهِمْ) in the position of the second object. (فَلَمَّا) The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an omitted clause, the implied form being: "so he informed them of their names; and when he informed them" — the clause was omitted because the meaning is clear; and لما is an adverb meaning "when" (ḥīna), or a connecting particle containing the meaning of condition, in any case. (أَنْبَأَهُمْ) the clause is in the genitive position by the annexation of the adverb to it if لما is made an adverb, or conjoined if it is for connection. (بِأَسْمائِهِمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنبأهم. (قالَ) the clause has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (أَلَمْ) The hamza is for confirmatory interrogation (istifhām taqrīrī) — the hamza, when it enters upon a negation, gives confirmation — and لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussion. (أَقُلْ) an imperfect verb jussive by لم, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنا". (لَكُمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to أقل. (إِنِّي) inna and its ism. (أَعْلَمُ) an imperfect nominative verb; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause of inna and what is within its scope is in the accusative position as reported speech. (غَيْبَ السَّماواتِ) the direct object of أعلم. (وَالْأَرْضِ) conjoined to السموات. (وَأَعْلَمُ) conjoined to the first أعلم. (ما) a relative noun in the accusative position as direct object. (تُبْدُونَ) an imperfect nominative verb; the clause تبدون has no position because it is a ṣila. (وَما) conjoined to the first ما. (كُنْتُمْ) kāna and its ism. (تَكْتُمُونَ) the verbal clause is in the accusative position as the khabar of كنتم.

* Rhetoric:
Ṭibāq (antithesis) between السموات and الأرض and between تبدون and تكتمون. Note that ṭibāq is among the expressions that contradict their meaning, and for that reason some called it al-taḍādd (opposition) and al-takāfuʾ (equivalence); it is the joining of two opposite meanings. There is no correspondence between the linguistic and technical meaning of muṭābaqa, for in the language it means agreement; it is said: "I made the two things conform (ṭābaqtu)" when you place one on the model of the other. Ibn al-Athīr marvels because he does not know whence this name was derived, there being no correspondence between the name and what it names; and Qudāma calls it al-takāfuʾ. There is no difference whether the opposition is real, notional, or an opposition of negation and affirmation. Of the ṭibāq of negation is the saying of al-Samawʾal:
وننكر إن شئنا على الناس قولهم ... ولا ينكرون القول حين نقول
(We disapprove, if we wish, of people's speech, yet they do not disapprove our speech when we speak.)
He made ṭibāq between ننكر, which is affirmative, and ولا ينكرون, which is negative. And ṭibāq becomes muqābala (balanced contrast) when two or more meanings are brought and then what corresponds to them is brought in order, as in the saying of al-Buḥturī:
فإذا حاربوا أذلوا عزيزا ... وإذا سالموا أعزّوا ذليلا
(When they fight they humble the mighty, and when they make peace they exalt the humble.)
People never ceased to marvel at al-Buḥturī's combining three antitheses in his saying:
وأمة كان قبح الجور يشحطها ... دهرا فأصبح حسن العدل يرضيها
(A nation whom the ugliness of tyranny drove far away for an age, and now the beauty of justice pleases it.)
until Abū l-Ṭayyib came and surpassed him, with sweetness of wording and elegance of craft, making antithesis between five and five:
أزورهم وسود الليل يشفع لي ... وأنثني وبياض الصبح يغري بي
(I visit them while the blackness of night intercedes for me, and I turn back while the whiteness of dawn incites against me.)
He made ṭibāq between visiting and turning back, between blackness and whiteness, between night and dawn, between يشفع and يغري, and between لي and بي.

dervis-irab:258-259.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حَاجَّ): he overcame his opponent by means of the argument. Among their expressions: "There was between them muḥājja and mulājja" (disputation and wrangling).
(خاوِيَةٌ): fallen, or empty of its people.
(يَتَسَنَّهْ): the hāʾ is either part of the root or a hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt). That is, the year did not pass over it, whereas a thing ordinarily changes with the passing of time. So the lām of "sana" (year) is either a wāw or a hāʾ. It was also said: its origin is "yatasannan", from "al-ḥamaʾ al-masnūn" (aged black mud). A full discussion of this word will come in the I'rab.
(نُنْشِزُها): we move them and raise some of them onto others for assembly.

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِي حَاجَّ إِبْراهِيمَ فِي رَبِّهِ): a resumptive clause, brought to express wonder at the story of one of the tyrants; the address is to the Prophet ﷺ, but the intended meaning is general. The hamza is for the interrogative of wonder; «لم» is a particle of negation, reversal (of tense) and jussive; «تر» is an imperfect verb, jussive through «لم», its sign of jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you". «إلى الذي» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «تر»; a muḍāf must necessarily be omitted, i.e. "to the story of the one who disputed". «حاجّ» is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; «إبراهيم» is its direct object; «في ربّه» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «حاجّ».
(أَنْ آتاهُ اللَّهُ الْمُلْكَ): «أن» is a particle of maṣdar and accusative; «آتاه» is a past verb in the position of the accusative through «أن», and the hāʾ is the direct object. The maṣdar formed from «أن» and the verb after it is in the accusative position as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with an implied lām, because one of the conditions of the mafʿūl li-ajlihi is missing, namely sameness of agent; and dropping the lām before «أن» and «أنّ» is regular. The meaning is: he went forward to dispute with Abraham and to quarrel with him out of arrogance and insolence, whereas it would have been more fitting for him to give thanks for the blessing and to be humble when raised up. This is preferable to making it an adverbial of time meaning "the time of the giving of the blessing". Maṣdars may indeed occur as adverbials, as in "khufūq al-najm" (the setting of the star) and "miqdam al-ḥājj" (the arrival of the pilgrim).
(إِذْ قالَ إِبْراهِيمُ): «إذ» is an adverbial for past time, attached to «حاجّ». Al-Zamakhsharī and al-Jalāl allowed it to be a badal (substitute) for «أن آتاه» if the latter is taken to mean "time"; but the grammarians have stated explicitly that nothing takes the place of an adverbial of time except a maṣdar expressed in its own wording, so it is not permissible to say "ajīʾu an yaṣīḥa al-dīk" (I will come when the rooster crows) nor "jiʾtu an ṣāḥa al-dīk" (I came when the rooster crowed). «قال إبراهيم» is a verb and agent, and the clause is in the genitive position by annexation.
(رَبِّيَ الَّذِي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ): «ربي» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «الذي» is its khabar (predicate); the clause «يحيي» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun and has no position; «يميت» is conjoined to «يحيي»; the clause «ربي…» etc. is the content of the saying.
(قالَ أَنَا أُحْيِي وَأُمِيتُ): the clause is resumptive. «قال» is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; «أنا» is a mubtadaʾ; «أحيي» is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being "I", and the clause is the khabar of «أنا»; the clause «أنا أحيي» is a nominal clause in the accusative position as the content of the saying; «أميت» is conjoined to «أحيي».
(قالَ إِبْراهِيمُ): a verb and agent, and the clause is resumptive, brought to move from one argument to a clearer one.
(فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْتِي بِالشَّمْسِ مِنَ الْمَشْرِقِ): the fāʾ is the "eloquent" fāʾ (al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa), which occurs in the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you are able, as you falsely and presumptuously claim, then Allah brings the sun from the east…". «إن» and its noun; the clause «يأتي» is its khabar; the clause after the fāʾ has no position because it is the apodosis of an implied non-jussive condition. The preposition and genitive noun «بالشمس» are attached to «يأتي», and «من المشرق» is a preposition and its genitive noun also attached to «يأتي».
(فَأْتِ بِها مِنَ الْمَغْرِبِ): the eloquent fāʾ is repeated for emphasis and as a prelude to the argument. «أت» is an imperative verb, indeclinable through the dropping of the weak letter, and the agent is "you"; «بها» is attached to «أت»; «من المغرب» is attached to it as well.
(فَبُهِتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction. «بهت» is among the verbs that have come only in the passive; «الذي» is the nāʾib fāʾil (deputy agent) in terms of wording, and it may be an agent in terms of meaning, which is perhaps preferable. «كفر» is a past verb with a latent agent, and the clause is the ṣila of «الذي».
(وَاللَّهُ لا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ): the wāw is resumptive; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «لا يهدي» is its khabar; «القوم» is a direct object; «الظالمين» is an adjective.
(أَوْ كَالَّذِي مَرَّ عَلى قَرْيَةٍ): the sense of the speech is: "or have you seen the like of the one who…". So «أو» is a conjunction and the kāf is a noun meaning "like"; the verb was omitted because «ألم تر» indicates it. In such constructions the verb of seeing is often omitted, the purpose being wonder; one says "Have you not seen the one who did such-and-such" meaning "look at him" . In any case the nominal kāf is conjoined to «الذي حاج ابراهيم», and «الذي» is a muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «مر على قرية» is the ṣila of the relative noun. As for the village, it was said that he meant Jerusalem when Nebuchadnezzar destroyed it.
(وَهِيَ خاوِيَةٌ عَلى عُرُوشِها): the wāw is for ḥāl (circumstantial); «هي» is a mubtadaʾ and «خاوية» a khabar; «على عروشها» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «خاوية». The meaning is that the roofs fell first and the buildings followed them.
This depiction is a poetic embodiment of the perishing of created things: the perishing begins with the living beings and worlds, and the inanimate things follow them. Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī had caught sight, as if by a sidelong glance, of the sky of this wondrous meaning, and he transferred it precisely, faster than phantoms move across eyelids, saying in an elegy:
أين الذي الهرمان من بنيانه؟ ... ما قومه؟ ما يومه؟ ما المصرع؟
(Where is he whose building the two pyramids are? What was his people? What was his day? What was his place of fall?)
تتخلف الآثار عن أصحابها ... حينا ويدركها الفناء فتتبع
(The monuments outlast their owners for a time, then perishing overtakes them and they follow.)
The second verse is the intended one. Its meaning is that the monuments, that is, the buildings, remain after their masters to point to their power and strength, then there befalls them after the masters what befell the masters of perishing; ruin will overtake them and they will collapse in disrepair, then the roofs and lofty ceilings will fall on top of them, and the monuments will vanish. The exegetes have taken curious paths concerning the story of this passer-by, which it is pleasant to consult in the longer works. Did he say what he said by way of denying the resurrection? Was he an unbeliever? All of these are conjectures out of which a winged tale is composed; who will give us the gifted writer?
(قالَ: أَنَّى يُحْيِي هذِهِ اللَّهُ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها): «قال» is a verb whose agent is "he". «أنى» has two possible analyses: one, that it means "when" (matā), so that it is an adverbial attached to «يحيي»; the other, that it means "how" (kayfa), so that it is a ḥāl from «هذه», the operator in it being «يحيي». The clause «يحيي» is in the genitive position by annexation if «أنى» is an adverbial, or is the content of the saying if it means "how". «يحيي» is an imperfect verb; «هذه» is a preposed direct object; «الله» is a postposed agent; «بعد موتها» is an adverbial of time also attached to «يحيي». The clause «قال» is resumptive, brought to express longing for it and yearning for its rebuilding while sensing despair of it.
(فَأَماتَهُ اللَّهُ مِائَةَ عامٍ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; «أماته الله» is a verb, direct object and agent; «مائة» is an adverbial of time attached to «أماته», and «عام» is a muḍāf ilayhi.
(ثُمَّ بَعَثَهُ): conjoined to «أماته»; it is conjoined with «ثم» to indicate delay and the length of the period.
(قالَ: كَمْ لَبِثْتَ): the clause is resumptive, brought as a reply to a question that may stir in the mind, as if it were said: "What did Allah the Exalted say to him when He raised him after death?" «كم» is an interrogative noun in the accusative position as an adverbial of time attached to «لبثت», and its specified noun is omitted, as if it were said: "How much time did you remain?" «لبثت» is a verb and agent, and the clause is in the accusative position as the content of the saying.
(قالَ: لَبِثْتُ يَوْماً أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ): the clause of saying is resumptive, to serve as the reply to the question; the clause «لبثت» is in the accusative position as the content of the saying; «يوما» is an adverbial of time attached to «لبثت»; «أو» is a conjunction; «بعض يوم» is conjoined to «يوما», strung on the same thread of the temporal adverbial.
(قالَ: بَلْ لَبِثْتَ مِائَةَ عامٍ): the clause «قال» is resumptive; «بل» is a conjunction joining an omitted clause which must be supplied, the implied form being: "You did not stay a day or part of a day; rather you stayed a hundred years." «مائة عام» is an adverbial; and the clause is the content of the saying.
(فَانْظُرْ إِلى طَعامِكَ وَشَرابِكَ لَمْ يَتَسَنَّهْ): the fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ, here the apodosis of an implied condition, its implied form being: "if doubt and lack of reassurance arise in you concerning the matter of the resurrection, then look." «انظر» is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; «إلى طعامك» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «انظر»; «شرابك» is conjoined to «طعامك»; «لم» is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; «يتسنه» is an imperfect verb jussive through «لم», its sign of jussive being the sukūn if the hāʾ is part of the root; if the hāʾ is a hāʾ of pause, the verb is jussive by the dropping of the weak letter, and then the hāʾ of pause is retained in pausal form and not in connected speech, and its ruling will come. If the verb is from "tasannun", which means alteration, it is jussive by an implied sukūn on the dropped weak letter for which the second nūn was substituted. The clause «لم يتسنه» is a ḥāl.
(وَانْظُرْ إِلى حِمارِكَ): conjoined to what precedes. He singled it out for mention only because the passer-by used to ride it, and because the lesson drawn from living creatures has a stronger effect. The i'rab of its like has already been given.
(وَلِنَجْعَلَكَ آيَةً لِلنَّاسِ): the wāw is a conjunction and the lām is for cause; «نجعلك» is an imperfect verb in the accusative through an implied «أن» after the lām of cause; the lām and the maṣdar governed by it are attached to an omitted verb, i.e. "We did all that in order to make you a sign"; the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "We"; the kāf is the first direct object and «آية» the second direct object; «للناس» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of «آية».
(وَانْظُرْ إِلَى الْعِظامِ كَيْفَ نُنْشِزُها): the wāw is a conjunction; «انظر» is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; «إلى العظام» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «انظر»; «كيف» is an interrogative noun in the accusative position as a ḥāl, and the owner of the ḥāl is the accusative pronoun in «ننشزها»; the clause is a badal (substitute) from «العظام» and is in the genitive or accusative position, because the verb «نظر» of eyesight is transitive with «إلى», but it is suspended from operating because of the interrogative, so it is in the accusative position, i.e. "to the state of the bones". «ننشزها» is an imperfect verb in the nominative; the hāʾ is the direct object and the agent is latent, its implied form being "We".
(ثُمَّ نَكْسُوها لَحْماً): «ثم» is a conjunction of order with delay; «نكسوها» is an imperfect verb taking two objects, the first being the hāʾ, and «لحما» is the second object.
(فَلَمَّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction joining something implied that the context requires, as if He said: "So Allah raised them up and clothed them with flesh, and he looked at them, and it became clear to him how the giving of life and the resurrection are completed." «لما» is a temporal, non-jussive particle attached to the apodosis; «تبين» is a past verb indeclinable on an overt fatḥa; the agent of «تبين» is a concealed pronoun referring to the manner of giving life; al-Zamakhsharī implied it in a curious way, saying: "when what had been obscure to him became clear to him", while al-Jalāl implied: "when that became clear to him by direct witnessing". The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «تبين», and the clause «تبين» is in the genitive position by annexation.
(قالَ: أَعْلَمُ أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): «قال» is a verb whose agent is latent; the clause «أعلم» is the content of the saying, and the clause of saying has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; «أن» with its noun and khabar takes the place of the two objects of «أعلم».

* Benefits:
1- The maṣdar substitutes for the adverbial when it is a muḍāf ilayhi and specifies a time or a quantity, e.g. "jiʾtuka ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr" (I came to you at the time of the afternoon prayer) and "miqdam al-ḥājj" (the arrival of the pilgrim).
2- The hāʾ of pause (hāʾ al-sakt): it is so called because one pauses on it without pausing on the end of the word. It has three places:
(a) The defective verb with its end dropped because of the jussive or the sukūn, such as: «لم يتسنه», "lam yaghzuh", "lam yakhshah", "lam yarmih", and "ighzuh", "ikhshah", "irmih"; and of it is His saying the Exalted: «فبهداهم اقتده». In all of this it is permissible, not obligatory, except in one case, namely where the verb has been subjected to dropping and remains on a single letter, like the imperative of "waʿā yaʿī", for you say "ʿih", dropping its first and last letters.
(b) The interrogative «ما» governed by a preposition: its alif must be dropped when it is governed by a preposition, as in "ʿamma", "mimma", "bima" and "fīma". When you pause on them you attach the hāʾ to preserve the fatḥa that indicates the alif.
(c) Every indeclinable word built on a vowel that does not resemble the declinable, such as the yāʾ of the first person, and "huwa" and "hiya": you pause on them with the hāʾ of pause to preserve the fatḥa. In the Qur'an: «ماهيه», «ماليه» and «سلطانيه». Ḥassān said:
إذا ما ترعرع منا الغلام ... فما إن يقال له: ما هوه؟
(When our boy grows up, it is not said of him: "Who is he?")
The proper state of the hāʾ of pause is to be vowelless, and vowelling it is a solecism according to the Basrans. Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī used to defy the grammarians, saying: وأحرّ قلباه ممن قلبه شبم ... ومن بجسمي وحالي عنده سقم
(Oh, how my heart burns for one whose heart is cold, and for one in whose view my body and condition are sick.)
He was, as you know, a Kufan, and the Kufans allow that. In fact the grammarians were greatly perplexed over this question, and were left bewildered before the saying of ʿUrwa about his beloved ʿAfrāʾ:
يا مرحباه بحمار عفرا ... ويا مرحباه بحمار ناجيه
(O welcome to the donkey of ʿAfrāʾ, and O welcome to the donkey of Nājiya.)
Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī defended Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī in his commentary on his Dīwān in an engaging discussion; it would be good if you consulted it.
3- The interrogative in this verse departs from its original meaning. The first, «ألم تر», means wonder, i.e. "Marvel, Muhammad, at this story"; and the second interrogative is for deeming something momentous, namely «أنى يحيي هذه الله بعد موتها».

A necessary historical glimpse:
ʿUzayr ibn Sharkhiyā was among the inhabitants of Jerusalem and was among those whom Nebuchadnezzar took captive. When he was freed from captivity and came and saw it in that state, riding on a donkey, he entered it and went about in it, and saw no one there.
Most of its trees were bearing fruit, so he ate of the fruit and pressed some grapes, then tied his donkey with a rope, put the rest of the fruit in a basket and the rest of the juice in a skin or small waterskin. Then Allah cast sleep upon him and he slept, and when he slept Allah took his soul from him and caused his donkey to die, while his juice and figs remained with him. When seventy years had passed since his death, Allah gave power to one of the kings of Persia, who marched with his troops until he reached Jerusalem and rebuilt it, and it became better than it had been, and its people returned to it, and Allah blinded the eyes to ʿUzayr throughout this period. When the hundred years had passed, Allah revived him, and he began to look at his donkey as the spirit moved in it and its limbs came together, and so on to the end of that story, which we wish a skilled storywriter would take up and make into an artistic tale. It condemns the saying of the Jews about ʿUzayr, that he is the son of Allah, exalted is Allah above that.

Important remarks:
1- We spoke about His saying the Exalted «ألم تر» in the section on I'rab, and we came across an important statement of al-Taftāzānī, the gist of which is: both the expression «ألم تر» and «أرأيت» are used with the intention of wonder, except that the first relates to the thing wondered at, so one says "Have you not seen the one who did such-and-such" meaning "look at him and marvel at his state", whereas the second relates to the like of the thing wondered at, so one says "Have you seen the like of the one who did such-and-such?" meaning that he is so strange that his like is not seen. It is not correct to say "alam tara ilā mithlihi" (have you not seen his like), since the implication would be "look at the like and marvel at the one who did such-and-such". Hence the conjoining of «كالذي مرّ» to «الذي حاج» was not straightforward, and interpretation was needed either in the conjoined, by making it attached to an omitted "have you seen…", or in the one conjoined to, considering it to be in the meaning of "have you seen like the one who disputed", so that conjoining to it becomes valid.
I say: this is a limitless subtlety of observation and depth, and an unrivalled scholarly thoroughness; we have not corrected our i'rab as he saw it, and have contented ourselves with recording this remark.
2- Abū al-Suʿūd al-ʿImādī, muftī of the Ottoman court, who held the Islamic fatwa office for thirty years, author of the commentary called "Irshād al-ʿAql al-Salīm ilā Mazāyā al-Kitāb al-Karīm" and who died in 1574 CE, said in his discussion of the kāf in His saying «أو كالذي»:
"The kāf is either a noun, as a group chose, brought to alert to the multiplicity of the evidences and that they are not restricted to what has been mentioned, as in your saying: 'The past verb is like naṣara'; or redundant (zāʾida), as others have preferred, the meaning being: 'Have you not seen the one who passed by a village, how Allah guided him and brought him out of the darkness of doubt into the light of sight and witnessing?' that is, you have seen that and witnessed it."
3- Ibn Hishām said in al-Mughnī: "Among the misconceptions in this chapter is the statement of some regarding His saying «وانظر إلى العظام كيف ننشزها» that the interrogative clause is a ḥāl. The correct view is that «كيف» alone is a ḥāl from the object of «ننشزها», and that the clause is a badal from «العظام»."
Al-Dasūqī cited in his gloss on Ibn Hishām that this clause cannot take the place of the thing substituted for, which is a condition for the validity of the badal. But al-Dasūqī overlooked that the attention is to the meaning, that is, to the bones and the manner of their raising, apart from the fact that this rule holds in the majority of cases.

dervis-irab:221-221.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلا): the waw is resumptive and لا is prohibitive. (تَنْكِحُوا): with fatḥa on the tāʾ, an imperfect of nakaḥa, jussive by لا; the waw is the agent. (الْمُشْرِكاتِ): a direct object, its sign of accusative being the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. (حَتَّى يُؤْمِنَّ): حتى is a particle of limit and of genitive; يؤمن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn because the nūn of the feminine plural is attached to it, and it is in the position of the accusative by an implied أن after حتى; the nūn of the feminine plural is the agent; the preposition and its genitive noun, from حتى and the interpreted maṣdar, are attached to تنكحوا. (وَلَأَمَةٌ): the waw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, introduced to explain the difference between the believing woman and the idolatress; the lām is the lām of inceptive (ibtidāʾ) and أمة is a mubtadaʾ; it is permissible to begin with an indefinite noun because it is qualified. (مُؤْمِنَةٌ): an adjective of أمة. (خَيْرٌ): the khabar. (مِنْ مُشْرِكَةٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to خير. (وَلَوْ): the waw is the waw of ḥāl and لو is conditional in the sense of إن. (أَعْجَبَتْكُمْ): a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "she", referring to the slave woman; the kāf is the direct object. The clause أعجبتكم is the khabar of an omitted kāna together with its noun, after لو; and the clause لو أعجبتكم is a ḥāl. The meaning is: a believing slave woman is better than an idolatress, even while she has pleased you with her beauty and wealth. Further explanation of this will come in the section on Benefits. (وَلا): the waw is a conjunction and لا is prohibitive. (تَنْكِحُوا): with ḍamma on the tāʾ, an imperfect of ankaḥa, jussive by لا; the waw is the agent. (الْمُشْرِكِينَ): a direct object. (حَتَّى يُؤْمِنُوا): حتى is a particle of limit and of genitive; يؤمنوا is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive (jussive in form) by an implied أن after حتى «[Translator's note: the source says "jussive"; the intended meaning is subjunctive, with the nūn dropped]». (وَلَعَبْدٌ مُؤْمِنٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ مُشْرِكٍ وَلَوْ أَعْجَبَكُمْ): the i'rab of its like has been given before. (أُولئِكَ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ. (يَدْعُونَ إِلَى النَّارِ): the clause is the khabar of the demonstrative; the clause is resumptive, introduced to explain the wisdom in that; and you may make it explicative (mufassira). In any case it has no grammatical position. (وَاللَّهُ يَدْعُوا إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ): conjoined to what precedes. (وَالْمَغْفِرَةِ): conjoined to الجنة. (بِإِذْنِهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "giving permission for that". (وَيُبَيِّنُ آياتِهِ): conjoined to يدعو; آياته is a direct object, its sign of accusative being the kasra standing in place of the fatḥa. (لِلنَّاسِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يبين. (لَعَلَّهُمْ): laʿalla and its noun. (يَتَذَكَّرُونَ): the verbal clause is the khabar of laʿalla, and the clause of hope is a ḥāl.

* Benefits:
The omission of kāna with its noun, leaving its khabar, is regular after the two conditionals إن and لو; its details will come in their places.
A historical glimpse: in this verse there is a lofty refinement, wonderful human teachings and a denunciation of racial and colour discrimination. It is said that this verse was revealed about ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa. He had a black slave woman with whom he grew angry one day and slapped her; then he came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him. The Prophet said to him: "And what is she, O ʿAbd Allāh?" He said: "She testifies that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah, she fasts Ramadan, performs ablution well and prays." He said: "This is a believer." ʿAbd Allāh said: "By Him who sent you with the truth, I shall surely free her and surely marry her." And he did so. Some of the Muslims criticised him and said: "He marries a slave woman!", and they offered him a free idolatress woman. Then the verse was revealed.

dervis-irab:222-223.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْمَحِيضِ): a mīmī verbal noun or a noun of time; al-ḥayḍ is the flowing of blood. The details are set out in the books of jurisprudence.

* I'rab:
(وَيَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْمَحِيضِ): speech conjoined to the rulings that precede. It is to be observed that the question is introduced with the waw three times and appears without it four times, because the questions that came with the waw were asked at one single time, so conjoining them with the waw was fitting; but where the times of the questions differ, the speech came bare of the waw, as a signal of the interruption and the difference of the periods. This is one of the secrets of the Qur'an and its marvellous inimitability. عن المحيض: attached to يسألونك. (قُلْ): an imperative verb whose latent agent is "you"; the clause is resumptive. (هُوَ): a mubtadaʾ. (أَذىً): the khabar; the nominal clause is the content of the saying. (فَاعْتَزِلُوا): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the eloquent fāʾ), that is, "if you wish to know its ruling, then keep apart"; the clause after it has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. (النِّساءَ): a direct object. (فِي الْمَحِيضِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "while they are in a state of menstruation". (فَإِذا): the fāʾ is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb of future time, governing its protasis in the genitive and itself accusative through its apodosis. (تَطَهَّرْنَ): a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn because the nūn of the feminine plural is attached to it; the nūn is an attached pronoun in the position of the nominative as agent; the clause تطهرن is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (فَأْتُوهُنَّ): the fāʾ links the apodosis of إذا; فأتوهن is an imperative verb, indeclinable through the dropping of the nūn; the waw is the agent and the hāʾ the direct object; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. (مِنْ حَيْثُ): من is a preposition, and حيث is an adverb of place, indeclinable on ḍamma in the position of the genitive by من; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to فأتوهن. (أَمَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ): a past verb, a direct object and an agent; the clause is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ): inna and its noun. (يُحِبُّ): an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He", referring to Allah the Exalted; the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of inna. (التَّوَّابِينَ): a direct object; the clause of inna and what follows it is explanatory of a reason and has no grammatical position. (وَيُحِبُّ الْمُتَطَهِّرِينَ): conjoined to the clause يحب التوابين. (نِساؤُكُمْ): a mubtadaʾ. (حَرْثٌ): the khabar. (لَكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of حرث. (فَأْتُوا): the fāʾ is resumptive, and أتوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable through the dropping of the nūn; the waw is the agent. (حَرْثَكُمْ): a direct object. The nominal clause and the verbal clause are both resumptive, introduced to explain the ruling in this social matter. For the Muslims had kept away from their women in application of the apparent sense of the verse of menstruation, and had put them out of their houses. Some of the Bedouins said: "O Messenger of Allah, the cold is severe and clothes are few. If we give them preference with the clothes, the rest of the household will perish, and if we keep the clothes for ourselves, the menstruating women will perish!" He said: "I only commanded you to keep apart from having intercourse with them, and you were not commanded to put them out of the houses as the non-Arabs do." Then the Jews, following their habit of obstinacy and wrangling and of creating division and confusion, began to circulate sayings that have no truth. Among them was their saying: whoever approaches his wife in her front from the direction of her back, the child comes squint-eyed. So the second and third verses were revealed, to ease matters for the servants and to secure their enjoyment, as will come in the section on Rhetoric. (أَنَّى شِئْتُمْ): a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), an adverb of place attached to أتوا; the clause شئتم is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (وَقَدِّمُوا لِأَنْفُسِكُمْ): conjoined to what precedes. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ): also conjoined. (وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّكُمْ مُلاقُوهُ): another conjunction; أن and what is within its scope stand in place of the two objects of اعلموا; ملاقوه is the khabar of أن, its sign of nominative being the waw because it is a sound masculine plural. (وَبَشِّرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): another conjunction to what precedes.

* Rhetoric:
1- The emphatic simile (tashbīh baligh): He first likened women to a tilth (ḥarth), because of the resemblance between the seed deposited in their wombs and seeds; the point of likeness is that each of them is the substance of what comes from it.
2- Metonymy (kināya): by "approaching the tilth" in any manner He alluded to approaching the woman in whatever manner a man wishes, without prohibition or blame, so long as the place approached is one, namely the place of the tilth.

dervis-irab:197-197.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الفسوق): One says "fasaqa ʿan amr Allāh", that is, he departed from it; and "fasaqat al-ruṭaba ʿan qishrihā" (the fresh date burst out of its skin) and "the mouse from its hole". Among the rare features of the letters fāʾ and sīn is that their coming together as the first and second radicals of a word indicates something repugnant in the meaning of the word, and this is a wonderful matter by which our language is distinguished from all other languages. For example: "fasaʾa l-thawb", i.e. he tore it, and you dislike that anyone should tear your garment; "fasiʾa" (with kasra on the sīn), when the chest sticks out and the back goes in, which is an ugly, repellent form; "fasakha l-ʿaqd" means he annulled the contract, and I do not suppose anyone is pleased to have a contract annulled for him; and "al-fasl" is the base, the unwholesome. Al-Farazdaq said:
فلا تقبلوا منهم أباعر تشترى ... بوكس ولا سودا تصحّ فسولها
(Do not accept from them camels bought at a loss, nor black ones whose baseness is sound.)

* I'rab:
(الْحَجُّ أَشْهُرٌ مَعْلُوماتٌ) mubtadaʾ and khabar; "maʿlūmāt" is a ṣifa of "ashhur". The known months are: Shawwāl, Dhū l-Qiʿda and ten days of Dhū l-Ḥijja according to Abū Ḥanīfa; according to al-Shāfiʿī, nine days of Dhū l-Ḥijja and the night of the Day of Sacrifice; and according to Mālik, the whole of Dhū l-Ḥijja in one of his opinions. Part of the month is given the standing of the whole month; you say, "I saw you in such-and-such a year", when the seeing took place only in an hour of the year, not all of it. The clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. (فَمَنْ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, because it comes as a detailed answer to one who asks for clarification of what was summarised, and "man" is a jussive-governing conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ. (فَرَضَ) the protasis, and its fāʿil is "huwa" (latent). (فِيهِنَّ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to "faraḍa". (الْحَجَّ) mafʿūl bihi, i.e. upon himself. (فَلا رَفَثَ) The fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis, "lā" is the lā of generic negation, and "rafath" is its ism; the meaning of "rafath" has already been given. (وَلا فُسُوقَ) conjoined to His saying "fa-lā rafatha". (وَلا جِدالَ فِي الْحَجِّ) also conjoined, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of "lā"; the nominal clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of "man". (وَما) The wāw is resumptive, and "mā" is a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi of "tafʿalū". (تَفْعَلُوا) the jussive protasis, its jussive sign being the omission of the nūn. (مِنْ خَيْرٍ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ) the apodosis; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi and "Allāh" is fāʿil. (وَتَزَوَّدُوا) The wāw is resumptive; "tazawwadū" is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (فَإِنَّ) The fāʾ is causal, and "inna" is a particle resembling the verb. (خَيْرَ الزَّادِ) ism of "inna" and its muḍāf ilayhi. (التَّقْوى) its khabar; the clause has no grammatical position. (وَاتَّقُونِ) The wāw is a conjunction; "ittaqūni" is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the first-person yāʾ, which is omitted and indicated by the kasra, is mafʿūl bihi. (يا أُولِي الْأَلْبابِ) "yā" is a vocative particle; "ulī l-albāb" is the one addressed, a muḍāf, its accusative sign being the yāʾ because it is annexed to the sound masculine plural; and "al-albāb" is muḍāf ilayhi. The clause is conjoined to the clause "tazawwadū".

* Rhetoric:
1- In this verse there is a wonderful kind of prohibition: the measure of the thing prohibited depends on where it occurs, so that it would be considered not deserving of prohibition if it occurred in any other place. The specification of the Hajj with the prohibition of lewdness, wickedness and disputation within it conveys that these acts outside the Hajj, although they are prohibited and ugly, have an ugliness that is as nothing compared with their occurrence in the Hajj; so avoiding them is imperative in every case, but avoiding them in the Hajj is something above ordinary avoidance. Prohibition in our Arabic language has branches and paths whose depths can scarcely be sounded. Among them is that you prohibit something which is in reality praiseworthy and commendable, but which destroys its owner if it reaches him. The immortal poet al-Mutanabbī noticed these secrets when he forbade his two companions to convey to Sayf al-Dawla his praise of him, lest he be driven further and cast himself into destructive dangers. He said, having soared as he pleased:
فلا تبلغاه ما أقول فإنّه ... شجاع متى بذكر له الطعن يشتق
(Do not convey to him what I say, for he is a brave man who, whenever the thrust is mentioned to him, longs for it.)
He did not mean, in asking his two companions to conceal from Sayf al-Dawla what they had heard of the qualities of his deeds and of the lance-thrusts of his horsemen, to be gentle with him and to fear that longing would drive him to throw himself into perils. Somewhat similar is the saying of Kuthayyir, the companion of ʿAzza:
فلا تذكراه الحاجبيّة إنّه ... متى تذكراه الحاجبيّة يحزن
(Do not mention to him the Ḥājibiyya, for whenever you mention the Ḥājibiyya to him he grieves.)
2- The eloquent simile (tashbīh baligh): piety (taqwā) is likened to provision (zād) on the ground of the common element of strengthening, tightening of the grip and restraint.
3- Elaboration (iṭnāb) in His saying: «يا أولي الألباب». The command to piety is not specific to people of understanding alone, and the address is not directed to them rather than others in urging it, since every human being is commanded to be pious. This is called mentioning the specific after the general, to draw attention to the superiority and greater weight of the specific over the general. People differ in rank only by their minds (albāb), which are the intellects. Al-Mutanabbī glanced at the sky of this meaning and said:
لولا العقول لكان أدنى ضيغم ... أدنى إلى شرف من الإنسان
(Were it not for intellects, the lowest lion would be nearer to nobility than man.)
4- The Qur'an used «الألباب» in the plural and did not bring it in the singular, because it is among the words whose singular is unpleasant and whose plural is sweet; and this is an inherent property of our language.

dervis-irab:198-199.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَفَضْتُمْ) means: you pushed yourselves forth and set out to leave it. Ifāḍa is pushing forth in abundance, from "afaḍtu l-māʾ" when I poured the water abundantly. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Afāḍa l-nās min ʿArafāt" means they pushed forth from it, and every push is an ifāḍa. "They afāḍū from Minā to Mecca on the Day of Sacrifice" means they returned to it; from this comes ṭawāf al-ifāḍa, i.e. the circumambulation of return from Minā to Mecca.
(عَرَفاتٍ) is a proper name for the place of standing. Sībawayh argued that it is a proper name from his saying: "hādhihi ʿarafātu mubārakan fīhā", with «mubārakan» in the accusative as a ḥāl; had it been indefinite it would have been followed by an adjective; and had it been indefinite the alif and lām would have entered it, yet they do not enter it. The ruling on its i'rab will come under the Benefits.
(الْمَشْعَرِ) is a mountain at the end of al-Muzdalifa called Quzaḥ; it is called "mashʿar" from "shiʿār", which is a sign.

* I'rab:
(لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُناحٌ) "laysa" is a defective past verb; "ʿalaykum" is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar of it; "junāḥ" is the postponed ism of "laysa". (أَنْ) a particle of masdar and of accusative. (تَبْتَغُوا) an imperfect verb accusative by "an", its accusative sign being the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; "an" and what is within its scope are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in that you seek", and the preposition and its genitive noun are a ṣifa of "junāḥ". (فَضْلًا) mafʿūl bihi. (مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to "tabtaghū" or to an omitted ṣifa of "faḍlan". (فَإِذا) The fāʾ is resumptive, and "idhā" is an adverb for what is to come of time, attached to the apodosis. (أَفَضْتُمْ) verb and fāʿil; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. (مِنْ عَرَفاتٍ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to "afaḍtum". (فَاذْكُرُوا) The fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis; "udhkurū" is an imperative verb with its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. (اللَّهَ) mafʿūl bihi. (عِنْدَ الْمَشْعَرِ) The adverb is attached to "udhkurū". (الْحَرامِ) ṣifa of "al-mashʿar"; you may also attach the adverb to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "being at the Sacred Landmark". (وَاذْكُرُوهُ) The wāw is a conjunction, and He repeated it for emphasis. "Udhkurūhu" is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. (كَما هَداكُمْ) The kāf is a preposition and "mā" is maṣdar; together with its genitive it is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq or a ḥāl, i.e. "remember Him with a fine remembrance", or "remember Him as He guided you"; the clause "hadākum" has no grammatical position because it follows a particle-type relative (mawṣūl ḥarfī). (وَإِنْ) The wāw is circumstantial, and "in" is the lightened form of the heavy "inna" (the rule for it when lightened has been given earlier; it is mostly left without effect). (كُنْتُمْ) "kāna" the defective with its ism. (مِنْ قَبْلِهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (لَمِنَ الضَّالِّينَ) The lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), and "mina l-ḍāllīn" is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of "kuntum". (ثُمَّ) a conjunction of sequence with delay. (أَفِيضُوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (مِنْ حَيْثُ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to "afīḍū"; what has been said about "ḥaythu" has already preceded. (أَفاضَ النَّاسُ) verb and fāʿil; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. (وَاسْتَغْفِرُوا اللَّهَ) The wāw is a conjunction; "istaghfirū Allāh" is verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) "inna" with its ism and its two khabars; the clause is causal and has no grammatical position.

* Benefits:
"ʿArafāt" is declined as the sound feminine plural, and likewise everything named by such a form, such as "Adhriʿāt"; this is the eloquent usage for it. Some permitted that it be declined as a diptote; and it is said that it is declined as the sound feminine plural except that it takes no tanwīn. The verse of Imruʾ al-Qays has been transmitted in the three ways:
تنورتها من أذرعات وأهلها ... بيثرب أدنى دارها نظر عال
(I looked at her fire from Adhriʿāt, while her people are in Yathrib; the nearest of her abodes is a lofty sight away.)

dervis-irab:18-20.t:
* Vocabulary:
(صُمٌّ) plural of أصمّ, the one who does not hear. One says صمّ يصمّ (with fatḥa on the ṣād in both), meaning his hearing became heavy; it is also said that the root meaning is "blocking", and one says "I stopped up (ṣamamtu) the bottle", meaning I blocked it.
(بُكْمٌ) plural of أبكم, the one who does not speak, that is, the mute.
(عُمْيٌ) plural of أعمى. ʿAmā (blindness) is a darkness in the eye that prevents the perception of visible things. Its verb is of the pattern عمي, fa-ʿila with kasra on the ʿayn, and its active participle is of the pattern أعمى, which is the regular analogy for ailments and defects.
(صيّب) it is the rain that pours down (yaṣūbu), that is, descends; its origin is ṣayyūb: the yāʾ and the wāw came together with the first of them quiescent, so the wāw was changed to yāʾ and the yāʾ was merged into the yāʾ.
(السّماء) everything that is above you and shades you is a "sky" (samāʾ). The word samāʾ is feminine, and sometimes made masculine. He said:
فلو رفع السماء إليه قوما ... لحقنا بالسماء مع السحاب
(Had the sky raised a people up to it, we would have reached the sky with the clouds.)

* I'rab:
(صُمٌّ) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "they are deaf"; the clause is resumptive. (بُكْمٌ) a second khabar. (عُمْيٌ) a third khabar. Although these predicates differ in wording, they are united in what they denote and mean, because they all come down to non-acceptance of the truth. (فَهُمْ) the fāʾ is a conjunction and هم is mubtadaʾ. (لا يَرْجِعُونَ) لا is negative and يرجعون is an imperfect verb, nominative, with the wāw as fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of هم, and the clause is conjoined to "they are deaf", that is, "they do not return to guidance". The meaning is that their faculties of perception have had their structures, built for sensation and comprehension, demolished. (أَوْ) a conjunction of distribution (lil-tafṣīl), that is, among those who look at their state, some liken them to the state of the one who kindled a fire and some liken them to the owners of a downpour. (كَصَيِّبٍ) the preposition and its genitive noun are conjoined to كمثل, and a muḍāf must be implied, that is, "like the owners of a downpour", by the evidence of يجعلون أصابعهم في آذانهم. (مِنَ السَّماءِ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of صيب. (فِيهِ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (ظُلُماتٌ) a postponed mubtadaʾ. (وَرَعْدٌ وَبَرْقٌ) conjoined to ظلمات. (يَجْعَلُونَ) an imperfect verb, nominative, with the wāw as fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, brought to answer an implied question, as if it had been asked, "And what is their state with that thunder?", and it was said, "They put...". (أَصابِعَهُمْ) mafʿūl bihi. (فِي آذانِهِمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the second object of يجعلون. (مِنَ الصَّواعِقِ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يجعلون, and min is causal; see the Benefits. (حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). (وَاللَّهُ) the wāw is parenthetical and الله is mubtadaʾ. (مُحِيطٌ) khabar. (بِالْكافِرِينَ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to محيط; the clause has no grammatical position because it is parenthetical between two clauses of a single story, namely «يجعلون أصابعهم» and «يكاد البرق». (يَكادُ) an imperfect verb, nominative, one of the verbs of approximation that work like كان; it has two dialects, fiʿala and fuʿila, which is why one says kidtu (with kasra on the kāf) and kudtu (with ḍamma). (الْبَرْقُ) the nominative ism of يكاد. (يَخْطَفُ) an imperfect verb, nominative, with a latent agent (permissibly latent), its implied form being "it", referring to البرق; the clause يخطف is the khabar of يكاد, and the khabar of these verbs can only be an imperfect verb. The clause يكاد is resumptive, as if it were the answer of someone who says, "And what is their state with that lightning?", and it was said: «يكاد». (أَبْصارَهُمْ) mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of genitive as the second term of the genitive construct. (كُلَّما) كل is accusative as an adverb of time; the adverbial sense has passed to كل from its annexation to the temporal maṣdar-forming ما, and ما with what follows it, (أَضاءَ), is in the interpretation of a maṣdar in the position of genitive as the second term of the construct. It is also said that ما is an indefinite noun that is qualified, meaning "time", the returning pronoun being omitted, the implied form being "every time it shone for them in it". So the clause أضاء in the first view has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the particle-like relative, and in the second its position is genitive as an adjective. Kullamā by itself contains the sense of a condition, and the operator in it is its apodosis. (لَهُمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أضاء. (مَشَوْا) a past verb, indeclinable on an implied ḍamma on the omitted alif, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause مشوا فيه has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (فِيهِ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to مشوا. (وَإِذا) the wāw is a conjunction and إذا is an adverb for the future time, governing its condition in the genitive, accusative by its apodosis. (أَظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa; the fāʿil is latent (permissibly latent), its implied form being "it", referring to البرق; the clause is in the position of genitive through the annexation of the adverb to it, and عليهم is attached to أظلم. (قامُوا) verb and agent; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (وَلَوْ) the wāw is resumptive and لو is conditional. Sībawayh's phrase is that it is "a particle for what would have occurred because of the occurrence of something else", which is better than the grammarians' saying that it is a "particle of prevention due to prevention"; interesting discussions of it will come in this book. (شاءَ اللَّهُ) verb and agent; the object of willing is omitted. This omission is permissible in the speech of the Arabs, who hardly ever mention the object of شاء except for a remarkable matter, as in the saying of al-KhurayMī:
فلو شئت أن أبكي دما لبكيته ... عليه ولكن ساحة الصبر أوسع
(Had I wished to weep blood I would have wept it over him, but the expanse of patience is wider.) Here أن and what follows it is in the interpretation of a maṣdar, the object of شئت, because it is a remarkable thing, so mentioning it is good. أراد ("he wanted") is like شاء in this ruling. (لَذَهَبَ) the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو, and ذهب is a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, whose fāʿil is latent (permissibly latent), its implied form being "he". (بِسَمْعِهِمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ذهب. (وَأَبْصارِهِمْ) conjoined to يسمعهم. [Translator's note: the source says "conjoined to يسمعهم", which does not match the verse; the intended word is evidently بسمعهم, "their hearing".] (إِنَّ) a particle resembling a verb. (اللَّهُ) its accusative ism. (عَلى كُلِّ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to قدير. (شَيْءٍ) muḍāf ilayhi. (قَدِيرٌ) khabar of inna. The clause لذهب has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition, and the clause إن الله is explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

* Rhetoric:
1- The explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya). He likened them to the deaf, the mute and the blind and omitted mention of the thing likened, which some rhetoricians count as though mentioned, so that for them it is an eloquent simile (tashbīh balīgh), which occurs often in their speech. Their poet said:
صم إذا سمعوا خيرا ذكرت به ... وإن ذكرت بسوء عندهم دفنوا
(Deaf when they hear a good thing mentioned of you; and if you are mentioned with evil in their presence, they bury [the thing].)
But the eloquent, rigorous masters forget the thing likened and turn away from imagining it entirely. Abū Tammām said, praising Khālid ibn Yazīd al-Shaybānī:
ويصعد حتى يظنّ الجهول ... بأنّ له حاجة في السماء
(He climbs until the ignorant man thinks he has some need in the sky.) He borrowed "ascending" from physical height for moral height, by way of the explicit metaphor, then built upon it what is built upon height in place, as embellishment and completion for the sake of exaggeration, and did not mention the thing likened.
2- The repeated representational simile. The Exalted likened the hypocrites, with their showing faith and concealing disbelief, to one who kindled a fire which then went out, and that in three respects:
a- The one who kindles a fire gains light by its illumination and the desolation of darkness leaves him; when it goes out, the illumination goes, and benefit and guidance are lost.
b- If the kindler of the fire does not feed it with fuel, its light goes; likewise the hypocrite, if he does not sustain faith, his faith goes.
c- The one who kindles a fire and gains light from it is in a dusky darkness of his own self; when the fire goes, he remains in two darknesses: the darkness of the night and the darkness of his own self. Then He likened the religion to the downpour (ṣayyib), because hearts come alive by it as the earth comes alive by rain; and what is connected to that: the likening of the disbelievers to the darknesses, and what is in it of promise and threat in the lightning and thunder, and of the trials and afflictions that strike the disbelievers in the thunderbolts.
3- He used the singular for thunder and lightning, although the apparent sense and context require their plural, as ظلمات was made plural, and although the plural is more eloquent than the singular, according to the saying of al-Buḥturī:
يا عارضا متلفّعا ببروده ... يختال بين بروقه ورعوده
(O cloud wrapped in its mantles, strutting between its lightnings and its thunders.) We say that the Qur'an inclined to the singular for an important point, which is that lightning and thunder were originally two maṣdars, and maṣdars are not pluralized (one says "the sky thundered, thundering" and "it flashed, flashing"), so the ruling of the origin was observed by leaving them unpluralized even though the sense of plurality is intended. This point escaped al-Buḥturī. It is not hidden that among words there are some whose singular is sweet and whose plural is ugly, and vice versa; all of that will come in its place in this wonderful book.
4- The free metaphor (majāz mursal) in His saying «يجعلون أصابعهم في آذانهم», because it is not the whole finger that is put in the ear; He mentioned the fingers and meant the fingertips, and the relation is that of wholeness (kulliyya). The figurative expression here is more eloquent than the literal, which is why He turned from it to it. He used the plural "fingers" because He did not mean a specific finger, since the state is one of bewilderment and perplexity: whichever finger happens to come to them they block their ears with, without dwelling on a customary order or a presumed specification.

* Benefits:
The chief judge Tāj al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAqīl, the commentator on Ibn Mālik's Alfiyya in grammar, claimed that من الصواعق is attached to حذر الموت, which involves fronting what depends on a maṣdar. Ibn ʿAqīl said: What led him to this is that if he attached it to يجعلون, it would be in the position of mafʿūl li-ajlihi, and this would require multiple objects of purpose without conjunction, which the grammarians forbid. He answered this objection by saying that the first object of purpose gives the reason for the "putting" in general, and the second gives its reason as restricted by the first; the general and the restricted are different, so the thing explained is multiple in meaning even if single in wording. Ibn Hishām took issue with Ibn ʿAqīl in Mughnī al-Labīb; refer to it if you wish, for there is pleasure and benefit in it.

dervis-irab:260-260.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَصُرْهُنَّ): with ḍamma on the ṣād, and a kasra is also possible; an imperative verb from "ṣāra yaṣūru" or from "ṣāra yaṣīru", meaning to gather or to incline. He said:
وفرع يصير الجيد وحف كأنه ... على الليت قنوان الكروم الدّوالح
(And hair that bends the neck, thick and black, as though upon the nape were clusters of laden vines.)
He describes the hair of his beloved as bending her neck because of its heaviness upon it, and likens it to clusters of vines weighed down with fruit. In Mukhtār al-Ṣiḥāḥ he says: "ṣārahu: he inclined it, of the pattern qāla and bāʿa; and it was read «فصرهن إليك» with ḍamma and kasra on the ṣād. Also ṣāra al-shayʾ, of both patterns: he cut it and separated it. Whoever explains it thus makes the verse have a preposing and postposing, i.e. 'take to yourself four of the birds, and cut them up'."

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قالَ إِبْراهِيمُ): the wāw is resumptive and the speech is resumptive, brought to adduce another proof of Allah's care for the believers; it also calls attention to the fact that sight and direct witnessing are indispensable for strengthening and rooting conviction, since Abraham was not in doubt about Allah's giving life to the dead. «إذ» is an adverbial attached to an implied "mention"; «قال إبراهيم» is a verb and agent, and the clause is in the genitive position by annexation.
(رَبِّ أَرِنِي كَيْفَ تُحْيِ الْمَوْتى): «رب» is the one addressed, a muḍāf to the omitted yāʾ of the first person, and the clause is in the accusative position as the content of the saying. «أرني» is an imperative verb from the visual "irāʾa", which takes one object, and with the entry of the hamza it became transitive to two. The origin of «أرني» is "ariʾīnī"; the first yāʾ was dropped giving "ariʾnī", then the vowel of the hamza was moved to the rāʾ and the hamza dropped. «أرني» is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the dropping of the weak letter; the nūn is for protection (wiqāya) and the yāʾ of the first person is the first direct object. «كيف» is an interrogative ḥāl; «تحيي» is an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; «الموتى» is a direct object; the clause «كيف تحيي الموتى» is in the accusative position as the second object of «أرني».
(قالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِنْ): «قال» is a past verb and the agent is "he"; the clause is resumptive, serving to affirm what has occurred, i.e. "Do you ask while you do not believe?"; the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīrī), because the question concerns a matter whose existence is established for the asker and the one asked alike.
