The wāw is a conjunction; «لم» is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; «تؤمن» is an imperfect verb jussive through «لم»; the interrogative clause is in the accusative position as the content of the saying.
(قالَ بَلى): a resumptive clause, brought to affirm belief. He used «بلى», which is a particle of response, to establish the negated belief; had the answer been «نعم», it would have been unbelief.
(وَلكِنْ لِيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي): the wāw is a conjunction joining an omitted clause whose implied form is "I asked You"; «لكن» is a disregarded particle of rectification (istidrāk); the lām of «ليطمئن» is for cause, and «يطمئن» is an imperfect verb in the accusative through an implied «أن». An omitted element must be supplied for the lām to be attached validly, i.e. "but I asked You the manner of giving life so that my heart may be at ease". «قلبي» is an agent, nominative by an implied ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, and the yāʾ is a muḍāf ilayhi.
(قالَ فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةً مِنَ الطَّيْرِ): a resumptive clause, brought to demonstrate Allah the Exalted's guardianship of the believers and His leading them along the stretches of the straight path. The fāʾ is the eloquent fāʾ, i.e. "if you wish to know that by sight, then take". «خذ» is an imperative verb and the agent is "you"; «أربعة» is a direct object; «من الطير» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of «أربعة».
(فَصُرْهُنَّ إِلَيْكَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; «صرهن» is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; the hāʾ is the direct object and the nūn is the sign of the feminine plural, with no position; «إليك» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "gathered to you".
(ثُمَّ اجْعَلْ عَلى كُلِّ جَبَلٍ مِنْهُنَّ جُزْءاً): «ثم» is a conjunction of order and delay; «اجعل» is an imperative verb and the agent is "you"; «على كل» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «اجعل» as its second object; «جبل» is a muḍāf ilayhi; «منهن» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of «جزءا» and when it was put before the described it was parsed as a ḥāl; «جزءا» is the first object.
(ثُمَّ ادْعُهُنَّ يَأْتِينَكَ سَعْياً): also a conjunction. «ادعهن» is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the dropping of the weak letter, the agent is "you", the hāʾ is the direct object and the nūn is the sign of the feminine with no position; «يأتينك» is an imperfect verb indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of the jussive as the answer to the request, the nūn is the agent and the kāf the direct object, and the clause is the answer to the request with no position; «سعيا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. swift walking. You may also parse it as a ḥāl, i.e. "hastening".
(وَاعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; «اعلم» is an imperative verb and the agent is "you"; «أن» with its noun and its two khabars takes the place of the two objects of «اعلم».

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there is concision by omission (ījāz bi-l-ḥadhf): the remainder of the story is omitted, since He, glory be to Him, related His commands without mentioning Abraham's, peace be upon him, carrying them out, because that is understood at once.

dervis-irab:247-248.t:
* Vocabulary:
(طالُوتَ) and likewise جالوت: two non-Arabic names, and for that reason they are diptotes (barred from tanwīn) because of being proper names and non-Arabic; so no regard is due to whoever says that they are Arabic names.
(التَّابُوتُ): from التّوب, which is returning and turning back, because what goes out of it keeps returning to it. Its tā' is an addition not for the feminine, like the tā' of ملكوت and جبروت. Legends have been spun around it in which the imagination plays its part.

* I'rab:
(وَقالَ لَهُمْ نَبِيُّهُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; قال is a past verb; ولهم is attached to «قال»; and نبيهم is the agent. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ بَعَثَ لَكُمْ طالُوتَ مَلِكاً) إنّ and its noun; the clause قد بعث is its khabar; طالوت is a direct object; and ملكا is a ḥāl from طالوت. إنّ and what follows is a nominal sentence in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said. (قالُوا: أَنَّى يَكُونُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ عَلَيْنا) The sentence is resumptive; أنى is an interrogative noun meaning كيف ("how"), in the position of an accusative ḥāl; يكون is a defective imperfect verb; and له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted advanced khabar of «يكون»; الملك is the postponed noun of يكون; and علينا is attached to الملك, because the root «ملك» is made transitive with «على»; you say: ملك على القوم أمرهم. The interrogative sentence and what is within its scope is in the position of an accusative, being the content of قالوا. That is: how can it be, when he is not of the tribe of kingship! His father was a simple labourer.
Thus racism and class-consciousness took root among the Jews from the most distant times. (وَنَحْنُ أَحَقُّ بِالْمُلْكِ مِنْهُ) The wāw is circumstantial; نحن is a mubtadaʾ and أحق its khabar; بالملك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أحق, and منه is also attached to أحق; and the clause following the wāw is in the position of an accusative ḥāl. (وَلَمْ يُؤْتَ سَعَةً مِنَ الْمالِ) The wāw is a conjunction: they added to racism and class-consciousness the love of wealth and reliance on it for precedence. لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussion; يؤت is an imperfect verb, passive, jussive because of لم, its deputy agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; and سعة is a second direct object. The origin of سعة is وسعة, and the wāw was dropped by analogy with the imperfect. And من المال is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of سعة. (قالَ: إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفاهُ عَلَيْكُمْ) قال is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", referring to the prophet; إنّ and its noun; اصطفاه is a verb with a latent agent and a direct object, and the clause is the khabar of إنّ; the clause of إنّ and what is within its scope is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said; and عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اصطفاه. (وَزادَهُ بَسْطَةً فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْجِسْمِ) The wāw is a conjunction; زاده is a verb with a latent agent and a first direct object; and بسطة is a second direct object. It is permissible to construe بسطة as a tamyīz (specification) if we say the verb takes a single object. And في العلم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of بسطة; and الجسم is conjoined to العلم. (وَاللَّهُ يُؤْتِي مُلْكَهُ مَنْ يَشاءُ) The wāw is a conjunction: اللَّه is a mubtadaʾ, the clause يؤتي is the khabar, ملكه is the first direct object, من is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as second direct object, and the clause يشاء is a ṣila [Translator's note: the source says «صفة» (adjective) here; translated as written]. (وَاللَّهُ واسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ) The wāw is resumptive; اللَّه is a mubtadaʾ, and واسع عليم are its two khabars. (وَقالَ لَهُمْ نَبِيُّهُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction or resumptive, introduced to demonstrate the soundness of his speech; قال is a past verb; ولهم is attached to «قال»; and نبيهم is the agent. (إِنَّ آيَةَ مُلْكِهِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ التَّابُوتُ) إنّ and its noun; ملكه is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive complement); and أن يأتيكم is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of a nominative, the khabar of إنّ; and إنّ and what is within its scope is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said. التابوت is the agent of يأتيكم and the kāf is an advanced direct object. (فِيهِ سَكِينَةٌ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted advanced khabar, and سكينة is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from التابوت. (مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of سكينة. (وَبَقِيَّةٌ مِمَّا تَرَكَ آلُ مُوسى وَآلُ هارُونَ) بقية is conjoined to سكينة; ومما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of بقية; and ترك آل موسى: the clause has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila; آل موسى is the agent of ترك; and آل هارون is conjoined to آل موسى. (تَحْمِلُهُ الْمَلائِكَةُ) An imperfect verb; the hā' is a direct object; الملائكة is its agent; and the clause is a second ḥāl from التابوت. (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآيَةً لَكُمْ) إنّ is a particle resembling the verb, and the sentence serves as a justification and has no grammatical position; في ذلك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted advanced khabar; the lām is the shifted lām; آية is the postponed noun of إنّ; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of آية; and the clause is justificatory with no grammatical position. (إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ) إن is conditional; كنتم is a defective past verb in the position of a jussive, being the protasis; the tā' is the noun of كان; and مؤمنين is its khabar.
The apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: "so reflect on the matter, take heed, and comply with the command of your Lord and His signs". The conditional sentence is resumptive.

dervis-irab:249-252.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَصَلَ) in the sense of انفصل ("separated"), so it is intransitive; it may also be transitive, in which case its object is omitted. One says: فصل العسكر عن البلد فصولا ("the army set out from the town").
(غُرْفَةً) with ḍamma on the ghayn, in the sense of a passive participle (what is scooped); the ghayn may also take fatḥa, as a maṣdar of single occurrence (maṣdar marra), and it has also been read thus.

* I'rab:
(فَلَمَّا فَصَلَ طالُوتُ بِالْجُنُودِ) The fā' is a conjunction on omitted clauses, supplied according to what the flow of speech requires; the implied form is: "so they acknowledged his kingship and called one another to jihad; and when…". لما is a temporal adverb, hence a noun, or a connective, hence a particle, containing the sense of a condition in either case. The clause فصل طالوت بالجنود is in the position of a genitive by annexation if it is an adverb; and بالجنود is attached to فصل or to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "the soldiers being his companions". (قالَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مُبْتَلِيكُمْ بِنَهَرٍ) The clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to a non-jussive-governing conditional; إنّ and its noun; مبتليكم is its khabar; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to مبتليكم; and the nominal sentence is the content of what was said. (فَمَنْ شَرِبَ مِنْهُ فَلَيْسَ مِنِّي) The fā' is the eloquent fā' (fā' faṣīḥa); من is a conditional noun governing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ; شرب is a past verb in the position of a jussive, being the protasis, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; منه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شرب; the fā' links the apodosis; ليس is a defective past verb whose noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; ومني is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; the clause after the fā' is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis; and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من. (وَمَنْ لَمْ يَطْعَمْهُ فَإِنَّهُ مِنِّي) The wāw is a conjunction; من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussion; يطعمه is an imperfect verb, jussive because of لم; the fā' links the apodosis; إنّ and its noun; ومني is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; the clause after the fā' is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis; and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من. (إِلَّا مَنِ اغْتَرَفَ غُرْفَةً بِيَدِهِ) إلا is a particle of exception; من is a relative noun in the position of an accusative as an exception from his words: فمن شرب منه. The second clause was inserted between the two out of concern for its content. The clause اغترف has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila; غرفة is a direct object, or an absolute object if we consider غرفة a maṣdar of single occurrence; and بيده is attached to an omitted adjective of غرفة. (فَشَرِبُوا مِنْهُ) The fā' is the eloquent fā'; شربوا is a verb and agent; and منه is attached to شربوا. (إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِنْهُمْ) إلا is a particle of exception; قليلا is excepted from his words: فشربوا منه; and منهم is attached to an omitted adjective of «قليلا». (فَلَمَّا جاوَزَهُ هُوَ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ) The fā' is a conjunction or resumptive; لما is a temporal adverb or a particle connective containing the sense of a condition in either case; the clause جاوزه is in the position of a genitive by annexation if we consider «لما» an adverb, otherwise it has no grammatical position; هو is a detached pronoun, emphasis (tawkīd) for the latent pronoun in «جاوزه»; الذين is conjoined to «هو»; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila of the relative noun; and معه is an adverb of place attached to جاوزه. The meaning is: "when he crossed it, and crossed it with him those who believed", namely those who confined themselves to the scoop, or those who did not taste the water at all, in order to point to the wisdom of the testing, which is that the wavering among them should turn back before meeting the enemy, because if the wavering were to remain among them and then flee, that would cause the soldiers to lose heart. How wonderful are the methods of the Qur'an! (قالُوا) A verb and agent. (لا طاقَةَ لَنَا الْيَوْمَ بِجالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِ) The clause is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said. لا is the lā of generic negation; طاقة is its noun; لنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; اليوم is an adverb attached to what the khabar is attached to, namely «لنا»; and likewise his words بجالوت. It is not permissible to attach any one of these adverbials to «طاقة», lest it require tanwīn, since it would become similar to a muḍāf, and no one has read it so. However, to avoid attaching all three to a single attachment, it is permissible to attach one of them to an omitted ḥāl, which then serves as an elucidation of the negation of capacity. (قالَ الَّذِينَ) A verb and agent, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to a non-jussive-governing conditional. (يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُمْ مُلاقُوا اللَّهِ) The clause يظنون has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of الذين; the wāw is the agent; أنّ with its noun and khabar stand in place of the two objects of يظنون; and اللَّه is the muḍāf ilayhi of his word «ملاقوا». (كَمْ مِنْ فِئَةٍ قَلِيلَةٍ) كم is declarative (khabariyya), in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; ومن فئة is the tamyīz of declarative كم, and this has already been discussed; and قليلة is an adjective of فئة; and the clause (غَلَبَتْ فِئَةً كَثِيرَةً بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ) is the khabar of «كم»; and the clause of كم and what is within its scope is in the position of an accusative, being the content of what was said. (وَاللَّهُ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ) The wāw is resumptive; اللَّه is a mubtadaʾ; مع is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar; and الصابرين is a muḍāf ilayhi. (وَلَمَّا بَرَزُوا لِجالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِ) The wāw is resumptive; لما is temporal or a connective containing the sense of a condition, and its i'rab has already been given; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to برزوا; and جنوده is conjoined to جالوت. (قالُوا) The clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to a non-jussive-governing conditional. (رَبَّنا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنا صَبْراً) ربنا is a vocative muḍāf from which the vocative particle has been omitted; أفرغ is an imperative verb whose meaning here is supplication; علينا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أفرغ;
and صبرا is a direct object, and the sentence is the content of what was said. (وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدامَنا) Conjoined to the clause أفرغ. (وَانْصُرْنا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكافِرِينَ) Also a conjunction. (فَهَزَمُوهُمْ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ) You may take the fā' as a conjunction on omitted clauses that the flow of speech requires, i.e. "so the battle was joined, the two armies clashed, and they routed them". Or you may take it as the eloquent fā', i.e. "if you wish to know what the battle resulted in: they routed them". And هزموهم is a verb, agent and direct object. (وَقَتَلَ داوُدُ جالُوتَ) The wāw is a conjunction; a verb, agent and direct object. (وَآتاهُ اللَّهُ الْمُلْكَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ) The wāw is a conjunction; آتاه is a past verb; the hā' is the first direct object; اللَّه is the agent; الملك is the second direct object; and الحكمة is conjoined to الملك. (وَعَلَّمَهُ مِمَّا يَشاءُ) Conjoined to «آتاه»; ومما is attached to علمه; the clause يشاء is a ṣila; and the direct object is omitted, because the crafts that David learned were many, among them the craft of iron, which became soft in his hand, and he understood the speech of birds and beasts. (وَلَوْلا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ) The wāw is resumptive; لولا is a particle of prevention due to existence, containing the sense of a condition; دفع is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "existent"; the name of Majesty is a muḍāf ilayhi; and الناس is a direct object of the maṣdar. (بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ) بعضهم is a substitute (badal) for الناس, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to دفع. (لَفَسَدَتِ الْأَرْضُ) The lām occurs in the answer of لولا, and the clause فسدت الأرض has no grammatical position because it is the answer to a non-jussive-governing conditional. The meaning is: the corruption of the earth was prevented by the existence of Allah's driving back of people, some by means of others. And this is something witnessed and seen. (وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ) The wāw is resumptive; ولكنّ and its noun; ذو فضل is its khabar; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of فضل. (تِلْكَ آياتُ اللَّهِ) A mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the sentence is explicative. (نَتْلُوها عَلَيْكَ بِالْحَقِّ) And the clause is in the position of an accusative ḥāl. You may take آيات الله as a substitute for the demonstrative, with the clause نتلوها as the khabar, but the first is more established. عليك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نتلوها; and بالحق is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "backed by the truth, supported by a certainty into which doubt does not seep". (وَإِنَّكَ لَمِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; إنّ and its noun; the shifted lām; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of إنك.

A historical-literary glance:
We said at the start of these verses that we would refer to a literary-historical event connected with Joshua, the successor of Moses, peace be upon them both, and in fulfilment of the promise we say: when Joshua fought the Giants, the day was a Friday; when the sun inclined to setting he feared that it would set before he had finished with them and the Sabbath would enter, when fighting them would not be lawful for him. So he called upon Allah the Exalted, and He turned the sun back for him until he had finished fighting them. Abū Tammām al-Ṭāʾī seized upon this winged poetic narrative and fashioned from it a novel meaning in poetry called talmīḥ (allusion), which is where a poet in his verse, or a prose writer in his writing, alludes to a well-known story by way of illustration; and he did it beautifully. He said:
لحقنا بأخراهم وقد حوّم الهوى ... قلوبا عهدنا طيرها وهي وقّع
فردّت علينا الشّمس والليل راغم ... بشمس لها من جانب الخدر مطلع
نضا ضوءها صبغ الدّجنّة وانطوى ... لبهجتها ثوب السماء المجزّع
فو الله ما أدري أأحلام نائم ... ألمّت بنا أم كان في الرّكب يوشع
(We caught up with the last of them, while passion hovered over hearts whose birds we had known to be settled. Then the sun was returned to us, night humbled, with a sun that rises from the side of the curtained chamber. Its light stripped off the dye of the cloud-darkness, and the striped garment of the sky was folded up before its brilliance. By Allah, I do not know whether it was a sleeper's dreams that visited us, or whether Joshua was in the riding party.) [Translator's note: in the source, the third and fourth verses are run together on one line.]
In the modern age Shawqī gazed at this lofty sky and said, at the opening of a poem in which he mourned the Egyptian leader Saʿd Zaghlūl:
شيّعوا الشمس ومالوا بضحاها ... وانحنى الركب عليها فبكاها
ليتني في الرّكب لمّا أفلت ... يوشع همّت فنادى فثناها
(They escorted the sun and turned aside with its forenoon, and the riding party bent over it and wept for it. Would that I had been in the party when it set; Joshua was moved, called out, and turned it back.) [Translator's note: in the source the second verse is run together with the first.]
But the affectation is evident in the setting of an elegy, and that does not fit with the heat of surging emotion.

A second historical glance:
This story was a fertile source of production and depiction. Goliath (Jālūt), the leader of the Giants, challenged the people of Joshua to single combat, and they feared him and held back, because he was a great giant of enormous body. But David, who was young, had not reached maturity and was tending sheep, came out against him with his famous sling and struck him with a stone, in a gripping story, killing him, and then took sole possession of the kingship. Thus racism appeared among the Children of Israel from the dawn of history until today.

dervis-irab:21-22.t:
* Vocabulary:
أندادا is the plural of nidd (with kasra on the nūn), which is the equal; it is said only of an equal that is opposed and contrary. Jarīr said: أتيما تجعلون إليّ ندّا ... وما تيم لذي حسب نديد (Do you make Taym an equal to me? And Taym is no peer of a man of lineage.)

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا) يا is a particle of vocative for the middle-distance one addressed; no other vocative particle occurs in the Qur'an. أي is the one addressed, an indefinite specified noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative. (النَّاسُ) a badal (substitute) of أي on the wording. (اعْبُدُوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn because its imperfect is one of the "five verbs"; the wāw is fāʿil. (رَبَّكُمُ) mafʿūl bihi, and the kāf is an attached pronoun in the position of genitive as the second term of the construct. (الَّذِي) a relative noun, naʿt (adjective) of ربكم. (خَلَقَكُمْ) a past verb, the kāf its object, and the agent is latent, its implied form being "He". (وَالَّذِينَ) the wāw is a conjunction and الذين is a relative noun conjoined to the kāf, that is, "and He created those who...". (مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted word that has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (لَعَلَّكُمْ) لعل is a particle of hope that governs the accusative, and the kāf is its ism. (تَتَّقُونَ) an imperfect verb, nominative, with the wāw as fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of لعل. The clause لعلكم تتقون has no position because its relation to what precedes is that of the result to the condition; it may also be parsed as a ḥāl, that is, "while you hope for piety and aspire to it". (الَّذِي) a relative noun in the position of accusative as a second adjective of ربكم. (جَعَلَ) a past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He"; the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (لَكُمُ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of فراشا and then was fronted. (الْأَرْضَ) the first object of جعل if it is from jaʿl in the sense of "making into" (taṣyīr). (فِراشاً) the second direct object; but if it is from jaʿl in the sense of "creating", then فراشا is an interpreted ḥāl. (وَالسَّماءَ) conjoined to His words الأرض. (بِناءً) conjoined to فراشا. (وَأَنْزَلَ) the wāw is a conjunction, and أنزل is conjoined to His words جعل. (مِنَ السَّماءِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزل. (ماءً) the object of أنزل. (فَأَخْرَجَ) conjoined to أنزل. (بِهِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخرج. (مِنَ الثَّمَراتِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective and was fronted. (رِزْقاً) mafʿūl bihi. (لَكُمُ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted second adjective of رزقا. (فَلا) the fāʿ is explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya) and لا is
prohibitive. (تَجْعَلُوا) an imperfect verb, jussive by لا, its sign of jussive being the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is explanatory of cause, with no position, serving like a resumptive clause, and the meaning is that this prohibition is caused by the bringing into being of these dazzling signs. (لِلَّهِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted word in the position of the second object of تجعلوا. (أَنْداداً) the first object of تجعلوا. (وَأَنْتُمْ) the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and أنتم is a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (تَعْلَمُونَ) an imperfect verb, its sign of nominative being the persistence of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the verbal clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أنتم, and the nominal clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.

* Benefits:
1- The grammarians' discussion was unsettled over the parsing of a noun made definite by al- after يا أيها. Most of them said that it is an adjective; their argument is that each of the vocative particle and al- is a particle of definiteness, and they dislike two particles for a single function, so أي was inserted to be the apparent one addressed, and the noun with al- is an adjective of it. This is objected to on the ground that it is a non-derived noun, as in يا أيها الرجل; the reply is that although it is non-derived it has the ruling of a derived noun, that is, "the one characterized by manhood". What we see is that one says: أي or أية is the one addressed, ها is a particle of alerting, and the word with al- is a badal of the one addressed if it is non-derived, otherwise it is parsed as a naʿt.
2- The earth (arḍ) was only called arḍ because it "earths" (tata'arraḍu) what is in its belly, meaning it eats what is in it.
3- When "hope" (tarajjī) occurs in the speech of Allah the Exalted, there are three interpretations:
a- لعل keeps its proper sense of hope and aspiration, but relative to the addressees. Sībawayh stated this interpretation in his book and al-Zamakhsharī in his Kashshāf.
b- لعل is for giving a reason, that is, "worship your Lord so that you may be pious"; Quṭrub stated it and al-Ṭabarī chose it in his great Tafsīr.
c- It is for exposing oneself to a thing, as if it were said: "Do that, exposing yourselves to the chance of becoming pious"; Abū al-Baqāʾ stated it and al-Mahdawī chose it in his Tafsīr al-Mumtiʿ.
4- When the adjective precedes the thing it describes, it is parsed as a ḥāl, and it is therefore permissible for the owner of the ḥāl to be indefinite, though it is ruled that it should be definite, because judging about something unknown generally yields no benefit. On this is the poet's line:
لميّة موحشا طلل ... يلوح كأنه خلل
(Mayya has a deserted ruin, which gleams as if it were the lining of a sword-sheath.)

dervis-irab:69-71.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فاقِعٌ): intensely yellow. For emphasis one says "aṣfar fāqiʿ", just as one says "aswad ḥālik" (jet black), "abyaḍ yaqaq" (brilliant white), "aḥmar qānin" (deep red) and "akhḍar nāḍir" (fresh green).
(لا ذَلُولٌ): not broken in for ploughing and turning over the earth.
(الشية): with kasra on the shīn: a mark; what is meant is that there is no patch in her of any colour other than yellow.

* I'rab:
(قالُوا): verb and agent. (ادْعُ): an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the weak letter, and its agent is latent, the implied form being "you"; and the clause is the quoted speech. (لَنا): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ادْعُ. (رَبَّكَ): a direct object. (يُبَيِّنْ): the answer to the request. (لَنا): attached to يُبَيِّنْ. (ما): an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ. (لَوْنُها): khabar, and the clause is in the accusative position as an object. (قالَ): a past verb. (إِنَّهُ): inna and its noun, and the clause (يَقُولُ) is its khabar. (إِنَّها بَقَرَةٌ): inna with its noun and khabar, and the clause is the quoted speech. (صَفْراءُ): an adjective of بَقَرَةٌ. (فاقِعٌ): a second adjective. (لَوْنُها): the agent of فاقِعٌ; and it is permissible that فاقِعٌ be a khabar placed first and لَوْنُها a delayed mubtadaʾ, with the clause a second adjective of بَقَرَةٌ, and both are good. (تَسُرُّ النَّاظِرِينَ): an imperfect verb with a latent agent and an object, and the clause is a third adjective of بَقَرَةٌ. (قالُوا ادْعُ لَنا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّنْ لَنا ما هِيَ): its i'rab has been given before, word for word, so renew your acquaintance with it. (إِنَّ): a particle resembling the verb. (الْبَقَرَ): its noun, and the clause is a justification of the question, with no position. (تَشابَهَ): a past verb whose agent is "he", and the clause is the khabar of inna. (عَلَيْنا): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تَشابَهَ. (وَإِنَّا): the wāw is a conjunction, and inna and its noun. (إِنْ): a particle of a jussive condition. (شاءَ): a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis. (اللَّهُ): the agent; and the apodosis of إِنْ is omitted, the implied form being "we would be guided". (لَمُهْتَدُونَ): the lām is the shifted lām, and مُهْتَدُونَ is the khabar of inna. (قالَ): a past verb. (إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ): inna and its noun, and the clause يَقُولُ is the khabar of inna. (إِنَّها بَقَرَةٌ): the i'rab of its like was given completely. (لا): a negative. (ذَلُولٌ): an adjective of بَقَرَةٌ. (تُثِيرُ الْأَرْضَ): a verbal clause in the nominative position as a second adjective; what is intended is the negation of her turning over the earth. (وَلا): the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is added to reinforce the first, because the meaning is "not broken in, turning over and watering", on the view that the two verbs are both adjectives of ذَلُولٌ; it is as if it were said "not a cow broken in whose description is that she is a turner-over and a waterer", so the negation is directed at the described and its description. We postpone discussion of this wonderful construction to the section of Benefits. (تَسْقِي الْحَرْثَ): an imperfect verb with a latent agent and a direct object. (مُسَلَّمَةٌ): a third adjective, i.e. Allah has kept her free of defects. (لا): the negative of generic negation, one of the sisters of inna. (شِيَةَ): its noun, indeclinable on fatḥa. (فِيها): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar, and the clause is a fourth adjective. (قالُوا): verb and agent. (الْآنَ): an adverb of time attached to جِئْتَ. (جِئْتَ): the clause جِئْتَ is the quoted speech. (بِالْحَقِّ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "bringing the truth". (فَذَبَحُوها): conjoined to an omitted element that the context requires, i.e. "so they sought her, found her and slaughtered her"; you may also make the fāʾ the fāʾ of eloquent omission, i.e. "so when they obtained this cow that combined the varied parts of this description, they slaughtered her". (وَما): the wāw is a conjunction and مَا is a negative. (كادُوا): kāda and its noun, because it is one of the verbs of approximation that work like kāna; and the clause (يَفْعَلُونَ) is the khabar of كادُوا.

* Rhetoric:
1- In these preceding verses there is the art of repetition (takrīr), which falls under prolixity (iṭnāb); it is as if they repeated the question in order to probe the reality of the cow. It is reported from the Prophet ﷺ: "Had they taken any cow at all and slaughtered it, it would have sufficed them; but they made it hard, so Allah made it hard for them."
2- The secrets of kāda in Arabic are many. It enters a verb to give the meaning of approximation in the predicate, so when negation enters it, it is only to negate the predicate, as if you said: "when he puts out his hand, he scarcely sees it". When kāda is used in an affirmative form, the verb is not realised; and when a negative particle accompanies it, the verb after it has occurred. For this reason there is disagreement over the meaning of "approximation" (kaydūda) here. In any case it is a vivid picture of the nature of the Jews and their resort to obstinacy and stubbornness: they did the slaughtering after long wrangling and a defiance that could go no further.

* Benefits:
1- The disagreement among the i'rab scholars flared up over His saying «وَلا تَسْقِي الْحَرْثَ». A dispute broke out between Abū Ḥātim and Abū l-Baqāʾ on one side and al-Zamakhsharī and Abū Ḥayyān on the other. In the i'rab we have chosen the easiest of the aspects and the closest to logic.
2- (الآن): an adverb of time that requires the present and restricts the imperfect to it. It is bound to adverbial use and is not inflected in other ways. It is indeclinable because it implies the meaning of demonstration, as if you said "this time". There is disagreement about the definite article entering it: it was said that it is purely for definiteness of presence, and it was said that it is a redundant, inseparable particle.

dervis-irab:72-73.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ادّارأتم): "you pushed one another away" (tadāfaʿtum), because disputants repel one another (yadraʾu baʿḍuhum baʿḍan), that is, push and jostle one another. The meaning is: each of you accused the other, in order to obliterate the traces of the crime and to ward suspicion off himself.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ): conjoined to the preceding story; their revelation follows the order of their occurrence. So Allah the Exalted had commanded them to slaughter the cow and they slaughtered her without knowing what lay behind that command; then after that the matter of the killing occurred, and He made manifest to them the wisdom that He had concealed. (قَتَلْتُمْ): the clause is in the genitive position through the annexation of the adverbial to it. (نَفْساً): a direct object. (فَادَّارَأْتُمْ): conjoined to قَتَلْتُمْ. (فِيها): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ادَّارَأْتُمْ. (وَاللَّهُ): the wāw is parenthetical, and اللَّهُ is a mubtadaʾ. (مُخْرِجٌ): khabar, and the clause has no position because it is parenthetical. (ما): a relative noun, the direct object of مُخْرِجٌ because it is an active participle. (كُنْتُمْ): kāna and its noun. (تَكْتُمُونَ): a verbal clause in the accusative position as the khabar of كُنْتُمْ; and the clause has no position because it is the ṣila of مَا. (فَقُلْنا): conjoined. (اضْرِبُوهُ): an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn; the wāw of the group is the agent, and the hāʾ is the object; and the clause is the quoted speech. (بِبَعْضِها): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اضْرِبُوهُ. (كَذلِكَ يُحْيِ اللَّهُ الْمَوْتى): كَذلِكَ is a preposition and its genitive noun in the accusative position as a fronted absolute object, because it was originally a description of the maṣdar, the implied form being "Allah gives life to the dead by a giving of life like that giving of life". (وَيُرِيكُمْ): conjoined to يُحْيِ, and the kāf is the first object. (آياتِهِ): the second object. (لَعَلَّكُمْ): laʿalla and its noun. (تَعْقِلُونَ): the clause is in the nominative position as the khabar of laʿalla.

dervis-irab:74-74.t:
* I'rab:
(ثُمَّ): a conjunction of delay, and of the improbability of hardness after the mention of what should make hearts soft. (قَسَتْ): a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa over the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents, and the tāʾ is the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine. (قُلُوبُكُمْ): the agent. (مِنْ بَعْدِ ذلِكَ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قَسَتْ, and ذلِكَ is a muḍāf ilayhi. (فَهِيَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and هِيَ is a mubtadaʾ. (كَالْحِجارَةِ): the kāf is a noun meaning "like", the khabar, and الْحِجارَةِ is a muḍāf ilayhi; you may also make it a preposition, with the preposition and its genitive noun as the khabar of هِيَ. (أَوْ): a conjunction of option, or of vagueness, or of classification. (أَشَدُّ): conjoined to the kāf if it is a noun, or to كَالْحِجارَةِ, because the preposition and its genitive noun are in the nominative position. (قَسْوَةً): a tamyīz (specification). The analogy would have been for it to say "aqsā", because the elative is formed from a triliteral verb that fulfils its conditions; but it departed from that because the course of the story calls for departing to prolixity and added intensification by mentioning the word "intensity" (shidda). (وَإِنَّ): the wāw is resumptive and إِنَّ is a particle resembling the verb. (مِنَ الْحِجارَةِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar placed first. (لَما): the lām is the shifted lām, and مَا is a relative noun in the accusative position as its delayed noun. (يَتَفَجَّرُ): an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the clause is a ṣila with no position. (مِنْهُ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يَتَفَجَّرُ. (الْأَنْهارُ): the agent of يَتَفَجَّرُ. (وَإِنَّ): conjoined to the first inna. (مِنْها): a preposition and its genitive noun, a khabar placed first. (لَما): the shifted lām, and مَا a relative noun, the delayed noun of inna. (يَشَّقَّقُ): an imperfect verb in the nominative. (فَيَخْرُجُ): conjoined to يَشَّقَّقُ. (وَإِنَّ مِنْها لَما يَهْبِطُ): conjoined to what precedes. (مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يَهْبِطُ, serving as a justification for it. (وَمَا): the wāw is resumptive and مَا is a Hijazi negative that works like لَيْسَ. (اللَّهِ): its noun, in the nominative. (بِغافِلٍ): the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and غافِلٍ is genitive in form by the bāʾ and accusative in position as the khabar of مَا. (عَمَّا): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to غافِلٍ. (تَعْمَلُونَ): the clause has no position because it is a ṣila.

* Rhetoric:
1- The loose simile (tashbīh mursal): it likened their hearts, in their recoil from the truth and their aloofness from its rulings, to hard stones; then it ascended in the simile, making the stones softer than their hearts.
2- The implicit, derivative metaphor in His saying «ثم قست قلوبكم»: the state of the hearts, in not taking heed or admonition from what stands before them and speaks with the tongue of circumstance, is likened to the recoiling stones, whose characteristics are hardness and solidity.
3- The rational trope (majāz ʿaqlī) in attributing fear to the stones, which is common in the tongues of the Arabs.

* Benefits:
(مَا al-ḥijāziyya) is so called because it works like لَيْسَ in the dialect of the people of the Hijaz; in the dialect of Tamīm it is a negative that does not work. Four conditions are required for it to work:
a- Its khabar must not precede its noun, otherwise it does not work. Among their proverbs: "ما مسئيء من أعتب" (He who apologises is not one who has done wrong).
b- The object of its khabar must not precede its noun, otherwise it does not work, as in: "ما بك أنا منتصر" (I am not one to be victorious through you).
c- It must not be followed by إِنْ, otherwise its working is void, as in the verse: "بني غدانة ما إن أنتم ذهب ... ولا صريف ولكن أنتم الخزف" (O sons of Ghudāna, you are not gold, nor pure silver, but you are pottery).
d- Its negation must not be broken by إِلَّا, otherwise its working is void, as in: «وما محمد إلا رسول».

dervis-irab:75-75.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الطمع): the soul's strong attachment to attaining something, so it is stronger than hope (rajāʾ). One says ṭamiʿa yaṭmaʿu ṭamaʿan, ṭamāʿan and ṭamāʿiya. Al-Mutanabbī said:
إلام طماعية العاذل ... ولا رأي في الحبّ للعاقل
(Until when the reproacher's eagerness? And the sensible man has no say in love.)

* I'rab:
(أَفَتَطْمَعُونَ): the hamza is for the interrogative, and what is meant by it is prohibition or disapproval. The discussion of the hamza entering the conjunctions has already been given. The meaning is: do not hope to convince these obstinate, rough ones, whose hearts are hard. (أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا): أَنْ and what follows it are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition. (لَكُمْ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يُؤْمِنُوا, on the basis that يُؤْمِنُوا is given the meaning of submission. (وَقَدْ): the wāw is a ḥāl, and قَدْ is a particle of certainty. (كانَ): a defective past verb. (فَرِيقٌ): its noun. (مِنْهُمْ): a preposition and its genitive noun, an adjective of فَرِيقٌ. (يَسْمَعُونَ): an imperfect verb in the nominative, the wāw is the agent, and the clause يَسْمَعُونَ is the khabar of كانَ. (كَلامَ اللَّهِ): a direct object. (ثُمَّ): a conjunction of delay. (يُحَرِّفُونَهُ): conjoined to يَسْمَعُونَ. (مِنْ بَعْدِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يُحَرِّفُونَهُ. (ما): a maṣdar particle, interpreted with what follows as a maṣdar in the genitive position through annexation. (عَقَلُوهُ): verb, agent and object. (وَهُمْ): the wāw is a ḥāl and هُمْ is a mubtadaʾ. (يَعْلَمُونَ): the clause is in the nominative position as their khabar, and the nominal clause is in the accusative position as a ḥāl, i.e. while they are aware of their disbelief, their stubbornness and their fabrication.

dervis-irab:76-77.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا): the wāw is resumptive or a conjunction; and إِذا is an adverb of the future time, governing its protasis in the genitive and attached to its apodosis. (لَقُوا): a past verb, indeclinable on fatḥa, and the wāw is the agent; the clause لَقُوا is verbal, with no grammatical position because the adverbial is annexed to it. (الَّذِينَ): a relative noun, direct object. (آمَنُوا): verb and agent, and the clause has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (قالُوا): verb and agent, and the clause has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (آمَنَّا): verb and agent, and the clause is in the accusative position as the quoted speech. (وَإِذا): conjoined to the first وَإِذا. (خَلا بَعْضُهُمْ): verb and agent, and the clause is in the genitive position through the annexation of the adverbial. (إِلى بَعْضٍ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خَلا. (قالُوا): the clause has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (أَتُحَدِّثُونَهُمْ): the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval, and تُحَدِّثُونَهُمْ is verb, agent and object, and the clause is in the accusative position as the quoted speech. (بِما): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تُحَدِّثُونَهُمْ. (فَتَحَ اللَّهُ): verb and agent, and the clause has no position because it is a ṣila. (عَلَيْكُمْ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to فَتَحَ. (لِيُحَاجُّوكُمْ): the lām is the lām of consequence or outcome, not of justification in meaning, because they did not intend that; rather the end and consequence was that. But it is like the lām of justification in its working. يُحَاجُّوكُمْ is an imperfect verb put in the accusative by an implied أَنْ, permissibly, after the lām of consequence or outcome; and the lām and its genitive noun are attached to تُحَدِّثُونَهُمْ. (بِهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يُحَاجُّوكُمْ. (عِنْدَ رَبِّكُمْ): the adverbial is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (أَفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ): the rule of the interrogative hamza when it enters a conjunction has frequently been given. (أَوَلا): the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation, whose meaning is to bring the addressee to acknowledge and admit, and it is not free of rebuke; the wāw is a conjunction which is in the intention of being placed before the hamza, but was postponed because of the strength of the hamza; and لا is a negative. (يَعْلَمُونَ): conjoined to an omitted verb; the meaning is: do they blame them for speaking of what was mentioned, and do they not know. (أَنَّ اللَّهَ): anna and its noun, and what follows it take the place of the two objects of يَعْلَمُونَ, and for that reason its hamza has fatḥa. (يَعْلَمُ): an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, the implied form being "He", and the clause is in the nominative position as the khabar of anna. (ما): a relative noun or a maṣdar particle, and in either case it, with what follows it, is the object of يَعْلَمُ. (يُسِرُّونَ): the clause has no position in any case. (وَما يُعْلِنُونَ): conjoined to it.

dervis-irab:34-36.t:
* Vocabulary:
(إِبْلِيسَ): there is disagreement about it, whether it is derived or not. The sound view is that it is a foreign proper name, and for this reason it is not fully declined (lam yanṣarif), because of being a proper name and foreign. Had it been derived from الإبلاس, i.e. despair, it would have been fully declined. This has been pointed out before.
(رَغَداً): it is said رغد العيش (with ḍamma), رغادة: it was spacious and soft, so it is رغيد; and رغد (with kasra), رغدا (with two fatḥas), so he is راغد.
(فَأَزَلَّهُمَا) It carries two meanings: first, "he made their slip manifest"; second, "he removed them far away".

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ) The wāw is a conjunction, and إذ is an adverb of past time. (قُلْنا): verb and fāʿil; the verbal clause is in the genitive position by the annexation of the adverb to it. (لِلْمَلائِكَةِ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قلنا. (اسْجُدُوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable with the omission of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil; the verbal clause is in the accusative position as reported speech. (لِآدَمَ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to اسجدوا. (فَسَجَدُوا) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and سجدوا is verb and fāʿil. (إِلَّا) a particle of exception. (إِبْلِيسَ) excepted by إلا; a connected exception (muttaṣil) if Iblis was originally one of the angels, while it was said to be disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) because he was not one of them. (أَبى) a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on the alif; the verbal clause is in the accusative position as ḥāl, i.e. while refusing the command, being arrogant toward it and disbelieving in it. (وَاسْتَكْبَرَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and استكبر is a past verb conjoined to أبى. (وَكانَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and كان is a defective past verb, its ism a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of كان. (وَقُلْنَا) The wāw is a conjunction, and قلنا is verb and fāʿil, conjoined to the earlier قلنا; the difference of the two times is not a preventing cause against conjoining a verb to a verb. (يا آدَمُ) yā is a vocative particle for a mid-distance addressee, and آدم is a singular proper-name vocative, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the accusative position. (اسْكُنْ) an imperative verb, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت". (أَنْتَ) tawkīd of the latent fāʿil in اسكن. (وَزَوْجُكَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and زوجك is conjoined to the latent pronoun in اسكن; conjoining the overt noun to the pronoun is made good by the emphasising of that pronoun with a detached pronoun. (الْجَنَّةَ) direct object, by extension (ʿalā l-sagha). (وَكُلا) The wāw is a conjunction, and كلا is an imperative verb, indeclinable with the omission of the nūn because its imperfect belongs to the five verbs; the alif is an attached pronoun in the nominative position as fāʿil. (مِنْها) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to كلا. (رَغَداً) an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "eating plentifully", so it is an absolute object; it may also be parsed as a ḥāl interpreted as a derived word, i.e. "living at ease, comfortable". (حَيْثُ) an adverb of place, indeclinable on the ḍamma, attached to كلا. Eating and plenty in Paradise were made unrestricted for them so that every avenue of excuse would be cut off from them should a single particular tree cross their mind, there being ample room to avoid it among the many trees of Paradise. (شِئْتُما) the verbal clause is in the genitive position by the annexation of the adverb of place to it. (وَلا تَقْرَبا) The wāw is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, and تقربا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, its sign of jussion being the omission of the nūn, and the alif is the fāʿil. (هذِهِ) a demonstrative in the accusative position as direct object. (الشَّجَرَةَ) badal from the demonstrative. (فَتَكُونا) The fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (sababiyya), and تكونا is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ of causation; the alif is an attached pronoun in the nominative position as ism of تكونا. (مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of تكونا. (فَأَزَلَّهُمَا) The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an implied omitted clause that the context requires, i.e. "so they ate of that very tree"; أزلهما is a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the accusative position as direct object, and the mīm and alif are two particles indicating the dual. (الشَّيْطانُ) fāʿil of أزل. (عَنْها) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to أزلهما, or to an omitted ḥāl. (فَأَخْرَجَهُما) conjoined to أزلهما. (مِمَّا) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أخرجهما. (كانا) a defective past verb, the alif its ism. (فِيهِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of كانا. (وَقُلْنَا) conjoined to what preceded, and the clause كان has no position because it is a ṣila of the relative. (اهْبِطُوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable with the omission of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil; the clause is reported speech. (بَعْضُكُمْ) mubtadaʾ. (لِبَعْضٍ) attached to His saying (عَدُوٌّ), which is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; or attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of عدو that was put before it. The clause بعضكم etc. is a nominal clause in the accusative position as ḥāl, i.e. "being enemies to one another". (وَلَكُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction, and لكم is attached to an omitted advanced khabar. (فِي الْأَرْضِ) attached to the "settling" to which the khabar is attached, or to an omitted ḥāl. (مُسْتَقَرٌّ) delayed mubtadaʾ. (وَمَتاعٌ) conjoined to مستقر. (إِلى حِينٍ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of متاع, i.e. "extending until the Day of Resurrection".

* Benefits:
(أَبى) is one of the affirmative verbs whose meaning is negation, and for this reason what follows إلا is left free (yufarraghu) with it, as it is with the negated verb. Allah the Exalted said: «ويأبى الله إلا أن يتم نوره». It is not permissible to say ضربت إلا زيدا as a freed exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), because إلا does not enter an affirmative sentence.

dervis-irab:37-38.t:
* I'rab:
(فَتَلَقَّى) The fāʾ is resumptive, and تلقى is a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa. (آدَمُ) fāʿil. (مِنْ رَبِّهِ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to تلقى. (كَلِماتٍ) direct object, accusative with the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural. (فَتابَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an omitted clause that the context requires, i.e. "so he said them, and He relented". (عَلَيْهِ) attached to تاب. (إِنَّهُ) inna and its ism. (هُوَ) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or support (ʿimād), with no position; it may also be a mubtadaʾ. (التَّوَّابُ) the first khabar of inna. (الرَّحِيمُ) the second khabar of inna; they may also be two khabars of هو, with the nominal clause as the khabar of inna. (قُلْنَا) verb and fāʿil. (اهْبِطُوا) the verbal clause is reported speech. (مِنْها) attached to اهبطوا. (جَمِيعاً) ḥāl from the wāw. The clause قلنا اهبطوا follows the clause وقلنا اهبطوا as emphasis of it, so that a new addition may be attached to it. (فَإِمَّا) The fāʾ is a conjunction, إن is conditional, and ما is redundant for emphasis. (يَأْتِيَنَّكُمْ) the protasis, jussive and indeclinable on the fatḥa because of its attachment to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the kāf is an attached pronoun in the accusative position as direct object. (مِنِّي) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأتينكم. (هُدىً) fāʿil, nominative, its sign of nominative being the implied ḍamma on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns. (فَمَنْ) The fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition, and من is a jussive conditional noun in the position of mubtadaʾ. (تَبِعَ) a past verb in the jussive position as the protasis, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "هو". (هُدايَ) object of تبع, its sign of accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, which is annexed to هدى; and the fāʾ with what follows it is in the jussive position as the apodosis. (فَلا) The fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition, which is "من", and لا is negative. (خَوْفٌ) mubtadaʾ; it is allowed to begin with it though it is indefinite because negation precedes it, which is one of the justifications for beginning with an indefinite. (عَلَيْهِمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of خوف; you may also make لا operate as laysa, so that خوف is its ism and عليهم its khabar. (وَلا) conjoined to the first لا, and (هُمْ) is a mubtadaʾ, or the ism of لا operating as laysa. (يَحْزَنُونَ) the verbal clause is in the nominative or accusative position as their khabar or the khabar of لا; and the clause of the protasis and its apodosis together is the khabar of من.

* Benefits:
The preferred view among the grammarians is that when a conditional noun occurs as mubtadaʾ — which is when it is followed by an intransitive verb, as in من يذهب أذهب معه (whoever goes, I go with him), or a transitive verb that has taken its object, as in «من يعمل سوءا يجز به» — the khabar is the clause of the protasis. There are among the grammarians those who make the clause of the apodosis the khabar, and among them those who make the khabar the clause of the protasis and apodosis together; and this is what we have chosen.

dervis-irab:39-41.t:
* Vocabulary:
(إِسْرائِيلَ): they differed about it, and the soundest view is that it is a foreign proper name, and for this reason it is a diptote. It is a compound in the manner of an annexation: إسرا is "servant" in Hebrew and إيل is "Allah". The Arabs have treated it in various dialects, the soundest being the dialect of the Qur'an. It is a title of Yaʿqūb. Abū Jaʿfar and al-Aʿmash read إسرائيل with a yāʾ after the alif and without hamza; from Warsh is related اسرائل with a hamza after the alif and without yāʾ, and اسرال with a pure alif between the rāʾ and the lām; and a reading is related from Nāfiʿ: اسرائين, in which they replaced the lām with a nūn, like أصيلان. Lām and nūn alternate in attested words, among them عنوان الكتاب and علوانه, and أبّنت and أبّلته when you praise him after his death, and others.

* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and الذين is a mubtadaʾ; the sentence is conjoined to His saying in the previous verse فمن تبع هداي, because it is its counterpart (qasīm). The requirement of the division would be for Him to say "and whoever does not follow My guidance", but He turned away from that so as to bring out the counterpart with disbelief recorded against it. (كَفَرُوا) the verbal clause has no position because it is a ṣila of the relative. (وَكَذَّبُوا) conjoined to كفروا, within the scope of the ṣila. (بِآياتِنا) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to كذبوا. (أُولئِكَ) a demonstrative, second mubtadaʾ. (أَصْحابُ النَّارِ) khabar of أولئك, and the nominal clause is the khabar of الذين. (هُمْ) a detached pronoun in the nominative position as mubtadaʾ. (فِيها) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to خالدون. (خالِدُونَ) their khabar, and the nominal clause is in the nominative position as a second khabar for the mubtadaʾ that is أولئك; it is possible that it is in the accusative position as ḥāl; and some parsed it as explicative (mufassira) with no position, explaining His saying «أولئك أصحاب النار», to show that their companionship of the Fire is not mere association but is for permanence and eternity — and this is a permissible and beautiful i'rab.
(يا بَنِي) yā is a vocative particle, and بني is an annexed vocative, its sign of accusative being the yāʾ in place of the fatḥa because it is joined to the sound masculine plural, and the structure of its singular has changed. The origin of ابن is wāw-based, the word بنوّة being evidence of it; it was also said that its origin is yāʾ-based because it is derived from البناء, which is placing one thing upon another, and the son is a branch of the father and so is set upon him. It forms a broken plural, so they said أبناء, and a sound plural, so they said بنون. (إِسْرائِيلَ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, its sign of genitive being the fatḥa in place of the kasra because it is a diptote, being a proper name and foreign. (اذْكُرُوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable with the omission of the nūn because of its attachment to the wāw of the group, the wāw being the fāʿil. (نِعْمَتِيَ) direct object, accusative, its sign of accusative being the fatḥa implied on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. (الَّتِي) a relative noun in the accusative position as adjective of نعمتي. (أَنْعَمْتُ) verb and fāʿil. (عَلَيْكُمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنعمت; the clause أنعمت has no position because it is a ṣila of the relative. (وَأَوْفُوا) conjoined to اذكروا. (بِعَهْدِي) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوفوا. (أُوفِ) an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the response to a request (jawāb al-ṭalab). (بِعَهْدِكُمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوف. (وَإِيَّايَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and إياي is a detached pronoun in the accusative position as a direct object put before an implied verb "ارهبوا", the verb فارهبون having exhausted its own object, which is the implied yāʾ; the original is فارهبوني. (فَارْهَبُونِ) As for the fāʾ in this construction, which is repeated often in the Qur'an, there are two views: one, that it is an implied response, its implied form being "be alert" or the like, as in your saying الكتاب فخذ, i.e. "be alert, take the book"; then the object was put first to correct the wording so that the fāʾ would not stand at the head; and the other, that it is redundant. (وَآمِنُوا) conjoined to what preceded. (بِما) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنوا. (أَنْزَلْتُ) verb and fāʿil; the clause has no position because it is a ṣila of the relative. (مُصَدِّقاً) ḥāl from the relative noun. (لِما) the lām is a preposition strengthening the transitivity, and ما is a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the genitive position by the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to مصدقا. (مَعَكُمْ) an adverb of place attached to an omitted element, with no position because it is the ṣila of the relative. (وَلا) The wāw is a conjunction and لا is prohibitive. (تَكُونُوا) an imperfect verb jussive by لا, its sign of jussion being the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is its ism. (أَوَّلَ) khabar of تكونوا. (كافِرٍ) muḍāf ilayhi. (بِهِ) attached to كافر. (وَلا تَشْتَرُوا) conjoined to ولا تكونوا. (بِآياتِي) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to تشتروا. (ثَمَناً) direct object of تشتروا. (قَلِيلًا) adjective. (وَإِيَّايَ فَاتَّقُونِ) the i'rab of this construction has been given before.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying: «أوف بعهدكم» there is an art called al-taʿaṭṭuf, whose gist is repeating the very same word within a sentence of speech; some call it the art of participation (mushāraka). The covenant includes in its general sense the covenant of Allah which He took from them and from all mankind, namely reflection (tadabbur) and weighing everything that befalls them in their lives by the balance of reason and reflection — a balance that does not err — and not by the balance of desire and conceit, which is a reckless balance.

* Benefits:
These foregoing verses contain several benefits, which we list in the following:
1- The requirement of analogy would be for Him to say "أول كافرين به" (first disbelievers in it) to agree with the wāw in His saying تكونوا, but He turned away from that for reasons, namely:
a- It is on the omission of the described noun (mawṣūf), the implied form being "first group disbelieving in it".
b- An indefinite noun to which a superlative (ism al-tafḍīl) is annexed must be singular, for example:
أنت أفضل رجل وأنتما أفضل رجل وأنتم أفضل رجل
(You are the best man; you two are the best man; you all are the best man.)
2- Such as His saying: «واياي فارهبون» is of the chapter of ishtighāl (preoccupation), and إيا in it is accusative by an omitted verb that the mentioned verb explains. It is not valid for the pronoun to be an object put before the verb that follows it, because the verb has made accusative the pronoun that comes after the protective nūn, which has been omitted for lightness.

dervis-irab:224-225.t:
* Vocabulary:
(عُرْضَةً): al-ʿurḍa, with ḍamma, is a thing that is set up and exposed. One says "he is ʿurḍa for such-and-such", that is, strong against it; and "he is ʿurḍa for the people", that is, they never cease falling into him; and "I made it ʿurḍa for such-and-such", that is, I set it up. The meaning is: do not make Allah like the target set up for archers, so that whenever you want to refrain from something, even if it is good, you resort to doing so by swearing an oath. (اللغو): what is fallen away, which is not heeded or counted, whether speech or otherwise; what is meant by it here is what the tongue slips into without the intention of swearing.

* I'rab:
(وَلا تَجْعَلُوا): the waw is resumptive, introduced to address a serious social problem, namely making the name of Allah an object exposed to your oaths, which you demean by swearing by Him too often. Or: do not make Him an intervening barrier by swearing by Him. This is because ʿurḍa is either in the sense of an active participle or in the sense of a passive one. لا is prohibitive and تجعلوا is an imperfect verb jussive by it. (اللَّهَ): the first direct object of تجعلوا. (عُرْضَةً): the second direct object. (لِأَيْمانِكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to عرضة. (أَنْ تَبَرُّوا): أن and what is within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar, a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) or a badal. (وَتَتَّقُوا وَتُصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ النَّاسِ): conjoined to أن تبروا; and بين is an adverb attached to تصلحوا. (وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ): a resumptive clause with no grammatical position; الله is a mubtadaʾ and سميع عليم are its two khabars. (لا): negative. (يُؤاخِذُكُمُ): an imperfect verb and a direct object. (اللَّهُ): its agent; the clause is resumptive. (بِاللَّغْوِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يؤاخذكم. (فِي أَيْمانِكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَلكِنْ): the waw is a conjunction and لكن is inoperative, for rectification (istidrāk). (يُؤاخِذُكُمُ): an imperfect verb and a direct object. (بِما كَسَبَتْ قُلُوبُكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يؤاخذكم; ما is either maṣdarī or a relative noun, and قلوبكم is the agent. (وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ): the waw is resumptive, الله is a mubtadaʾ and غفور حليم are its two khabars.

dervis-irab:226-228.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُؤْلُونَ): they swear. Īlāʾ from a woman is for a man to say: "By Allah, I will not come near you for four months or more." There are discussions about this verb that belong to the science of jurisprudence, to which one returns in their proper places.
(فاؤُ): they returned.
(التربص): waiting and deliberation. The poet said:
تربّص بها ريب المنون لعلها ... تطلّق يوما أو يموت حليلها
(Wait for the misfortunes of fate to befall her; perhaps she will be divorced one day, or her husband will die.)
(قروء): the plural of qurʾ, which is the state of purity, as al-Shāfiʿī held, or menstruation, as Abū Ḥanīfa held. The disagreement of the jurists where the language allows both possibilities is very fine. As an instance of its application to purity is the saying of al-Aʿshā:
أفي كل عام أنت جاشم غزوة ... تشدّ لأقصاها عظيم عزائكا
مورثة مالا وفي الحي رفعة ... لما ضاع فيها من قروء نسائكا
(Is it in every year that you undertake a campaign, tightening for its farthest reaches the great resolve of your determination? It brings wealth by inheritance, and exalted standing in the tribe, for what was lost in it of the qurūʾ of your women), that is, their periods of purity. As an instance of its application to menstruation is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «Leave the prayer during the days of your aqrāʾ.»

* I'rab:
(لِلَّذِينَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (يُؤْلُونَ): an imperfect verb, with the waw as agent; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (مِنْ نِسائِهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يؤلون. The verb of īlāʾ should by right be made transitive with «ʿalā», but He made it imply the meaning of distancing, because those who swear distance themselves from their women «[Translator's note: the source repeats the word "their women" (نسائهم نسائهم) here]». (تَرَبُّصُ): a delayed mubtadaʾ, and (أَرْبَعَةِ أَشْهُرٍ): أربعة أشهر is its muḍāf ilayhi; the speech is resumptive, to complete the legislation. (فَإِنْ فاؤُ): the fāʾ is resumptive and إن is conditional; فاءوا is a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of the jussive as the protasis. (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the fāʾ links the apodosis; inna with its noun and two khabars; the clause of inna and what follows is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (وَإِنْ عَزَمُوا الطَّلاقَ): the waw is a conjunction and إن is conditional; عزموا is a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of the jussive as the protasis; and الطلاق is accusative by removal of the preposition, because عزم is made transitive with «ʿalā»; the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then let them carry it out". (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ): the fāʾ is a conjunction to the omitted apodosis, standing as a giving of reason; inna with its noun and two khabars. (وَالْمُطَلَّقاتُ): the waw is resumptive and المطلقات is a mubtadaʾ. (يَتَرَبَّصْنَ): an imperfect verb, indeclinable on sukūn because the nūn of the feminine plural is attached to it, the nūn being the agent; the clause يتربصن is the khabar of المطلقات, and the resumptive clause has no grammatical position, introduced to explain the rulings of divorce. (بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يتربصن; the bāʾ has the sense of cause, that is, "for the sake of themselves", because the souls of women yearn toward men, so they are best placed to curb its eagerness. (ثَلاثَةَ قُرُوءٍ): the grammarians said it is a direct object of يتربصن, but I think that the accusative as an adverb of time is preferable, the adverb being attached to يتربصن, that is, "for the duration of three qurūʾ". (وَلا يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ): the waw is a conjunction, لا is negative, and يحل is an imperfect verb conjoined to يتربصن. (أَنْ يَكْتُمْنَ): أن is a maṣdar and subjunctive particle; يكتمن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of the accusative by أن, and the nūn of the feminine plural is the agent; أن and what is within its scope is in the interpretation of a maṣdar, the agent of يحل. (ما): a relative noun in the position of the accusative as direct object. (خَلَقَ اللَّهُ): a verb and an agent; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (فِي أَرْحامِهِنَّ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to خلق. (أَنْ): conditional. (كُنَّ): a defective past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the nūn of the feminine plural is an attached pronoun in the position of the nominative as the noun of kāna. (يُؤْمِنَّ): the khabar of كن; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, that is, "then they should not dare to do that". (بِاللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يؤمن. (وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ): conjoined to the Majestic Name. (وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ): the waw is a conjunction and بعولتهن is a mubtadaʾ. (أَحَقُّ): the khabar. (بِرَدِّهِنَّ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أحق. (فِي ذلِكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "in the state of the taking back being within the period of that waiting". (إِنْ أَرادُوا إِصْلاحاً): إن is a particle of jussive conditional; أرادوا is a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of the jussive as the protasis, and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being: "then their husbands have more right to take them back"; the waw is the agent and إصلاحا is the direct object. (وَلَهُنَّ): the waw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (مِثْلُ الَّذِي عَلَيْهِنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): مثل is a delayed mubtadaʾ, the relative noun is its muḍāf ilayhi, عليهن is the ṣila of the relative noun, and بالمعروف is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "being in the manner that is not rejected by the Law and by custom". The details of these rulings are in the books of jurisprudence. (وَلِلرِّجالِ): the waw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (عَلَيْهِنَّ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it precedes what it describes. (دَرَجَةٌ): a delayed mubtadaʾ. (وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ): the waw is resumptive, الله is a mubtadaʾ and عزيز حكيم are its two khabars.

* Benefits:
It has been observed that He annexed the number three to قروء, which is among the plurals of multitude (jumūʿ al-kathra). This is because, when He made المطلقات plural, and three periods were obligatory for each of them, He made القروء a plural of multitude so that the speech would be harmonious; or it is a matter of latitude, putting one of the two plurals in the place of the other, for the subtlety just indicated.

dervis-irab:229-229.t:
* I'rab:
(الطَّلاقُ مَرَّتانِ): a mubtadaʾ and a khabar; the clause is resumptive, to state the number of permissible divorces. (فَإِمْساكٌ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, as if it were said: "if you have learned how divorce is done, then one of two things is incumbent on you". إمساك is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is, "incumbent on you is keeping them"; we have only implied the khabar before it to make it permissible to begin with an indefinite noun. (بِمَعْرُوفٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of إمساك. (أَوْ تَسْرِيحٌ بِإِحْسانٍ): أو is a conjunction, تسريح is conjoined to إمساك, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of تسريح. What is meant by iḥsān is the continued conferring of kindness, or the payment of all her financial rights, in order to mend the breach that the divorce has caused. (وَلا): the waw is resumptive or a conjunction, and لا is negative. (يَحِلُّ): an imperfect verb in the nominative. (لَكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يحل. (أَنْ تَأْخُذُوا): أن and what follows is in the interpretation of a maṣdar, the agent of يحل. (مِمَّا): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تأخذوا or to an omitted ḥāl. (آتَيْتُمُوهُنَّ): the clause is the ṣila of the relative; the waw after the mīm, which is the mīm of the masculine plural, is for the lengthening of the ḍamma of the mīm. (شَيْئاً): a direct object. (إِلَّا أَنْ يَخافا): إلا is a particle of restriction because of the preceding negation, or of exception; أن and the verb after it are in the interpretation of a maṣdar. There has been severe disagreement over the i'rab of this maṣdar. The apparent view is that it is accusative as a ḥāl, that is, "except being fearful". The difficulty with this is that Sībawayh in his book prevented أن with a verb from occurring as a ḥāl, stating this at the end of the chapter "This is the chapter in which the nominative is preferred". On this there is no way out but to return to the second of the aspects of exception, which is that the speech is complete and negated, so we put it in the accusative as an exception from the direct object, which is «شيئا». It is as if it were said: "It is not lawful for you to take anything for any reason except for the reason of fear of not upholding the limits of Allah; that is what permits you to take." The preposition of cause would then have been omitted before «أن», which is permissible in Arabic. So reflect and ponder. (أَلَّا يُقِيما حُدُودَ اللَّهِ): أن and what is within its scope is in the position of the accusative as the object of يخافا; حدود الله is a direct object, and لا is negative. (فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ): the fāʾ is resumptive and إن is conditional; خفتم is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis, and the tāʾ is the agent. (أَلَّا يُقِيما حُدُودَ اللَّهِ): أن and what follows is in the position of the accusative as the direct object of خفتم. (فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْهِما): the fāʾ links the apodosis; لا is the lā of generic negation, جناح is its noun, and عليهما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of لا. (فِيمَا افْتَدَتْ بِهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; the clause افتدت is the ṣila of the relative, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to افتدت; the clause فلا جناح is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ): تلك, the demonstrative, is a mubtadaʾ, and حدود الله is its khabar. (فَلا تَعْتَدُوها): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, that is, "if you have come to know these rulings, then do not transgress them"; the clause after it has no grammatical position. The clause «تلك حدود الله» is resumptive; لا is prohibitive and تعتدوها is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, with the waw as agent and the hāʾ as direct object. (وَمَنْ يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ اللَّهِ): the waw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, introduced to mention the threat after the prohibition of transgressing them; من is a jussive conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ, and يتعد is the protasis, jussive, its sign of jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; and حدود الله is a direct object. (فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ): the fāʾ links the apodosis; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ, هم is a second mubtadaʾ and الظالمون is its khabar, the second mubtadaʾ with its khabar being the khabar of the first; or هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position and الظالمون is the khabar of أولئك. The clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من».

dervis-irab:200-202.t:
* Vocabulary:
(المناسك): plural of "mansak", with fatḥa or kasra on the sīn; it is a maṣdar mīmī (noun of action with initial mīm) or a noun of place, the former being preferable, i.e. the acts of worship of your Hajj.

* I'rab:
(فَإِذا) The fāʾ is resumptive, and "idhā" is an adverb for what is to come of time, governing its protasis in the genitive and being put in the accusative by its apodosis. (قَضَيْتُمْ) verb and fāʿil; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. (مَناسِكَكُمْ) mafʿūl bihi, and the kāf is an attached pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ) The fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis; "udhkurū Allāh": imperative verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. (كَذِكْرِكُمْ) The kāf with its genitive noun is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "remember Allah with a remembrance like your remembrance of your fathers", or a ḥāl. (آباءَكُمْ) mafʿūl bihi of the maṣdar which is annexed to its fāʿil. (أَوْ أَشَدَّ ذِكْراً) This conjunction is among the things that trouble the one who parses, and there are opinions about it in whose mazes the student is lost. Since the opinions which the grammarians and exegetes have adduced are equal in weight, we saw fit to summarise them in a simple, accessible form: 1- "ashadda" is conjoined to the kāf, i.e. "like your remembrance or the remembrance of a people stronger than them in remembrance".
2- "ashadda" is conjoined to "ābāʾikum", so it is accusative, meaning "or stronger than the remembrance of your fathers".
3- "ashadda" is conjoined to the remembrance (dhikr) itself, and the words must then be taken as a rational trope (majāz ʿaqlī), like their sayings "shiʿrun shāʿir" (a poet's poem) and "jinna junūnuhu" (his madness went mad), and the like. There remains in these views a more troublesome matter: the elative is annexed to what follows it when that is of the same kind as what precedes it, as when you say "dhikruka ashaddu dhikr" (your remembrance is the strongest remembrance) and "wajhuka aḥsanu wajh" (your face is the finest face); and when what follows it is put in the accusative as a tamyīz, what follows is other than what precedes, as when you say "ʿAlī ajmalu wajhan": the beauty belongs to the face, not to ʿAlī. And if you said "Zayd akramu aban", Zayd would be among the sons; and if you said "Zayd akramu ab", Zayd would be among the fathers.
4- Finally, a view to which Abū l-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī resorted after devices had failed him; he said: "In my opinion the sentence is carried according to the meaning, and the implied form is: 'or be stronger in remembering Allah than you are in remembering your fathers'. This meaning is indicated by the saying of the Exalted «فاذكروا الله», i.e. be those who remember Him."
After citing these views, Abū Ḥayyān described them all as weak and said: "It is possible for us to carry the verse to the meaning that they were commanded to remember Allah with a remembrance equal to the remembrance of their fathers or stronger, by a clear elucidation which they overlooked, namely that «أشدّ» is accusative as a ḥāl, being an adjective (naʿt) of His word «ذكرا» had it come later; when it was fronted it became accusative as a ḥāl, like their saying:
لمية موحشا طلل ... يلوح كأنه خلل
(Of Mayya there is a desolate ruin, gleaming as though it were a sword-sheath lining.)
Had it come later it would have been 'li-Mayya ṭalalun mūḥishun'. Likewise, had this come later it would be «أو ذكرا أشد», meaning than your remembrance of your fathers, and «أو ذكرا أشد» would then be conjoined to the position of the kāf in «كذكركم»."
We say: perhaps this is closer to logic and nearer to understanding, and some later exegetes have been content with it in their lengthy marginal notes. (فَمِنَ النَّاسِ) The fāʾ is resumptive, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (مَنْ) a relative noun, postponed mubtadaʾ. (يَقُولُ) an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is a latent pronoun, the implied form being "huwa", referring to "man"; the wording of "man", which is singular, has been observed; had its meaning been observed He would have said "yaqūlūna". The resumptive clause has no grammatical position, and it is brought to explain the state of the disbelievers and the state of the believers and the difference between the two requests. The clause «يقول» is the ṣila of "man". (رَبَّنا) the one addressed, a muḍāf in the accusative, the vocative particle having been omitted. (آتِنا) an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the weak letter, the fāʿil being latent, the implied form being "anta", and the first-person plural pronoun is the first object of "āti"; the second object is omitted, i.e. "our share"; and (فِي الدُّنْيا) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to "ātinā".
