(وَما) The wāw is circumstantial and "mā" is negative. (لَهُ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (فِي الْآخِرَةِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (مِنْ خَلاقٍ) "min" is a redundant preposition, and "khalāq" is genitive in form and nominative in position because it is a postponed mubtadaʾ. (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ رَبَّنا آتِنا فِي الدُّنْيا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً) conjoined to the preceding clause, whose i'rab has been given; here the second object is stated explicitly, as encouragement and instruction. (وَقِنا) The wāw is a conjunction, and "qi" is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the weak letter, its fāʿil being a latent pronoun, the implied form being "anta", and the plural pronoun is the first object of "qi". (عَذابَ النَّارِ) second object of "qi". (أُولئِكَ) a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. (لَهُمْ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (نَصِيبٌ) a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of the demonstrative; the clause is resumptive, to explain the state of the second group, since the state of the first group was mentioned earlier in His saying «وما له في الآخرة من خلاق». (مِمَّا) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ṣifa of "naṣīb". (كَسَبُوا) a past verb with its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of the relative "mā". (وَاللَّهُ) The wāw is resumptive and "Allāh" is a mubtadaʾ. (سَرِيعُ الْحِسابِ) its khabar. The resumptive clause is brought to explain His, the Exalted's, power to reckon with all creatures in less than the twinkling of an eye.

* Rhetoric:
In one of the ways of parsing His saying «أشد ذكرا» there is an allusion to the rational trope, whose discussion has already preceded; we add to this trope some elaboration and say: Attributing the remembrance to the remembrance is impossible, but it is closely associated with it, so that it becomes as if it were a rational person, separate from it, performing it. Fine is the saying of Abū Tammām:
تكاد عطاياه يجنّ جنونها ... إذا لم يعوّذها بنغمة طالب
(His gifts almost go mad with madness, if he does not shield them with the plea of a petitioner.)
He attributed madness to its own verbal noun, and the secret in it is the intense association which we explained, which makes the non-rational rational because of its intense occurrence from it. Students are almost confused about the difference between it and the implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya), though there is in it no intended resemblance. Abū Firās said:
سيذكرني قومي إذا جدّ جدهم ... وفي الليلة الظّلماء يفتقد البدر
(My people will remember me when their earnestness is earnest, and in the dark night the full moon is missed.)
Abū l-Ṭayyib has a short poem which came in the pattern of the rational trope, and it is among the fine poetry:
صحب الناس قبلنا ذا الزمانا ... وعناهم من أمره ما عنانا
وتولوا بغصّة كلّهم منه وإن سرّ بعضهم أحيانا ربما تحسن الصّنيع لياليه ولكن تكدّر الإحسانا
كلما أنبت الزمان قناة ... ركب المرء في القناة سنانا
(People kept company with this age before us, and what concerned us of its affairs concerned them. All of them departed from it with a lump in the throat, though it pleased some of them at times. Perhaps its nights do good, but they sully the good done. Whenever time grows a spear-shaft, a man fixes a spearhead on that shaft.)
[Translator's note: the second couplet is printed in the source as one run of text, without the usual division into hemistichs; it is rendered here as printed.]

* Benefits:
The prepositional "min" is added with the fāʿil, the mafʿūl bihi and the mubtadaʾ, on condition that it is preceded by a negation, prohibition or interrogative, and that the noun it governs is indefinite; in that case the addition is regular. More examples of it will come.

dervis-irab:203-203.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تُحْشَرُونَ): you are gathered. When the letters ḥāʾ and shīn occur as the first and second radicals of a word they indicate the meaning of gathering, filling and mustering; this is what we have investigated, and for it we mustered everything our hands could reach of the sources and lengthy reference works of the language. From it come "al-ḥashshāsh", i.e. the gatherer of grass or the buyer of hashish, which is a plant from which an intoxicating substance is extracted; and "al-ḥishma", which is modesty, and it indicates that a person collects himself lest some slip escape him. From it also come "al-ḥasham", i.e. the servants gathered together.

* I'rab:
(وَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ) The wāw is a conjunction; "udhkurū" is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and "Allāh" is mafʿūl bihi. (فِي أَيَّامٍ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to "udhkurū". (مَعْدُوداتٍ) ṣifa of "ayyām"; these are the three days of al-tashrīq, which are three days after the Day of Sacrifice, which is the view of al-Shāfiʿī, or the Day of Sacrifice and two days after it, which is the view of Abū Ḥanīfa. (فَمَنْ) The fāʾ is resumptive and "man" is conditional, a mubtadaʾ. (تَعَجَّلَ) a past verb in the position of a jussive, the protasis. (فِي يَوْمَيْنِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to "taʿajjala". (فَلا إِثْمَ) The fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ; "lā" is the lā of generic negation, and "ithm" is its ism, indeclinable on fatḥa. (عَلَيْهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of "lā"; the clause joined with the fāʾ is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of "man". (وَمَنْ تَأَخَّرَ فَلا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ) its i'rab has preceded, and the clause is conjoined. (لِمَنِ اتَّقى) The lām is a preposition, "man" is a relative noun in the position of genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "that option"; the negation of sin for the one who hastens and the one who delays is for the one who has been pious. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ) The wāw is a conjunction; "ittaqū" is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi. (وَاعْلَمُوا) conjoined to "ittaqū". (أَنَّكُمْ) "anna" and its ism. (إِلَيْهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to "tuḥsharūna". (تُحْشَرُونَ) an imperfect verb with its fāʿil (deputy agent); the verbal clause is the khabar of "anna"; "anna" and what follows it are in the interpretation of a maṣdar standing in the place of the two objects of "iʿlamū".
[Translator's note: the source says "fāʿil" for the wāw of the passive verb «تُحْشَرُونَ»; it is rendered as written, with "(deputy agent)" added for clarity.]

dervis-irab:204-206.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَلَدُّ الْخِصامِ): "aladd" is an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha), and "ladad" is intensity of disputation. One says "I left so-and-so yataladdad", i.e. looking about to the right and left in his bewilderment, unable to settle in any state; it is thus a word in motion that depicts a composite image. "Al-khiṣām" is the maṣdar of "khāṣama", as al-Khalīl said; and al-Zajjāj said: "al-Khiṣām" is the plural of "khaṣm", like "ṣaʿb, ṣiʿāb" and "ḍakhm, ḍikhām".

* I'rab:
(وَمِنَ النَّاسِ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; the clause is linked to the clause «فمن الناس» etc. (مِنَ) a relative noun, postponed mubtadaʾ. (يُعْجِبُكَ قَوْلُهُ) an imperfect verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi and a postponed fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative. (فِي الْحَياةِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «قوله» or to «يعجبك»; on the first, the speech issues in this life; on the second, the admiration arises in it. (الدُّنْيا) ṣifa of "al-ḥayāh". (وَيُشْهِدُ) The wāw is resumptive or a conjunction; "yushhidu" is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, the implied form being "huwa". (اللَّهَ) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi. (عَلى ما) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to "yushhidu". (فِي قَلْبِهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative, i.e. of what the speech signifies. (وَهُوَ) The wāw is circumstantial and "huwa" is a mubtadaʾ. (أَلَدُّ الْخِصامِ) khabar. (وَإِذا) The wāw is a conjunction and "idhā" is an adverb for what is to come of time, attached to the apodosis. (تَوَلَّى) a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, the implied form being "huwa"; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation. (سَعى) a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, the implied form being "huwa"; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. (فِي الْأَرْضِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to "saʿā". (لِيُفْسِدَ فِيها) The lām is causal and "yufsida" is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied "an" after the causal lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to "yufsida". (وَيُهْلِكَ الْحَرْثَ وَالنَّسْلَ) conjoined to «ليفسد». (وَاللَّهُ) The wāw is resumptive and "Allāh" is a mubtadaʾ. (لا) negative. (يُحِبُّ الْفَسادَ) an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, the implied form being "huwa", i.e. Allah the Exalted, and "al-fasād" is mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of "Allāh". (وَإِذا قِيلَ) The wāw is a conjunction to His saying «يعجبك», and you may make it resumptive; "idhā" is an adverb for what is to come of time, and the clause "qīla" is in the position of genitive by annexation. (لَهُ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to "qīla". (اتَّقِ اللَّهَ) "ittaqi" is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the weak letter, its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, the implied form being "anta", and the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (أَخَذَتْهُ الْعِزَّةُ) a past verb with the quiescent feminine tāʾ, the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi and "al-ʿizza" is its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. (بِالْإِثْمِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "accompanied", the bāʾ being that of accompaniment.
It is also permissible that they be attached to «أخذته», in which case the bāʾ is merely for transitivity. (فَحَسْبُهُ جَهَنَّمُ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, as if he answered about his destiny; "ḥasbuhu" is a fronted khabar and "Jahannam" a postponed mubtadaʾ. (وَلَبِئْسَ الْمِهادُ) The wāw is the wāw of oath, and the lām falls in the answer to the oath, i.e. "by Allah"; "biʾsa" is a past, non-conjugating verb to express blame, "al-mihād" is its fāʿil, and the one specified for blame is omitted, i.e. "it"; the clause is the answer to an oath and has no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:42-43.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَلا تَلْبِسُوا): it is said لبست الشيء بالشيء: I mixed it with it; and the maṣdar is اللّبس, with the fatḥa on the lām (and the lām being doubled in pronunciation as in the printed form).

* I'rab:
(وَلا تَلْبِسُوا) The wāw is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, and تلبسوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, its sign of jussion being the omission of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الْحَقَّ) direct object. (بِالْباطِلِ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to تلبسوا; the bāʾ is for association (mulābasa) or for instrumentality. (وَتَكْتُمُوا): the wāw is a conjunction, and تكتموا is an imperfect verb jussive, conjoined to تلبسوا and coming under the ruling of the prohibition; you may also make the wāw one of accompaniment (maʿiyya), in which case تكتموا is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after it, preceded as it is by a prohibition. (الْحَقَّ) direct object. (وَأَنْتُمْ) The wāw is circumstantial, and أنتم is a detached pronoun in the nominative position as mubtadaʾ. (تَعْلَمُونَ) an imperfect verb, nominative by the presence of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil; the verbal clause تعلمون is the khabar of أنتم, and the nominal clause وأنتم تعلمون is circumstantial. (وَأَقِيمُوا) The wāw is a conjunction, and أقيموا is an imperative verb, indeclinable with the omission of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil. (الصَّلاةَ) direct object. (وَآتُوا الزَّكاةَ) conjoined to أقيموا الصلاة. (وَارْكَعُوا) likewise a conjunction. (مَعَ) an adverb of place attached to اركعوا. (الرَّاكِعِينَ) muḍāf ilayhi.

dervis-irab:44-46.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بِالْبِرِّ): البر with the kasra on the bāʾ means kindness (ṣila), obedience, righteousness and truthfulness; البر with the fatḥa on the bāʾ is the open land; and البر with its ḍamma is wheat, the single grain being برّة.
(الْخاشِعِينَ): al-khushūʿ is submission and abasement; of the figurative uses of this root are أرض خاشعة, i.e. a low-lying land, and خشعت الجبال, and خشعت دونه الابصار (eyes were lowered before him).

* I'rab:
(أَتَأْمُرُونَ) The hamza is for a disapproving question (istifhām inkārī); rather, the disapproval here passes on to rebuke, reproach and astonishment at the state of these Jews, for there is nothing uglier to the mind than that a person command another to good while he does not do it himself. تأمرون is an imperfect verb, nominative by the presence of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil. (النَّاسَ) direct object. (بِالْبِرِّ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to تأمرون. (وَتَنْسَوْنَ) conjoined to تأمرون. (أَنْفُسَكُمْ) direct object. (وَأَنْتُمْ) The wāw is the wāw of ḥāl, and أنتم is a detached pronoun in the nominative position as mubtadaʾ. (تَتْلُونَ) an imperfect verb, nominative by the presence of the nūn; the verbal clause تتلون is the khabar of أنتم, and the nominal clause وأنتم is circumstantial, from the fāʿil of تنسون. (الْكِتابَ) direct object. (أَفَلا) The hamza is for a disapproving question, the fāʾ is a conjunction, and لا is negative. (تَعْقِلُونَ) an imperfect verb, nominative by the presence of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil; the secret of this construction will come.
(وَاسْتَعِينُوا) conjoined to what preceded. (بِالصَّبْرِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استعينوا. (وَالصَّلاةِ) conjoined to الصبر. (وَإِنَّها) The wāw is circumstantial, and inna with its ism. (لَكَبِيرَةٌ) the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and كبيرة is the khabar of inna. (إِلَّا) a particle of restriction. (عَلَى الْخاشِعِينَ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to كبيرة; it is a freed exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh), because what precedes إلا contains nothing attached to كبيرة from which an exception could be made; it is like your saying "it is hard on me"; and because the speech is interpreted as a negation, i.e. "it is not light and not easy except for the humble"; so take note of this, for it is one of the subtleties. (الَّذِينَ) a relative noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the genitive position as adjective of الخاشعين. (يَظُنُّونَ) an imperfect verb, nominative by the presence of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil; the clause has no position because it is a ṣila of the relative. (أَنَّهُمْ) anna with its ism. (مُلاقُوا) its khabar. (رَبِّهِمْ) muḍāf ilayhi; and anna with what is within its scope fills the place of the two objects of يظنون. (وَأَنَّهُمْ) conjoined to أنهم. (إِلَيْهِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to راجعون. (راجِعُونَ) khabar of أنهم.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying: وأنتم تتلون الكتاب the speech is headed with the pronoun for added emphasis and to record the rebuke and reproach against them, after their leaving of doing righteousness was expressed as "forgetting", to add emphasis to the abandonment, that is, as if righteousness never stirred in their souls and never crossed their minds; because forgetting a thing results in leaving it, or it uses the cause for the effect.

* Benefits:
1- The rule in Arabic is that the pronoun of the third person does not refer to anything other than the nearest antecedent except by evidence. The apparent requirement was that the pronoun in His saying انها refer to الصلاة because it is the nearest, following the apparent requirement; and the khabar of the first was withheld because the addressee knows that the first is included implicitly in what the other is included in, and this is regular in their speech. al-Anṣārī said:
نحن بما عندنا وأنت بما ... عندك راض والأمر مختلف
(We are, with what we have, and you with what you have, content; and the matter differs.)
He meant "we are content, and you are content with what you have", so he withheld the khabar of the first since evidence stands for its meaning. Of this is the saying of another:
إن شرخ الشباب والشعر الأسود ما لم يعاص كان جنونا
(Indeed the prime of youth and black hair, if not disobeyed, is madness.)
It was also said that it refers to the maṣdar understood from His saying واستعينوا, i.e. seeking help.
2- When the interrogative hamza and a conjunction meet, there are two schools:
a- The school of Sībawayh: the hamza is intended to come after the conjunction, but since it has the head of the speech it was put before it; this differs from هل.
b- The school of al-Zamakhsharī: the wāw, fāʾ and thumma after the hamza stand in their own place and there is no advancing or delaying; he places between the hamza and the conjunction an implied clause upon which the conjunction can be made, and which suits the context. Here he implies: "Do you act, and then not reason?" We see nothing to prefer one school over the other.
3- The shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa): it is the lām of inceptive (lām al-ibtidāʾ) that was shifted to the khabar because inna entered upon it; it may also be shifted to the ism, for example: «إن من الشعر لحكمة وإن من البيان لسحرا» (Indeed some poetry is wisdom, and some eloquence is sorcery).

dervis-irab:47-48.t:
* Vocabulary:
(عَدْلٌ) with the fatḥa on the ʿayn: it is the ransom, because it is equivalent to the one ransomed in value and worth even if not of its kind; and with the kasra on the ʿayn it is what is equal in kind and body. It is said ʿadl and ʿadīl.

* I'rab:
(يا) a vocative particle for a mid-distance addressee. (بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ) an annexed vocative; it was discussed shortly before. (اذْكُرُوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable with the omission of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil. (نِعْمَتِيَ) direct object. (الَّتِي) a relative noun in the accusative position as adjective of نعمتي. (أَنْعَمْتُ) verb and fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila of the relative. (عَلَيْكُمْ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنعمت. This sentence came before in its very text, and was repeated only for emphasis, for "striking the staff", and to alert their minds, dulled against hearing good. (وَأَنِّي) The wāw is a conjunction, and anna with its ism is conjoined to نعمتي, so it is in the accusative position; for that reason its hamza has the fatḥa. (فَضَّلْتُكُمْ) the clause is in the nominative position as the khabar of أني. (عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to فضّلتكم; the al in العالمين is for a specific reference (ʿahd), not for the genus, so that it would not be necessary to hold that they were preferred over all people; what is meant is over the worlds of their time. (وَاتَّقُوا) The wāw is a conjunction, and اتقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable with the omission of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil. (يَوْماً) direct object with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the punishment of a day" or "the terror of a day"; its accusative may also be as an adverb (ẓarf), with the direct object omitted, its implied form being "fear the punishment on a day". (لا) negative. (تَجْزِي) an imperfect verb. (نَفْسٌ) fāʿil of تجزي; the verbal clause is in the accusative position as adjective of يوما. (عَنْ نَفْسٍ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to تجزي. (شَيْئاً) direct object; its accusative may also be as a maṣdar, i.e. "does not compensate any compensation", and in it is an indication of fewness and slightness. (وَلا) The wāw is a conjunction, and لا is negative. (يُقْبَلُ) a passive imperfect verb. (مِنْها) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يقبل. (شَفاعَةٌ) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (وَلا) conjoined to what preceded. (يُؤْخَذُ) a passive imperfect verb. (مِنْها) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يؤخذ. (عَدْلٌ) nāʾib fāʿil. (وَلا) likewise a conjunction. (هُمْ) a detached pronoun in the nominative position as mubtadaʾ. (يُنْصَرُونَ) a passive imperfect verb, the wāw an attached pronoun in the nominative position as nāʾib fāʿil; the verbal clause is their khabar.

* Rhetoric:
He brought the last conjoined clause, «ولا هم ينصرون», as a nominal clause although the clauses before it are verbal, for emphasis and to indicate fixity and permanence, i.e. that they are never to be helped, and no account is to be taken of any temporary success they may meet.

dervis-irab:23-24.t:
* Vocabulary:
(السورة) a portion of the Qur'an of which the least is three verses; among its meanings is a lofty rank. Al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī said:
ألم تر أنّ الله أعطاك سورة ... ترى كلّ ملك دونها يتذبذب
(Do you not see that Allah gave you a rank, beside which you see every king wavering?)
(وَقُودُهَا) with fatḥa on the wāw: it is what a fire is kindled with, of firewood and the like. With ḍamma it is a maṣdar of waqada ("it blazed"). The same is said of what comes on this pattern, such as al-waḍūʾ, al-ṭahūr and al-saḥūr.

* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ) the wāw is resumptive; the speech is resumptive, brought to answer those who doubted the Qur'an out of obstinacy and contentiousness. إن is conditional, jussing two verbs. (كُنْتُمْ) كان is a defective past verb, the tāʾ its ism; the defective verb is in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). (فِي رَيْبٍ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of كنتم. (مِمَّا) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of ريب, and ما is a relative. (نَزَّلْنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, and نا is a pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil; the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (عَلى عَبْدِنا) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نزلنا; the returning pronoun is omitted, that is, "We sent it down gradually". He did not say أنزلناه because the Qur'an was sent down in instalments, by gradual stages. (فَأْتُوا) the fāʾ links the apodosis, because the clause is a request and cannot serve as a condition; أتوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn because its imperfect is one of the "five verbs", and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis. (بِسُورَةٍ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أتوا. (مِنْ مِثْلِهِ) attached according to what the pronoun returns to. It either returns to the Qur'an, in which case they are attached to an omitted adjective of سورة, or it returns to عبدنا, in which case they are attached to His words فأتوا. The meaning on the first view covers several matters:
a- "Bring a sura like it" in the beauty of its composition, the marvel of its description, and the splendour and concision of its style.
b- "Bring a sura like it" in the unseen character of its reports and its accounts of earlier peoples and of what will be.
c- "Bring a sura like it" in what it contains of command and prohibition, promise and threat, glad tidings and warning, rulings and parables.
d- "Bring a sura like it" in its truthfulness and its protection from distortion and alteration, and its other distinguishing features.
e- "Bring a sura like it" in its far-reaching implications, its rulings that keep pace with the developments of the ages and the progress of the sciences, and its accompaniment of human civilization in its various circumstances and states.
The meaning on the second view also covers several matters:
a- "Bring one like the Messenger", that is, from an unlettered man (ummī) who cannot write, in his original natural state.
b- "Bring one like the Messenger", that is, from a messenger who did not study with scholars, did not sit with the wise, did not busy himself with the reports of the ancients, and who was never reported to have done any of that in any circumstance.
c- "Bring one like the Messenger", that is, from any man, even as you suppose in your claim that he is a poet or a madman. Both meanings, as you see, are fine and beautiful.
(وَادْعُوا) conjoined to His words فأتوا, and the wāw is fāʿil. (شُهَداءَكُمْ) mafʿūl bihi of ادعوا, and the kāf is in the position of genitive as the second term of the construct. (مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ادعوا, and the meaning is "and call, apart from Allah, your witnesses". The shuhadāʾ are either the plural of shahīd, for intensiveness, like ʿalīm and ʿulamāʾ, or the plural of shāhid, like shāʿir and shuʿarāʾ. It is also possible that they are attached to an omitted ḥāl of His words شهداءكم, the implied form being "being separate from Allah the Exalted" or "being different from Allah". (إِنْ) conditional; see an important discussion of it in the Benefits section. (كُنْتُمْ) كان is a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis, and the tāʾ is its ism. (صادِقِينَ) its khabar; the apodosis is omitted, that is, "then do that". (فَإِنْ) the fāʾ is resumptive and إن is conditional. (لَمْ) a particle of negation, reversal (of tense) and jussive. (تَفْعَلُوا) an imperfect verb, jussive by لم, its sign of jussive being the omission of the nūn. (وَلَنْ) the wāw is parenthetical and لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity. (تَفْعَلُوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by لن, its sign of accusative being the omission of the nūn; the clause has no grammatical position because it is parenthetical between the condition and its apodosis. (فَاتَّقُوا) the fāʾ links the apodosis, and اتقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil. (النَّارَ) mafʿūl bihi. (الَّتِي) a relative noun in the position of accusative as an adjective of النار. (وَقُودُهَا) a nominative mubtadaʾ, and the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of genitive as the second term of the construct. (النَّاسُ) khabar. (وَالْحِجارَةُ) conjoined to الناس; the nominal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (أُعِدَّتْ) a past passive verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent pronoun (permissibly latent), its implied form being "it". (لِلْكافِرِينَ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أعدت; the verbal clause is in the position of accusative as an inseparable (lāzima) ḥāl of النار. We said "inseparable" in reply to some parsers such as Abū Ḥayyān and Ibn ʿAṭiyya, who made the clause resumptive to avoid making it a ḥāl of النار, because the meaning would become "fear the Fire in the state of its being prepared for the disbelievers", whereas it is prepared for them whether they fear it or not. But adding "inseparable" averts this suspicion.

* Rhetoric:
1- Brevity by condensation (ījāz al-qiṣar) in His words: «فاتقوا النار». Ījāz is the gathering of many meanings under few words with clarity and eloquence.
2- Brevity by omission (ījāz al-ḥadhf) in His words «فاتقوا النار» as well. Ījāz by omission is by omitting a word, a clause or more, with a clue that identifies what is omitted, because whoever guards himself against the Fire protects himself from all the destructive sins, whose enumeration would be long, and abandons arrogance and obstinacy.
3- The parenthetical interjection (iʿtirāḍ): in His words: «ولن تفعلوا». It occurs in speech for many purposes, and the purpose here is emphasis that this is not possible for them, however much they strive and their efforts combine for it. Among its marvels is the saying of ʿAwf ibn Muḥallim al-Khuzāʿī:
إن الثمانين، وبلغتها، ... قد أحوجت سمعي إلى ترجمان
(Indeed the eighty years, and may you reach them, have made my hearing need an interpreter.) His words "and may you reach them" are a parenthetical between the ism of إن and its khabar; its benefit is to pray that the addressee's life extend to eighty, while disclaiming responsibility for not hearing because of old age and the heaviness of hearing. And the saying of al-Mutanabbī is exceedingly beautiful:
وخفوق قلب لو رأيت جحيمه- يا جنّتي- لظننت فيه جهنّما
(And the throbbing of a heart, if you saw its blaze, O my paradise, you would think hell was in it.) The parenthetical is in his words "O my paradise". And the saying of Abū Nuwās, who had fallen in love with al-Amīn:
قد هام قلبي ولا أقول بمن ... أخاف من لا يخاف من أحد
إذا تفكّرت في هواي له ... مسست رأسي هل طار عن جسدي؟
إني- على ما ذكرت من فرقي- لآمل أن أناله بيدي
(My heart has gone wild, and I will not say for whom: I fear one who fears no one. When I think of my love for him, I touch my head to see whether it has flown from my body. Yet, despite the fear I mentioned, I hope to reach him with my hand.) The parenthetical is in his words "despite the fear I mentioned", and in it is a beauty that cannot be fathomed.

* Benefits:
1- The failure of attempts at the challenge: the Qur'an called on Quraysh to try to imitate the Qur'an, as a challenge to them, in many places, the most prominent being the verse before us. It appears that they tried to answer this challenge but were unable in the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, and the desire to imitate the Qur'an did not cease after his life. Musaylima the Liar, who appeared in al-Yamāma among the Banū Ḥanīfa, tried; so did Ṭulayḥa ibn Khuwaylid, who claimed prophethood among the Banū Asad, al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī, who claimed prophethood in Yemen, and Sajāḥ, who appeared among the Banū Taghlib. There is no way to be certain that the speech these people brought is truly attributed to them; rather, we think it likelier that it comes from the imagination of later storytellers. Among this feeble speech attributed to Musaylima is that he used to say: «O frog, daughter of two frogs, clean what you clean; half of you is in the water and half in the mud; you neither disturb the water nor keep the drinker away». It is perfectly clear that this nonsense is in no way from the language of the pre-Islamic Arabs, yet al-Jāḥiẓ was deceived by it, or else was mocking it when he said: «I do not know what provoked Musaylima so that his opinion of the frog turned bad». As for the revelation of al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī, as he says, an angel whom he named Dhū Ḍimār used to bring it down to him, by his claim; he was an eloquent man who was skilled in the rhymed prose of the soothsayers, but his speech has been lost and nothing of it has reached us. As for the revelation of Ṭalḥa [Translator's note: the source writes Ṭulayḥa above and Ṭalḥa here], an angel whom he named Dhū al-Nūn used to bring it down to him, as he claims; then he turned from Dhū al-Nūn and said, "No, it is Jibrīl". Nothing is known of his alleged Qur'an. As for Sajāḥ, she claimed a Qur'an, but her revelation fell silent when she met Musaylima and married him in that lewd and ridiculous marriage whose shameful details the books of literature and history relate. Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya and al-Bāqillānī mentioned that when ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Muqaffaʿ reached His words «حتى إذا جاء أمرنا وفار التنور» to His words «وقيل بعدا للقوم الظالمين», he abandoned composing his Qur'an and said, "Humans cannot produce the like of this", and gave up the rivalry and burned what he had fabricated. Al-Bāqillānī says that some people claimed that Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ rivalled the Qur'an in his book «al-Durra al-Yatīma», but nothing in what Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ composed in that book could be considered an imitation of the Qur'an.
Our great poet Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī, as the narrators say, claimed prophethood in the desert of al-Samāwa and composed speech which he called a Qur'an, among which are his words: «By the travelling star, the revolving sphere, the night and the day, the disbelievers are in peril. Go on in your way, and follow those messengers who came before you, for Allah will crush through you the deviation of whoever is heretical in his religion and strays from His path». But al-Mutanabbī abandoned this attempt. We, however, doubt these reports greatly, because al-Mutanabbī was too sensible to attribute such nonsense to himself, and for other reasons that cannot be discussed now.
Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī was also accused of this charge in his book «al-Fuṣūl wa-l-Ghāyāt fī Muḥādhāt al-Suwar wa-l-Āyāt». Among what is in that book: «Glory to You, Eternal of eternities! Does death have kinship with sleep? When I wake I picture none of the dead; when I doze, one newly dead meets me, and one I lost long ago. I ask them and they answer, I converse with them and they speak, as though they were suspended by the rope of life. If sleep were truthful, I would rest content with what the dwellers of the graves tell, but dozing is very false». Muṣṭafā Ṣādiq al-Rāfiʿī, among our modern men of letters, stated in his delightful book «Iʿjāz al-Qur'an» what he wrote: «This, without doubt, is a slander against al-Maʿarrī which a skilled enemy wanted for him, since the man was better acquainted with himself and with the rank of the speech he is said to rival». As for Dr. Ṭāhā Ḥusayn, he mentioned in his book «Maʿa Abī al-ʿAlāʾ fī Sijnihi» what amounts to this: Did Abū al-ʿAlāʾ intend to rival the Qur'an in al-Fuṣūl wa-l-Ghāyāt, as some of the ancients thought? Yes and no. Yes, if we understand by rivalry merely influence and imitation; and no, if we understand by rivalry that Abū al-ʿAlāʾ regarded the Qur'an as a supreme model in literary art, was influenced by it, and strove to imitate it, as every writer is influenced by the supreme artistic models he admires. That is something beyond doubt, for the slightest glance at the book al-Fuṣūl wa-l-Ghāyāt makes you feel that Abū al-ʿAlāʾ tried to imitate the short suras and the long. What matters is not whether he succeeded in this imitation or not; rather it is certain that success was not decreed for him, as it was not for anyone else.
2- The grammarians and the scholars of legal theory stated that conditional إن is made to govern only what is doubtful. So you do not say "If the sun sets I will come to you" but rather "When the sun sets I will come to you", while إن governs both what is doubtful and what is known. Doubt is impossible for Allah, so how did it come here? The answer is that the divine attributes do not enter into the conventions of Arabic, which are built on the attributes of creatures; and this is put in the position of their speech among themselves, as if it were said: "The custom among people is doubt about the matter of the Deity, the Messenger and the Return, and it is not that which is settled with certainty in the mind except after investigation and the establishment of proofs."

dervis-irab:1-5.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الم): the letters with which many sūras begin are, in all likelihood, names of the sūras they open. As to their nature and the wisdom behind them, opinions differ and aims diverge, so that it is difficult for the researcher, if we do not say impossible, to exhaust them. We can classify these opinions into two kinds:
1- That they belong to the ambiguous (mutashābih), the matter of which we leave to Allah; and we are satisfied with what satisfied the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and their Successors. These said: it is no part of religion for someone given to affectation to invent whatever reasons he wishes, whose inventor rarely escapes error.
2- That they are like the rest of the speech in the Qur'an, so we must speak of them, probe their depths and plumb the meanings folded within them, acting on the saying of the Exalted: «أفلا يتدبرون القرآن»? According to this opinion we favour that their meaning is challenge (taḥaddī) and a presage that this Qur'an is composed of the very letters with which the Arabs compose their poems and put together their sermons and rhymed prose, and that they are nevertheless unable to produce its like or imitate it. This is an interpretation consistent with the inimitability (iʿjāz) of the Qur'an by which it is distinguished. The Encyclopaedia of Islam, in its article on the Qur'an, says what amounts to this: the scholars have laboured much to understand the intent of these letters. These letters occur in twenty-nine sūras, all of them Meccan except the openings of Sūrat al-Baqara and Sūrat Āl ʿImrān, which belong to the Medinan period, and the total number of different letters repeated in these openings is fourteen.
We admired a study written by Dr. Zakī Mubārak in his book "al-Nathr al-Fannī" and wished to quote from it what is pleasing. The author of al-Nathr al-Fannī said, in summary: I was talking about the openings of the sūras with Monsieur Blachère, and he presented to me a new interpretation worthy of consideration, worthy of study and verification, the gist of which is:
that the letters الم, الر, حم, طسم are the letters: [Translator's note: the source text here is garbled and incomplete («الحروف:.. التي توجد في بعض المواطن من:-»); it is translated as far as it is intelligible] which are found in some places of: they are nothing but signs and musical indications, whose melodies are indicated by one, two or three letters, so they are vocal symbols. It is not unlikely, then, that the openings of the sūras are vocal signs to guide the recitation. Perhaps what Dr. Zakī Mubārak adduced is connected, closely or remotely, with what we have given of the meaning of challenge and of rapping the staff at the obstinate, who probed the depths of the Qur'an and perceived by their rhetorical instinct the eloquence by which it is distinguished. Al-Suyūṭī, in his delightful book al-Itqān, has an opinion supporting what we have held, for he said: the intention was to take the Arabs, who are the people of eloquence and rhetoric, by surprise with symbols and signs with which they had no familiarity, so that their attention would increase and their minds and souls be alerted.
(رَيْبَ): rayb is doubt and the disquiet and agitation of the soul. In the ḥadīth: «دع ما يريبك إلى ما لا يريبك» ("Leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt"). Now rayb has three meanings in the language: the first is doubt, and this is what is meant here; the second is suspicion; Jamīl said:
بثينة قالت: يا جميل اربتني ... فقلت: كلانا يا بثين ريب
(Buthayna said: "O Jamīl, you have made me suspicious." I said: "We are both, O Buthayna, objects of suspicion.")
and the third is need. He said:
قضينا من تهامة كل ريب ... وخيبر ثم أجمعنا السيوفا
(We fulfilled every need in Tihāma and Khaybar, then we gathered up the swords.)
(يُنْفِقُونَ): nafaqa al-shayʾ and nafada mean the same. Everything that comes with nūn as first radical and fāʾ as second indicates the sense of exhaustion, going out and departing. One says nafatha al-shayʾa min fīhi: he threw it out of his mouth; and nafatha fī al-ʿuqad (he blew on the knots). Among their sayings are «لا بد للمصدور أن ينفث» ("the one with a chest ailment must expectorate") and «هذه نفثة مصدور» ("this is the expectoration of a chest-sufferer"). Nafaqa al-ḥimār: the donkey died. A full account of this chapter is more than the scope of this book can hold, and it is one of the marvels by which our noble language is distinguished; you will meet many like it in this wonderful book. (الْمُفْلِحُونَ): those who attain their desire, before whom the faces of victory have opened. Everything that comes with fāʾ as first radical and lām as second indicates the sense of opening and splitting, such as falaqa and falaḥa.

* I'rab:
(الم): a word whose wording is intended and not its meaning, in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "this is Alif Lām Mīm". (ذلِكَ): a demonstrative in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ; the lām is for distance and the kāf for address. (الْكِتابُ): the khabar of «ذلك». This is preferable to making it a substitute for the demonstrative, because what is intended is to inform that it is the holy Book, deserving this name, to reinforce the challenge. The clause is inceptive and has no grammatical position; though it is permissible to make it a substitute for the demonstrative, in which case the clause «لا ريب فيه» is a khabar for the demonstrative. (لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ): lā is the lā of generic negation, and «ريب» is its noun, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of accusative as the noun of lā; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element which is its khabar. The clause is a khabar for «ذلك», or a ḥāl from «الكتاب». (هُدىً): a third khabar of «ذلك». (لِلْمُتَّقِينَ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «هدى», because it is a maṣdar; and you may make it an adjective of «هدى». (الَّذِينَ): a relative noun in the position of genitive, an adjective of «المتقين». (يُؤْمِنُونَ): a nominative imperfect verb, the sign of its nominative case being the retention of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs; and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative, an agent. The verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative. (بِالْغَيْبِ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يؤمنون». (وَيُقِيمُونَ): the clause is conjoined to the clause «يؤمنون», entering within the scope of the ṣila. (الصَّلاةَ): direct object. (وَمِمَّا): the wāw is a conjunction, and «مما» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «ينفقون». (رَزَقْناهُمْ): a past verb, an agent and a direct object; the clause «رزقناهم» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of «ما», and the returning pronoun is omitted, that is, "We provided them with it". (يُنْفِقُونَ): a nominative imperfect verb conjoined to «يقيمون», entering within the scope of the ṣila as well. (وَالَّذِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction, and the relative noun is conjoined to the first relative, included with it in the string of the God-fearing. (يُؤْمِنُونَ): a nominative imperfect verb, the wāw an agent; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative. (بِما): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يؤمنون». (أُنْزِلَ): a passive past verb, its deputy agent a latent pronoun implied in it, its implied form being "he", referring to «ما», that is, the Qur'an; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative. (إِلَيْكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «أنزل». (وَما): the wāw is a conjunction, and «ما» is conjoined to «بما أنزل إليك», and the clause (أُنْزِلَ) has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative. (مِنْ قَبْلِكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element, a ḥāl; this is preferable to attaching them to «أنزل». (وَبِالْآخِرَةِ): the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يوقنون». (هُمْ): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ. (يُوقِنُونَ): a nominative imperfect verb, the wāw its agent; the nominal clause is conjoined to the verbal clause, namely «ومما رزقناهم ينفقون», and the secret of the difference between the two clauses will come in the section on rhetoric. (أُولئِكَ): a demonstrative indeclinable on kasra, in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ; the kāf is for address. (عَلى هُدىً): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of «أولئك». (مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element, an adjective of «هدى»; and the clause is resumptive and has no position. (وَأُولئِكَ هُمُ): «أولئك» is mubtadaʾ, and «هم» is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or support (ʿimād), with no position. (الْمُفْلِحُونَ): the khabar of «أولئك»; and you may parse «هم» as mubtadaʾ and «المفلحون» as its khabar, the nominal clause being the khabar of «أولئك».

* Rhetoric:
In these verses are several arts, which we set out below:
1- Definiteness: in making «الكتاب» definite by the alif and lām, to magnify its matter; and it is originally a maṣdar. The Exalted said: «كتاب الله عليكم».
2- Fronting: «الريب» was put before the preposition and its genitive noun because it is more apt to be mentioned, in readiness for its picture, so that it becomes embodied before the hearer.
3- Putting the maṣdar «هدى» in place of the derived adjective hādin, which goes further in expressing its permanence and continuity.
4- Free trope (majāz mursal): in the saying «هدى للمتقين», its relation being consideration of what it will become, that is, those who will come to piety (taqwā).
5- Concision: in mentioning «المتقين», because wiqāya (guarding) is a comprehensive name for everything against which one must guard.
6- Explicit metaphor of the subordinate kind (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tabaʿiyya) in the saying «على هدى»: the condition of the God-fearing is likened to the condition of one who has mounted the back of his horse; the thing likened was dropped and the word «على», indicating being above, was borrowed to show that something rises above and tops what follows it, either in reality, as in "Zayd is on the roof", or in judgement, as in «عليه دين» ("he has a debt"): the debt, because of its binding nature and his bearing it, is as if he were riding on it and carrying it. The subtlety in it is that the metaphor is by means of a particle, and in carrying it out it is said: a mere connection between guidance and the guided is likened to a mere connection between one who is above and that which is above him, on the ground of firm position in each; so the likening passed from universals to particulars; then «على», which is one of the particulars of the thing likened to, was borrowed for a particular of the particulars of the thing likened, by way of the explicit subordinate metaphor. Like the noble verse is the saying:
لسنا وإن أحسابنا كرمت ... يوما على الآباء نتكل
(Even though our lineages are noble, we do not, one day, rely on our fathers.)
So consider this discussion, for it is of such subtlety and beauty; and examples of it will occur in the Noble Qur'an, like lawful magic.
7- Repetition: in the saying «يؤمنون بالغيب» and «يؤمنون بما انزل إليك», and in the repetition of the relative noun even though the one described is one; the one described may also be different, so it is repetition of the wording without the meaning. Its benefit is fixing it in the mind and affecting the emotions, and it is frequent in poetry.
8- Omission: in the saying «الم», meaning "this is Alif Lām Mīm", and «هدى», meaning "it is guidance", the mubtadaʾ being omitted; and in the saying «ينفقون», meaning "wealth", the direct object being omitted. Spending in the way of praiseworthy deeds and noble acts has enthralled the souls of the Arab poets; how beautiful is the saying of Diʿbil:
قالت سلامة: اين المال؟ قلت لها: ... المال ويحك لاقى الحمد فاصطحبا
(Salāma said: "Where is the wealth?" I said to her: "The wealth, woe to you, met praise and they went off together.")
9- Fine division (ḥusn al-taqsīm), an art of rhetoric whose gist is that the speaker comprehends all the divisions of the meaning he is engaged in, leaving nothing of it behind. These verses comprehended all the praiseworthy attributes and the acts of worship to which the believers devote themselves, because acts of worship are all confined to two types: bodily and financial, and both must be fulfilled for all acts of worship to be accepted. How beautiful is the noble ḥadīth saying: «يقول العبد مالي مالي وإنما له من ماله ثلاث: ما أكل فأفنى، أو لبس فأبلى أو أعطى فاقتنى، وما سوى ذلك فهو ذاهب وتاركه للناس» ("The servant says: 'My wealth, my wealth,' but he has of his wealth only three: what he ate and consumed, or wore and wore out, or gave and thereby acquired; and whatever is besides that is going away and he leaves it to the people"). His saying «مالي مالي» is a direct object of an omitted verb, that is, "I love my wealth", and the second is emphasis of the first.

dervis-irab:78-79.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أُمِّيُّونَ): those who cannot write or read well. The singular is ummī, related either to the mother (umm), because writing is not the work of women among them; or to the umma, meaning stature and creation, as if the one who neither writes nor reads stands on his natural disposition and constitution; or to the umma (community), because it is simple before it comes to know the branches of knowledge. [Translator's note: the source prints «شعل النساء»; «شغل» (work/occupation) appears to be meant, and it is translated accordingly.]
(أَمانِيَّ): the plural of umniyya, with the yāʾ doubled or lightened. Originally it is what a person estimates within himself and guesses at, and for that reason it is applied to falsehood. The meaning is that they do not know the Book except as they have guessed or imagined in their inner fancies: that they are God's chosen people, that Allah will pardon them, and that their forefathers the prophets will intercede for them; all of which is nothing but embellished lies that their rabbis fabricated for them, and which they passed on from one to another without scrutiny or reflection.
(الويل): a maṣdar with no verb of its own wording. Nothing has come from this root, whose first radical is wāw and second yāʾ, except wayl, wayḥ, ways and wayb. It is not dualised or pluralised, though it was said that it is pluralised as waylāt. Imruʾ al-Qays said: "ويوم دخلت الخدر خدر عنيزة ... فقالت: لك الويلات إنك مرجلي" (And the day I entered the howdah, the howdah of ʿUnayza, she said: Woe to you, you will make me go on foot!).
When it is annexed, the best case for it is the accusative as an absolute object, because it is a maṣdar of a verb the Arabs let die; and when it is not annexed, the best case is the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and beginning with it is permissible because it implies a specific meaning. Al-wayl means disgrace and anguish. Al-Khalīl said: it is the intensity of evil. Others said: al-wayl is destruction.

* I'rab:
(وَمِنْهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, and مِنْهُمْ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar placed first. (أُمِّيُّونَ): a delayed mubtadaʾ. (لا): a negative. (يَعْلَمُونَ): an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the agent. (الْكِتابَ): a direct object, and the clause لا يَعْلَمُونَ is an adjective of أُمِّيُّونَ. (إِلَّا): a particle of exception. (أَمانِيَّ): excepted by إِلَّا, and it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because the wishes are not included under the signification of "the Book"; for this reason its accusative is obligatory despite the negative preceding. That is so in every place where it is good to put "lākin" (but) in the position of إِلَّا, whereupon the disconnection of the meaning of the second from the meaning of the first is known. (وَإِنْ): the wāw is a ḥāl and إِنْ is a negative. (هُمْ): a mubtadaʾ. (إِلَّا): a particle of restriction because of the preceding negative. (يَظُنُّونَ): an imperfect verb and agent, and the verbal clause is their khabar. (فَوَيْلٌ): the fāʾ is resumptive, and وَيْلٌ is a mubtadaʾ for which beginning with it is permissible because it implies the meaning of supplication and terrifying. (لِلَّذِينَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar of وَيْلٌ. (يَكْتُبُونَ): verb and agent, and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. (الْكِتابَ): a direct object. (بِأَيْدِيهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يَكْتُبُونَ. (ثُمَّ يَقُولُونَ): conjoined to يَكْتُبُونَ. (هذا): a mubtadaʾ. (مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar, and the nominal clause is the quoted speech. (لِيَشْتَرُوا): the lām is the lām of justification, and يَشْتَرُوا is an imperfect verb put in the accusative by an implied أَنْ, permissibly, after the lām of justification, and the wāw is the agent. (بِهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يَشْتَرُوا. (ثَمَناً): a direct object. (قَلِيلًا): an adjective. (فَوَيْلٌ): its i'rab has been given, and He repeated it for emphasis. (لَهُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar of وَيْلٌ. (مِمَّا): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to وَيْلٌ. (كَتَبَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ): verb and agent, and the clause has no position because it is the ṣila of مَا. (وَوَيْلٌ لَهُمْ مِمَّا يَكْسِبُونَ): conjoined to what precedes, and its i'rab has already been given.

* Rhetoric:
(Prolixity, al-iṭnāb) by mentioning "their hands": He mentioned them although writing is done only with them, in order to depict the state in the soul as it occurred and to embody it before the listener until he almost sees it, and in order to put the matter on record against them, as you say to one who denies knowing what he wrote and signed: "you wrote it with your right hand". [Translator's note: the source prints «وتجسيبها»; «وتجسيمها» (embodying it) appears to be meant.]

dervis-irab:80-82.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقالُوا): the wāw is resumptive; قالُوا is verb and agent. (لَنْ): a particle of negation, of the accusative and of futurity. (تَمَسَّنَا): an imperfect verb put in the accusative by لَنْ, and نَا is an attached pronoun in the accusative position as direct object. (النَّارُ): the agent, and the verbal clause is in the accusative position as the quoted speech. (إِلَّا): a particle of restriction. (أَيَّاماً): accusative as an adverbial of time, attached to تَمَسَّنَا. (مَعْدُودَةً): an adjective of أَيَّاماً. (قُلْ): an imperative verb whose agent is a pronoun latent in it obligatorily, the implied form being "you", and the clause is resumptive. (أَتَّخَذْتُمْ): the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) attached to the quinquiliteral past verb is dropped because of the meeting of two hamzas, and the clause is in the accusative position as the quoted speech. (عِنْدَ اللَّهِ): the adverbial is attached to اتَّخَذْتُمْ. (عَهْداً): a direct object. (فَلَنْ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquent omission (fāʾ faṣīḥa), because it discloses an implied condition, the implied form being "if you have taken a covenant with Allah, then never". (يُخْلِفَ): an imperfect verb put in the accusative by لَنْ. (اللَّهِ): the agent. (عَهْدَهُ): a direct object. (أَمْ): a conjunction equivalent to the interrogative, so it is the connected one (muttaṣila); it is possible that it is the disconnected one (munqaṭiʿa), meaning "rather" (bal), and both give the meaning of affirmation and rebuke. (تَقُولُونَ): conjoined to what precedes. (عَلَى اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تَقُولُونَ. (ما): a relative noun, the object of تَقُولُونَ. (لا): a negative. (تَعْلَمُونَ): an imperfect verb and the wāw is the agent, and the clause has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (بَلى): a particle of response that affirms what comes after a negative particle. (مَنْ): a conditional noun that jusses, a mubtadaʾ. (كَسَبَ): a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis, and its agent is a latent pronoun, the implied form being "he". (سَيِّئَةً): a direct object. (وَأَحاطَتْ): conjoined to كَسَبَ. (بِهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أَحاطَتْ. (خَطِيئَتُهُ): the agent of أَحاطَتْ. (فَأُولئِكَ): the fāʾ links to the apodosis, and the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ. (أَصْحابُ النَّارِ): its khabar. (هُمْ): a mubtadaʾ. (فِيها): attached to خالِدُونَ. (خالِدُونَ): the khabar of هُمْ, and the nominal clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis of the jussive condition. (وَالَّذِينَ): the wāw is a conjunction, and الَّذِينَ is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ. (آمَنُوا): verb and agent, and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ): conjoined to آمَنُوا. (أُولئِكَ): also a mubtadaʾ. (أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ): the khabar of أُولئِكَ, and the nominal clause is the khabar of الَّذِينَ. (هُمْ): a mubtadaʾ. (فِيها): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to خالِدُونَ. (خالِدُونَ): their khabar, and the nominal clause is a second khabar of the relative noun.

* Benefits:
(بَلى) is a particle of response like نَعَمْ. The difference between them is that بَلى is specific to occurring after a negative, to make it an affirmative; whereas نَعَمْ, and likewise أَجَلْ, are such that the response with them follows what precedes them in its affirmation and negation. If you say to a man "Do I not have a thousand dirhams from you?" and he says "balā", that is binding on him; if he says "naʿam", it is not binding on him. Among the particles of response are also إِي and جَيْرِ.

dervis-irab:83-83.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ أَخَذْنا): its i'rab has been given many times. (مِيثاقَ): a direct object. (بَنِي): a genitive muḍāf ilayhi, its genitive sign being the yāʾ because it is attached to the sound masculine plural. (إِسْرائِيلَ): a muḍāf ilayhi, its genitive sign being the fatḥa in place of the kasra because it is a foreign proper name. (لا): a negative. (تَعْبُدُونَ): an imperfect verb in the nominative, and the wāw is the agent. (إِلَّا): a particle of restriction. (اللَّهَ): a direct object, and the clause has no position because it is explicative, and the report has the meaning of a prohibition, i.e. [Translator's note: the source breaks off here after «أي», with the next word «وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ» following directly; the sentence is left incomplete as written]. (وَبِالْوالِدَيْنِ): the wāw is a conjunction on the position of the omitted أَنْ in لا تَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ, so the meaning of the speech is: "when We took the covenant of the Children of Israel that you worship none but Allah, and that you be good to your parents". بِالْوالِدَيْنِ: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb of the maṣdar, i.e. "and be good to your parents". (إِحْساناً): an absolute object of an omitted verb. (وَذِي الْقُرْبى وَالْيَتامى وَالْمَساكِينِ): conjoined to الْوالِدَيْنِ. (وَقُولُوا): a conjunction, but an omitted element must be implied, i.e. "and We said: say". (لِلنَّاسِ): attached to the omitted verb. (حُسْناً): an adjective of an omitted absolute object, or "a good saying". (وَأَقِيمُوا): also conjoined to what precedes. (الصَّلاةَ): a direct object. (وَآتُوا الزَّكاةَ): conjoined to أَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ. (ثُمَّ): a conjunction, conjoined to an omitted element, i.e. "so you accepted the covenant". (تَوَلَّيْتُمْ): verb and agent. (إِلَّا): a particle of exception, because the speech is complete and affirmative. (قَلِيلًا): excepted by إِلَّا. (مِنْكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of قَلِيلًا. (وَأَنْتُمْ): the wāw is a ḥāl, and أَنْتُمْ is a mubtadaʾ. (مُعْرِضُونَ): the khabar, and the nominal clause is in the accusative position as a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
1- The clause لا تَعْبُدُونَ is a report whose meaning is a prohibition, and this is more eloquent than stating it explicitly.
2- Iltifāt (shift of address): from the third person to the second in His saying «لا تَعْبُدُونَ», and from addressing the Children of Israel of old to addressing those of them who were present in the time of the Prophet ﷺ.

dervis-irab:84-85.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَظاهَرُونَ): "you help one another"; one of the two tāʾs was dropped. The origin of muẓāhara is mutual aid, derived from al-ẓahr (the back), because each strengthens the other and so becomes a back for him. (تُفادُوهُمْ): you rescue them from captivity with money.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ أَخَذْنا مِيثاقَكُمْ): the i'rab of this clause was given shortly before. (لا تَسْفِكُونَ دِماءَكُمْ): also a report whose meaning is a prohibition, and the i'rab of this clause was given before. (وَلا تُخْرِجُونَ أَنْفُسَكُمْ مِنْ دِيارِكُمْ): conjoined to what precedes, i.e. you acknowledged against yourselves after the delay and the length of time. (ثُمَّ أَقْرَرْتُمْ): ثُمَّ is a conjunction, and أَقْرَرْتُمْ is verb and agent. (وَأَنْتُمْ تَشْهَدُونَ): its i'rab has been given. (ثُمَّ): a conjunction of delay. (أَنْتُمْ): a mubtadaʾ. (هؤُلاءِ): a demonstrative in the accusative position as a blame, by an omitted verb, the implied form being "I blame"; it was also said that it is in the accusative position as a vocative whose vocative particle is omitted. (تَقْتُلُونَ): an imperfect verb and the wāw is the agent, and the clause تَقْتُلُونَ is the khabar of أَنْتُمْ. (أَنْفُسَكُمْ): a direct object. It was also said that the demonstrative is the khabar and the clause تَقْتُلُونَ is a ḥāl; the Arabs have said: "ها أنت ذا قائما" (Here you are, standing), and the demonstrative is used in form to predicate of the pronoun, as if he said "you are the present one". (وَتُخْرِجُونَ): conjoined to تَقْتُلُونَ. (فَرِيقاً): a direct object. (مِنْكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of فَرِيقاً. (مِنْ دِيارِهِمْ): attached to تُخْرِجُونَ. (تَظاهَرُونَ): an imperfect verb in the nominative and the wāw is the agent; the clause is in the accusative position as a ḥāl from the wāw, i.e. "helping one another against them". (عَلَيْهِمْ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تَظاهَرُونَ. (بِالْإِثْمِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, and the meaning is "you help one another against them while they are clothed in sin". (وَالْعُدْوانِ): conjoined to الْإِثْمِ. This verse is a wonder in the truthfulness of its depiction of the reality of these people, whose confirmation we witness today. (وَإِنْ): the wāw is resumptive and إِنْ is conditional. (يَأْتُوكُمْ): the protasis, jussive, its sign of jussive being the omission of the nūn; the wāw is the agent and the kāf is the object. (أُسارى): a ḥāl. (تُفادُوهُمْ): the apodosis, jussive. (وَهُوَ): the wāw is a ḥāl, and هُوَ is a mubtadaʾ; it is what is called the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and it will be discussed later. (مُحَرَّمٌ): a khabar placed first. (عَلَيْكُمْ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to مُحَرَّمٌ. (إِخْراجُهُمْ): a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is in the nominative position as the khabar of the pronoun of the matter. It is also permissible to parse His saying مُحَرَّمٌ as the khabar of هُوَ and إِخْراجُهُمْ as the deputy agent of مُحَرَّمٌ, because it is a passive participle. (أَفَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِبَعْضِ الْكِتابِ وَتَكْفُرُونَ بِبَعْضٍ): the i'rab of its like has been given. (فَما): the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquent omission, because it discloses an implied condition, as if it were said "if you wish to know the recompense of him who does that", and مَا is a negative. (جَزاءُ): a mubtadaʾ. (مَنْ): a relative noun in the genitive position through annexation. (يَفْعَلُ): an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, the implied form being "he", and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. (ذلِكَ): the demonstrative, direct object. (مِنْكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "while it is from you". (إِلَّا): a particle of restriction. (خِزْيٌ): the khabar of جَزاءُ, because it is a complete exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh). (فِي الْحَياةِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of خِزْيٌ. (الدُّنْيا): an adjective of الْحَياةِ. (وَيَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ): the wāw is resumptive, and the adverbial is attached to يُرَدُّونَ. (يُرَدُّونَ): the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is resumptive. (إِلى أَشَدِّ الْعَذابِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يُرَدُّونَ. (وَمَا): the wāw is resumptive and مَا is a Hijazi negative that works like لَيْسَ. (اللَّهُ): its noun, in the nominative. (بِغافِلٍ): the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and غافِلٍ is in position the khabar of مَا. (عَمَّا): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تَعْمَلُونَ. (تَعْمَلُونَ): the verbal clause is the ṣila of the relative noun.

dervis-irab:230-231.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ضِراراً): a maṣdar in the sense of iḍrār (causing harm). A man would divorce his wife and leave her until the end of her waiting period (ʿidda) drew near, then take her back, not out of desire for her but to prolong the waiting period against her; so this was forbidden. The details are in the books of jurisprudence.

* I'rab:
(فَإِنْ طَلَّقَها فَلا تَحِلُّ لَهُ): the fāʾ is resumptive or a conjunction, and إن is conditional; طلقها is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis, and the hāʾ is the direct object; the fāʾ links the apodosis, لا is negative and تحل is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "she", that is, the divorced woman; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تحل; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (مِنْ بَعْدُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "being after the two divorces". (حَتَّى تَنْكِحَ زَوْجاً غَيْرَهُ): حتى is a particle of limit and of genitive; تنكح is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after حتى; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تحل; زوجا is a direct object and غيره is an adjective. (فَإِنْ طَلَّقَها): the clause is resumptive and its like has gone before; the agent is a latent pronoun referring to the second husband. (فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْهِما أَنْ يَتَراجَعا): the fāʾ links; لا is the lā of generic negation and جناح is its noun, indeclinable on fatḥa; عليهما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of it; the clause فلا جناح is an apodosis; أن and what is within its scope is a maṣdar accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "in returning to each other", and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl; the pronoun refers to the wife and the first husband. (إِنْ ظَنَّا): إن is conditional; ظنا is a past verb, indeclinable on fatḥa, and the alif is the agent; it is the protasis, and its apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes. (أَنْ يُقِيما): أن and what is within its scope is an accusative maṣdar standing as the two objects of ظنا; the alif is the agent. (حُدُودَ اللَّهِ): a direct object. (وَتِلْكَ): the waw is resumptive and تلك is a mubtadaʾ. (حُدُودَ اللَّهِ): the khabar «[Translator's note: the source gives the word in the accusative form, حُدُودَ, as it appears in the verse text; as a khabar it is nominative]». (يُبَيِّنُها): an imperfect verb with a latent agent referring to Allah the Exalted, and the hāʾ is the direct object; the clause is in the position of the nominative as a second khabar, or a ḥāl. (لِقَوْمٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «نبينها» «[Translator's note: the source says نبينها ("we make them clear") although the verb it just parsed is يبينها]». (يَعْلَمُونَ): the clause is an adjective of قوم. (وَإِذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ): the waw is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, introduced to complete the explanation of the rulings of divorce. إذا is an adverb of future time implying the meaning of condition, attached to the apodosis; the clause طلقتم النساء is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and النساء is the direct object of طلقتم. (فَبَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; بلغن is a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and the nūn of the feminine plural is the agent; أجلهن is the direct object. (فَأَمْسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ): the fāʾ links the apodosis; أمسكوهن is an imperative verb, an agent and a direct object; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أمسكوهن. (أَوْ سَرِّحُوهُنَّ بِمَعْرُوفٍ): the clause is conjoined to the one before it. (وَلا تُمْسِكُوهُنَّ ضِراراً): the waw is a conjunction and لا is prohibitive; تمسكوهن is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, its sign of jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the waw is the agent and the hāʾ the direct object, and the nūn is the sign of the feminine; ضرارا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq, or a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl; the three aspects are equally preferable. (لِتَعْتَدُوا): the lām is for giving a reason, and تعتدوا is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «ضرارا», so it is a reason for a reason, as you say: "I struck my son for discipline so that he may benefit"; it is not permissible to make it a second reason, so that the mafʿūl li-ajlihi is not multiplied. The meaning of iʿtidāʾ is wrongdoing by exceeding the stated limits. (وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذلِكَ): the waw is resumptive; من is a conditional mubtadaʾ; يفعل is the protasis, its agent "he", and ذلك is the direct object. (فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ): the fāʾ links the apodosis; قد is a particle of confirmation; ظلم is a past verb whose agent is "he", and نفسه is a direct object; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis; the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar of «من». (وَلا تَتَّخِذُوا آياتِ اللَّهِ هُزُواً): the waw is a conjunction or a resumptive particle, and لا is prohibitive; تتخذوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, with the waw as agent; آيات الله is the first direct object and هزوا the second direct object of تتخذوا, that is, "mocked at". (وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ): the waw is a conjunction; اذكروا is an imperative verb with an agent; نعمة الله is a direct object and عليكم is attached to نعمة. (وَما أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنَ الْكِتابِ وَالْحِكْمَةِ): the waw is a conjunction; ما is a relative noun conjoined to نعمة; the clause أنزل is the ṣila of «ما»; عليكم is attached to أنزل; من الكتاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; and الحكمة is conjoined to الكتاب. (يَعِظُكُمْ بِهِ): an imperfect verb in the nominative whose latent agent is "He", and the kāf is the direct object; the clause is a ḥāl; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يعظكم. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ): the waw is a conjunction; اتقوا is conjoined to اذكروا. (وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ): conjoined to what precedes; أن and what is within its scope stand in place of the two objects of اعلموا.

dervis-irab:232-232.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ): al-ʿaḍl is confinement and constriction; from it comes "the hen was ʿuḍilat" when her egg gets stuck and does not come out. Ibn Harma looked toward the heaven of the Qur'an and took the word in an elegant way when he said:
وإن قصائدي لك فاصطنعني ... عقائل قد عضلن عن النكاح
(My poems are for you, so take me into your favour: they are noble maidens who have been barred from marriage.)
He likened the poems to women and strengthened that with ʿaḍl, which is preventing from marriage.
The ʿayn with the ḍād, when they occur as the first and second radicals of a word, have a strange secret: they then convey the meaning of confinement and severity. From this comes sayf ʿaḍb, that is, a severe, cutting sword, and al-ʿaḍud (the upper arm) is well known, being the strongest limb in a person. This is among the strangest features by which our Arabic language is distinguished.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ): the waw is resumptive; إذا is an adverb of future time attached to the apodosis; the clause طلقتم النساء is in the position of the genitive through the annexation of the adverb to it. And النساء is a direct object. (فَبَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; بلغن is a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and the nūn is the agent; أجلهن, that is, their waiting period, is a direct object; the clause is conjoined to the clause طلقتم. (فَلا تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ): the fāʾ links, and لا is prohibitive; تعضلوهن is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, with the waw as agent and the hāʾ as direct object; the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of إذا. (أَنْ يَنْكِحْنَ أَزْواجَهُنَّ): أن and what follows is a maṣdar accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "from marrying". Abū Ḥayyān held that the maṣdar is in the position of the accusative as a badal from the pronoun, a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), and there is no harm in what he held. And أزواجهن is a direct object. (إِذا تَراضَوْا بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): إذا is an adverb of future time implying the meaning of condition, attached to تعضلوهن or to ينكحن. The clause تراضوا is in the position of the genitive by annexation; بينهم is an adverb attached to تراضوا; and بالمعروف is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl from the agent of تراضوا, or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is, "mutual consent being in accordance with what is right"; and there is no objection to attaching the two to تراضوا, that is, "they consented to what is good in religion and in manliness". (ذلِكَ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ, and the pointing is to all that He detailed of the rulings. (يُوعَظُ بِهِ): a passive imperfect verb; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يوعظ; the clause يوعظ به is the khabar of the demonstrative, and the clause of the demonstrative is resumptive. (مَنْ كانَ): من is a relative noun in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʾil of يوعظ; كان is a defective past verb and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he"; the clause is the ṣila. (مِنْكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ): the verbal clause is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كان. (ذلِكُمْ أَزْكى لَكُمْ وَأَطْهَرُ): ذلكم is a mubtadaʾ and أزكى is its khabar; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أزكى or أطهر; the clause is resumptive. (وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ): the waw is resumptive, الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يعلم is the khabar. (وَأَنْتُمْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ): the waw is a conjunction, أنتم is a mubtadaʾ, لا is negative, and the clause لا تعلمون is the khabar of أنتم.

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is a delightful majāz mursal (unrestricted figurative usage), namely His saying: (أَنْ يَنْكِحْنَ أَزْواجَهُنَّ). The naming of the women as "their husbands" by those who divorced them is a majāz mursal whose relation is consideration of what once was.

dervis-irab:207-209.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَشْرِي): sells.
(السلم): submission (istislām); it is read with kasra or fatḥa on the sīn.
(كَافَّةً): from "kaff" (restraining), as if they were restrained from any one of them straying.

* I'rab:
(وَمِنَ النَّاسِ) The wāw is a conjunction and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (مِنَ) a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is conjoined to His saying «فمن الناس» to complete their categories. (يَشْرِي نَفْسَهُ) an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila of the relative. (ابْتِغاءَ مَرْضاتِ اللَّهِ) mafʿūl li-ajlihi, and what follows it is muḍāf ilayhi. (وَاللَّهُ) The wāw is resumptive and "Allāh" is a mubtadaʾ. (رَؤُفٌ) khabar. (بِالْعِبادِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «رءوف». (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) the i'rab of its like has preceded. (ادْخُلُوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (فِي السِّلْمِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «ادخلوا»; the clause is resumptive. (كَافَّةً) a ḥāl from the wāw in «ادخلوا» and from «al-silm», because it is used as masculine and feminine. (وَلا) The wāw is a conjunction and "lā" is prohibitive. (تَتَّبِعُوا) an imperfect verb jussive by "lā", its jussive sign being the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (خُطُواتِ الشَّيْطانِ) mafʿūl bihi and muḍāf ilayhi. (إِنَّهُ) "inna" and its ism. (لَكُمْ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «عدو». (عَدُوٌّ) khabar. (مُبِينٌ) ṣifa; the clause is causal and has no grammatical position. (فَإِنْ زَلَلْتُمْ) The fāʾ is resumptive, "in" is conditional, and "zalaltum" is a past verb with its fāʿil, in the position of a jussive as the protasis. (مِنْ بَعْدِ ما جاءَتْكُمُ الْبَيِّناتُ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «زللتم»; "mā" is maṣdar, interpreted together with the verb after it as a maṣdar in the position of genitive by annexation; "jāʾatkum al-bayyināt" is verb, mafʿūl bihi and fāʿil. (فَاعْلَمُوا) The fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis; "iʿlamū" is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis. (أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ) "anna" with its ism and its two khabars, standing in the place of the two objects of «اعلموا».

dervis-irab:210-211.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الظّلل): plural of "ẓulla" (with ḍamma on the ẓāʾ), which is anything that shades you, like "ẓilāl", plural of "ẓill".
(الْغَمامِ): the white, thin cloud, which is a place where mercy is expected; it covers the sky and changes its colour. Among the wonders of the letters ghayn and mīm is that when they occur as the first and second radicals of a word they indicate the meaning of covering, veiling a thing and hiding it. From it come "ghimd al-sayf", the scabbard of the sword which hides it; "taghammada Allāhu fulānan bi-raḥmatihi", i.e. He covered him; "ghamarahu l-māʾ", i.e. the water covered him; "arḍ ghamiqa", land which the dews flood; and on the authority of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb: "The Jordan is a ghamiqa land and al-Jābiya is a pleasant land"; and "ghumma l-hilāl", the crescent was hidden. This is among the wonders.

* I'rab:
(هَلْ) an interrogative particle whose meaning is denial and rebuke. (يَنْظُرُونَ) an imperfect verb in the nominative and the wāw is the fāʿil; its meaning is "they wait", or "they look", from "naẓar". (إِلَّا) a particle of restriction. (أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ) "an" is a particle of maṣdar and of accusative; it and what is within its scope are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, the object of «ينظرون»; the clause is resumptive, brought to rebuke those who hold back from Islam, or those who slip and err. (اللَّهُ) fāʿil of «يأتيهم». (فِي ظُلَلٍ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يأتيهم». (مِنَ الْغَمامِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ṣifa of «ظلل». (وَالْمَلائِكَةُ) The wāw is a conjunction and "al-malāʾika" is conjoined to "Allāh". (وَقُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ) conjoined to «يأتيهم», entering within the scope of the waiting; you may also make it a resumptive clause. (وَإِلَى اللَّهِ) The wāw is a conjunction and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «ترجع». (تُرْجَعُ) an imperfect passive verb. (الْأُمُورُ) nāʾib fāʿil. (سَلْ بَنِي إِسْرائِيلَ) "sal" is an imperative verb, indeclinable on sukūn, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, the implied form being "anta"; "banī" is mafʿūl bihi in the accusative, its accusative sign being the yāʾ because it is annexed to the sound masculine plural, and "Isrāʾīl" is muḍāf ilayhi, its genitive sign being the fatḥa in place of the kasra because it is a diptote; the clause is resumptive. (كَمْ آتَيْناهُمْ) "kam" is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of «آتيناهم»; "ātaynāhum" is verb, fāʿil and first mafʿūl bihi; the clause «آتيناهم» stands in the place of the second object of «سل», because it is suspended from operating (muʿallaqa) while operating in meaning. «Sal» was suspended although it is not among the verbs of the heart because asking is the cause of knowing, so the cause was treated like the effect in that. Some permitted that "kam" be declarative (khabariyya), which would cut off the clause in which it occurs. (مِنْ آيَةٍ) the tamyīz of the interrogative "kam"; when the two are separated, it is better to bring "min". There is disagreement about "min": it is said to be redundant, and in the marginal notes to al-Mughnī they preferred it to be explicative (bayāniyya) with the tamyīz omitted. «Min āya»: both attached to the verb. More of this discussion will come in the Benefits. (بَيِّنَةٍ) ṣifa; the clause «سل بني إسرائيل» is resumptive, to denounce the Children of Israel who disbelieve in the favour of Allah and change it.
