(وَمَنْ) The wāw is resumptive; the clause is resumptive, brought to add reproach and establish the argument against them; "man" is conditional, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (يُبَدِّلْ) the protasis. (نِعْمَةَ اللَّهِ) mafʿūl bihi. (مِنْ بَعْدِ ما جاءَتْهُ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl; "mā" is maṣdar, interpreted with what follows as a maṣdar in the position of genitive by annexation; "jāʾathu" is a past verb with a mafʿūl bihi, and its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, the implied form being "hiya". (فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ) The fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis, and "inna" with its ism. (شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ) its khabar; the clause of "inna" and what follows is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis of the jussive conditional.

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of the Exalted «في ظلل من الغمام» there is a mujāz mursal (non-metaphorical trope) whose relation is causality, because the cloud is a place where mercy or punishment is expected and their cause: from it the rains pour down, and from it may arise destructive, sweeping torrents, and destroying thunderbolts descend.

* Benefits:
Ibn Hishām gave a section on the parsing of this verse, which we summarise as follows because of its importance:
"His saying, the Exalted: «سل بني إسرائيل كم آتيناهم من آية»: If you take «min» as redundant, then «kam» is a mubtadaʾ, or the object of an implied «ātaynā» after it. If you take it as explicative of «kam», as it is explicative of «mā» in «ما ننسخ من آية», neither of the two views is permissible, because there would then be no referent returning to «kam»; rather it is a fronted second object, like «أعشرين درهما أعطيتك». Al-Zamakhsharī permitted that «kam» be declarative (khabariyya). [Translator's note: the source text, which appears garbled here, reads: "i.e. that all that preceded was based on «kam» being an interrogative noun; and this is its opposite".] Then he said: "The grammarians did not mention that declarative «kam» suspends the operator from operating. Some permitted «min» to be redundant, but it is only added after interrogation with «hal» specifically; perhaps his permitting that is according to the view of one who does not require the sentence to be non-affirmative in every case, or according to one who requires that outside the chapter of tamyīz, and holds that in «raṭl min zayt» and «khātam min ḥadīd» it is redundant and not affirmative." End."
Now, "kam" comes in two kinds: interrogative and declarative, and much of the discussion of them will come in this book.

dervis-irab:212-212.t:
* I'rab:
(زُيِّنَ) a past passive verb. (لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «زين», and the clause «كفروا» is the ṣila of the relative and has no grammatical position. (الْحَياةُ) nāʾib fāʿil. (الدُّنْيا) ṣifa of "al-ḥayāh"; the clause is resumptive, brought to denounce those who made this world and its enchanting pleasures their goal in it. (وَيَسْخَرُونَ) conjoined to the clause «زين»; it is also possible that it is a khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and they mock", in which case it would be the conjoining of a nominal clause to a verbal one, to indicate that He brought the first as a verbal clause to indicate renewal and occurrence. (مِنَ الَّذِينَ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يسخرون». (آمَنُوا) verb and fāʿil; the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of «الذين». (وَالَّذِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction and «alladhīna» is a mubtadaʾ. (اتَّقَوْا) the clause is the ṣila of the relative. (فَوْقَهُمْ) an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar of «alladhīna». (يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ) attached to what the adverb is attached to. (وَاللَّهُ) The wāw is resumptive and "Allāh" is a mubtadaʾ. (يَرْزُقُ) an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, referring to Allah, the Name of Majesty; the clause is the khabar of the Name of Majesty "Allāh". (مِنَ) a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. (يَشاءُ) an imperfect verb; the clause is the ṣila of "man". (بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يرزق».

* Rhetoric:
In this verse there is a contrast between the clauses: the adornment of the life of this world in the eyes of those who disbelieved, and their mockery of the believers, are expressed with verbal clauses, to indicate occurrence, and that it is a passing matter that does not remain long before it disappears through numerous diverting causes.
As for the superiority of those who were pious over them, it is a matter of lasting permanence upon which no change comes.

dervis-irab:25-25.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَبَشِّرِ) Bushra (glad tidings) is informing of what makes manifest the joy of the one informed. From it come al-basharah (the surface of the skin) and tabāshīr al-ṣubḥ (the first gleams of dawn): what appears of the first of its light. On this lexical explanation there is an interesting juristic discussion. The jurists said: if a man says to his slave, "Whichever of you gives me glad tidings of the arrival of so-and-so is free", and they give him the news one by one, the first of them is freed, because he is the one who made the man's joy manifest by his news, and not the rest; but if he had said, in place of "gives me glad tidings", "informs me", they would all be freed, because they all informed him.

* I'rab:
(وَبَشِّرِ) the wāw is a conjunction, conjoining the description of the clause of the believer's reward to the description of the clause of the disbeliever's punishment. The fāʿil of بشر is a latent pronoun (obligatorily latent), its implied form being "you". (الَّذِينَ) a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (آمَنُوا) verb and agent; the clause has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (وَعَمِلُوا) conjoined to آمنوا, included within the scope of the ṣila, and the wāw is fāʿil. (الصَّالِحاتِ) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, its sign of accusative being the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural. (أَنَّ) a particle resembling a verb, which governs the noun in the accusative and the khabar in the nominative; it, with what follows it, is in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition; its discussion will come in the Benefits section. (لَهُمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar of أن. (جَنَّاتٍ) its postponed ism, its sign of accusative being the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural. (تَجْرِي) an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of nominative being the implied ḍamma on the yāʾ, its appearance prevented by heaviness. (مِنْ تَحْتِهَا) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تجري. (الْأَنْهارُ) the nominative fāʿil. (كُلَّما) an adverb of time containing the sense of a condition, and ما is either maṣdar-forming or an indefinite specified noun; this was discussed a little earlier. (رُزِقُوا) a past passive verb, and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil; the verbal clause has no position, or is in the position of genitive as an adjective, that is, "every time at which they were provided". (مِنْها) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to رزقوا. (مِنْ ثَمَرَةٍ) the preposition and its genitive noun are a badal ishtimāl (inclusive substitute) of His words منها. An example: "I ate of your orchard, of the pomegranates, something; I praised you", so the place of من ثمرة is the place of your saying "of the pomegranates". (رِزْقاً) the second object of رزقوا, the first object being the nāʾib fāʿil, which is the wāw. It is unlikely that رزقا is a maṣdar accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq. The clause كلما رزقوا is a second adjective of جنات, or a ḥāl; and you may make it resumptive, with no grammatical position. (قالُوا) verb and agent; the clause has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (هذَا) a demonstrative noun, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (الَّذِي) a relative noun, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as khabar; the nominal clause is in the position of accusative as the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (رُزِقْنا) a past passive verb, and نا is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil; the clause رزقنا has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun, and the returning pronoun is omitted, that is, "we were provided it". (مِنْ قَبْلُ) من is a preposition of beginning of the extent; it is also said that قبل is an adverb indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording and not in meaning, in the position of genitive after من; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to رزقنا or to an omitted ḥāl. (وَأُتُوا) the wāw is resumptive and أتوا is a past passive verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil. (بِهِ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أتوا; the clause is resumptive, brought to report about this which they were provided. (مُتَشابِهاً) a ḥāl, that is, resembling the fruit they were familiar with in the world, because a human being is more at ease with the familiar and inclines to it; it is also said that parts of it resemble other parts in colour though they differ in taste. The first meaning is preferable, by the evidence of what precedes, namely His words: «هذا الذي رزقنا من قبل». (وَلَهُمْ) the wāw is a conjunction, and لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (فِيها) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (أَزْواجٌ) a postponed mubtadaʾ. Zawj is that with which another is paired, so zawj is said of both woman and man; zawja with tāʾ is rare, and al-Farrāʾ said that it is a dialect. (مُطَهَّرَةٌ) naʿt of أزواج. (وَهُمْ) the wāw is a conjunction and هم is mubtadaʾ. (فِيها) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to خالدون. (خالِدُونَ) khabar of هم.

* Rhetoric:
1- The free metaphor (majāz mursal) in His words تجري من تحتها الأنهار, the relation being locality (maḥalliyya). This is if nahr is the channel of the water, as some lexicographers said; but if it means the water in the channel, there is no figure in it. It has two forms: with fatḥa on the hāʾ and with sukūn.
2- The eloquent simile (tashbīh balīgh) in His words: هذا الذي رزقنا من قبل. It is called eloquent because the particle of likeness is omitted, so the two sides of the simile are equal in rank. Among its examples is the saying of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ describing a night:
ليلتي هذه عروس من الزنج عليها قلائد من جمان
(This night of mine is a bride from the Zanj, on her necklaces of pearls.)

* Benefits:
1- The preposition is sometimes omitted by usage (samāʿan), and the genitive noun becomes accusative after its omission, by analogy with the direct object. Among it is the saying of Jarīr:
تمرّون الديار ولم تعوجوا ... كلامكم عليّ إذن حرام
(You pass by the abodes and do not turn aside; your speech to me then is forbidden.) That is, "you pass by the abodes". The omission of the preposition is analogical before maṣdar-forming أن and before أنّ, the one resembling a verb, with fatḥa on the hamza.
2- The plural of a non-rational noun may be described with a plural that matches it. The Exalted said: «جنات معروشات», and outside the Qur'an معروشة is permissible. And the broken plural denoting rational beings may also be described with the feminine singular, and may be described with the plural as in the verse, namely «أزواج مطهرة», and outside the Qur'an مطهرات is permissible.

dervis-irab:253-253.t:
* I'rab:
(تِلْكَ الرُّسُلُ فَضَّلْنا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلى بَعْضٍ) A resumptive nominal sentence, introduced to establish the condition of the company of messengers whose stories are mentioned in the sura. The demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ and الرسل the khabar; فضلنا is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, and «نا» is the agent; and the clause فضلنا is circumstantial (ḥāl). It is permissible to construe الرسل as a substitute (badal) for the demonstrative, with the clause فضلنا as the khabar; بعضهم is a direct object and على بعض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to فضلنا. (مِنْهُمْ مَنْ كَلَّمَ اللَّهُ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted advanced khabar; من is a relative noun, a postponed mubtadaʾ; كلم الله is a verb and agent, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila; the returning pronoun ('āʾid) is omitted and is the direct object; and the nominal sentence is resumptive with no grammatical position. It is permissible to construe it as a substitute for the clause فضلنا, in both of the preceding ḥāl analyses, or as a second khabar of the demonstrative. (وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَهُمْ دَرَجاتٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; رفع is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", referring to Allah the Exalted; بعضهم is a direct object; and درجات is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. «في درجات». Abū l-Baqāʾ construed it as an interpreted ḥāl from «بعضهم», i.e. "possessing ranks"; and both are sound. (وَآتَيْنا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ الْبَيِّناتِ)
The wāw is a conjunction; آتينا is a verb and agent; عيسى is a direct object; ابن is a substitute for «عيسى» or an adjective of it; مريم is a muḍāf ilayhi; and البينات is a second direct object, its accusative marked by kasra in place of fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural. (وَأَيَّدْناهُ بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ) The wāw is a conjunction; أيدناه is a verb, agent and direct object; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أيدناه; and القدس is a muḍāf ilayhi. (وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ) The wāw is resumptive and لو is conditional; شاء الله is a verb and agent, and the object of the willing is omitted, its implied form being: "their not fighting one another". (مَا اقْتَتَلَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ) ما is negative; اقتتل الذين is a verb and agent; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun; and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to a non-jussive-governing conditional. (مِنْ بَعْدِ ما جاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّناتُ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اقتتل, or are a substitute for his words «من بعدهم» with the preposition repeated; and ما is a maṣdar particle, interpreted together with what follows as a maṣdar in the position of a genitive by annexation, i.e. "after the coming of the clear proofs". (وَلكِنِ اخْتَلَفُوا) The wāw is resumptive, and the sentence is resumptive, introduced to rectify what precedes; ولكن is a particle of rectification that does not govern; اختلفوا is a verb and agent. (فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ آمَنَ) The fā' is of ramification; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted advanced khabar; من is a relative noun, a postponed mubtadaʾ; آمن is a past verb whose agent is "he", and the clause is a ṣila. (وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ كَفَرَ) Conjoined to the preceding clause. (وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ مَا اقْتَتَلُوا) Its i'rab has preceded; it is repeated to emphasise the speech. (وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ ما يُرِيدُ) The wāw is resumptive; ولكنّ is a particle resembling the verb, its noun is اللَّه, and the clause يفعل is its khabar; ما is a relative noun, a direct object; and the clause بريد [Translator's note: sic, for «يريد»] is the ṣila of the relative noun.

* Rhetoric:
In his words «ورفع بعضهم درجات» is the art of vagueness (fann al-ibhām), with a magnification and a proclamation of rank in it such that, had he spoken the name, its vagueness would not have been matched, because of the testimony it contains that he is the unmistakable eminent one, distinguished above the rest. He means Muḥammad ﷺ, and sufficient for him is the Qur'an that was sent down to him, the miracle that remains for all time. So not mentioning is more eloquent than mentioning, and vagueness more eloquent than clarity. Al-Ḥuṭayʾa was asked: who is the greatest of poets? He named Zuhayr and al-Nābigha, then said: "and if I wished I would name the third", meaning himself. Had he stated this openly, it would not have had this degree of grandeur.

dervis-irab:254-254.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الخلة) with ḍamma on the khā': affection and friendship; it was so named because it permeates (tatakhallalu) the limbs, i.e. enters their interstices. And الخليل is the friend, for his intimacy with you and his affection permeating your inner parts. It may be that الخليل is in the sense of an active or a passive participle.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) يا is a vocative particle; أيّ is an indefinite-but-specified addressed noun, indeclinable on ḍamma in the position of an accusative; the hā' is for alerting; الذين is a substitute for أيها; آمنوا is a verb and agent, and the clause آمنوا is a ṣila. (أَنْفِقُوا مِمَّا رَزَقْناكُمْ) An imperative verb, the wāw its agent; ومما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنفقوا; رزقناكم is a verb, agent and object, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of ما; and the whole sentence is resumptive. (مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ) The preposition and its genitive noun are also attached to أنفقوا; there is no objection to attaching two particles to one word because they differ in meaning: the first «من» is partitive and the second is for starting-point; أنْ and what follows are interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of a genitive by annexation, i.e. "before the coming of"; and يوم is the agent of يأتي. (لا بَيْعٌ فِيهِ وَلا خُلَّةٌ) The lā of generic negation is disregarded (does not govern) because of its repetition, and its rulings will come in another place. بيع is a mubtadaʾ, which may begin the sentence because the negation precedes it; فيه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar; and ولا خلة is conjoined to «لا بيع». (وَلا شَفاعَةٌ) Also a conjunction. (وَالْكافِرُونَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; الكافرون is a mubtadaʾ, هم a second mubtadaʾ and الظالمون its khabar, and the nominal sentence is the khabar of «الكافرون»; or «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or ʿimād (support), and «الظالمون» is the khabar of «الكافرون».

dervis-irab:255-255.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْقَيُّومُ) on the pattern fayʿūl: from قام بالأمر when one manages it in the best way of management. Its origin is «قيووم»: the wāw and the yā' came together with the first of them bearing sukūn, so the wāw was changed to yā' and the yā' was assimilated into it, and it became «قيوما». Umayya ibn Abī l-Ṣalt said:
لم تخلق السماء والنجوم ... والشمس معها قمر يعوم
قدّره المهيمن القيوم ... والحشر والجنة والجحيم
إلّا لأمر شأنه عظيم
(The heaven and the stars were not created, and the sun with the moon swimming beside it, which the Overseer, the Self-Sustaining decreed, and the gathering, the Garden and the Blaze, except for a matter of great consequence.)
(السنة) with kasra on the sīn: the languor and slackness that precede sleep, with awareness remaining. It is what is called drowsiness (nuʿās). ʿAdī ibn al-Riqāʿ said, and did well:
وسنان أقصده النعاس فرنّقت ... في عينه سنة وليس بنائم
(Drowsy; sleepiness has struck him, and a drowsiness has hovered in his eye, though he is not asleep.)
For this reason sleep (nawm) is negated, because it is a removal of the senses, and the sina is affirmed in the verse.
(الكرسي) is well known. The yā' is not the yā' of attribution (nisba); had it been for attribution, it would have passed into the category of the adjective. Its origin is from the piling of things one upon another, and from it comes الكرّاسة (the quire); it was so named because its leaves are piled one upon another. In common usage it is what one sits upon. One says: تكرس فلان الحطب وغيره when he gathers it; and كرّس البناء when he lays its foundation.
(يَؤُدُهُ) burdens him and is hard for him.

* I'rab:
(اللَّهُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ) A magnificent resumptive speech, introduced to gather the rulings of divinity and the affirmative and negative attributes of the Deity. اللَّه is a mubtadaʾ; لا is the lā of generic negation; إله is its noun, indeclinable on fatḥa; إلا is a particle of restriction; and «هو» is a substitute for the position of لا and its noun. The i'rab of the testimony has already been given in detail. The nominal sentence «لا إله إلا هو» is the khabar of اللَّه; الحي is a second khabar and القيوم a third.
You may construe the two as adjectives of اللَّه. (لا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلا نَوْمٌ) The clause is a fourth khabar of the mubtadaʾ; لا is a negative; تأخذه is an imperfect verb with its direct object; سنة is the agent of تأخذه; and لا نوم is conjoined to سنة. (لَهُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ) The clause is a fifth khabar; له is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted advanced khabar; ما is a relative noun in the position of a nominative, a postponed mubtadaʾ; في السموات is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted element with no grammatical position because it is a ṣila; and ما في الأرض is conjoined to ما في السموات. (مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ) The sentence is resumptive, introduced to refute the polytheists who claimed that the idols intercede for them.
من is an interrogative noun whose meaning is negation, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; ذا is a demonstrative in the position of a nominative as khabar of «من»; and الذي is a relative noun, a substitute; or «من ذا» as a whole is an interrogative noun, the mubtadaʾ, and «الذي» is the khabar. Know that «ذا» occurring after interrogative «ما» may be made a relative noun by agreement, and as for that occurring after «من» it is more often a demonstrative [Translator's note: the source repeats the clause «ذا الواقعة بعد ما الاستفهامية يجوز جعلها اسم موصول اتفاقا، وأما الواقعة بعد…» two or three times in garbled fashion; translated once]. يشفع is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", and the clause has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila. (عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ) The adverb is attached to يشفع, or to an omitted ḥāl from the pronoun in يشفع; إلا is a particle of restriction; and بإذنه, the preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (يَعْلَمُ ما بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَما خَلْفَهُمْ) The clause is a sixth khabar; يعلم is an imperfect verb whose agent is a latent pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted; ما is a relative noun, a direct object; بين is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun; أيديهم is a muḍāf ilayhi; the wāw is a conjunction; ما is conjoined to the first «ما»; and the adverb is attached to the omitted ṣila. (وَلا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ) The clause is conjoined to what precedes; لا is a negative; يحيطون is an imperfect verb and the wāw is the agent; بشيء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يحيطون; and من علمه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of شيء. (إِلَّا بِما شاءَ) إلا is a particle of restriction; بما, the preposition and its genitive noun, is attached to an omitted substitute for شيء with the preposition repeated; and the clause شاء has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of ما, and the object of the willing is omitted, its implied form being: "that He make them know of it". (وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ) The clause is a seventh khabar, or you may take it as accusative ḥāl; وسع كرسيه is a past verb and agent; السموات is a direct object; and الأرض is conjoined to السموات. (وَلا يَؤُدُهُ حِفْظُهُما) The wāw is a conjunction; لا is a negative; ويئوده is an imperfect verb with a direct object; حفظهما is the agent; the hā' is a muḍāf ilayhi; and the mīm and the alif are two letters denoting the dual. (وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ) The wāw is a conjunction; هو is a mubtadaʾ; العليّ is its khabar and العظيم a second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
This verse contains the most important matters connected with the divine Essence.
Abū Hurayra reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Everything has a summit, and the summit of the Qur'an is al-Baqara. In it is a verse that is the chief of the verses of the Qur'an, and it is the Verse of the Throne (Āyat al-Kursī)."
We summarise below the arts of rhetoric it contains:
1- Istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya (explicit metaphor) in his words «وسع كرسيه السموات والأرض»: the word is a figurative expression for His knowledge, the Exalted, or His dominion, and a true depiction of His greatness; the thing likened is omitted, namely knowledge, power and greatness, and the meanings of majesty and all-embracing encompassment that follow from sitting upon the king's throne.
Ibn Qutayba's observation:
However, Ibn Qutayba observed in his book «Mushkil al-Qur'an» that this contradicts the texts of the language. He refuted the Muʿtazilites in their opinions, saying, verbatim:
"They have interpreted the Qur'an with the strangest interpretation, wanting to bring it back to their doctrines and to make the interpretation bear their sects. A party of them said, of «وسع كرسيه السموات والأرض», that it means 'His knowledge'. They brought for that an unknown piece of evidence, the poet's words «ولا يكرسىء علم الله مخلوق», as if for them it were: ولا يعلم علم الله مخلوق ('no created being knows the knowledge of Allah'). But الكرسي is not hamzated whereas يكرسىء is hamzated. They shrink from attributing a throne to Allah." But we do not agree with Ibn Qutayba in his opinion, for many of the People of the Sunna held that view.

The opinion of al-Taftāzānī:
Al-Taftāzānī said: it is an instance of applying a sensory, imagined compound to a verified rational meaning.

The opinion of al-Qurṭubī:
In al-Qurṭubī's exegesis: "Ibn ʿAbbās said: His Throne is His knowledge, and al-Ṭabarī preferred it. It is also said that His Throne is His power with which He holds the heavens and the earth, as you say: 'make a throne for this wall', that is, something that props it."
This is close to the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās. This is a long discussion in which argument branches out between the People of the Sunna and the Muʿtazila, so the lengthier works should be consulted on it.
2- Concision (ījāz): Āyat al-Kursī contains a concision that offers no hope for imitation or emulation, and it may be said that the expression is united with the thing expressed in depicting the true King, who is not contested, in the most graceful wording and most precise description. It contains what is called al-faṣl (disjunction) in the science of maʿānī, which is omitting the conjunction to indicate that each attribute of this great King is independent in itself, as follows:
(a) The first sentence: «الله لا إله إلا هو الحي القيوم لا تأخذه سنة ولا نوم»: in it He made clear His upholding, Glory be to Him, the management of creation and the ordering of their affairs, the perfecting of their livelihoods and His dominion over it without being heedless of it for the blink of an eye [Translator's note: the source reads «همينته» and «معايشتهم»; translated as «هيمنته» (dominion) and «معايشهم» (livelihoods)].
(b) The second sentence: «له ما في السموات وما في الأرض»: in it He made clear that He is the owner of what He manages, uncontested in His ownership.
(c) The third sentence: «من ذا الذي يشفع عنده إلا بإذنه»: in it He made clear the majesty of His station and the diminutiveness of everyone before His limitless power.
(d) The fourth sentence: «ولا يحيطون بشيء من علمه إلا بما شاء»: in it He depicted His encompassing of the affairs and conditions of creation such that nothing is hidden from Him.
(e) The fifth sentence: «وسع كرسيه السموات والأرض» to the end of the verse: in it He proclaimed His relation to all that is known, and that everything with Him is by measure.
3- Concision of concision (ījāz al-ījāz): Āyat al-Kursī contains what no other verse of Allah, Glory be to Him, contains, for it comprises seventeen places in which the name of Allah the Exalted appears, overt in some and latent in others, in the following order:
1- الله, 2- هو, 3- الحي, 4- القيوم, 5- the pronoun in لا تأخذه, 6- the pronoun in له, 7- the pronoun in عنده, 8- the pronoun in بإذنه, 9- the pronoun in يعلم, 10- the pronoun in علمه, 11- the pronoun in شاء, 12- the pronoun in كرسيه, 13- the pronoun in يئوده, 14- وهو, 15- العلي, 16- العظيم, 17- the latent pronoun contained in the maṣdar «حفظهما», for it is a maṣdar annexed to its object, which is the overt pronoun, and it must have an agent, namely Allah. This appears when the maṣdar is unpacked, so that one says:
ولا يئوده أن يحفظهما هو ("nor does it burden Him that He should guard them").
One of the eminent scholars tried to bring them to twenty-one places, considering that the derived nouns occurring in it need a pronoun, such as الحي, القيوم, العلي and العظيم, so each of them counts as two, and thereby four places are added to the seventeen, making a total of twenty-one. Another eminent scholar disputed with him and said: this is very subtle, but a derived noun applies to what it describes only on account of its bearing a pronoun, so it cannot be distinguished, by virtue of standing alone, from the pronoun; therefore the derived noun does not bear a pronoun after it has become a proper name through naming. Do you not see that when you say:
زيد كريم, «كريم» applies to Zayd only because it bears his pronoun, so that if you consider it by itself you do not find it specific to Zayd, but you may apply it to anyone of mankind described by generosity. This is among the subtlest topics of the science of maʿānī, so ponder it, and may Allah protect you.

dervis-irab:256-257.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الطَّاغُوتُ): every object of worship besides Allah; the plural is طواغ and طواغيت. There is much disagreement about this word; it may be singular or plural, masculine or feminine. The Exalted said in al-Zumar: «والذين اجتنبوا الطاغوت أن يعبدوها».
More discussion of it will come.
(العروة الوثقى) العروة originally: the place of gripping by the hand, and the root denotes attachment. The ʿurwa of a bucket or jug is its handle; of a garment, the sister of its button; and one says اعتراه الهمّ when grief clung to him. He said:
وإني لتعروني لذكراك هزّة ... كما انتفض العصفور بلّله القطر
(A tremor seizes me at the thought of you, as the sparrow shakes when the rain has drenched it.)
(الْوُثْقى): on the pattern fuʿlā of the elative, the feminine of الأوثق, like فضلى as the feminine of الأفضل. Its plural is وُثَق; it is what one trusts and clings to.
(انْفِصامَ): breaking off; the origin of الفصم is breaking.

* I'rab:
(لا إِكْراهَ فِي الدِّينِ) A resumptive sentence, introduced to show that the rational person does not need to be compelled into religion, but chooses the true religion spontaneously. لا is the lā of generic negation; إكراه is its noun; and في الدين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar. (قَدْ تَبَيَّنَ الرُّشْدُ مِنَ الْغَيِّ) The clause is justificatory with no grammatical position; قد is a particle of affirmation; تبين is a past verb and الرشد its agent; and من الغي is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تبين. (فَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِالطَّاغُوتِ) The fā' is the eloquent fā'; من is a conditional noun governing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ; يكفر is the jussive protasis and its agent is a latent pronoun referring to «من»; and بالطاغوت is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يكفر. (وَيُؤْمِنْ بِاللَّهِ) The wāw is a conjunction; يؤمن is conjoined to يكفر; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يؤمن. (فَقَدِ اسْتَمْسَكَ بِالْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقى) The fā' links the apodosis because it is accompanied by قد; استمسك is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun referring to من; بالعروة is attached to استمسك; and الوثقى is an adjective of العروة. The clause accompanied by the fā' is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis; the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of من; and the clause «من يكفر» has no grammatical position because it is the answer to a non-jussive-governing conditional [Translator's note: the source says «غير حازم», sic, for «غير جازم»; the statement itself is as written]. (لَا انْفِصامَ لَها) The clause is in the position of an accusative ḥāl from العروة; لا is the lā of generic negation; انفصام is its noun, indeclinable on fatḥa; and لها is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted khabar of لا. (وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ) The clause is either resumptive, introduced to move people to faith and deter them from disbelief, or a parenthetical appended remark (iʿtirāḍ tadhyīlī) serving that same aim; اللَّه is a mubtadaʾ and سميع عليم are its two khabars. (اللَّهُ وَلِيُّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) The clause is resumptive, to show the excellence in the bringing out; اللَّه is a mubtadaʾ, ولي a khabar, الذين a muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause آمنوا a ṣila. (يُخْرِجُهُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ) The clause is either a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in «ولي», or a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ «الله»; من الظلمات is attached to يخرجهم, and إلى النور is attached to يخرجهم, because the two meanings differ, i.e. beginning from the darknesses and ending at the light; or it is a ḥāl from the relative noun. (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا) The wāw is a conjunction; الذين is a mubtadaʾ and the clause كفروا is the ṣila. (أَوْلِياؤُهُمُ الطَّاغُوتُ) A mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the nominal sentence is the khabar of الذين, the link being the pronoun. (يُخْرِجُونَهُمْ مِنَ النُّورِ إِلَى الظُّلُماتِ) The i'rab of its like has preceded. (أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ) A mubtadaʾ and khabar; النار is a muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause is circumstantial. (هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ) A mubtadaʾ and khabar; فيها is attached to خالدون; and the clause is a second ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
1- العروة الوثقى is an explicit, representational metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tamthīliyya): he likened the one who follows the path of Allah to one who has taken hold of a firm, safe rope that does not break, so he is safe from slipping and from falling into the pits of error and misguidance.
2- Explicit metaphor in borrowing darknesses and light for misguidance and guidance.
3- In his words, the Exalted, «يخرجونهم من النور إلى الظلمات» is the art of negating a thing by affirming it (nafy al-shayʾ bi-ījābih), a wonderful art whose gist is that the speaker affirms something in his speech and figuratively negates what stems from it, the thing actually negated in the inner part of the speech being the very thing he affirmed. The upshot of what we have said is that those who disbelieved had never had light from which they could be brought out; the outward sense of the speech may suggest that they originally had light and were then brought out of it, whereas what is meant is the negation of light from them altogether. Like it is the saying of Muslim ibn al-Walīd, known as Ṣarīʿ al-Ghawānī:
لا يعبق الطيب خديه ومفرقه ... ولا يمسح عينيه من الكحل
(Perfume does not scent his cheeks and the parting of his hair, nor does he wipe kohl from his eyes.)
And like it is the saying of Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
أفدي ظباء فلاة ما عرفن بها ... مضغ الكلام ولا صبغ الحواجيب
ولا برزن من الحمّام ماثلة ... أوراكهنّ صقيلات العراقيب
(I would ransom the gazelles of the open plain who knew there neither chewing of words nor dyeing of eyebrows, nor did they come out of the bath with their hips swaying and their heels polished.)
The outward sense of the speech is that they did not come out of the bath in that condition, while what is meant in its inner part is that there was no bath at all; more on it will come in this book.
It is also possible that it is a case of mushākala (conformity), which has preceded. Its gist is that the mention of the second bringing-out conforms to the first, along the lines of the saying «قلت اطبخوا لي جبة وقميصا» ("I said, cook me a jubba and a shirt"), while granting that "those who disbelieved" means those who never had faith at all; so ponder.
4- He made darknesses plural and light singular for a wonderful rhetorical secret. It contains an allusion to the oneness of the truth and the multiplicity of kinds of darknesses, which are the misguidances, and how many they are; and because the path of truth is clear in its landmarks, without confusion, and without branching in its ways, whereas the path of misguidance is confused for whoever travels it.

dervis-irab:49-49.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَسُومُونَكُمْ): from سامه خسفا, when he inflicted injustice upon him. ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm said:
إذا الملك سام الناس خسفا ... أبينا أن نقرّ الذّلّ فينا
(When the king inflicts humiliation on the people, we refuse to let disgrace settle among us.)
Its origin is from سام السلعة, when he asked for it (the price of the goods).
(بَلاءٌ): affliction and testing.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ) The wāw is a conjunction, and إذ is an adverb of past time attached to an implied "اذكر"; it has been discussed before. (نَجَّيْناكُمْ) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn; نا is an attached pronoun in the nominative position as fāʿil, and the kāf is an attached pronoun in the accusative position as direct object; the clause is in the genitive position by the annexation of the adverb to it. (مِنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to نجيناكم; فرعون is muḍāf ilayhi, its sign of genitive being the fatḥa in place of the kasra because it is a diptote, being a proper name and foreign. "Pharaoh" is applied to everyone who ruled the Amalekites in Egypt, like Caesar for the king of the Romans and Chosroes for the king of the Persians. (يَسُومُونَكُمْ) the clause is in the accusative position as ḥāl, and it may be resumptive. (سُوءَ الْعَذابِ) second direct object, because سام is transitive to two; it may also be accusative as a maṣdar, in which case it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "they inflict upon you an infliction of the evil of punishment". (يُذَبِّحُونَ) the clause is explicative (tafsīriyya) with no position; you may also make it a badal for the clause يسومونكم. (أَبْناءَكُمْ) direct object. (وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ) conjoined to يذبحون; al-istiḥyāʾ is sparing alive. (نِساءَكُمْ) object of يستحيون; نساء is a plural of نسوة, and نسوة is a plural of امرأة in meaning; it was also said that النسوة and النساء are both plurals of امرأة by meaning. (وَفِي ذلِكُمْ) The wāw is resumptive, and the preposition and its genitive noun are an advanced khabar. (بَلاءٌ) delayed mubtadaʾ. (مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of بلاء. (عَظِيمٌ) second adjective of بلاء.

dervis-irab:50-52.t:
* Vocabulary:
(واعَدْنا) and وعدنا are of one meaning; it is not of the chapter of mufāʿala that requires participation, like your saying عافاه الله ("may Allah grant him well-being") and عاقبت اللص ("I punished the thief").
(مُوسى): a foreign proper name, not fully declined. It is originally a compound; the original is موشى with the dotted shīn, because water in Hebrew is called مو and tree is called شا; the Arabs Arabised it and said موسى. As for the well-known موسى, the razor, it is derived from ماس يميس when one struts in his walk, and the yāʾ was changed to wāw because it came after a ḍamma, as in موقن, because the razor moves at the throat with it; it was also said it is derived from أوسيت رأسه when you shaved it. The razor is both masculine and feminine, and is pluralised as مواسي and موسيات.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ) its i'rab has been given often. (فَرَقْنا) verb and fāʿil; the clause is in the genitive position by the annexation of the adverb to it. (بِكُمُ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to فرقنا, or to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "we split it in association with you"; the meaning is that the splitting of the sea took place by your entering it. (الْبَحْرَ) direct object. (فَأَنْجَيْناكُمْ وَأَغْرَقْنا) likewise conjunctions. (آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ) direct object, and فرعون is muḍāf ilayhi. (وَأَنْتُمْ) a detached pronoun in the nominative position as mubtadaʾ. (تَنْظُرُونَ) the verbal clause is in the nominative position as the khabar of أنتم, and the nominal clause is in the accusative position as ḥāl from the kāf in أنجيناكم.
(وَإِذْ) conjoined to the first إذ. (واعَدْنا) the clause is in the genitive position by the annexation of the adverb to it. (مُوسى) first direct object. (أَرْبَعِينَ) second direct object; it is not permissible to make it accusative as an adverb because the meaning would be spoiled, since the promise was not made within forty nights; its sign of accusative is the yāʾ because it is joined to the sound masculine plural. (لَيْلَةً) an overt specification (tamyīz), and the governor in this kind is the numeral noun before it. (ثُمَّ) a conjunction of order with delay. (اتَّخَذْتُمُ) conjoined to واعدنا. (الْعِجْلَ) first direct object, and the second object is omitted because it is understood from the context, i.e. "as a god". (مِنْ بَعْدِهِ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَأَنْتُمْ) The wāw is circumstantial, and أنتم is a mubtadaʾ. (ظالِمُونَ) its khabar; the nominal clause is in the accusative position as ḥāl. (ثُمَّ عَفَوْنا) conjoined to what preceded. (عَنْكُمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to عفونا. (مِنْ بَعْدِ ذلِكَ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; the demonstrative points to the maṣdar understood from اتخذ, i.e. "after that taking". (لَعَلَّكُمْ) laʿalla with its ism. (تَشْكُرُونَ) the verbal clause is in the nominative position as the khabar of لعل, and the clause of hope is circumstantial.

[Translator's note: the printed text gives «أي إليها» ("i.e. to it") for the omitted second object of اتخذتم; I have rendered the sense "as a god", which is not in the source text, and have marked it here as my addition for clarity.]

dervis-irab:53-54.t:
* Vocabulary:
(لِقَوْمِهِ): al-qawm is a collective noun with no singular from its own wording; its singular is rather "imruʾ" (man), and by analogy it should not be pluralised, but its pluralisation is irregular: they said aqwām, and a plural of its plural, they said aqāwīm. It was said to be specific to men. Allah the Exalted said: «لا يسخر قوم من قوم ... ولا نساء من نساء», and Zuhayr said:
وما أدري وسوف إخال أدري ... أقوم آل حصن أم نساء
(I do not know — and I shall think I know — whether the family of Ḥiṣn are men or women.)
And it was said that it is not specific to men but applies to men and women. Allah the Exalted said: «إنا أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه». The first view is more correct, and the inclusion of women in "qawm" here is by extension, giving precedence to men over women. They were called qawm because they "stand up" (yaqūmūna) for affairs.
(بارِئِكُمْ): al-bāriʾ is the Creator; it is said برأ الله الخلق, i.e. He created them. The origin of the root برأ indicates the separation of a thing and its distinction from something; it is said برأ المريض من مرضه when the illness leaves him and separates from him; and برىء المدين من دينه when the debt leaves him and falls from him. From it comes al-Bāriʾ among the attributes of Allah the Exalted, because He is the One who brought creation out of non-existence and separated them from it into existence.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ) discussed before. (آتَيْنا) verb and fāʿil; the clause is in the genitive position by the annexation of the adverb to it. (مُوسَى) first direct object. (الْكِتابَ) second direct object. (وَالْفُرْقانَ) The wāw is a conjunction, and الفرقان is conjoined to الكتاب; what is meant by "the Book" is the Torah, and by "the Criterion" what distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and guidance from error, conjoined to it although the meaning is one. (لَعَلَّكُمْ) laʿalla with its ism. (تَهْتَدُونَ) the verbal clause is the khabar of لعل, and the clause of hope is circumstantial. (وَإِذْ قالَ مُوسى) conjoined to what preceded. (لِقَوْمِهِ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to قال. (يا قَوْمِ) yā is a vocative particle, and قوم is a vocative annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person. (إِنَّكُمْ) inna and its ism. (ظَلَمْتُمْ) the verbal clause is the khabar of inna. (أَنْفُسَكُمْ) direct object. (بِاتِّخاذِكُمُ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to ظلمتم; the bāʾ is causal, i.e. "because of your taking". (الْعِجْلَ) direct object of the maṣdar اتخاذ. (فَتُوبُوا) The fāʾ is explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya), because wrongdoing is the cause of repentance, and توبوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable with the omission of the nūn. (إِلى بارِئِكُمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to توبوا. (فَاقْتُلُوا) The fāʾ is a conjunction of immediate succession. (أَنْفُسَكُمْ) direct object; the meaning of the killing will come in the chapter on Rhetoric. (ذلِكُمْ) a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. (خَيْرٌ) khabar. (لَكُمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to خير, because it is a superlative (ism tafḍīl) contrary to analogy, the analogy being "akhyar"; likewise شر, whose analogy is "ashar". (عِنْدَ) an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl. (بارِئِكُمْ) muḍāf ilayhi. (فَتابَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction upon an omitted clause, the implied form being "so you did what He commanded you, and He relented". (عَلَيْكُمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to تاب. (إِنَّهُ) inna and its ism. (هُوَ) a separating pronoun or support, with no position. (التَّوَّابُ) the first khabar of inna. (الرَّحِيمُ) the second khabar of inna; or هو is a mubtadaʾ with التواب الرحيم as its two khabars, and the nominal clause as the khabar of inna.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying: «فاقتلوا أنفسكم» there is a majāz mursal (unrestricted figurative usage) whose relation is regard for what a thing leads to, i.e. "give yourselves up to be killed as a purification for them", that is, so that this judgment issued may be carried out; and this is one of the views about the killing. It was also said that what is meant by killing the selves is humbling them and curbing their wildness, for "killing" comes in the sense of humbling; from it is the saying of Ḥassān ibn Thābit in describing wine:
إن التي ناولتني فرددتها ... قتلت، قتلت، فهاتها لم تقتل
(The one you handed me and I sent back — it has been "killed", "killed"; so bring it to me unkilled.)
He meant mixing it with water so that its sharpness goes away.
2- Iltifāt (shift of person) in His saying: «فتاب عليكم»; the iltifāt here is from the first person that the course of the speech requires, since the requirement of the context was for Him to say: "so I guided you and relented toward you".

dervis-irab:55-56.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ) discussed before. (قُلْتُمْ) verb and fāʿil; the clause is in the genitive position by the annexation of the adverb to it. (يا) a vocative particle for a mid-distance addressee. (مُوسى) a singular proper-name vocative. (لَنْ) a particle of negation, accusative and futurity. (نُؤْمِنَ) an imperfect verb made accusative by لن, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "نحن"; the clause is reported speech. (لَكَ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to نؤمن. (حَتَّى) a particle of limit and of genitive. (نَرَى) an imperfect verb made accusative by an obligatorily implied أن after حتى. (اللَّهَ) direct object. (جَهْرَةً) absolute object, because it is a maṣdar of جهر, i.e. "he recited in a loud voice", so it stands in the position of that which is seen with the eye; it may also be parsed in the accusative as ḥāl, i.e. "seeing openly". (فَأَخَذَتْكُمُ) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and أخذتكم is a past verb; the tāʾ is the silent tāʾ of the feminine, and the kāf is an attached pronoun in the accusative position as an advanced direct object. (الصَّاعِقَةُ) fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to قلتم. (وَأَنْتُمْ) The wāw is circumstantial, and أنتم is a detached pronoun in the nominative position as mubtadaʾ. (تَنْظُرُونَ) an imperfect verb, the wāw being the fāʿil; the clause تنظرون is the khabar of أنتم, and the clause أنتم تنظرون is in the accusative position as ḥāl. (ثُمَّ) a conjunction of order with delay. (بَعَثْناكُمْ) a past verb, fāʿil and direct object. (مِنْ بَعْدِ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to بعثناكم. (مَوْتِكُمْ) muḍāf ilayhi. (لَعَلَّكُمْ) laʿalla with its ism, and the clause (تَشْكُرُونَ) is its khabar; and the clause بعثناكم is conjoined to the clause فأخذتكم.

dervis-irab:233-233.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الحول): the year, because it "turns" (taḥūlu), that is, passes; the plural is ḥuʾūl «[Translator's note: the source prints ḥiʾūl/ḥuʾūl with a hamza, apparently for ḥuwūl]», with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, and aḥwāl. One says of a woman "she gives birth only to taḥāwīl", that is, she bears one year and the next year does not bear. And ḥawliyyāt Zuhayr are his long poems, whose composition takes up a whole year.
(تُضَارَّ): the imperfect of ḍārra with shadda on the rāʾ, and for that reason its last letter takes fatḥa, as will come.
(الفصال): with kasra on the fāʾ, weaning before two years; faṣalat al-umm raḍīʿahā means the mother weaned her suckling. This is the time of its faṣāl, as one says the time of its fiṭām.

* I'rab:
(وَالْوالِداتُ): the waw is a conjunction or resumptive, and the clause is conjoined or resumptive, introduced to complete these rulings; and الوالدات is a mubtadaʾ. (يُرْضِعْنَ): an imperfect verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and the nūn is the agent. (أَوْلادَهُنَّ): a direct object; the clause is the khabar of الوالدات. (حَوْلَيْنِ): an adverb of time attached to يرضعن. (كامِلَيْنِ): an adjective, because it is something about which one is lenient: you say "I stayed with so-and-so two years" without having completed them. (لِمَنْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "that ruling is for the one who"; the clause is resumptive. (أَرادَ أَنْ يُتِمَّ الرَّضاعَةَ): the clause أراد has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of من, and أن and what is within its scope is in the interpretation of a maṣdar, a direct object. «من» then applies to the mother, as if it were said: "for the one among the mothers who wants to complete the suckling". It is also permissible to attach the preposition and its genitive noun to يرضعن, so that it applies to the father, as if it were said: "for the sake of the one among the fathers who wants to complete the suckling". (وَعَلَى الْمَوْلُودِ لَهُ رِزْقُهُنَّ وَكِسْوَتُهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): the waw is a conjunction; على المولود is attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and له is a preposition and its genitive noun in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʾil of المولود, because it is a passive participle. And رزقهن is a delayed mubtadaʾ, and كسوتهن is conjoined to it. And بالمعروف is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (لا تُكَلَّفُ نَفْسٌ إِلَّا وُسْعَها): the clause is explicative and has no grammatical position; لا is negative, تكلف is a passive imperfect verb, نفس is the nāʾib fāʾil, إلا is a particle of restriction, and وسعها is a second direct object. Kallafa, with shadda on the lām, is a verb that takes two objects. ʿUrwa said:
يكلفني عمي ثلاثين ناقة ... ومالي يا عفراء غير ثمان
(My uncle burdens me with thirty she-camels, while I have, O ʿAfrāʾ, only eight.)
So the yāʾ is the first object and ثلاثين the second object. (لا تُضَارَّ والِدَةٌ بِوَلَدِها): لا is prohibitive and تضار is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, its sign of jussive being sukūn, and the fatḥa has taken its place for lightness in the doubled verb; the verb is passive. In the Seven readings it was also read with ḍamma on the rāʾ of تضار, on the basis that «لا» is negative. والدة is the nāʾib fāʾil, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تضار; the clause is a ḥāl. (وَلا مَوْلُودٌ لَهُ بِوَلَدِهِ): conjoined to what precedes; the bāʾ in both cases is for cause, that is, the child is annexed to her at one time and to him at another, as a kind of appeal to each of the two parents and an entreaty that they take care of him and work for his good, so that he may not be a cause of harming them. For this reason some of the astute among the Qur'an's parsers made it redundant, but there is no need to claim redundancy. (وَعَلَى الْوارِثِ مِثْلُ ذلِكَ): the waw is a conjunction; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and مثل ذلك is a delayed mubtadaʾ. (فَإِنْ أَرادا فِصالًا): the fāʾ is resumptive and the clause is resumptive, introduced to exhaust the ruling in this social matter. إن is conditional; أرادا is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis, the alif is the agent, and فصالا is the direct object. (عَنْ تَراضٍ مِنْهُما وَتَشاوُرٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of فصالا; منهما is an adjective of تراض, and تشاور is conjoined to تراض. (فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْهِما): the fāʾ links the apodosis; لا is the lā of generic negation, جناح is its noun and عليهما its khabar; the clause is the apodosis. (وَإِنْ أَرَدْتُمْ أَنْ تَسْتَرْضِعُوا أَوْلادَكُمْ): the waw is a conjunction and إن is conditional; أردتم is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis, and the tāʾ is the agent; أن and what is within its scope is in the interpretation of a maṣdar, a direct object of أردتم; and أولادكم is a second direct object of تسترضعوا, the first object being omitted. The meaning is: "that you seek wet nurses for your children". Sībawayh stated this i'rab; al-Shihāb, in his gloss on al-Bayḍāwī, noted that arḍaʿa takes one object, and if the sīn and tāʾ are added to it, it takes two; and al-Zamakhsharī also followed this. It was also said that it takes the second object only through a preposition, so أولادكم would be accusative by removal of the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun would be in the place of the second object. Al-Zajjāj said the implied form is: "that you seek for your children a nurse other than the mother". (فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ): its i'rab has gone before. (إِذا سَلَّمْتُمْ ما آتَيْتُمْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): إذا is an adverb of future time governing its protasis in the genitive and itself accusative through its omitted apodosis; the clause سلمتم is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; ما is a relative noun in the position of the accusative as direct object; the clause آتيتم has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila; and بالمعروف is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ): the waw is resumptive. The clause «اتقوا الله», consisting of a verb, an agent and a direct object, is resumptive, introduced to stress the safeguarding of what has been legislated concerning children and wet nurses and not neglecting their rights. (وَاعْلَمُوا): conjoined to واتقوا. (أَنَّ اللَّهَ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ): أن and what follows stand in place of the two objects of اعلموا; the clause تعملون is the ṣila of ما, and بصير is the khabar of أن.

* Benefits:
The doubled verb (al-fiʿl al-muḍaʿʿaf), when it is jussive or built on sukūn, admits three dialects:
1- Fatḥa in every case, which in our view is preferable because of its lightness on the tongue.
2- Kasra in every case, as if they likened it to the meeting of two sukūns.
3- Following the vowel of the first radical (ittibāʿ). The saying of Jarīr has been transmitted with all three dialects:
فغضّ الطرف إنك من نمير ... فلا كعبا بلغت ولا كلابا
(So lower your gaze, for you are of Numayr; you have reached neither Kaʿb nor Kilāb.)

dervis-irab:6-7.t:
* Vocabulary:
(سَواءٌ): a noun meaning equality (istiwāʾ), treated like the maṣdars, and for this reason it is neither dualised nor pluralised. They said "humā wa-hum sawāʾ" ("the two of them and they are alike"). When they want the dual wording they say sayyān, and if you wish you may say sawāʾān; and in the plural, hum aswāʾ, and also, contrary to analogy, hum sawās and sawāsiya, meaning "two who are equal" and "persons who are equal". And sawāʾ is the just middle between two limits. One says "ḍaraba sawāʾahu", meaning "he struck its middle", and "ji'tuhu fī sawāʾ al-nahār", meaning "in the middle of the day". When sawāʾ is followed by the hamza of equalisation (hamzat al-taswiya), there must be an «أم» whether the two items are two nouns or two verbs; and if it is followed by two verbs without the hamza of equalisation, the second is conjoined with «أو», as in "sawāʾun ʿalayya qumta aw qaʿadta"; and if it is followed by two maṣdars, the second is conjoined with wāw or with «أو», as in "sawāʾun ʿalayya qiyāmuka wa-quʿūduka" and "qiyāmuka aw quʿūduka". (غِشاوَةٌ): the pattern fiʿāla from ghashāhu or ghashiyahu, when he covered it. This pattern is for what envelops a thing, like the headband (ʿiṣāba) and the turban (ʿasāma) [Translator's note: so in the source; ʿasāma is presumably a slip for ʿimāma]. In the ghayn, kasra, ḍamma and fatḥa are all permitted.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ): inna and its noun; and the clause (كَفَرُوا), consisting of verb and agent, has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative. (سَواءٌ): a fronted khabar, or the khabar of inna. (عَلَيْهِمْ): a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «سواء». (أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ): the interrogative hamza has the meaning of equalisation; it and the verb after it are, in interpretation, a maṣdar, a postponed mubtadaʾ, or the agent of sawāʾ, which is treated like the maṣdars [Translator's note: the source reads «فاعل نسواء», evidently a misprint for «لسواء»]; and the clause is the khabar of inna. (أَمْ): a connective (ʿāṭifa muttaṣila); its ruling will come in the section of benefits. (لَمْ تُنْذِرْهُمْ): lam is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; «تنذرهم» is an imperfect verb jussive through lam, its agent a latent pronoun obligatorily implied, its implied form being "you"; and the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative, a direct object; and the clause is conjoined to the clause «أأنذرتهم». (لا): negative. (يُؤْمِنُونَ): a nominative imperfect verb, the sign of its nominative case being the retention of the nūn, the wāw an agent; the clause «لا يؤمنون» is a khabar after a khabar, and you may make it explicative, with no grammatical position. (خَتَمَ): past verb. (اللَّهُ): agent. (عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «ختم». (وَعَلى سَمْعِهِمْ): conjoined to the saying «على قلوبهم». (وَعَلى أَبْصارِهِمْ): the wāw is resumptive, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (غِشاوَةٌ): postponed mubtadaʾ. (وَلَهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element. (عَذابٌ): postponed mubtadaʾ. (عَظِيمٌ): naʿt of «عذاب»; and the clause is conjoined to the preceding clause.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the ascription of sealing to the hearts there is a representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya): their hearts, in their recoiling from the truth and not listening to it, are likened to hearts upon which Allah has set a seal, namely the hearts of beasts; it is a likening of an intelligible to a sensible. Or it is a rational trope (majāz ʿaqlī), which is a wide chapter among the Arabs: they say "the valley flowed with them" when they perished, and "the ʿanqāʾ flew away with so-and-so" when his absence was long.
2- The hearing is given in the singular because the thing heard is one, unlike the hearts and the eyes, because of the diversity of what is perceived and what is seen.
3- The indefiniteness of «العذاب» here points to its being a kind of it whose quantity and quality are unknown, and its description as «عظيم» is to remove the suggestion of its being little or rare, and to emphasise that it reaches the extreme of greatness.

* Benefits:
1- The hamza of equalisation is the one that falls after sawāʾ and after mā ubālī, mā adrī and laytā shiʿrī; and its rule is: it is the hamza that enters a clause in whose place a maṣdar can be put, as previously stated.
2- «أم» has two states:
(a) Connected (muttaṣila), confined to two kinds, because it is preceded either by the hamza of equalisation, as in the verse, or by a hamza with which specification is sought, as in:
أزيد في الدّار أم عمرو؟
("Is Zayd in the house, or ʿAmr?")
It is called muttaṣila because what comes before it and after it cannot dispense with each other; it is also called muʿādila (equating), because it equates the hamza in the first kind, since both indicate equalisation.
(b) Disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), which is preceded by a pure statement, as in the saying of the Exalted: «تنزيل الكتاب لا ريب فيه من رب العالمين أم يقولون افتراه». It is called munqaṭiʿa because what is after it is cut off from what is before it, each being an independent speech with no connection to the other.

dervis-irab:8-10.t:
* Vocabulary:
(النَّاسِ): a collective noun (ism jamʿ) with no singular from its wording and its root. According to Sībawayh and al-Farrāʾ, the root is hamza, nūn, sīn, and its hamza was dropped irregularly, its original being unās; and the Qur'an has spoken with this original: the Exalted said: «يوم ندعو كلّ أناس بإمامهم». Al-Kisāʾī held that its root is nūn, wāw, sīn, derived from al-naws, which is movement; one says nāsa yanūsu nawsan, and al-naws is the swaying of a thing in the air, and from it is the swaying (naws) of the earring in the ear. Abū Nuwās was so called because two locks of hair used to sway at his ears [Translator's note: the source reads «كاتنا», evidently «كانتا»]; his real name is al-Ḥasan ibn Hāniʾ. We have lengthened this discussion only because some modern dictionaries have confused its origin, listing it under the root anas while others list it under nawas, and thereby they lost the student and the consulter in mazes with no exits.
(يُخادِعُونَ): khidāʿ originally means concealing; from it come the two akhdaʿān, which are two veins hidden in the neck, and from it also al-mikhdaʿ, the inner part of the house; then it came to be used for showing something other than what is in the soul.
(يَشْعُرُونَ): shuʿūr is perceiving a thing from an aspect that is subtle and hidden. It is derived from shiʿr (hair) because of its fineness; it was also said that it is perception by the sense, derived from al-shiʿār, the garment next to the body, and mashāʿir al-insān are his senses. Shaʿara bi-l-amr, of the patterns naṣara and karuma, means he knew of it and understood it, and from it the poet (shāʿir) is so called, for his acuteness and the subtlety of his knowledge. The correct view is that shuʿūr is the perception of what is subtle, whether sensory or mental.
(مَرَضٌ): maraḍ is the maṣdar of mariḍa, and in the language it is applied to weakness and languor. They said: sickness in the heart is languor toward the truth; in the body, the languor of the limbs; in the eye, the languor of the gaze, and this is beautiful, sung by the poets. He said:
مرضي من مريضة الأجفان ... علّلاني بذكرها علّلاني
(My sickness is from one with languid eyelids; console me, console me with mention of her.)
Maraḍ is also applied meaning darkness. He said:
في ليلة مرضت من كلّ ناحية ... فما يحس بها نجم ولا قمر
(On a night that was sick on every side, so neither star nor moon was felt in it.)

* I'rab:
(وَمِنَ النَّاسِ): the wāw is resumptive, and the speech is a new start, brought to mention the hypocrites who believed with their tongues and disbelieved with their hearts. He, glory be to Him, began with mention of the God-fearing, then followed with the disbelievers outwardly and inwardly, and third with the hypocrites. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (مِنَ): a relative noun in the position of nominative, a postponed mubtadaʾ; it is also permissible that «من» be an indefinite described noun in the position of nominative, a postponed mubtadaʾ, as though it were said "and among the people are people"; its discussion will come. (يَقُولُ): a nominative imperfect verb, its agent a latent pronoun implied in it, its implied form being "he"; the verbal clause has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of «من» if it is relative, and an adjective of it if it is an indefinite described noun. (آمَنَّا): verb and agent; the verbal clause is in the position of accusative, the thing said. (بِاللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «آمنا». (وَبِالْيَوْمِ): conjoined to «بالله». (الْآخِرِ): naʿt of «اليوم». (وَما): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «ما» is a Ḥijāzī negative that works like laysa. (هُمْ): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative, the noun of mā. (بِمُؤْمِنِينَ): the bāʾ is a redundant preposition for emphasis, because there is no redundant preposition in the Qur'an, but it is the grammatical convention that has so run; for the rhetoricians it is a particle that cannot be dispensed with. The nominal clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (يُخادِعُونَ): an imperfect verb, the sign of its nominative case being the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs, the wāw an agent; the verbal clause is resumptive, as though it were asked "Why do they feign belief?" and it was said "they deceive"; it may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun latent in «يقول», that is, "deceiving Allah and those who believe". (اللَّهَ): direct object of «يخادعون». (وَالَّذِينَ): conjoined to «الله». (آمَنُوا): the verbal clause has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative. (وَما): the wāw is circumstantial and «ما» is negative. (يَخْدَعُونَ): an imperfect verb, the sign of its nominative case being the retention of the nūn, the wāw an agent. (إِلَّا): a particle of restriction. (أَنْفُسَهُمْ): direct object, and the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of genitive by annexation. (وَما): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive, and «ما» is negative. (يَشْعُرُونَ): a nominative imperfect verb; the clause is conjoined to the clause «وما يخدعون», or resumptive. (فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are a fronted khabar. (مَرَضٌ): postponed mubtadaʾ. (فَزادَهُمُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «زاد» is a past verb, and the hāʾ [Translator's note: the source says "hāʾ", the pronoun being «هم»] is a direct object; the clause is conjoined to what the khabar is attached to; it is possible that the fāʾ is resumptive and the clause «زادهم الله» is optative (duʿāʾiyya), with no position. (اللَّهُ): agent of «زادهم». (مَرَضاً): second direct object; and «زاد» is used both intransitively and transitively to two objects, the second not being the first. (وَلَهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive, and the preposition and its genitive noun are a fronted khabar. (عَذابٌ): postponed mubtadaʾ. (أَلِيمٌ): adjective of «عذاب». (بِما): the bāʾ is a preposition of cause, and «ما» is a relative noun in the position of genitive through the bāʾ. (كانُوا): kāna and its noun. (يَكْذِبُونَ): an imperfect verb and agent; the clause is the khabar of «كانوا», and the clause of kāna with its noun and khabar has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative. It is permissible that it be maṣdar-forming, and the meaning according to the first is "for that which they lie about", and according to the second "because of their lying". The preposition and its genitive noun are a second adjective of «عذاب», or a maṣdar, that is, "because of their lying".

* Rhetoric:
1- Isomorphism (mushākala) in their "deceiving Allah", because the form mufāʿala implies participation in the meaning; it was applied to Him, the Exalted, to correspond with what is mentioned of the hypocrites' deceit, like the answering of their scheming with scheming. An example of this art in poetry is the saying of one of them:
قالوا: التمس شيئا فجد لك طبخه ... قلت: اطبخوا لي جبة وقميصا
(They said: "Ask for something, and we will cook it for you." I said: "Cook me a cloak and a shirt.")
2- Trope: in the deceit ascribed to Him, because of their engaging in the acts of the deceiver, thinking that they can do so, given the truth of its negation; and so He said: «وما يخدعون إلا أنفسهم».
3- Explicit metaphor in His saying: «في قلوبهم مرض», where sickness is borrowed for the rust that has settled on their hearts of ignorance, evil belief and the like, the kinds of ignorance leading to destruction.

* Benefits:
1- «من» comes as an indefinite described noun in a position that is specific to indefinites, like the saying of Suwayd ibn Abī Kāhil:
ربّ من أنضجت غيظا قلبه ... لو تمنّى لي موتا لم يطع
(How many a one whose heart I cooked with rage; were he to wish me dead, he would not be able to.)
2- The Ḥijāzī mā is the one that works like laysa. It was called Ḥijāzī only because the revelation came in the dialect of the people of the Ḥijāz, and its rulings are set out in the books of grammar.

dervis-irab:26-27.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَسْتَحْيِي) Ḥayāʾ (shyness, modesty) is a change and shrinking that comes over a person from fear of what he may be blamed and censured for. Among the sayings of the Arabs: "So-and-so is shyer than a girl kept in her chamber." And Laylā said:
وأحيا حياء من فتاة حييّة ... وأشجع من ليث بخفّان حادر
(Shyer in modesty than a bashful girl, and braver than a thick-necked lion of Khaffān.)
(البعوض) the well-known biting insect; its derivation is from baʿḍ, which is cutting, and from it comes baʿḍ al-shayʾ ("part of a thing"), because it is a piece of it.
(النقض) annulment and undoing of arrangement.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ) a particle resembling a verb. (اللَّهَ) its accusative ism. (لا) negative. (يَسْتَحْيِي) an imperfect verb, nominative, whose fāʿil is latent (permissibly latent), its implied form being "He", referring to Allah; the verbal clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إن. (أَنْ يَضْرِبَ) أن is a maṣdar-forming particle governing the accusative, and يضرب is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied (permissibly implied) أن; أن with what follows it is in the interpretation of a maṣdar in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, if يستحيي is transitive by itself, or in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition; its discussion has come a little earlier. (مَثَلًا) mafʿūl bihi of يضرب. (ما) there are many views on it; the most preferable, in our view, is that it is the ibhāmiyya (indefinite-making) ما, which, when it accompanies an indefinite noun, adds to it spread, generality and vagueness. You say, "Give me a book, ما you want", that is, any book you wish. It is parsed as an adjective of the noun before it. (بَعُوضَةً) badal of مثلا. (فَما) the fāʾ is a conjunction and ما is a relative noun in the position of accusative, conjoined to بعوضة. (فَوْقَها) an adverb of place attached to an omitted word that has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. What is meant:
"what exceeds it" in the meaning for which the parable was coined, namely smallness and insignificance, or "what exceeds it in size", as though He intended thereby to answer their disdain at coining a parable with the fly and the spider, since both are bigger than the gnat. You say: "So-and-so does not mind being stingy with half a dirham or what is above it," meaning a dirham or two. Beautiful is the hadith of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in what Muslim relates from Ibrāhīm from al-Aswad, who said: Some young men of Quraysh entered upon ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, while she was at Minā, and they were laughing. She said, "What makes you laugh?" They said, "A man fell upon the rope of a tent, and his neck or his eye nearly went." She said, "Do not laugh, for I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'There is no Muslim who is pricked by a thorn, or by what is above it, except that a degree is written for him by it and a sin is erased from him.'" It may mean what is beyond the thorn and exceeds it in smallness, and it may mean what is more severe and painful than the thorn. (فَأَمَّا) the fāʾ is resumptive and أما is a particle of condition and distribution. (الَّذِينَ) a relative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (آمَنُوا) verb and agent; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of الذين. (فَيَعْلَمُونَ) the fāʾ links the apodosis, and يعلمون is an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of nominative being the persistence of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause يعلمون is in the position of nominative as the khabar of الذين. (أَنَّهُ) أنّ is a particle resembling a verb, and the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as its ism. (الْحَقُّ) its khabar; أن and what is within its scope take the place of the two objects of يعلمون. (مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَأَمَّا) the wāw is a conjunction and أما is a particle of condition and distribution. (الَّذِينَ) a relative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (كَفَرُوا) verb and agent; the clause has no position, being the ṣila of the relative noun. (فَيَقُولُونَ) the fāʾ links the apodosis, and يقولون is an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of nominative being the persistence of the nūn, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the relative noun. (ماذا) an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a fronted object of أراد; or ما is an interrogative noun and ذا a relative noun (in this case specifically) in the position of nominative as khabar of ما, and the clause is in the position of accusative as the content of the saying; on the first view the clause أراد is parsed as the content of the saying. (أَرادَ) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa. (اللَّهَ) fāʿil of أراد. (بِهذا) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أراد. (مَثَلًا) an emphatic tamyīz, or a ḥāl of the demonstrative, that is, "as an illustration by it", or of the fāʿil, that is, "illustrating". (يُضِلُّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, whose fāʿil is latent (permissibly latent), its implied form being "He"; the verbal clause is resumptive, running in the course of explanation and clarification of the two clauses introduced by أما. It is also said that it is in the position of accusative as an adjective of مثلا, the meaning being "a parable by which people are divided into the misguided and the guided". (بِهِ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يضل. (كَثِيراً) mafʿūl bihi. (وَيَهْدِي) conjoined to يضل. (بِهِ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يهدي. (كَثِيراً) mafʿūl bihi. (وَما يُضِلُّ) the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive, and ما is negative. (بِهِ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يضل. (إِلَّا) a particle of restriction. (الْفاسِقِينَ) mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position, or is circumstantial. (الَّذِينَ) a relative noun in the position of genitive because it is an adjective of الفاسقين. (يَنْقُضُونَ) an imperfect verb, nominative; the clause has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (عَهْدَ اللَّهِ) mafʿūl bihi and muḍāf ilayhi. (مِنْ بَعْدِ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ينقضون. (مِيثاقِهِ) muḍāf ilayhi; the pronoun returns to the name Allah or to al-ʿahd, and an interesting explanation of mīthāq will come in the Benefits section. (وَيَقْطَعُونَ) conjoined to His words ينقضون. (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (أَمَرَ) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa. (اللَّهِ) fāʿil of أمر. [Translator's note: the source shows الله with the genitive ending here, although it is the fāʿil.] (بِهِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أمر. (أَنْ يُوصَلَ) أن is a maṣdar-forming particle governing the accusative, and يوصل is a passive imperfect verb whose nāʾib fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "it"; أن and what is within its scope are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, a badal of the pronoun in به, the meaning being "and they sever what Allah ordered to be joined"; or it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, the implied form being "from dislike that it be joined" or "lest it be joined". (وَيُفْسِدُونَ) conjoined to يقطعون. (فِي الْأَرْضِ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يفسدون. (أُولئِكَ) a demonstrative noun, indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (هُمُ) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or ʿimād, with no position. (الْخاسِرُونَ) khabar of أولئك; and you may parse هم as mubtadaʾ and الخاسرون as its khabar, the nominal clause being in the position of nominative as khabar of أولئك.

* Rhetoric:
1- Parable-coining (tamthīl): the Arabs took great care over tamthīl, and the scholars of rhetoric mention two manifestations of it:
a- One is that the meaning appears from the outset in the form of a parable.
b- The other is what follows meanings to clarify them and establish them in the souls. In both cases it clothes meanings with splendour and beauty, raises their worth, stirs movement and life in them, and embodies them for the reader until he can almost feel them by touch. People have never ceased to coin parables with beasts, birds and insects. Among the finest that the Arabs composed in this is the book Kalīla wa-Dimna, which is said to have been translated from Persian by ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Muqaffaʿ; and in French there are the fables of La Fontaine.
It is related from al-Ḥasan and Qatāda: when Allah mentioned the fly and the spider in His Book and coined a parable of them for the polytheists, the Jews laughed and said, "This does not resemble the speech of Allah", so Allah, glory be to Him, sent down the verse. What supports the view that it was sent down about them is that it includes the breaking of covenants, which is among their most prominent traits. Our Arabic literature is full of parables drawn from various vermin and all insects. Their poet said:
وإنّي لألقى من ذوي الضغن منهم ... وما أصبحت تشكو من الوجد ساهره
كما لقيت ذات الصفا من خليلها ... وما انفكت الأمثال في الناس سائره
(I meet from those of them who bear rancour, and the sleepless one does not complain of passion, what Dhāt al-Ṣafā met from her friend; and proverbs have never ceased to travel among people.) Dhāt al-Ṣafā: the Arab legend says she had killed a relative of her ally, so they pledged by Allah that she would pay the blood-money for that slain man... to the end of that delightful legend.
2- The implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya) in His words: «ينقضون عهد الله». He likened the covenant to a twisted rope, then omitted the thing likened to and hinted at it by something of its characteristics or necessary attributes, namely unravelling, because it is one of the two states of a rope, which are unravelling and twisting.
3- Antithetical balance (muqābala), which is a multiplicity of antitheses (ṭibāq) in speech. He made antitheses between يضل and يهدي and between يقطعون and يوصل.

* Benefits:
1- (أمّا) is a particle of condition and distribution. Its first mīm may be replaced by yāʾ out of dislike for doubling, as in the saying of ʿAmr ibn Abī Rabīʿa:
رأت رجلا أيما إذا الشمس عارضت ... فيضحي وأيما بالعشيّ فيخصر
(She saw a man who, when the sun faces him, goes out into the open [lit. "as for when..."], and in the evening feels the chill.) One of six things separates أما from the answering fāʾ:
a- The mubtadaʾ: as in the verse mentioned above.
b- The khabar: such as "As for in the house, ʿAlī [is there]."
c- The condition clause, as in His words: «فأمّا إن كان من المقربين فروح وريحان».
d- A noun governed by an omitted verb, as in His words: «وأما ثمود فهديناهم».
e- A noun accusative in wording or in position by the answer, as in His words: «فأما اليتيم فلا تقهر».
And an adverb governed by أما because of the sense of the verb for which it stands, such as "As for today, I am going."
Also, أما can be for emphasis and condition, standing in for مهما, as in "Ammā baʿd, jihād is a door among the doors of Paradise", the implied form being "whatever there be of anything". The wāw sometimes stands in for أما, so one says wa-baʿd; this usage is common in sermons and letters, and to it the poet alluded in his words:
لقد علمت قيس بن عيلان أنني ... إذا قلت: أما بعد أني خطيبها
(Qays ibn ʿAylān knows that I, when I say "Ammā baʿd", am their orator.)
2- ماذا: it has two aspects:
