a- ذا is compounded with ما, both losing their individual character, as a single interrogative noun, parsed according to its position.
b- ذا is a relative noun meaning "that which", so it is the khabar of the interrogative ما, and the effect of this appears in the answer to it. For this reason we gave both aspects in the i'rab. The words of the Exalted «يسألونك ماذا ينفقون؟ قل العفو» have been read with العفو accusative and nominative, on the two interpretations. And Labīd said:
ألا تسألان المرء ماذا يحاول ... أنحب فيقضى أم ضلال وباطل
(Will you two not ask the man what he is trying to do: a vow to be fulfilled, or error and falsehood?) It was reported that أنحب is nominative as a badal of ذا on the second view; and had he said أنحبا, as a badal of the whole of ماذا, accusative as the object of يحاول, it would have been permissible.

dervis-irab:188-188.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تُدْلُوا بِها): "you cast them". Adlā l-dalwa means he lowered the bucket into the well; and he watered his land with the dāliya and the dawālī, which are water-wheels. He lowered (dallā) something into a pit, and he himself dangled (tadallā); he dangled his legs from the bed, and lowered him by a rope from a roof or a mountain. Al-Farazdaq said:
هما دلّتاني من ثمانين قامة ... كما انقضّ باز أقتم الرّيش كاسره
(The two of them lowered me from eighty fathoms, as a dusky-feathered hawk swoops down, breaking its wings.)
Al-dawālī are black grapes that are not jet black. I do not know on what the author of al-Munjid based his claim that it is a post-classical coinage (muwallada). I have examined everything whose first radical is dāl and second lām, and it all conveys the meaning of hanging down and slipping away. From it comes al-dalaj, which is night travel, and the slipping away in it is not hidden; and dalafa al-shaykh means the old man walked faster than a creep, as if he were hanging down from a high place. This is a wonder in its own right.

* I'rab:
(وَلا تَأْكُلُوا): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to establish another ruling that concerns property and the ways of acquiring it. لا is prohibitive, and تَأْكُلُوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, the wāw being the agent. (أَمْوالَكُمْ): a direct object. (بَيْنَكُمْ): an adverbial attached to an omitted ḥāl from أَمْوالَكُمْ, i.e. "do not eat them while they are among you". (بِالْباطِلِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تَأْكُلُوا, i.e. do not take them by means of falsehood. (وَتُدْلُوا): the wāw is a conjunction, and تُدْلُوا is an imperfect verb conjoined to تَأْكُلُوا, falling within the scope of the prohibition; you may also make it a wāw of accompaniment, in which case تُدْلُوا is in the accusative by an implied أَنْ after it. (بِها): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تُدْلُوا. (إِلَى الْحُكَّامِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "resorting, seeking judgement". (لِتَأْكُلُوا): the lām is for justification, and تَأْكُلُوا is an imperfect verb put in the accusative by an implied أَنْ after the lām of justification, the wāw being the agent; the preposition and its genitive noun are in the accusative position as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). (فَرِيقاً): a direct object. (مِنْ أَمْوالِ النَّاسِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective. (بِالْإِثْمِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "clinging to what makes one liable to sin, such as false testimony and the false oath". (وَأَنْتُمْ): the wāw is a ḥāl, and أَنْتُمْ is a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ. (تَعْلَمُونَ): an imperfect verb in the nominative, with an agent, and the clause is the khabar; and the clause after the wāw of ḥāl is a ḥāl.

dervis-irab:189-189.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مَواقِيتُ): the plural of mīqāt, whose origin is mawqāt; the wāw was changed to yāʾ because of the kasra before it. They are landmarks by which people time the affairs of their livelihood.

* I'rab:
(يَسْئَلُونَكَ): an imperfect verb in the nominative, with an agent and an object, and the clause is resumptive, brought to explain the wisdom in the variation of the new moons, after they had pressed their question about it. It is reported that Muʿādh ibn Jabal and Thaʿlaba ibn Ghanm al-Anṣārī said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the matter with the crescent that appears thin, then grows until it is full and complete, then keeps waning until it returns as it began, never being in one state?" So the verse came with the comprehensive, decisive ruling. The wisdom sought from the changing of the crescent is the timing of livelihoods and their regularity on a single, wondrous pattern. Al-hilāl is singular, and it is plural according to the difference of its time; and it is pluralised by analogy as ahilla, which is the analogy for the doubled fiʿāl form, such as ʿinān and aʿinna, zimām and azimma, sinān and asinna. (عَنِ الْأَهِلَّةِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يَسْئَلُونَكَ. (قُلْ): an imperative verb whose agent is latent, the implied form being "you", and the clause is resumptive. (هِيَ مَواقِيتُ): a nominal clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar, in the accusative position as the quoted speech. (لِلنَّاسِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of مَواقِيتُ. (وَالْحَجِّ): conjoined to النَّاسِ. (وَلَيْسَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought for the sake of a digression (istiṭrād), the mention of which will come; or it is as if it were a reversal of their question, and that their likeness in it is as the likeness of one who leaves the door of the house and enters it from its back. لَيْسَ is a defective past verb. (الْبِرُّ): the noun of لَيْسَ. (بِأَنْ تَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ): the bāʾ is a redundant preposition in the khabar of لَيْسَ; أَنْ with what follows it is in the interpretation of a maṣdar, the khabar of لَيْسَ; and الْبُيُوتَ is a direct object. (مِنْ ظُهُورِها): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تَأْتُوا. (وَلكِنَّ): the wāw is a conjunction, and لكِنَّ is a particle of rectification resembling the verb. (الْبِرُّ): its noun, in the accusative; and an omitted element must be implied for the speech to be coherent, as if it were said: "What you do by way of probing in the question is not righteousness, but righteousness". (مَنْ): a relative noun, the khabar of لكِنَّ; and it cannot be without an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the righteousness of him who". (اتَّقى): the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no position. (وَأْتُوا): the wāw is a conjunction; and conjoining an imperative sentence to a declarative one is permissible, for two declarative clauses have preceded, namely "righteousness is not" and "but righteousness is the one who fears Allah", and two imperative clauses are conjoined to them, namely "and come to the houses" and "and fear Allah". (الْبُيُوتَ): a direct object. (مِنْ أَبْوابِها): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أْتُوا. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ): the clause is conjoined to the imperative clause. (لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ): laʿalla and its noun, and the clause تُفْلِحُونَ is its khabar, and the clause of hope is a ḥāl.

* Rhetoric:
"Digression" (al-istiṭrād): a subtle, branching art to which the speaker inclines in one of the purposes of speech, making you imagine that he continues in it; then he leaves it for another because of a connection between them, then returns to the first. Here He mentioned the new moons and their variation, that they are timings for the pilgrimage, and that their likeness in asking is as the likeness of one who leaves the door of the house and enters from its back. For some of the Anṣār, when they entered the state of iḥrām, none of them would enter an orchard (ḥāʾiṭ, that is, a garden), a house or a tent by its door; if he was of the people of the clay-built (madar), he would cut a hole in the back of his house through which he entered and left, or would make a ladder by which to climb; and if he was of the people of hair-tents (wabar), he would go out from behind the tent. So that was said to them. Among the fine examples of this art is the saying of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib:
لنا نفوس لنيل المجد عاشقة ... فان تسلّت أسلناها على الأسل
لا ينزل المجد إلا في منازلنا ... كالنوم ليس له مأوى سوى المقل
(We have souls that are lovers of the attainment of glory; if they find consolation, we make them flow on the spear-points. Glory descends only in our dwellings, like sleep, which has no shelter but the eyes.)

* Benefits:
The scholars of rhetoric differed about the question: is it a question about the cause or about the wisdom? Al-Zamakhsharī, al-Rāghib and al-Qāḍī al-Bayḍāwī chose that it is a question about the wisdom, as the answer indicates, bringing the speech out according to the apparent requirement, because it is the original. Al-Sakkākī chose that it is a question about the cause, because the wisdom is obvious and does not deserve to be asked about, and the answer is of the "wise style" (al-uslūb al-ḥakīm).
Each party went on at length in arguing for what it claims, and the matter ended with them pelting one another with stinging words, which this place has no room for. How excellent are the men of our heritage; how thorough their investigation and how abundant their digging!

dervis-irab:190-192.t:
* Vocabulary:
«ثقفتموهم»: "you found them". Thaqifa l-shayʾ: he took it, or won it, or reached it. Thaqiftu the knowledge and the craft in the shortest time, if I was quick to take it. A thaqif laqif boy: one quick to learn; he has attained thaqāfa, with fatḥa on the thāʾ. The thāʾ and the qāf, when they come together at the beginning of a word, indicate the meaning of taking by overpowering: al-thiql (weight) is well known, the bearer staggers under it because it overpowers him; and illness weighed him down (athqalahu) when it overpowered him. Al-thaqāl, with fatḥa on the thāʾ, is the woman of large buttocks, heavy in movement.
Al-Rāʿī said:
ثقال إذا راد النساء فريدة ... صناع فقد صادت لدى الغوانيا
(Heavy when women roam, a unique one, deft; she has hunted among the beauties.) [Translator's note: the source verse seems corrupt in places; reproduced as printed.]
Thaqaba l-shayʾ bi-l-mithqab: he pierced the thing with the awl; the pearl-pierced the pearl; and the women pierced their veils for their eyes.
Al-Muthaqqib al-ʿAbdī said:
أرين محاسنا وكننّ أخرى ... وثقّبن الوصاوص للعيون
(They showed some charms and hid others, and pierced the face-veils for the eyes.)

* I'rab:
(وَقاتِلُوا): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to explain the rulings of fighting; it is the first verse revealed about fighting in Medina to exalt the word of Allah. قاتِلُوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent. (فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to قاتِلُوا. (الَّذِينَ يُقاتِلُونَكُمْ): the relative noun is a direct object, and the clause يُقاتِلُونَكُمْ is the ṣila. (وَلا تَعْتَدُوا): the wāw is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, and تَعْتَدُوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, the wāw being the agent. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ): inna and its noun. (لا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ): لا is a negative, and يُحِبُّ is an imperfect verb in the nominative whose agent is latent, referring to Allah, and الْمُعْتَدِينَ is a direct object; and the clause لا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ is the khabar of inna, and the clause of inna and what follows it is justificatory. (وَاقْتُلُوهُمْ): also a conjunction, and the command to kill them is repeated for emphasis. (حَيْثُ): an adverb of place, indeclinable on ḍamma, attached to اقْتُلُوهُمْ. (ثَقِفْتُمُوهُمْ): verb, agent and object; the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural and has been lengthened by a redundant wāw; and the verbal clause is in the genitive position through annexation. (وَأَخْرِجُوهُمْ): conjoined to اقْتُلُوهُمْ. (مِنْ حَيْثُ): the preposition is brought onto حَيْثُ, which is governed in the genitive only by it and by the bāʾ; and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أَخْرِجُوهُمْ. (أَخْرَجُوكُمْ): verb, agent and object, and the clause is in the genitive position through annexation. (وَالْفِتْنَةُ): the wāw is parenthetical, and الْفِتْنَةُ is a mubtadaʾ. (أَشَدُّ): the khabar. (مِنَ الْقَتْلِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أَشَدُّ; and the clause is parenthetical, with no position, running the course of a proverb, as will come. (فَإِنْ): the fāʾ is resumptive, and إِنْ is conditional. (قاتَلُوكُمْ): a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, the wāw is the agent and the kāf is the object; and the verb is in the position of a jussive as the protasis. (فَاقْتُلُوهُمْ): the fāʾ links to the apodosis, and اقْتُلُوهُمْ is an imperative verb with agent and object, and the clause فَاقْتُلُوهُمْ is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis. (كَذلِكَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar placed first. (جَزاءُ الْكافِرِينَ): a delayed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is resumptive. (فَإِنِ): the fāʾ is resumptive, and إِنْ is conditional. (انْتَهَوْا): a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis. (فَإِنِ): the fāʾ links to the apodosis, and إِنَّ is a particle resembling the verb. (اللَّهَ): the noun of inna. (غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): two khabars of inna.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «والفتنة أشد من القتل» there is the art of proverb-sending (irsāl al-mathal): it is a clause brought on the pattern of a proverb, because expulsion from the homeland is the trial after which there is no trial. It was said to someone: "What is harsher than death?" He said: "That with which one wishes for death." Expulsion from the homeland is like the drawing out of the soul from the body. Ibn al-Rūmī said:
فقد ألفته النفس حتى كأنه ... لها جسد إن بان غودر هالكا
(The soul has grown so used to it that it is as if it were its body; if it parted, she would be left perishing.)
Perhaps the prince of the creative poets in this is Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī. If we wished to cite him, the space would be too narrow for us; it is enough for you to go back to his dīwān and find what captivates you.

dervis-irab:193-194.t:
* I'rab:
(وَقاتِلُوهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, and قاتِلُوهُمْ is an imperative verb with agent and object. He commanded them to fight to avert the occurrence of the trial, which is expulsion from the homeland. (حَتَّى): a particle of limit and of governing the genitive, and what is meant by it here is justification. (لا): a negative. (تَكُونَ): an imperfect verb put in the accusative by an implied أَنْ after حَتَّى, and it is here a complete verb; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to قاتِلُوهُمْ; and (فِتْنَةٌ) is the agent of تَكُونَ. (وَيَكُونَ): conjoined to تَكُونَ, and it is here defective. (الدِّينُ): its noun. (لِلَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar. It is not unlikely that it is also complete, so that الدِّينُ is the agent and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "sincerely for Allah". (فَإِنِ): the fāʾ is resumptive, and إِنْ is conditional. (انْتَهَوْا): a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis. (فَلا): the fāʾ links to the apodosis, and لا is the negative of generic negation. (عُدْوانَ): its noun, indeclinable on fatḥa. (إِلَّا): a particle of restriction. (عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of لا, and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis. (الشَّهْرُ الْحَرامُ): الشَّهْرُ is a mubtadaʾ and الْحَرامُ an adjective. (بِالشَّهْرِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar; and an omitted muḍāf must be implied, i.e. the violation of the sanctity of the sacred month, which is Dhū l-Qaʿda of the seventh year of the Hijra, [for] the violation of the sanctity of the sacred month, which is Dhū l-Qaʿda of the sixth year. For they fought you in the year of al-Ḥudaybiyya; so when they went out for the ʿumra of fulfilment in Dhū l-Qaʿda of the seventh year and disliked fighting in it, it was said to them: this month is the counterpart of that month, and its violation for its violation, and the recompense of every evil is an evil like it. [Translator's note: the source text of this passage is slightly disordered, with a repeated clause on the violation of the sacred month; translated as printed.] (الْحَرامُ): an adjective, and the clause is resumptive. (وَالْحُرُماتُ قِصاصٌ): the wāw is a conjunction, الْحُرُماتُ is a mubtadaʾ, and قِصاصٌ is the khabar. (فَمَنِ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquent omission, and مَنْ is a conditional mubtadaʾ. (اعْتَدى): a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis. (عَلَيْكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اعْتَدى. (فَاعْتَدُوا): the fāʾ links to the apodosis, and اعْتَدُوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn, the wāw being the agent; the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, and the clause that occurs after the fāʾ of eloquent omission has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (عَلَيْهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to His saying فَاعْتَدُوا. (بِمِثْلِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اعْتَدُوا, or to an omitted ḥāl. (مَا): a maṣdar particle. (اعْتَدى): a past verb; the maṣdar formed from مَا and اعْتَدى is a muḍāf ilayhi, i.e. "with the like of his aggression". (عَلَيْكُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to اعْتَدى. (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to warn against excess in taking vengeance, because the soul is naturally disposed to love excess in vengeance; اتَّقُوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn, the wāw being the agent, and the divine name is a direct object. (وَاعْلَمُوا): conjoined to اتَّقُوا. (أَنَّ اللَّهَ): anna and its noun. (مَعَ الْمُتَّقِينَ): مَعَ is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar, and الْمُتَّقِينَ is a muḍāf ilayhi; and أَنَّ with what is within its scope takes the place of the two objects of اعْلَمُوا.

dervis-irab:195-195.t:
* Vocabulary:
(التهلكة): one of the rare maṣdars, not among those that run on analogy. In al-Qāmūs: it may take all three vowels on the lām. Al-Jawharī in his Ṣiḥāḥ and al-Rāzī in his Mukhtār limited themselves to the three vowels on the lām of mahlak; as for al-tahluka, it has ḍamma on the lām.

* I'rab:
(وَأَنْفِقُوا): the wāw is resumptive, and the clause is resumptive, brought to command striving with wealth after the command to strive with the self. أَنْفِقُوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable by the omission of the nūn, the wāw being the agent. (فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أَنْفِقُوا. (وَلا تُلْقُوا): the wāw is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, and تُلْقُوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, the wāw being the agent. (بِأَيْدِيكُمْ): the bāʾ is redundant, as in "aʿṭā bi-yadihi" (he gave with his hand) for the one who submits, because ألقى is a verb that takes its object directly. It was also said that تُلْقُوا is given the meaning of a verb that takes its object with the bāʾ, i.e. "do not betake yourselves with your hands"; and it was said that the second object is omitted, the implied form being "and do not cast yourselves with your hands". (إِلَى التَّهْلُكَةِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تُلْقُوا. (وَأَحْسِنُوا): the wāw is a conjunction, and أَحْسِنُوا is an imperative verb with its agent. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ): inna and its noun. (يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ): an imperfect verb with a latent agent and an object; the clause يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ is the khabar of inna, and the clause of inna with what is within its scope is justificatory, with no position.

* Rhetoric:
The loose trope (majāz mursal) in "the hands", by which the selves are meant, because seizing and movement are done by them; it is a loose trope whose relation is partiality, from naming the part and intending the whole, or causality, because the hand is the cause of movement, as was said before.

* Historical glimpse:
The commentators differed on the meaning of casting the hands into destruction. The nearest thing said about it is that a man of the Muhājirūn charged at the enemy's line and the people shouted at him: "He is casting his hand into destruction!" Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī said: "We know this verse best; it was revealed only about us. We accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and helped him, and attended the engagements with him, and preferred him to our families, our wealth and our children. When the war laid down its burdens we returned to our families, our children and our wealth to improve them and stay with them; so the destruction was staying with family and wealth and abandoning jihad." Others said in the interpretation of this verse: "and do not cast yourselves by your own hands into destruction" means by extravagance and wasting the means of livelihood, or by holding back from the campaign and from spending on it, for that strengthens the enemy and gives them power over you. On the authority of Aslam Abū ʿImrān, who said: "We campaigned against the City", meaning Constantinople, "with ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir over the people of Egypt and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Khālid ibn al-Walīd over the whole force. We drew up in two lines, and I never saw two lines wider or longer than they, with the Romans pressing their backs to the wall of the city. A man of ours charged at the enemy, and the people said: 'Stop! There is no god but Allah! He casts his hand into destruction!' Abū Ayyūb al-Anṣārī said: 'You interpret this verse like this, that if a man charges, fighting and seeking martyrdom? This verse was revealed only about us, the company of the Anṣār. When Allah helped His Prophet and made Islam manifest, we said among ourselves: we have left our families and our wealth so as to stay with them and improve them.' So Allah sent down the report from heaven." Abū ʿImrān said: "Abū Ayyūb never ceased to strive in the way of Allah until he was martyred and was buried at Constantinople." I say: this expedition is different from the famous expedition in which Abū Ayyūb died, which Yazīd ibn Muʿāwiya later made in the year 49 of the Hijra, with a group of the leading Companions. Then Yazīd campaigned there in the year 52, and that is the one in which Abū Ayyūb died; his grave is there to this day, and a famous mosque has been built over it. We have dwelt on this matter only because it suits our present condition and the condition of every nation that lags behind in jihad, neglects the mobilisation of capacities and the gathering of energies.

dervis-irab:28-29.t:
* Vocabulary:
(اسْتَوى) he became level, upright and straight, like an arrow let fly.
(فَسَوَّاهُنَّ) He created them, or He made them into.

* I'rab:
(كَيْفَ) an interrogative noun, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as ḥāl; the sense of the question here is rebuke. (تَكْفُرُونَ) an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign of nominative being the persistence of the nūn, and the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil. (بِاللَّهِ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تكفرون. (وَكُنْتُمْ) the wāw is circumstantial, with qad implied after it, according to the established rule that when a past verb occurs as a circumstantial clause, qad must be present, overt or implied; كان and its ism. (أَمْواتاً) the accusative khabar of كان; the verbal clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (فَأَحْياكُمْ) the fāʾ is a conjunction, and أحيا is a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on the alif; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He", and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi. (ثُمَّ) a conjunction of sequence with delay. (يُمِيتُكُمْ) an imperfect verb, nominative; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He", referring to Allah. (ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ) also a conjunction; He conjoined with ثم only because of the extended delay between the two states. (ثُمَّ) also a conjunction. (إِلَيْهِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ترجعون. (تُرْجَعُونَ) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. (هُوَ) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (الَّذِي) a relative noun in the position of nominative as khabar. (خَلَقَ) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, its fāʿil being a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He". (لَكُمْ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to خلق. (ما) a relative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (فِي الْأَرْضِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted word that has no position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (جَمِيعاً) a ḥāl of the direct object, which is ما, contrary to those among the commentators who parsed it as emphasis (tawkīd) of ما; had that been so, it would have been said جميعه. (ثُمَّ) a conjunction of sequence with delay. (اسْتَوى) a past verb conjoined to خلق. (إِلَى السَّماءِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استوى. (فَسَوَّاهُنَّ) the fāʾ is a conjunction and سوى is a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on the alif; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He", and the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. (سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ) a ḥāl if سوّى has the sense of bare creation, because it indicates the bare number, and similar is His saying the Exalted: «فتمّ ميقات ربه أربعين ليلة»; or a badal of the pronoun in فسواهن. If سوّى has the sense of "made into", it is a second object. Abū Ḥayyān denied this parsing, but there is no justification for his denial. (وَهُوَ) the wāw is resumptive and هو is mubtadaʾ. (بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ) the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to عليم. (عَلِيمٌ) khabar of هو.

* Benefits:
كيف: a noun indeclinable on the fatḥa, most often used interrogatively. Its grammatical position is either the khabar of what follows it, if it occurs before what cannot dispense with it, such as "How are you?" and "How were you?"; or a second object of ظن and its sisters, such as "How do you think the matter?"; or accusative as a ḥāl of what follows it, if it occurs before what can dispense with it, such as "How did your brother come?", that is, "in what state did he come?"; or accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq, such as «ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بأصحاب الفيل».

dervis-irab:213-213.t:
* I'rab:
(كانَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً) "kāna" with its ism and khabar. (واحِدَةً) ṣifa. (فَبَعَثَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction to an implied clause, omitted for brevity and concision, i.e. "the people were agreed upon the truth, then they differed, so He sent". The speech is resumptive, brought to indicate how the prevailing disagreement among people arose, and the deviation that led to their division, as indicated by what follows. "Baʿatha" is a past verb. (اللَّهُ) fāʿil. (النَّبِيِّينَ) mafʿūl bihi. (مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنْذِرِينَ) two ḥāls, the second conjoined to the first. (وَأَنْزَلَ) conjoined to «فبعث». (مَعَهُمُ) an adverb of time attached to an omitted ḥāl from «al-kitāb», i.e. "and He sent down the Book accompanying them at the time of sending down". (الْكِتابَ) mafʿūl bihi. (بِالْحَقِّ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أنزل», the bāʾ being that of association, i.e. He sent it down a sending down accompanied by the truth. (لِيَحْكُمَ) The lām is causal and "yaḥkuma" is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied "an" after the causal lām; the causal lām and its interpreted genitive noun are also attached to «أنزل». (بَيْنَ النَّاسِ) the adverb of place is attached to «يحكم», and "al-nās" is muḍāf ilayhi. (فِيمَا) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يحكم». (اخْتَلَفُوا) verb and fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative «mā». (فِيهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «اختلفوا». (وَمَا) The wāw is a conjunction and "mā" is negative. (اخْتَلَفَ) a past verb. (فِيهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «اختلف». (إِلَّا) a particle of restriction. (الَّذِينَ) fāʿil of «اختلف». (أُوتُوهُ) a past passive verb; the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil, which is the first object, and the hāʾ is the second mafʿūl bihi. (مِنْ بَعْدِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «اختلف». (مَا) maṣdar, interpreted with what follows as a maṣdar, muḍāf ilayhi, i.e. after the coming of the clear proofs. (جاءَتْهُمُ الْبَيِّناتُ) verb, a fronted mafʿūl bihi, and "al-bayyināt" a postponed fāʿil. (بَغْياً) mafʿūl li-ajlihi, i.e. out of envy on their part; it is also said to be an interpreted ḥāl, which is not far-fetched. (بَيْنَهُمْ) the adverb of place attached to an omitted ṣifa of «بغيا». (فَهَدَى اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) The fāʾ is a conjunction; "hadā" is a past verb, "Allāh" is fāʿil, and "alladhīna" with its ṣila is mafʿūl bihi. (لِمَا) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «هدى», and "mā" is relative. (اخْتَلَفُوا) verb and fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of "mā". (فِيهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «اختلفوا». (مِنَ الْحَقِّ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl from «mā». (بِإِذْنِهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl from «alladhīna āmanū», i.e. "permitted to them", so it is a ḥāl from the mafʿūl bihi. (وَاللَّهُ) The wāw is resumptive and "Allāh" is a mubtadaʾ. (يَهْدِي) an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, the implied form being "huwa", referring to Allah the Exalted; the clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of "Allāh". (مِنْ) a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. (يَشاءُ) the clause is the ṣila of the relative and has no grammatical position. (إِلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يهدي», and «mustaqīm» is a ṣifa.

* Rhetoric:
In this noble verse there is the figure of inversion (qalb), which is common in their speech. Al-Sakkākī, al-Zamakhsharī and al-Jawharī gave as an example the saying of the Exalted: «ويوم يعرض الذين كفروا على النار», whose original is: "and on the day the Fire is presented to those who disbelieved". They also exemplified it in poetry with the saying of ʿUrwa ibn al-Ward:
فديت بنفسه نفسي وما لي ... وما آلوك إلا ما أطيق
(I ransomed his soul with my soul and my wealth, and I spare you nothing but what I am unable to do.)
The original is "I ransomed his soul with my soul": the one ransomed is the soul of the beloved and the one ransomed with is the poet's own soul, not the reverse as the apparent sense of the verse suggests. And with the saying of al-Mutanabbī:
وعذلت أهل العشق حتى ذقته ... فعجبت كيف يموت من لا يعشق
(I used to blame the people of love until I tasted it, and I wondered how one who does not love can die.)
for its original is "how does one who loves not die", and the correct view is the opposite: that what is meant is that he came to see that there is no cause of death other than love. On the verse which we have in hand Abū Jaʿfar al-Ṭabarī said: "The meaning of that is only: Allah guided those who believed to the truth in that of the Book of Allah about which those who were given it differed, and Allah, blessed and exalted, addressed them only in the idiom of the Arabs." And Abū Jaʿfar exemplified it with the saying of al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī:
كانت فريضة ما تقول كما ... كان الزّناء فريضة الرجم
(What you say was an obligation, as adultery was the obligation of stoning.)
whereas in fact stoning is the obligation of adultery.

dervis-irab:214-214.t:
* Vocabulary:
(زُلْزِلُوا): they were shaken violently, in a manner resembling an earthquake (zalzala), by the terror and fright that befell them. The repetition of the zāy and the lām gives the sense of repeated shaking, time after time. Ibn Jinnī alluded to this chapter in the book al-Khaṣāʾiṣ and called it "the strength of the word for the strength of the meaning", as Ibn al-Athīr mentioned in the book al-Mathal al-Sāʾir. The sum of what the two established is that when a word is on a pattern and is then moved to another, longer pattern, it must contain more meaning than it did before: "ikhshawshana" indicates more roughness than "khashuna", and "iʿdhawdhaba l-māʾ" indicates more sweetness than "ʿadhuba". Many examples will come in this book.
(حَسِبْتُمْ): "ḥasibtu Zaydan qāʾiman aḥsibuhu" is of the pattern "taʿiba", that is, with kasra on the sīn in the past and fatḥa in the imperfect, in the language of all the Arabs except Banū Kināna, who put kasra on the sīn of the imperfect also, together with kasra on the sīn of the past, contrary to analogy; "ḥisbānan" with kasra, meaning "I thought him". And "ḥasabtu al-māl ḥasban" is of the pattern "qatala", that is, with fatḥa on the sīn in the past and ḍamma in the imperfect: I counted it up; likewise in the maṣdar, and "ḥusbānan" with ḍamma.

* I'rab:
(أَمْ) a disconnected conjunction (munqaṭiʿa) taken as "bal", with the interrogative hamza omitted; the meaning is "rather, did you think", and the interrogation is for rebuke and denial. (حَسِبْتُمْ) verb and fāʿil. (أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا) "an" is a particle of maṣdar and accusative, and "tadkhulū" is an imperfect verb accusative by "an", its accusative sign being the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الْجَنَّةَ) mafʿūl bihi by extension; "an" and what follows are in the interpretation of a maṣdar standing in the place of the two objects of «حسبتم». (وَلَمَّا) The wāw is circumstantial and "lammā" is a particle of negation and jussive. (يَأْتِكُمْ) an imperfect verb jussive by "lammā", its jussive sign being the omission of the weak letter, and the kāf is the mafʿūl of «يأتكم». (مَثَلُ) fāʿil of «يأتكم». (الَّذِينَ) muḍāf ilayhi. (خَلَوْا) verb and fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of «alladhīna». (مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «خلوا». (مَسَّتْهُمُ) "massa" is a past verb, the tāʾ is the quiescent feminine tāʾ, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. (الْبَأْساءُ) fāʿil. (وَالضَّرَّاءُ) conjoined to «al-baʾsāʾ»; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position, as if someone had said: "How was that example, and what is its nature?" and it was said: "Adversity and hardship touched them"; you may also make it explicative; in any case it has no grammatical position. (وَزُلْزِلُوا) The wāw is a conjunction and "zulzilū" is a past passive verb, the wāw being nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to «مستهم». (حَتَّى يَقُولَ الرَّسُولُ) "ḥattā" is a particle of limit and genitive, "yaqūla" is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied "an" after "ḥattā", and "al-rasūl" is fāʿil. (وَالَّذِينَ) conjoined to "al-rasūl". (آمَنُوا) the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of «alladhīna». (مَعَهُ) the adverb of place attached to «آمنوا». (مَتى نَصْرُ اللَّهِ) "matā" is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of time, the adverb attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and "naṣr Allāh" is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is in the position of accusative as the content of the saying. (أَلا) a particle of opening and alerting. (إِنَّ نَصْرَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ) "inna" with its ism and khabar; the clause is resumptive.

dervis-irab:215-215.t:
* I'rab:
(يَسْئَلُونَكَ) an imperfect verb in the nominative, its nominative sign being the retention of the nūn, the wāw is the fāʿil, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi. (ماذا) What has been said about «mādhā» has preceded, so we may parse it as an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi of «ينفقون»; and it is permissible to parse "mā" as an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ and "dhā" as a relative noun in the position of nominative as khabar, the clause being in the position of accusative as a fronted object of «ينفقون». The clause «يسألونك» is resumptive, brought to ask about the money spent and where it is to be spent.
They said: The questioner was ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ, an old man possessed of wealth, who asked the Prophet ﷺ: What should he spend, and on whom should he spend? All this concerns voluntary charity. (يُنْفِقُونَ) an imperfect verb in the nominative, its nominative sign being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is in the position of accusative as the second object of «يسألونك». (قُلْ) an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, brought to give the answer to the question. (ما أَنْفَقْتُمْ) "mā" is conditional, in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi of «أنفقتم», and «anfaqtum» is a verb in the position of a jussive, the protasis, with its fāʿil; the clause is the content of the saying. (مِنْ خَيْرٍ) the preposition and its genitive noun are in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (فَلِلْوالِدَيْنِ) The fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "so it is for the parents"; the nominal clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis. (وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ وَالْيَتامى وَالْمَساكِينِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ) all conjoined to "al-wālidayn". (وَما تَفْعَلُوا مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ) its i'rab has preceded in the previous verse.

* Benefits:
A general rule for parsing the conditional particles "man, mā, mahmā": if the protasis verb requires a direct object, they are accusative in position as mafʿūl bihi; if it is intransitive, or transitive and has already received its object, they are nominative in position as mubtadaʾ.
"Ḥaythumā" is in the position of accusative as an adverb of place. [Translator's note: the source text here reads "ḥaythumā ... ẓarf zamān" (adverb of time); it is rendered as written, though "ḥaythumā" is ordinarily an adverb of place.]
"Matā, ayyāna, ayna, annā" are in the position of accusative as adverbs of time. [Translator's note: as printed; "ayna" and "annā" are ordinarily adverbs of place.]
"Kayfamā" is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of the protasis.
"Ayy" depends on what it is annexed to.

dervis-irab:216-216.t:
* I'rab:
(كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِتالُ) "kutiba" is a passive verb, "ʿalaykum" is attached to «kutiba», and "al-qitāl" is nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, brought to explain the legitimacy of fighting. The meaning of «kutiba» is "was made obligatory", and the obligation is either individual (ʿayn) when the enemy enters the land, or collective (kifāya) when the enemy is in his own land. (وَهُوَ) The wāw is circumstantial and "huwa" is a mubtadaʾ. (كُرْهٌ) khabar. (لَكُمْ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «kurh»; the nominal clause after the circumstantial wāw is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (وَعَسى) The wāw is resumptive and "ʿasā" is a past, non-conjugating verb to express hope; here it is complete (tāmma), and that is regular with "ʿasā", "ikhlawlaqa" and "awshaka" when "an" follows them. (أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا) "an" and what is within its scope are in the interpretation of a maṣdar, the fāʿil of «ʿasā». (شَيْئاً) mafʿūl bihi. (وَهُوَ) The wāw is circumstantial and "huwa" is a mubtadaʾ. (خَيْرٌ) khabar. (لَكُمْ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «khayr»; the nominal clause after the wāw is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. Here there is a difficulty, which we take up in the chapter of Benefits. (وَعَسى أَنْ تُحِبُّوا شَيْئاً وَهُوَ شَرٌّ لَكُمْ) its i'rab has preceded. (وَاللَّهُ) The wāw is resumptive and "Allāh" is a mubtadaʾ. (يَعْلَمُ) an imperfect verb with a latent fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. (وَأَنْتُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction and "antum" is a mubtadaʾ. (لا تَعْلَمُونَ) "lā" is negative and «taʿlamūna» is an imperfect verb, the wāw being the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of «antum».

* Rhetoric:
In the verse there is antithesis (ṭibāq) between loving and disliking, and between «kurh» and «sharr», which is then called contrast (muqābala); its discussion has preceded.

* Benefits:
In the verse the coming of a ḥāl from an indefinite noun, without any of its well-known conditions, is troublesome. For this reason some who parse leaned towards parsing the clause «وهو خير لكم» as a ṣifa of «shayʾan». The wāw entered the clause which falls as a ṣifa only because its form is the form of a ḥāl; so, as the wāw enters it as a circumstantial, it enters it as an adjective. That is what al-Zamakhsharī permitted in the saying of the Exalted: «وما أهلكنا من قرية إلا ولها كتاب معلوم», and it will come in its place.

dervis-irab:217-218.t:
* I'rab:
(يَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ الشَّهْرِ الْحَرامِ) a resumptive clause with no grammatical position, brought to explain the ruling on fighting in the sacred month, which is Rajab. "Yasʾalūnaka" is verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «yasʾalūnaka»; "al-ḥarām" is a ṣifa. (قِتالٍ) badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from «al-shahr». (فِيهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ṣifa of «qitāl». The reasoning for it is that the question about the month was only with regard to the fighting that took place in it; the meaning is "they ask you about fighting in the sacred month". Sībawayh recited: فما كان قيس هلكه هلك واحد ... ولكنه بنيان قوم تهدّما (Qays's death was not the death of one man, but the demolition of a people's edifice.)
(قُلْ) an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent, the implied form being "anta", O Muḥammad; the clause is resumptive. (قِتالٍ) a mubtadaʾ; it is permissible to begin with it though indefinite because it is qualified. (فِيهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar. (كَبِيرٌ) ṣifa of «al-qitāl». (وَصَدٌّ) conjoined to «qitāl», so it is a mubtadaʾ; it is permissible to begin with it because it is included in what it is conjoined to of definites. (عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «ṣadd». (وَكُفْرٌ بِهِ) conjoined to «ṣadd», and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «kufr». (وَالْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ) conjoined to «sabīl Allāh», i.e. "and from the Sacred Mosque". (وَإِخْراجُ أَهْلِهِ) conjoined to «ṣadd». (أَكْبَرُ) the khabar of all that preceded; they are four, and it is predicated of them by «akbar» because it is an elative in which the one and the many are equal when it is free of the alif and lām and of annexation. (عِنْدَ اللَّهِ) the adverb of place attached to «akbar». (وَالْفِتْنَةُ) The wāw is resumptive and "al-fitna" is a mubtadaʾ. (أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ) khabar; the clause has no grammatical position, and it is possible to parse the wāw as circumstantial, in which case the clause is accusative as a ḥāl; and "mina l-qatl" is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «akbar». (وَلا يَزالُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction and "lā yazālūna" is a defective imperfect verb, among the sisters of kāna, and the wāw is its ism. (يُقاتِلُونَكُمْ) an imperfect verb, fāʿil and mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of «yazālūna». (حَتَّى يَرُدُّوكُمْ) "ḥattā" is a particle of limit and genitive, or of causation, and "yaruddūkum" is an imperfect verb accusative by an implied "an" after "ḥattā". (عَنْ دِينِكُمْ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «yaruddūkum». (إِنِ) conditional. (اسْتَطاعُوا) a past verb in the position of a jussive, the protasis, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "they will turn you back". (وَمَنْ) The wāw is resumptive and "man" is a jussive-governing conditional noun, mubtadaʾ. (يَرْتَدِدْ) the protasis. (مِنْكُمْ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (عَنْ دِينِهِ) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «yartadid». (فَيَمُتْ) The fāʾ is a conjunction and "yamut" is an imperfect verb jussive, conjoined to «yartadid». (وَهُوَ) The wāw is circumstantial and "huwa" is a mubtadaʾ. (كافِرٌ) khabar; the nominal clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (فَأُولئِكَ) The fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis and «ulāʾika» is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. (حَبِطَتْ أَعْمالُهُمْ) verb and fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of «ulāʾika», and the demonstrative clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis, and the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of «man». (فِي الدُّنْيا) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «ḥabiṭat». (وَالْآخِرَةِ) conjoined to «al-dunyā». (وَأُولئِكَ) The wāw is a conjunction and «ulāʾika» is a mubtadaʾ. (أَصْحابُ النَّارِ) khabar. (هُمْ) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ. (فِيها) The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to His saying «khālidūna». (خالِدُونَ) khabar; the clause «hum fīhā khālidūna» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ) "inna" and its ism. (آمَنُوا) the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of «alladhīna». (وَالَّذِينَ هاجَرُوا وَجاهَدُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ) conjoined to what preceded. (أُولئِكَ) the demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. (يَرْجُونَ) an imperfect verb with its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of «ulāʾika». (رَحْمَتَ اللَّهِ) mafʿūl bihi; the demonstrative clause is a nominal clause in the position of nominative as the khabar of «inna». (وَاللَّهُ) The wāw is resumptive and "Allāh" is a mubtadaʾ. (غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ) khabar [Translator's note: the source says "khabar of inna li-llāh", rendered here as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ «Allāh»; the source wording is «خبر ان لله», which appears to be a slip].

dervis-irab:57-57.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الغمام): the white cloud.
(وَظَلَّلْنا): We made it shade you.
(الْمَنَّ): a particular plant used as food, called al-tarnajbīn (manna).
(السَّلْوى): a well-known bird called السمانى (quail), with ḍamma on the sīn and fatḥa on the nūn, followed by a shortened alif; it is known in the land of Syria as al-farrī.

* I'rab:
(وَظَلَّلْنا) The wāw is a conjunction, and ظللنا is verb and fāʿil. (عَلَيْكُمُ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ظللنا. (الْغَمامَ) direct object. This clause is connected with what precedes in the context of remembrance, yet separate from it in occurrence, for the shading continued until their entry into the Promised Land; and had Allah not driven the clouds to them to shade them in the wilderness (al-tīh), the sun would have scorched them and burnt their faces. There is no sense in describing the clouds as thin, as many commentators said; rather the context requires their density, since the "ample shade" (al-ẓill al-ẓalīl) that the form of the verb taẓlīl conveys is attained only by a dense cloud that blocks the heat of the sun and its glare. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «بحساب كثيف» ("by a dense reckoning"); the sense clearly requires «بسحاب كثيف» ("by a dense cloud"), and I have translated accordingly.] (وَأَنْزَلْنا) conjoined to وظللنا. (عَلَيْكُمُ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزلنا. (الْمَنَّ) direct object. (وَالسَّلْوى) conjoined to المن. (كُلُوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable with the omission of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil; the clause كلوا is in the accusative position as reported speech, i.e. "and We said: eat". (مِنْ طَيِّباتِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كلوا. (ما) a relative noun in the genitive position by annexation. (رَزَقْناكُمْ) verb, fāʿil and object; the clause has no position because it is a ṣila of the relative. (وَما) The wāw is a conjunction and ما is negative. (ظَلَمُونا) verb, fāʿil and object; the clause is conjoined to an omitted clause that the context requires, the implied form being "so they wronged themselves by ingratitude for that ample blessing". (وَلكِنْ) The wāw is circumstantial, and لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), left inoperative because its nūn was lightened. (كانُوا) kāna and its ism. (أَنْفُسَهُمْ) direct object, advanced, of يظلمون. (يَظْلِمُونَ) an imperfect verb, the wāw being the fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the clause of لكن with what is within its scope is in the accusative position as ḥāl.

dervis-irab:58-58.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْقَرْيَةَ): derived from قريت, i.e. I gathered, because it gathers its people; you say قريت الماء في الحوض, i.e. I gathered it. There is disagreement about the town: it was said to be Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), and it was said to be Jericho, a town in the Jordan valley.
(حِطَّةٌ): a fiʿla form (with kasra on the ḥāʾ) from al-ḥaṭṭ (lowering, putting down).

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ) discussed before. (قُلْنَا) verb and fāʿil; the clause is in the genitive position by the annexation of the adverb to it. (ادْخُلُوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable with the omission of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil; the clause is in the accusative position as reported speech. (هذِهِ) the hāʾ is a particle of alerting, and ذه is a demonstrative in the accusative position as an object by extension. (الْقَرْيَةَ) badal from the demonstrative. (فَكُلُوا) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and كلوا is conjoined to ادخلوا. (مِنْها) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to كلوا. (حَيْثُ) an adverb of place, indeclinable on the ḍamma, attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "moving about". (شِئْتُمْ) verb and fāʿil; the clause is in the genitive position by the annexation of the adverb to it. (رَغَداً) absolute object or ḥāl. (وَادْخُلُوا) conjoined to ادخلوا. (الْبابَ) direct object, by extension. (سُجَّداً) ḥāl, i.e. humble and lowly, in the manner of one prostrating. (وَقُولُوا) conjoined to وادخلوا. (حِطَّةٌ) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "our request is ḥiṭṭa" or "our affair is ḥiṭṭa"; the nominal clause is reported speech. The original in it is the accusative, because its meaning is "lower from us our sins", but it was turned to the nominative to indicate the permanence of the lowering and steadfastness in it. (نَغْفِرْ) an imperfect verb jussive because it is the response to a request. (لَكُمْ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نغفر. (خَطاياكُمْ) direct object. (وَسَنَزِيدُ) The wāw is resumptive, and نزيد is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "نحن". (الْمُحْسِنِينَ) direct object.

* Benefits:
Every adverb of place that is bounded and non-derived cannot be made accusative as an adverb, but must be governed in the genitive by في, as in جلست في الدار (I sat in the house), أقمت في البلد (I stayed in the town) and صليت في المسجد (I prayed in the mosque); except when it occurs after دخل, نزل and سكن, in which case it may be made accusative as an adverb or by removal of the preposition (nazʿ al-khāfiḍ); the sound view is that it is accusative as an object by extension.

dervis-irab:234-237.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُتَوَفَّوْنَ): in the passive, that is, their souls are taken by death. It is taken from tawaffaytu al-dayn, "I received the debt in full". The mutawaffī (with kasra on the fāʾ) is Allah, and the mutawaffā (with fatḥa) is the servant. It is related that Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī was walking behind a funeral when a man said to him: "Who is the mutawaffī?", with kasra on the fāʾ. He said: "Allah the Exalted." This was one of the reasons that moved ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib to lay down grammar.
(المقتر): the one whose provision is narrow.

* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنْكُمْ): the statements of the exegetes, the grammarians and the authorities of the language are troubled over the i'rab of this eloquent construction; each of them put forward an argument and mustered all he had to establish what he thought. For this reason it is hard for the parser to prefer one over another. We shall summarise what we saw as nearest to the truth among them:
The view of Sībawayh: it is that «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is, "among what is recited to you is their ruling". The like of it will occur in the Noble Qur'an, among it «والسارق والسارقة». The clause «يتربصن» is explicative of the recited ruling and has no grammatical position.
The view of al-Zamakhsharī: it is that «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ with an omitted muḍāf, he meant: "the wives of those who die among you", and its khabar is the clause يتربصن.
The view of al-Mubarrad: it is to make the clause «يتربصن» the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the implied form being "their wives shall wait", the nominal clause being the khabar of «الذين», and the link being the pronoun, that is, the nūn in «يتربصن»; and the clause is resumptive, introduced to state another ruling.
منكم: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَيَذَرُونَ): conjoined to يتوفون. (أَزْواجاً): a direct object. (يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ): an imperfect verb, indeclinable on sukūn, and the i'rab of the clause has already passed. (أَرْبَعَةَ أَشْهُرٍ): an adverb of time attached to يتربصن. (وَعَشْراً): conjoined to أربعة. He mentioned the number [in the feminine form] because he meant ten nights, the days being included with them, and you never see them using the masculine; you say "I fasted ten" and "I travelled ten". The poet said:
أشوقا ولمّا يمض لي غير ليلة ... فكيف إذا جدّ المطيّ بنا عشرا
(Is it longing, when but a single night has passed for me? How will it be when the mounts press on with us for ten?)
(فَإِذا بَلَغْنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ): the fāʾ is resumptive; إذا is an adverb of future time attached to the apodosis; بلغن is a verb and an agent, and أجلهن is a direct object; the verbal clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. (فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ): the fāʾ links the apodosis, لا is the lā of generic negation, جناح is its noun, and عليكم is attached to an omitted khabar of it; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. (فِيما فَعَلْنَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause فعلن is the ṣila of the relative; في أنفسهن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to فعلن; and بالمعروف is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, that is, "being in accord with what is right". (وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ): the waw is resumptive and الله is a mubtadaʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to خبير; the clause تعملون is the ṣila of the relative; and خبير is the khabar of the Majestic Name. (وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيما عَرَّضْتُمْ بِهِ): its i'rab has gone before, and the waw is a conjunction. (مِنْ خِطْبَةِ النِّساءِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. (أَوْ أَكْنَنْتُمْ فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ): أو is a conjunction; the clause أكننتم is conjoined to عرضتم; and في أنفسكم is attached to أكننتم. (عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ): the clause stands as a giving of reason and has no grammatical position; أن and what follows stand in place of the two objects of علم; the clause ستذكرونهن is the khabar of أن. (وَلكِنْ لا تُواعِدُوهُنَّ سِرًّا): the waw is a conjunction to an omitted clause on which the rectification (istidrāk) falls, that is, "so mention them". «لكن» is lightened and inoperative; لا is prohibitive; تواعدوهن is an imperfect verb jussive by the prohibitive لا; the hāʾ is the first object and سرا is its second object, because sirr here means marriage. It is also permissible to parse it as an interpreted ḥāl, that is, "concealing it from the people", or accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "in secret", and it is also permissible to parse it as a mafʿūl muṭlaq, that is, "a secret promising". The first is the right aspect. We have only hinted at these aspects because some have said that the verb of promising (muwāʿada) does not take two objects. The Arabs very often use sirr in the sense of marriage. Al-Aʿshā said:
ولا تقربن من جارة إنّ سرها ... عليك حرام فانكحن أو تأبدا
(Do not approach a neighbour woman, for her sirr is forbidden to you; so marry, or go off and live alone.)
And تأبدا is an imperative verb whose alif is converted from the nūn of emphasis, that is: flee from human company, O you who are addressed. (إِلَّا أَنْ تَقُولُوا قَوْلًا مَعْرُوفاً): إلا is a particle of exception, أن is maṣdarī, and تقولوا is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by أن; أن and what follows is a maṣdar in the position of the accusative as an exception from «سرا»; قولا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq and معروفا an adjective. (وَلا تَعْزِمُوا عُقْدَةَ النِّكاحِ): the waw is a conjunction and لا is prohibitive; تعزموا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا; and عقدة النكاح is accusative by removal of the preposition, that is: "on the knot of marriage". (حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْكِتابُ أَجَلَهُ): حتى is a particle of limit and of genitive; يبلغ is an imperfect verb in the subjunctive by an implied أن after حتى; الكتاب is the agent and أجله the direct object; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to تعزموا. (وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ): the waw is a conjunction; اعلموا is an imperative verb, indeclinable through the dropping of the nūn, and the waw is the agent; أن and its noun; the clause يعلم is the khabar of أن, and أن and what it enters stand in place of the two objects of اعلموا; ما is a relative noun, a direct object; and في أنفسكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣila of ما, that is, "settled in your souls". (فَاحْذَرُوهُ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa, that is, "if you have known that, then beware of Him". (وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ): the waw is a conjunction; اعلموا is an imperative verb, indeclinable through the dropping of the nūn, and the waw is the agent; أن with its noun and two khabars stand in place of the two objects of اعلموا. (لا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ): the clause is resumptive. (إِنْ طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ): إن is conditional and طلقتم is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the apodosis is omitted, that is, "then do not give them the dower"; the clause is resumptive. (ما لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ): ما is maṣdarī and adverbial of time, or conditional; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; and تمسوهن is an imperfect verb jussive by لم. (أَوْ تَفْرِضُوا لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً): the apparent view is that أو is a conjunction and تفرضوا is conjoined to تمسوهن. But two things make this difficult. The first is that the meaning would become: "there is no blame on you concerning the dowers of women if you divorce them during the period in which one of these two things is absent", although if the fixing of a dower is absent without consummation, the dower of the like is due, and if consummation is absent without the fixing, half of the named dower is due; so how can the negation of blame be sound when one of the two things is absent? The second is that the divorced women for whom a dower has been fixed are mentioned a second time in His saying: «And if you divorce them...» (the verse), and the mention of the touched women was left out because of what is understood from what precedes; and if تفرضوا were jussive, the touched women and those with a fixed dower would be equal in the mention. Ibn al-Ḥājib undertook to answer the first difficulty by refusing that the meaning is "the period of the absence of one of them", but rather "the period in which neither of them occurred", through the negation of both together, because it is an indefinite noun in the context of explicit negation, unlike the first view, which negates only one of them. Some answered the second by saying that the mention of those with a fixed dower was only to specify half for them, not to state that they have something in general. In any case it is preferable to make أو in the sense of إلى and to make تفرضوا accusative by the أن that has the sense of إلا or إلى. So consider this section. The sum of what has gone before is that the jussive, by conjunction to تمسوهن, leads to a difference between the two verses in construction, and non-difference is preferable; and the clause is conjoined to the omitted apodosis of إن. The meaning is: "if you divorce women at a time of no touching and no fixing of a dower, then do not give them the dower". (وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ): conjoined to "then do not give them the dower", that is, give them what they may enjoy. (عَلَى الْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and قدره is a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause is a ḥāl. (وَعَلَى الْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ): conjoined to what precedes. (مَتاعاً بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): متاعا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq; متاعا is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) in the sense of the maṣdar, that is, tamtīʿan; and بالمعروف is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective. (حَقًّا عَلَى الْمُحْسِنِينَ): a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, and على المحسنين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the maṣdar. (وَإِنْ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ): conjoined to what precedes, and its i'rab has already passed. (مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «طلقتموهم» «[Translator's note: the source prints طلقتموهم with a final mīm; the verb in the verse is طلقتموهن]»; and أن and what is within its scope is in the interpretation of a maṣdar, genitive by annexation, that is, "before the touching". (وَقَدْ فَرَضْتُمْ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً): the waw is the waw of ḥāl; قد is a particle of confirmation; فرضتم is a verb and an agent; لهن is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to فرضتم; and فريضة is either a direct object, being in the sense of the passive participle, that is, "something fixed", or a mafʿūl muṭlaq in the sense of "fixing". (فَنِصْفُ): the fāʾ links the apodosis, and نصف is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, that is, "incumbent upon you is half", or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "what is obligatory is half". (ما فَرَضْتُمْ): ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by annexation; the clause فرضتم is the ṣila of the relative; and the clause after the fāʾ is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (إِلَّا أَنْ يَعْفُونَ): إلا is a particle of exception, and أن and what is within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the accusative as a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because their waiving of half and its dropping is not of the same kind as their entitlement. There are delightful jurisprudential discussions in this ruling, to be taken from their proper places. يعفون is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on sukūn because the nūn of the feminine plural is attached to it, and the operator has no effect on its form, though it is in the position of the accusative; the nūn is a pronoun and not a sign of i'rab, as in your saying: الرجال يعفون. (أَوْ يَعْفُوَا): conjoined to يعفون, its sign of accusative being the fatḥa. (الَّذِي): the agent of يعفو. (بِيَدِهِ عُقْدَةُ النِّكاحِ): بيده is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and عقدة النكاح is a delayed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the ṣila of the relative. (وَأَنْ تَعْفُوا أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوى): the waw is resumptive; أن and what is within its scope is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ; أقرب is the khabar, and للتقوى is attached to أقرب. (وَلا تَنْسَوُا): the waw is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, and تنسوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, with the waw as agent. (الْفَضْلَ): a direct object. (بَيْنَكُمْ): an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ): inna and its noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to بصير; the clause تعملون is the ṣila of ما; and بصير is the khabar of inna; the clause is a giving of reason for what precedes.

* Rhetoric:
1- In this verse is a delightful art, namely the art of taʿrīḍ (indirect allusion). Some include it in the chapter of kināya, but we see that it is an art standing on its own. It is here in His saying: «concerning what you hint at of the proposal to women», as if one were saying to the woman he wishes to propose to: "You are beautiful", or "Who finds the like of you?", or the like. Among the fine instances of taʿrīḍ in poetry is the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī hinting at Kāfūr:
ومن ركب الثور بعد الجوا ... د أنكر أظلافه والغبب
(Whoever rides the bull after the thoroughbred finds its hooves and its dewlap objectionable.)
He means that whoever rides the bull, when it was his habit to ride the thoroughbred, finds objectionable the bull's hooves and its ghabab, that is, the flesh hanging beneath the bull's jaw; but as for one like Kāfūr, who had ridden the bull before, he does not find that objectionable if he rides it after the thoroughbred. And he also has, concerning him, asking him for more gifts:
أبا المسك هل في الكأس فضل أناله ... فإني أغني منذ حين وتشرب
(O Abū al-Misk, is there any surplus in the cup that I may have? For I have been singing for a while, and you drink.)
He is saying: my praise of you delights you as singing delights the drinker, so it is time you gave me to drink from the surplus of your cup.

dervis-irab:59-59.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الرجز) with kasra on the rāʾ and sukūn on the jīm: punishment.

* I'rab:
(فَبَدَّلَ) The fāʾ is resumptive, and بدل is a past verb. (الَّذِينَ) a relative noun, fāʿil; and the clause (ظَلَمُوا) has no position because it is a ṣila of the relative. (قَوْلًا) direct object. (غَيْرَ) adjective of قولا. (الَّذِي) a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi. (قِيلَ) a passive past verb. (لَهُمْ) the preposition and its genitive noun attached to قيل. (فَأَنْزَلْنا) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and أنزلنا is conjoined to the preceding clause. (عَلَى الَّذِينَ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزلنا. (ظَلَمُوا) the clause has no position because it is a ṣila of the relative. (رِجْزاً) direct object. (مِنَ السَّماءِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of رجزا, or to أنزلنا. (بِما) the bāʾ is a preposition and ما is a maṣdar particle, interpreted with what follows it as a maṣdar governed in the genitive by the bāʾ, i.e. "because of their disobedience". (كانُوا) kāna and its ism, and the clause (يَفْسُقُونَ) is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In this verse is a kind of rhetoric of subtle approach, which is putting the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, to add to the ugliness of their affair. al-Buḥturī observed it at the opening of his sīn-rhymed ode, saying:
صنت نفسي عما يدنّس نفسي ... وترفعت عن جدا كلّ جبس
(I guarded my soul from what would defile my soul, and I rose above the gifts of every base wretch.)
He did not say "يدنسها" (would defile it); he put the overt noun in place of the pronoun for this noble purpose.

dervis-irab:60-60.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَعْثَوْا): it is said عثا يعثوا and عثي يعثى, i.e. he caused corruption.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذِ) discussed before. (اسْتَسْقى) a past verb. (مُوسى) fāʿil. (لِقَوْمِهِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to استسقى. (فَقُلْنَا) The fāʾ is a conjunction, and قلنا is verb and fāʿil. (اضْرِبْ) an imperative verb, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت"; the clause is in the accusative position as reported speech. (بِعَصاكَ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اضرب. (الْحَجَرَ) direct object. (فَانْفَجَرَتْ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ faṣīḥa (the eloquent fāʾ), about which the discussion will come in the Benefits; انفجرت is a past verb, and the tāʾ is the silent tāʾ of the feminine, i.e. "so he complied with the command and struck", or "so if you strike, then it has gushed forth". (مِنْهُ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to انفجرت. (اثْنَتا عَشْرَةَ) fāʿil of انفجرت, its sign of nominative being the alif because it is joined to the dual; and عشرة is a part of the compound number, indeclinable always on the fatḥa. (عَيْناً) an overt specification (tamyīz). (قَدْ) a particle of verification. (عَلِمَ) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa. (كُلُّ أُناسٍ) fāʿil. (مَشْرَبَهُمْ) direct object; the clause has no position because it is resumptive. (كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable with the omission of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil; واشربوا is conjoined to كلوا. (مِنْ رِزْقِ اللَّهِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to whichever of the two verbs you wish. (وَلا تَعْثَوْا) The wāw is a conjunction, لا is prohibitive, and تعثوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, its sign of jussion being the omission of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil. (فِي الْأَرْضِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تعثوا; and the clause كلوا واشربوا is the reported speech of an omitted saying, a parallel of which has preceded. (مُفْسِدِينَ) ḥāl, its sign of accusative being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural.

* Benefits:
The fāʾ faṣīḥa: it was so named because it makes clear (afṣaḥat) something implied. When the bursting forth was mentioned right after the command to strike, it indicated that what the command sought was the bursting forth; therefore the striking was omitted, on the implication "so he struck it", to indicate that the one commanded complied with the command. That is, what is omitted may be a clause which is the mentioned cause; so it was called faṣīḥa by way of a rational figurative usage (majāz ʿaqlī).

dervis-irab:61-61.t:
* Vocabulary:
(البقل): everything the earth brings forth of herbage that has no stem; its plural is buqūl.
(القثّاء): well known (cucumbers); the singular is qiththāʾa, with kasra or ḍamma on the qāf, and the hamza is original because the verb is اقثأت الأرض, i.e. its cucumbers became abundant.
(الفوم): wheat, and it was said garlic, and perhaps the latter is preferable by the evidence of the reading of Ibn Masʿūd «وثومها».
(الْمَسْكَنَةُ): a maṣdar mīmī from al-sukūn (stillness) and abasement, because the miskīn (poor man) is little in movement and rising owing to the poverty he has; and miskīn is a mifʿīl form of intensification from it. They said: "no Jew is found who is rich in soul."
(باؤُ): they returned.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يا مُوسى) its i'rab was given shortly before. (لَنْ نَصْبِرَ) لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity, and نصبر is an imperfect verb made accusative by لن, its fāʿil an obligatorily latent pronoun, its implied form being "نحن". (عَلى طَعامٍ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نصبر. (واحِدٍ) adjective of طعام. (فَادْعُ) The fāʾ is resumptive, and ادع is an imperative verb, indeclinable with the omission of the weak letter, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت". (لَنا) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ادع. (رَبَّكَ) direct object. (يُخْرِجْ) an imperfect verb jussive because it is the response to a request. (لَنا) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يخرج. (مِمَّا) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يخرج. (تُنْبِتُ) an imperfect verb. (الْأَرْضُ) fāʿil; the clause تنبت الأرض has no position because it is a ṣila of the relative. (مِنْ بَقْلِها) the preposition and its genitive noun are a badal with repetition of the preposition, or attached to an omitted ḥāl from the omitted pronoun, which is the one referring back to the relative, i.e. "تنبته". (وَقِثَّائِها وَفُومِها وَعَدَسِها وَبَصَلِها) nouns conjoined to بقلها. (قالَ) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, its fāʿil a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; the clause is resumptive. (أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ) The hamza is for a disapproving question together with rebuke, and the clause أتستبدلون is reported speech. (الَّذِي) a relative noun, direct object. (هُوَ) mubtadaʾ. (أَدْنى) khabar; the nominal clause has no position because it is a ṣila. (بِالَّذِي) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تستبدلون. (هُوَ) mubtadaʾ. (خَيْرٌ) khabar. (اهْبِطُوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable with the omission of the nūn, the wāw being the fāʿil; the clause is the reported speech of an omitted saying, i.e. "We said". (مِصْراً) direct object, in the sense "go down to". (فَإِنَّ) The fāʾ is explanatory of cause, and inna is a particle resembling the verb. (لَكُمْ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted advanced khabar of inna. (ما) a relative noun in the accusative position as ism of inna, and the clause (سَأَلْتُمْ) has no position because it is a ṣila. (وَضُرِبَتْ) The wāw is resumptive, and ضربت is a passive past verb, the tāʾ being the silent tāʾ of the feminine. (عَلَيْهِمُ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ضربت. (الذِّلَّةُ) nāʾib fāʿil of ضربت. (وَالْمَسْكَنَةُ) conjoined to الذلة. (وَباؤُ) conjoined to ضربت. (بِغَضَبٍ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to باءوا. (مِنَ اللَّهِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of غضب. (ذلِكَ) a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. (بِأَنَّهُمْ) the bāʾ is a preposition, and anna with its ism; anna and what is within its scope is in the genitive position by the bāʾ, i.e. "all that was because of their disbelief"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar, and the clause is resumptive with no position. (كانُوا) kāna and its ism, and the clause is the khabar of anna. (يَكْفُرُونَ) the verbal clause is the khabar of كانوا. (بِآياتِ اللَّهِ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يكفرون. (وَيَقْتُلُونَ) conjoined to يكفرون. (النَّبِيِّينَ) direct object. (بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ) a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "while being wrongdoers, denying the truth in their own belief; and had they been fair they would have acknowledged the reality". (ذلِكَ) a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. (بِما عَصَوْا) the bāʾ is a preposition and ما is a maṣdar particle interpreted with the verb as a maṣdar governed in the genitive by the bāʾ; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of ذلك. (وَكانُوا) conjoined to عصوا, and كان with its ism. (يَعْتَدُونَ) a verbal clause in the accusative position as khabar of كانوا.

* Rhetoric:
The kināya (metonymy) in "abasement and poverty were struck upon them", which is a kināya of attribution (kināya ʿan nisba): He wished to establish the permanence of abasement and poverty upon them, so He alluded to it by their being "struck" upon them as a building is struck (pitched). The poets have aimed at the heights of this kināya; al-Farazdaq said, satirising Jarīr:
ضربت عليك العنكبوت بنسجها ... وقضى عليك به الكتاب المنزل
(The spider has struck its weaving over you, and the revealed Book has decreed it against you.)

* Benefits:
The bāʾ with substitution (ibdāl) enters upon what is abandoned, not upon what is brought.

dervis-irab:11-13.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الفساد): corruption (fasād) is a thing's going out of its state of uprightness; its opposite is ṣalāḥ (soundness). Corruption in the earth is stirring up wars, provoking sedition (fitan), and disrupting people's livelihoods.
(السُّفَهاءُ): plural of safīh, meaning one ascribed to safah; and safah is lightness of judgement and flimsiness required by deficiency of intellect, and its opposite is forbearance (ḥilm). One says safiha, with kasra on the fāʾ, and safuha, with ḍamma on it.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذا): the wāw is resumptive and the clause after it is a new start with no position; it is also possible that the wāw is a conjunction and the clause after it conjoined to the clause «يكذبون», so that it is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the khabar of kāna, and what is conjoined to a khabar is a khabar. In this case it is part of the cause for which they deserved the painful punishment. And «إذا» is an adverb of future time, governing its protasis in the genitive and being put in the accusative by its apodosis. (قِيلَ): a passive past verb, its deputy agent a latent pronoun implied in it, its implied form being "he", referring to Allah the Exalted; there is an important discussion of this expression that will come in the section of benefits. The clause «قيل» is in the position of genitive, the adverb being annexed to it. (لَهُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «قيل». (لا): lā of prohibition, which jusses. (تُفْسِدُوا): an imperfect verb jussive through lā, the sign of its jussive case being the dropping of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs, the wāw an agent. (فِي الْأَرْضِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «تفسدوا». (قالُوا): verb and agent; the verbal clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (إِنَّما): inna with the preventing mā (kāffa and makfūfa). (نَحْنُ): mubtadaʾ. (مُصْلِحُونَ): the khabar of «نحن», nominative, the sign of its nominative case being the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; and the clause is in the position of accusative, the thing said. (أَلا): a particle of alerting, with which speech is opened. (إِنَّهُمْ): inna is a particle resembling the verb and the hāʾ is its noun. (هُمُ): a separating pronoun or support, with no grammatical position; you may also parse «هم» as mubtadaʾ. (الْمُفْسِدُونَ): its khabar, and the nominal clause is in the position of nominative, the khabar of inna. (وَلكِنْ): the wāw is a conjunction, and lākin is the lightened form of the heavy one, for mere rectification (istidrāk). (لا): negative. (يَشْعُرُونَ): a nominative imperfect verb, the wāw an agent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes. (وَإِذا قِيلَ): the wāw is resumptive or a conjunction, and discussion of it has preceded; and the verbal clause «قيل» is in the position of genitive, the adverb being annexed to it. (لَهُمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «قيل», and the clause «قيل» is in the position of genitive, the adverb being annexed to it. (آمِنُوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable on dropping of the nūn, and the wāw; the clause has no position because it is explicative. The deputy agent is a maṣdar, namely «القول», and it was implied because the clause after it explains it; the implied form: "and when a saying was said to them, which is 'believe'", because command and prohibition are speech. The grammarians have forbidden that a clause stand in the place of the agent, because a clause is not an agent and so does not stand in its place. (كَما): the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, the implied form being "believe with a belief like the belief of the people"; Sībawayh preferred that it be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, whether the kāf is a particle or a noun meaning "like", and the owner of the ḥāl is the maṣdar understood from the preceding verb; and «ما» is maṣdar-forming. (آمَنَ النَّاسُ): verb and agent. (قالُوا): verb and agent, and «إذا» is attached to «قالوا», and the clause has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (أَنُؤْمِنُ): the hamza is of denying interrogation, and «نؤمن» is an imperfect verb, its agent a latent pronoun obligatorily implied, its implied form being "we". (كَما): its parsing has just preceded. (آمَنَ السُّفَهاءُ): verb and agent. (أَلا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ السُّفَهاءُ وَلكِنْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): the parsing of the like of this clause has just preceded.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the verse the interrogative departs from its original meaning, which is the seeking of knowledge, to other purposes understood from the content of the speech; the details are in the science of maʿānī, and the matter returns to sound taste. Voltaire spoke truly when he said: «ذوقك أستاذك» ("Your taste is your teacher").
2- Variation (taghāyur): an art that is almost [Translator's note: the source reads «يكاد يكون من المرقص», which is unclear; translated as it stands]. In the first closing phrase there occurred «لا يشعرون», and in the second closing phrase there occurred «لا يعلمون», for a wonderful secret that only the inspired grasp.
