The detail of it: the matter of religion, and the standing upon the fact that the believers are on the truth while the hypocrites are on falsehood, is a matter that needs far-sightedness and inference, so that the observer acquires knowledge and cognition; whereas hypocrisy and the wrongdoing in it that leads to the clashing of sedition and the vastness of corruption in the earth is a worldly matter based on customs, known to people, indeed like something perceived by the senses among them; therefore He said of it: «لا يشعرون». Also, since He mentioned foolishness (safah) in the second verse, which is total ignorance, the mention of knowledge was more fitting, so He said: «لا يعلمون». This is among the subtleties, so be alert to it.

* Benefits:
1- The deputy agent of «قيل»: the grammarians take it to be a pronoun for its maṣdar, and the clause of prohibition explains that adverb [Translator's note: so in the source]. It was also said that the adverb is the deputy agent, and so the clause is in the position of accusative. They disagreed about a clause's occurring as agent or deputy agent; the sound view is that a clause whose wording itself is meant is given the ruling of single words, which is why it can occur as mubtadaʾ, as in «لا حول ولا قوة كنز من كنوز الجنة» ("lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata is a treasure from the treasures of Paradise") and in the proverb «زعموا مطيّة الكذب» ("They claimed is the mount of falsehood"); and for this reason the khabar needs no link.
2- (أَلا): it was said that it is a simple particle with which speech is opened, alerting that what follows is certainly realised; and it was said that it is a particle compounded of the interrogative hamza and the negative particle, and an interrogative that enters a negative gives confirmation. Its sister is «أما», which is among the preliminaries of an oath, as in the saying:
أما والذي بكى وأضحك والذي ... أمات وأحيا والذي أمره الأمر
(By Him who made weep and made laugh, and who gave death and gave life, and whose command is the Command.)

dervis-irab:14-15.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الطّغيان): the maṣdar of ṭaghā ṭughyānan, with ḍamma or kasra on the ṭāʾ; the lām of ṭaghā, it was said, is yāʾ, and it was said wāw; its meaning is transgressing the limit.
(يَعْمَهُونَ): ʿamah is wavering and bewilderment. It is close to blindness (ʿamā), but between them there is a general-and-specific relation, because ʿamā is applied to the departure of the light of the eye and to error in judgement, whereas ʿamah is applied only to error in judgement.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذا): conjoined to what precedes, and the parsing of «إذا» has been repeated, so it is inferred from what precedes. (لَقُوا): its original is laqiyū; it is a past verb indeclinable on ḍamma because it is attached to the wāw of the group; the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ so it was dropped and its vowel moved to the qāf; the wāw is an agent, and the clause is in the position of genitive, the adverb being annexed to it. (الَّذِينَ): a relative noun, direct object. (آمَنُوا): verb and agent; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative. (قالُوا): verb and agent; the verbal clause has no position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (آمَنَّا): verb and agent; the verbal clause is the thing said. (وَإِذا): conjoined to the preceding «وإذا». (خَلَوْا): a past verb, indeclinable on an implied ḍamma on the omitted alif, dropped because of the meeting of two sākins, the wāw an agent; the clause is in the position of genitive, the adverb being annexed to it. (إِلى شَياطِينِهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «خلوا», and the meaning of «إلى» is the end of the limit; its discussion will come in the section of benefits. (قالُوا): a past verb; the clause has no position. (إِنَّا): inna is a particle resembling the verb, and nā an attached pronoun in the position of accusative, its noun. (مَعَكُمْ): maʿa is an adverb of place attached to an omitted element which is the khabar of inna, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «إنا معكم» is nominal, in the position of accusative, the thing said. (إِنَّما): kāffa and makfūfa. (نَحْنُ): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ. (مُسْتَهْزِؤُنَ): the khabar of «نحن», nominative, the sign of its nominative case being the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the nominal clause is an emphasis of the clause «إنا معكم», so it is within the scope of the thing said; you may also make it resumptive, with no position, based on a question arising from the claim of being "with" them, as though it were said to them when they said «إنا معكم»: "Then why do you follow the believers in the word of belief?", and they said: «إنما نحن مستهزئون»; or it is a justification of the "withness". (اللَّهُ): mubtadaʾ. (يَسْتَهْزِئُ): an imperfect verb, its agent a latent pronoun optionally implied, referring to Allah; the verbal clause is the khabar. (بِهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يستهزئ». (وَيَمُدُّهُمْ): the wāw is a conjunction, and «يمدهم» is a nominative imperfect verb conjoined to «يستهزئ»; the agent is latent, its implied form being "he", and the hāʾ [Translator's note: in the source; the pronoun is «هم»] is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative, a direct object. (فِي طُغْيانِهِمْ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يمدهم». (يَعْمَهُونَ): a nominative imperfect verb, the wāw an agent; the verbal clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يمدهم».

* Rhetoric:
These two verses contain several arts of rhetoric, which we summarise below:
1- Contrast between the clauses: they addressed the believers with a verbal clause, namely «آمنا», and addressed their devils with a nominal clause, namely «إنا معكم», because the nominal clause is more firmly established than the verbal clause. Their belief is of short range, going no further than the movement of the tongue, or the duration of their meeting with the believers, whereas their relying on their devils is permanently continuous and renewed, more attached to their souls and more connected to what has taken root in them.
2- The difference between the clause «مستهزئون» and the clause «يستهزئ»: because Allah's mocking of them is renewed time after time and state after state, casting them into the mazes of bewilderment and confusion, to increase the exemplary punishment of them.
3- Isomorphism (mushākala): it is established that mockery is a kind of frivolity and play, which do not befit Allah the Exalted, and He is exalted above them; but He called the requital of mockery "mockery"; so it is a verbal isomorphism, no less and no more.
4- Obligatory separation (faṣl) in the saying «الله يستهزىء بهم»: because in conjoining it to any of the preceding clauses there is a strong obstacle, as it would then enter within the scope of what the hypocrites said, whereas Allah's mocking of them and His forsaking them are established and continuous, whether they are alone with their devils or not. So the clause is resumptive in every case, because it is a place where a question arises, "What is the outcome of their affair? What is the end of their state?", so it is begun anew as an answer to this question.

* Benefits:
The grammarians mentioned meanings for the prepositional «إلى». The first is termination, which is its original; the second is accompaniment, as in the saying of the Exalted: «مَنْ أَنْصارِي إِلَى اللَّهِ», that is, "with Allah"; the third is clarification, being the one that clarifies the agency of its genitive noun after what indicates love or hate, from a verb of wonder or a noun of preference, as in «رَبِّ السِّجْنُ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ»; the fourth is synonymy with lām, as in «وَالْأَمْرُ إِلَيْكِ»; the fifth is agreement with «في», as in the saying of al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī:
فلا تتركني بالوعيد كأنني ... إلى الناس مطليّ به القار أجرب
(Do not leave me with your threats, as though I were, among the people, a scabby camel smeared with tar.)
the sixth is agreement with «عند», as in the saying of Abū Kabīr al-Hudhalī:
أم لا سبيل إلى الشباب وذكره ... أشهى إليّ من الرحيق السّلسل
(Or is there no way back to youth, and the mention of it is more desirable to me than smooth pure wine?)
and the seventh is emphasis, as in the reading of some: «أفئدة من الناس تهوى إليهم» with fatḥa on the wāw of «تهوى», on the basis that «تهوى» is made to contain the meaning "inclines".

dervis-irab:238-240.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْوُسْطى): the most excellent, from their saying for the most excellent: al-awsaṭ. It is not from al-wasaṭ whose meaning is being in the middle between two things, because the pattern fuʿlā has the meaning of superiority, and the superlative is built only from what admits of difference, that is, increase and decrease; and wasaṭ in the sense of "choice" admits of both, unlike "being in the middle between two things", which admits of neither, and for that reason it is not permissible to build the superlative form (afʿal al-tafḍīl) from it.
(قانِتِينَ): obedient, or silent.
(رجالا): the plural of rājil, that is, those going on foot.

* I'rab:
(حافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَواتِ): resumptive speech, introduced to state the rulings of the prayer of fear. حافظوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable through the dropping of the nūn, and the waw is the agent; على الصلوات is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to حافظوا. (وَالصَّلاةِ): conjoined to الصلوات. (الْوُسْطى): an adjective. (وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قانِتِينَ): the waw is a conjunction; قوموا is conjoined to حافظوا; لله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قانتين, and قانتين is a ḥāl from the agent of قوموا. (فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ): the fāʾ is resumptive and إن is conditional; خفتم is a past verb with its agent, in the position of the jussive as the protasis. (فَرِجالًا): the fāʾ links the apodosis, and رجالا is a ḥāl; its operator is omitted, the implied form being "then pray" or "then guard them on foot"; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (أَوْ رُكْباناً): conjoined to «رجالا». (فَإِذا أَمِنْتُمْ): the fāʾ is resumptive; إذا is an adverb of future time attached to the apodosis, and the clause أمنتم is in the position of the genitive by annexation. (فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ): the fāʾ links the apodosis of إذا; اذكروا الله is a verb, an agent and a direct object, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional. (كَما عَلَّمَكُمْ): the kāf and what it governs is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq or a ḥāl, and ما is maṣdarī; the clause علمكم has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila of a particle-type relative «[Translator's note: the source says "jawāb mawṣūl ḥarfī", literally "apodosis of a particle relative"; the intended word is evidently ṣila]». (ما لَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْلَمُونَ): ما is a relative noun, the second object of علمكم; the clause لم تكونوا is the ṣila and the clause تعلمون is the khabar of «نكونوا» «[Translator's note: the source prints نكونوا with a nūn; the verb in the verse is تكونوا]»; what is meant is "what you did not know of the prayer of fear", which is set out in the books of jurisprudence. (وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنْكُمْ): the waw is resumptive and الذين is a mubtadaʾ; the clause يتوفون is the ṣila, and the waw is the nāʾib fāʾil; منكم is attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْواجاً): conjoined to يتوفون, and أزواجا is a direct object. (وَصِيَّةً لِأَزْواجِهِمْ): وصية is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, that is, "they bequeath a bequest", and this verbal clause is the khabar of الذين; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of وصية. (مَتاعاً إِلَى الْحَوْلِ): it is permissible to put متاعا in the accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, that is, "they provide for them a provision", or as a badal from وصية, or as a ḥāl. It was also said that it is accusative by وصية, and it was said by an omitted verb, that is, "provide for them a provision". And إلى الحول is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of متاعا, that is, "extending to the year". (غَيْرَ إِخْراجٍ): غير is a ḥāl, that is, "while they are not to be driven out of their dwelling" «[Translator's note: the source prints "ʿayr mukhrajāt" for "ghayr mukhrajāt"]». Al-Akhfash said it is an adjective of His saying متاعا, as if He had said: "not an expulsion"; Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī chose it, and there is no objection to it. It was also said that it is accusative by removal of the preposition. We have only listed these aspects because they are equal in preference. (فَإِنْ خَرَجْنَ): the fāʾ is resumptive and إن is conditional; خرجن is a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of the jussive as the protasis. (فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ): the fāʾ links the apodosis, and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. (فِي ما فَعَلْنَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِنَّ مِنْ مَعْرُوفٍ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl; the clause فعلن is the ṣila of the relative; في أنفسهن is attached to His saying فعلن; and من معروف is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl. (وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ): the clause is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ and عزيز حكيم are its two khabars.

* I'rab:
(وَلِلْمُطَلَّقاتِ مَتاعٌ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ): the waw is resumptive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar; متاع is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and بالمعروف is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of متاع. (حَقًّا عَلَى الْمُتَّقِينَ): حقا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, and على المتقين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «حقا». (كَذلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آياتِهِ): كذلك is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq or a ḥāl; الله is the agent of يبين; لكم is attached to يبين; and آياته is a direct object. (لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ): laʿalla and its noun; the clause تعقلون is its khabar; and the clause of hope is a ḥāl.
